title: Export fails on 48 kHz devices (IR cache ignores sample rate), and a failed or hung export leaves Tone's global context stuck on the dead offline context
evidence: reverbIR.ts:43 and :47 key the decoded and processed IR caches by `type` and `${type}:${quant}` only (162-163), with no sample rate. loadNativeIr decodes on whichever context asks first (94 `ctx.decodeAudioData(bytes)`), and applyDecayEnvelope builds the processed IR at the native buffer's rate (121 `const sr = native.sampleRate`, 127 `ctx.createBuffer(..., len, sr)`). The file header (6-9) assumes a single context ('never throws on assignment'). Return A ships with reverb on (returnsSlice.ts:47-48 `reverb: { ...base.reverb, enabled: true, wet: 1 }`), so the live return sync (usePlaybackEngine.ts:634-640) loads the hall IR on the live context at engine start. renderProject.ts:174 forces `opts.sampleRate ?? 44100` (exportAudio passes none). Its Return A chain (213-216 `chain.update(ret.effects)`) reaches EffectChain.ts:1294-1296 `const real = getProcessedIr(this.ctx, type, decay); if (real) { this.reverbConvolver.buffer = real; ...}`, which assigns a live-rate buffer to a ConvolverNode on a 44.1 kHz OfflineAudioContext. Mismatched rates must throw NotSupportedError, and standardized-audio-context passes the setter straight to the native node (src/factories/convolver-node-constructor.ts:50-51). Tone's Offline (node_modules/tone/build/esm/core/context/Offline.js:43-51) runs `setContext(context); yield callback(context); ... setContext(originalContext)` with no try/finally, and renderProject's dispose loop (293-300) is not in a finally either. A hang causes the same stuck state: `await Promise.all(inits)` (285) has no timeout, and PianoSampler.init only resolves in `onload` from tonejs.github.io (PianoSampler.ts:18-65). ExportAudioDialog.tsx:256-260 only shows an 'Export failed' toast.
impact: On a 48 kHz output (most Windows PCs, Chromebooks, iPads and many Macs), every export of a default project fails once the real IR has loaded. It works on 44.1 kHz machines, which can hide the bug in testing. After a failure, Tone.getTransport() and getContext() return the never-rendered offline context, so Play, the metronome, MIDI Parts and transport-scheduled clips silently stop working until the page is reloaded, and the half-built graph's gate loops leak. A blocked sample CDN leaves export stuck on 'Rendering…' with the same breakage.
recommendation: Render at the live rate (`opts.sampleRate ?? audioEngine.getSampleRate()`, which is also Tone.Offline's own default). Key nativeCache and processedCache by ctx.sampleRate and decode once per rate. Capture `const live = Tone.getContext()` before rendering and restore it, plus dispose every chain, in a finally. Add a timeout and an error path to instrument loading, and stop playback before rendering. Add an export test at 48 kHz.
verifierNote: The IR caches have no sample rate in their keys (reverbIR.ts:43,47,162-163), and applyDecayEnvelope builds the IR at `native.sampleRate` (reverbIR.ts:121,127). renderProject forces `opts.sampleRate ?? 44100` (renderProject.ts:174), exportAudio.ts:76 passes no rate, and on enable the Return A chain reaches `this.reverbConvolver.buffer = real` (EffectChain.ts:1294-1296, called at 1328). The standardized-audio-context setter writes straight through to the native node (convolver-node-constructor.js:29-30), so a 48 kHz IR on a 44.1 kHz offline context throws NotSupportedError. Tone's Offline.js:43-51 has no try/finally around `yield callback(context)`, so the global context stays on the offline one, and the dispose loop at renderProject.ts:293-300 never runs.
impactNote: All links in the chain check out. reverbIR.ts:43/47 key nativeCache and processedCache by type and `${type}:${quant}` only. loadNativeIr decodes on whichever context asks first (reverbIR.ts:94), and applyDecayEnvelope builds the new buffer at native.sampleRate (121, 127). Return A ships with reverb enabled (returnsSlice.ts:47-48), so the live engine loads the IR at the hardware rate. renderProject.ts:174 forces `opts.sampleRate ?? 44100`, and exportAudio.ts:76 passes no rate. During the render, `chain.update(ret.effects)` (renderProject.ts:214) reaches EffectChain.update → applyReverbIr (EffectChain.ts:1328), which calls getProcessedIr and assigns the buffer (1293-1296) with no try/catch. The standardized-audio-context setter passes the buffer straight to the native node (convolver-node-constructor.ts:50-51). Chrome then throws NotSupportedError, because the spec requires the buffer and context sample rates to match. Tone's Offline.js:41-51 calls setContext(context) and awaits the callback with no try/finally, so after a throw the global context and transport stay on the dead OfflineContext. The disposables loop (renderProject.ts:293-300) is also skipped, which leaks the gate intervals. On a 48 kHz device (most Windows PCs and Chromebooks), exporting any project with the default Return A fails. Play, metronome and MIDI then stop working until a reload, and the only feedback is a toast. A hung `await Promise.all(inits)` (renderProject.ts:285) gives the same stuck state. Users will notice immediately, and it hides on 44.1 kHz test machines.
regressionRisks: Rendering at the live rate changes the exported sample rate on 48 kHz machines from 44.1 kHz to 48 kHz. Check the WAV/MP3 encoders and any '44.1 kHz' UI labels. Keying the IR caches by rate doubles IR memory when two rates are in use, so keep PROCESSED_CACHE_MAX bounded. Restoring the context in a finally must restore the same Tone Context object so that live TrackEngines and listeners like transport.on('loop') stay bound. If you stop playback before rendering, reset the isPlaying store state too, or the UI and transport will disagree. ReverbPedal shares the same getProcessedIr path and must move to the new rate-aware key. Add an export test that runs at 48 kHz.

title: Recording over an earlier take corrupts or orphans it: remainders ignore offsetSeconds, drop assetId and gain, and lose their buffer reference
evidence: overwriteAudioRegion.ts:8-11 says 'offsetSeconds is not honored by the scheduler'. That is out of date: AudioClipScheduler.ts:33-35 and 53-56 do honor it. The left remainder is sliced from sample 0 (89 `sliceBuffer(ctx, buffer, 0, endSample)`) and the right one from `toTick - clip.startTick` (102-108); both ignore the clip's offsetSeconds. The new clips copy only id, startTick, duration and fades (92-98, 112-118), with no offsetSeconds, assetId or gain. Meanwhile the original clip is removed from the track (79) and its buffer from the store (121). This runs after every audio take (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1129-1136). Clips without an assetId are only uploaded on the next manual cloud Save; autosave writes metadata to localStorage only (useAutosave.ts; localSession.ts:17). After a refresh only clips with an assetId are fetched again (load-audio.ts:74, useCollabAudioLoader.ts:30-33), and the Timeline draws a fake seeded-random waveform for clips with neither a buffer nor an assetId (Timeline.tsx:983-988).
impact: Recording a new take over part of a clip whose start was trimmed makes the surviving parts play the wrong audio, shifted by the trim. The surviving parts no longer point at the original cloud file. If the page refreshes or crashes before the next manual Save, they come back as silent clips with a fake waveform, and the student's earlier take is gone from the project. A later Save re-uploads the remainders as new files, duplicating storage.
recommendation: Make overwrite non-destructive. Keep the original buffer and asset, and create remainder clips that reference the same assetId with an adjusted offsetSeconds and duration; the scheduler and serializer already support this. Never evict buffers here, and apply the whole overwrite as one store update so it is one undo step. Use the same approach for Timeline split (Timeline.tsx:1660-1690, 1945-1970).
verifierNote: The left remainder is sliced from sample 0 (overwriteAudioRegion.ts:89) and the right from `toTick - clip.startTick` (102-108), with no offsetSeconds. The new clips copy only id, startTick, duration and fades (92-98, 112-118), and the original buffer is evicted (121). Only the new take is uploaded at once (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1141-1158). Remainders have no assetId or original bytes, and autosave writes only metadata to localStorage (localSession.ts:14-18). After a reload, loaders refetch only clips with an assetId (load-audio.ts:74).
impactNote: overwriteAudioRegion runs after every audio take (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1129-1136). For each clip that overlaps the take, it removes the original from the track (overwriteAudioRegion.ts:79) and evicts its buffer and original bytes (121). It then adds remainders built only from id, startTick, duration and fades (92-98, 112-118), so assetId, offsetSeconds and gain are dropped. The left slice starts at sample 0 (89) and the right slice at toTick - clip.startTick (102-108), both ignoring the clip's offsetSeconds, even though AudioClipScheduler.ts:52-56 honors offsets. The header comment at lines 8-11 is out of date. Only the new take is uploaded right away (1141+). The remainders have no assetId and no original bytes, and autosave writes to localStorage only (useAutosave.ts:11-21). After a reload or crash, useCollabAudioLoader.ts:30-33 fetches only clips that have an assetId, so the surviving parts of the earlier take come back silent with a fake waveform. In a collab session, peers never receive the remainder audio. Re-recording a section of an earlier take is a core student flow, and the loss is silent and permanent if the student relies on autosave.
regressionRisks: Remainders that share one assetId need care in three places: server-side asset GC or delete-on-clip-remove (deleting one half must not delete the shared asset), the cloud Save upload dedupe (don't re-upload when an assetId already exists), and Yjs clip sync, where peers must map assetId to a shared buffer. AudioBufferStore and pitchBufferCache are keyed by clip id, so reference-share the AudioBuffer or key by asset. Make the overwrite a single store update or a single pushUndo, or undo history changes shape: today removeAudioClip and addAudioClip each may push a separate undo step. Older saved projects whose remainders were created by slicing (no offset) must keep loading unchanged. Timeline split (Timeline.tsx:1660, 1951) has the same slice-and-evict logic and should change together for consistency.

title: 'Leave without saving' deletes the user's pre-existing cloud project
evidence: LeaveSavePrompt.tsx:43-58: `const { sessionSaved, projectId } = useStore.getState(); if (token && projectId && !sessionSaved) { await studioProjectsApi.remove(token, projectId); }`. The comment assumes projectId is 'the auto-created draft project (minted on the first record-stop)', but nothing guarantees that. collabSlice.ts:116-124 `_setRoomInfo` resets `sessionSaved: false` and leaves projectId untouched. CollabToolbar.tsx:61-74 runs Create Session / Join from whatever project is open, and CollabProvider.tsx:432-449 never touches projectId. ensureProjectId returns the existing id (api.ts:222-227), and sessionSaved is only set when `isCollabActive` is true (api.ts:307-311), which is false during any reconnect. Only the ?collab= URL boot resets projectId (DawApp.tsx:368-369).
impact: Example: a host opens a saved song, clicks Create Session, the class works on it, then the host clicks Leave Session → 'Leave without saving', expecting only the session's changes to be discarded. The app sends DELETE /projects/<that song>. The same happens to anyone who used Join Room while a saved project was open, and to a user who saved during a connection blip.
recommendation: Record the id of a draft minted during this session (e.g. sessionDraftProjectId, set in ensureProjectId while in a session) and only ever delete that one. Never delete a project that existed before _setRoomInfo. Relabel the choices: 'Save my copy' / 'Discard session changes'. Set sessionSaved based on session membership, not socket state. Add a test: host with a saved project leaves without saving.
verifierNote: LeaveSavePrompt.tsx:45-47 runs `if (token && projectId && !sessionSaved) await studioProjectsApi.remove(token, projectId)`. createAndJoinRoom and joinRoomById (CollabProvider.tsx:432-449) never clear projectId, and _setRoomInfo only resets sessionSaved (collabSlice.ts:116-124). So a host who starts a session from a saved song, or a joiner with their own project open, sends DELETE /projects/<their song> (api.ts:182-186) when they pick 'Leave without saving'. The Leave button is shown to owners too (CollabToolbar.tsx:255-272). The API returns deletedAt, so it may be a soft delete, but the project still vanishes from the user's library.
impactNote: LeaveSavePrompt.tsx:43-47 deletes whatever projectId is in the store when sessionSaved is false. createAndJoinRoom/joinRoomById (CollabProvider.tsx:432-449) never reset projectId. ensureProjectId returns an existing id unchanged (api.ts:222-227). _setRoomInfo sets sessionSaved:false (collabSlice.ts:116-124). The host reaches this prompt from the toolbar Leave button (CollabToolbar.tsx:255-260). Example: a teacher opens a saved song from the dashboard (?project=), clicks Create Session, then Leave → 'Leave without saving', and the server receives DELETE for that song. The same happens to a joiner who used Join while their own saved project was open. This is permanent data loss on a common teacher path.
regressionRisks: If deletion is limited to a draft minted during the session, true drafts can be left behind; the hourly orphan cron mentioned in the comment covers those. Setting sessionSaved from session membership instead of socket state depends on the inSession/connection split (collab-09). If the prompt labels are changed, check tutorial copy and anchors in tutorials.ts. Saved projects are unaffected because this only changes client logic.

title: Presence publishing becomes a self-sustaining broadcast loop that re-renders the whole editor and starves autosave
evidence: CollabProvider.tsx:541-564 subscribes with a selector that returns a new object, `(state) => ({ selectedTrackId, selectedClipId, editingClipId })`, and no equalityFn. subscribeWithSelector defaults to Object.is (node_modules/zustand/esm/middleware.mjs:252-258), so the listener runs on every store set and calls `awareness.setLocalState({...current, ..., lastActiveAt: Date.now(), ...})`. setLocalState always emits 'update' (node_modules/y-protocols/awareness.js:134); the provider broadcasts every 'update' (node_modules/y-partykit/dist/chunk-W4BXM3IL.mjs:291-303, 316); the server relays it to all connections (y-partykit/dist/index.mjs:123-132). On the receiving peer, applyAwarenessUpdate emits 'change' because lastActiveAt differs (awareness.js:278-288). Its onAwarenessChange then builds a new Map and calls `_setRemoteUsers` (CollabProvider.tsx:375-386). That is a store set, so that peer's presence listener fires and broadcasts back. lastActiveAt is never read anywhere (grep).
impact: With two or more users, presence updates bounce back and forth at network round-trip speed, even when everyone is idle. With three or more users, each broadcast triggers a reply from every other client, so traffic compounds. During playback, each 33 ms position tick also broadcasts. Every `_setRemoteUsers` re-renders the entire editor: useStudioMonitor subscribes to `remoteUsers` inside DawAppInner (useStudioMonitor.ts:25, DawApp.tsx:84), and TimelineWithHeaders, Timeline, LibraryPanel and the bottom ChannelStrip are not memoized. MasterTrackHeader (`useRemoteUsers().length > 0`, line 42) and every remotely-locked TrackHeader (line 76) re-render too. useAutosave resets its 1.5 s debounce on every set (useAutosave.ts:19-25), so crash-recovery autosave never writes during a session. PartyKit message volume and cost scale the same way.
recommendation: Publish presence only when the selection actually changes (`{ equalityFn: shallow }` or three primitive subscriptions). Drop lastActiveAt from per-change updates; if idle locks need it, refresh it at most every ~10 s. In onAwarenessChange, only call _setRemoteUsers when a peer's selection, name or colour changed. Move remoteUsers into a small presence store, and make useStudioMonitor use store.subscribe inside an effect instead of a render subscription. Add narrow hooks (useHasPeers, useTrackLockOwner returning primitives).
verifierNote: CollabProvider.tsx:542-563 subscribes with a selector that returns a new object and passes no equalityFn. subscribeWithSelector falls back to Object.is (zustand middleware.mjs:252-258), so the listener runs on every store set and calls setLocalState with a fresh lastActiveAt. That always emits 'update' (awareness.js:134), which the provider broadcasts. On the peer, applyAwarenessUpdate emits 'change' because the deep-equality check fails on lastActiveAt (awareness.js:278-288). Its handler then calls _setRemoteUsers (CollabProvider.tsx:386), a store set that fires that peer's own listener. The result is a self-sustaining ping-pong. useStudioMonitor reads remoteUsers at DawAppInner level (useStudioMonitor.ts:25), and useAutosave restarts its 1.5 s debounce on every set (useAutosave.ts:19-25), so both effects described are real.
impactNote: The store uses subscribeWithSelector (store/index.ts:48-49). The selector at CollabProvider.tsx:543-550 returns a new object and no equalityFn, so Object.is fails on every set (zustand middleware.mjs:252-258) and setLocalState runs with a new lastActiveAt (line 559). On the receiving peer, applyAwarenessUpdate emits 'change' when the deep state differs (awareness.js:~278-288). onAwarenessChange calls _setRemoteUsers with a new Map (CollabProvider.tsx:375-386), which is another store set, so that peer broadcasts back. The two peers ping-pong at network round-trip speed. With 3 or more peers every message gets N-1 replies, so traffic grows quickly. Locally, every unrelated store set (e.g. the 33 ms position tick) also triggers a local 'change' → _setRemoteUsers → another update. lastActiveAt is never read (grep shows only the types and two writes). useStudioMonitor subscribes to remoteUsers inside DawApp (useStudioMonitor.ts:25, DawApp.tsx:84), so the whole editor re-renders on every bounce. useAutosave resets its debounce on every set (useAutosave.ts:19-25), so autosave never fires during a session. On Chromebooks this shows up as constant jank in any session with 2 or more people.
regressionRisks: Low. Adding a shallow equalityFn (or three primitive subscriptions) and dropping lastActiveAt from per-change updates breaks no readers. If onAwarenessChange gets a diff guard, the selection tiebreaker in that handler (lines 391-407) must still run when a peer's selectedTrackId changes. Moving remoteUsers into a separate store touches useTrackPresence/useRemoteUsers (presence.ts) and the TrackHeader lock styling. Tutorial anchors are unaffected.

title: Dock note editors use the clip's timeline start as the note origin: clips not at bar 1 look empty and new notes land in the wrong bar
evidence: Clip events are stored relative to the clip. MidiScheduler.ts:16,29 computes `startTicks = event.startTick + offsetTicks`, and the offset is clip.startTick (usePlaybackEngine.ts:672-681). Timeline.tsx:655-656 says 'Events are clip-relative (playback adds clip.startTick)', and PianoRollModal.tsx:87-92 therefore anchors the editor at min(event ticks, clip.startTick). PianoRoll treats clipStartTick as the editor's origin: PianoRoll.tsx:345-347 `songOffset = timelineStartTick + clipStartTick` and 657 `relTick = ev.startTick - clipStartTick`. The dock instead passes the clip's timeline start: ChannelStrip.tsx:334-335 `clipStartTick={selectedClip?.startTick ?? 0}` and `timelineStartTick={selectedClip?.startTick ?? 0}`; KeyboardView.tsx:331-332 does the same. DrumMachineView.tsx:170 sets `clipStartTick = clip?.startTick ?? 0`, draws notes at `(ev.startTick - clipStartTick) * pixelsPerTick` (502-503; also 607, 695, 863) and stores new notes at `snapToGrid(x / pixelsPerTick + clipStartTick)` (743-744, 920-921, 973-974, 1008), while its playhead uses `position - clipStartTick` (1282). Clips start after bar 1 all the time: paste at the playhead (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:125 `startTick: position`), Cmd+D (152), arrow-key nudge (330), timeline drags. Related, cross-slice: Cmd+D computes the copy's offset as if events were absolute (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:143-147), so for a clip at bar 2 or later the copy lands on top of the original.
impact: Take any clip that doesn't start at tick 0: one that was pasted, duplicated, nudged, or belongs to a later section. The dock's PIANO ROLL, KeyboardView's Piano Roll mode and the drum grid draw its notes off the left edge, so the editor looks empty (the dock roll's ruler is also shifted by a second clip.startTick). Every note the student adds is saved clip.startTick ticks after where they clicked: a kick drawn on beat 1 of a clip at bar 5 plays at bar 9. The same clip edits correctly in PianoRollModal, so the result depends on which editor was used.
recommendation: Share one 'editor origin' helper with PianoRollModal and use it everywhere. Pass clipStartTick as the clip-relative origin (0, or the smallest event tick) and timelineStartTick = clip.startTick. In DrumMachineView treat events as clip-relative: x = (ev.startTick − origin) × ppt, and a new note's tick = snap(x / ppt) + origin. Keep the playhead at position − clip.startTick. Add a regression test with a clip at startTick 7680. Fix Cmd+D to use the clip-relative content length (or durationTicks).
verifierNote: Clip events are clip-relative: MidiScheduler.ts:29 `event.startTick + offsetTicks` with offset = clip.startTick (usePlaybackEngine.ts:680). Yet ChannelStrip.tsx:334-335 passes `clipStartTick={selectedClip?.startTick ?? 0}` and `timelineStartTick={selectedClip?.startTick ?? 0}`, and PianoRoll.tsx:347/657/1050 subtract and add clipStartTick, so for a clip at 7680 the notes draw off-screen and new notes are stored 7680 ticks late. DrumMachineView.tsx:170/502/743 and KeyboardView.tsx:331-332 have the same bug. The Cmd+D side note also holds: useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:143-147 seeds the reduce with midiClip.startTick, so duration is 0 and the copy lands on top of the original.
impactNote: Playback treats events as clip-relative. MidiScheduler.ts:29 adds offsetTicks, and usePlaybackEngine.ts:672-681 passes clip.startTick as that offset. The dock editors subtract the clip's timeline start anyway. ChannelStrip.tsx:334-335 passes clip.startTick as both clipStartTick and timelineStartTick, so PianoRoll.tsx:347 counts it twice (songOffset) and PianoRoll.tsx:657 computes relTick = ev.startTick - clip.startTick, which is negative. KeyboardView.tsx:331-332 does the same. DrumMachineView.tsx:170 sets clipStartTick = clip.startTick, draws notes at (ev.startTick - clipStartTick) (502) and stores clicks at x/ppt + clipStartTick (743). The paste at useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:125 (startTick: position) and Cmd+D at 143-151 easily create clips that don't start at bar 1. So a student who pastes or duplicates and then edits in the dock sees an empty grid and writes notes far after the clicked spot. That is silent corruption of saved data in a core flow. PianoRollModal.tsx:87-92 already computes the origin correctly, so a shared helper is a sound fix. The Cmd+D duplicate math (143-147) is also wrong for a clip starting at a non-zero tick.
regressionRisks: Some code still treats events as absolute ticks. Timeline.tsx split (~1625-1640) filters events with `ev.startTick >= splitTick`, comparing them to an absolute tick, and gives the right-hand clip unshifted events. Fixing only the editors could hide or expose differently any projects that already contain absolute-tick events from older split/drum-view edits. Audit split, the prismSlice clip builders, importJamSession and applyDemoDrums for consistent tick conventions. Consider a one-time migration or heuristic only if saved data shows absolute events. The DrumMachineView playhead must stay at position - clip.startTick. The tutorial checks count events, not positions, so they are unaffected. In collab, peers receive the corrected events through the normal updateMidiClipEvents path, so there is no protocol change.

title: The mastering chain, master fader and bypass are never saved or reset: lost on refresh and carried into the next project
evidence: serializeSession() (SessionSerializer.ts:274-337) saves tracks, prism, chordRegions, `returns: state.returns` (333) and `masterAutomation` (334), but not masteringFxChain, masteringEffects, masteringBypass or masterVolume. serializeSessionForCloud() (429-505) likewise sends only `returns` (502) and per-track settings. deserializeSession (762-793), deserializeCloudProject (611-627) and resetSessionToEmpty (649-678) never set those four keys, and resetSessionToEmpty doesn't reset `returns` either. The only other writers are the slice defaults (masteringSlice.ts:88-91: `masteringFxChain: []`, `masterVolume: 0.8`) and the collab sync. Grepping src/lib, src/features and src/daw/persistence for 'mastering' finds nothing else. renderProject.ts:165-171 bounces with whatever masteringEffects and masterVolume are currently in the store.
impact:
Each kind of reload behaves differently:
- **Browser refresh / crash recovery:** every mastering effect added in MASTER (or through the Master track's FX pop-out), plus the master fader, silently resets to empty and 0.8. Tracks, sends and returns do come back, so the student's tutorial STAGE 5 work disappears without warning.
- **Opening a saved cloud project:** its mastering was never saved, and the module-singleton store keeps the previous project's chain, bypass and master level. Project B plays and exports through project A's compressor or saturator.
- **New project (resetSessionToEmpty):** inherits the old mastering chain and any modified return buses.
- **Collab:** this is the only path that carries mastering, so solo and collab users get different results.
recommendation: Add `mastering: { fxChain, effects, bypass, masterVolume }` to SessionData and to the cloud payload. Ideally this is a project-level field; until the API has one, carry it on track[0].settings the way masterAutomation already is. Restore it with DEFAULT_EFFECTS backfill, mirroring restoreReturns. Reset mastering and returns to defaults in deserializeCloudProject, deserializeSession and resetSessionToEmpty when the payload lacks them. Add a round-trip test that checks mastering survives a save and that loading project B clears project A's chain.
verifierNote: serializeSession only writes `returns: state.returns` and `masterAutomation` (SessionSerializer.ts:333-334). deserializeCloudProject (611-627), resetSessionToEmpty (649-678) and deserializeSession (762-793) never set masteringFxChain, masteringEffects, masteringBypass or masterVolume, and resetSessionToEmpty doesn't reset returns either. The only other writers of these keys are the slice defaults (masteringSlice.ts:88-91) and collab (YjsDocManager.ts:414-420, yjsToZustand.ts:241-269). The store has no zustand persist, so mastering is lost on refresh and carries over into the next project loaded in the same session.
impactNote: Every part of the evidence checks out. serializeSession saves only `returns: state.returns` and `masterAutomation` (SessionSerializer.ts:333-334). Neither deserializeCloudProject (611-627) nor deserializeSession (762-793) sets masteringFxChain, masteringEffects, masteringBypass or masterVolume. resetSessionToEmpty (649-678) resets masterAutomation but not mastering or returns. The local autosave path (src/lib/studio-projects/localSession.ts:16,46) goes through these same functions, so a refresh restores tracks, sends and returns but leaves mastering at the slice defaults (masteringSlice.ts:88-91: [] and 0.8). Loading project B or starting a new project inherits A's chain, bypass and master level, and renderProject bounces with them. Only collab carries these fields (YjsDocManager.ts:414-420). Users will notice this in two flows: the tutorial's STAGE 5 mastering work disappears after a refresh, and project B plays and exports through project A's compressor. That is silent data loss plus cross-project bleed, so critical is justified.
regressionRisks: Old saves and old cloud projects have no mastering field. Loads must reset mastering to defaults when it's missing; restoring 'whatever is in the store' would keep the bleed. Backfill masteringEffects from DEFAULT_EFFECTS, as restoreReturns does, so old EffectChain slots don't come back undefined. Keep masteringFxChain and the `enabled` flags consistent. Carrying the data on track[0].settings, like masterAutomation, is lost on projects with zero tracks, so search for it the way masterAutomationFromCloud does. Collab join must not let a stale local restore overwrite the Y 'mastering' map, or the reverse. After loading, call resetUndoHistory as now. Restoring a non-empty chain rebuilds the mastering EffectChain, so expect a short click if this happens during playback; loads already stop the transport (isPlaying: false). Add tests for the save/load round trip and for loading B after A.

title: Cloud save then reopen drops the chord lane, mode, time signature, markers, mastering and Score/Lead Sheet marks
evidence: serializeSessionForCloud (SessionSerializer.ts:429-505) returns only name, composerName, bpm, prism {rootNote, rhythmName, genre, swing}, returns and tracks (490-503; CloudProjectInput 393-418). There is no chordRegions, mode, timeSignature, markers, mastering*/masterVolume, leadSheet*/score* marks or pitchData. deserializeCloudProject spreads freshProjectHarmony() (613), which sets mode 'ionian' and empties chordRegions, leadSheetSections/Repeats and the score marks (512-544). The code comment says 'Chord symbols aren't part of a cloud project yet, so it opens with none' (612). Both open paths then call offerChordAnalysis() (DawApp.tsx:139-140; FileMenu.tsx:222-223), which opens the prompt whenever chordRegions is empty and harmony notes exist (unisonSlice.ts:144-148).

title: Every SoundFont track receives every SoundFont channel: cross-talk, doubled level, mute/solo/FX don't isolate
evidence: SoundFontAdapter.init connects the module-level synth to each track with `sharedSynth!.connect(nativeOutput)` (SoundFontAdapter.ts:99-102). In spessasynth_lib 4.3.3, `connect(destinationNode) { for (let i = 0; i < 17; i++) this.worklet.connect(destinationNode, i); }` (node_modules/spessasynth_lib/dist/index.js:497-500). The processor writes each MIDI channel's dry audio to outputs 1–16 and the reverb/chorus send to output 0 (`processSplit(A.slice(1), A[0][0], A[0][1])` in spessasynth_processor.min.js). The per-channel API, `connectChannel(targetNode, channelNumber)` → output `channelNumber % 16 + 1` (index.js:574-576), is never used. So each TrackEngine input (gain → FX → audible gate → pan, TrackEngine.ts:33-37) receives every SoundFont track's notes. Two or more SoundFont tracks is routine: Prism's generated Chords track is `instrument: 'soundfont'` (prismSlice.ts:1706-1711), every demo already has a SoundFont bass (demoProjects.ts:172, 212, 272), and MIDI-loop drops default to soundfont with one track per sequence (Timeline.tsx:2642-2648). PrismSuggestionModal also inits a preview adapter with `audioEngine.getMasterGain()` as its output (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:198-202), so while it is open all SoundFont channels also bypass the tracks straight to master.
impact: With 2 SoundFont tracks every SoundFont note plays twice (about +6 dB; about +9.5 dB with 3), through both tracks' EQ/comp/reverb/pan. Muting or soloing a SoundFont track doesn't remove its notes, because they still arrive through the other SoundFont strip. Volume and pan only half-work, and meters show signal on empty tracks. Students mixing a Prism arrangement get contradictory results, and the summed level can clip the master.
recommendation: Route per channel: in init use `sharedSynth.connectChannel(nativeOutput, this.channel)`, and in dispose `disconnectChannel(nativeOutput, this.channel)`. Decide what to do with output 0 (synth-wide reverb/chorus): either disable the synth effects (setSystemParameter('effectsEnabled', false), or CC91/CC93 = 0 per channel) and rely on the DAW return buses, or connect output 0 once to a dedicated return. Keep insertion effects off, since per-channel outputs can go silent with them (index.js:568-569). Add a regression test that two adapters connect to different outputs.
verifierNote: SoundFontAdapter.ts:99 calls `sharedSynth!.connect(nativeOutput)` for every adapter, and spessasynth_lib index.js:497-498 connects all 17 worklet outputs (`for (let i = 0; i < 17; i++) this.worklet.connect(destinationNode, i)`). `connectChannel` (index.js:574) is never used. So every SoundFont TrackEngine input (TrackEngine.ts:33-37) gets every channel. Prism's Chords track is `instrument: 'soundfont'` (prismSlice.ts:1710) and the preview modal inits an adapter straight onto master (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:201), so with two or more SoundFont tracks mute, solo, pan and FX don't isolate.
impactNote: The bug is real and users will hear it. SoundFontAdapter.ts:99 calls `sharedSynth!.connect(nativeOutput)`, and in spessasynth_lib (dist/index.js:497-500) that connects all 17 worklet outputs (the synth declares numberOfOutputs: 18) to every SoundFont track's input. `connectChannel` (index.js:574-576) is never used. The comment at SoundFontAdapter.ts:33-35 shows channels are already allocated per track, but the audio is never split per channel. As soon as a project has 2 or more SoundFont tracks (Prism chords plus a demo bass, or several MIDI-loop drops), every GM note goes through every SoundFont strip. Muting or soloing one of them does nothing audible, it gets louder, and both FX chains are applied. The Prism preview (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:198-202) also connects every channel straight to master while the modal is open. A student mixing in the editor hits this in the core mixing flow.
regressionRisks: Output 0 carries the synth-wide reverb and chorus send. With per-channel routing only, GM tracks lose the reverb they currently get from GeneralUser's default CC91/CC93 and will sound drier than in saved projects users already know. Either disable synth effects on purpose and rely on DAW returns, or route output 0 once to a shared return. Don't connect it to each track, or the doubling comes back. The library says connectChannel is 'meant for visualization' and goes silent when insertion effects are on, so keep insertion effects off. dispose() must switch to disconnectChannel, because the current disconnect(nativeOutput) would otherwise tear down other routes. When 16 or more tracks share channels round-robin (allocateChannel), they still share audio; that is acceptable. The ConstantSource activator trick still has to run. No changes to project data, collab or tutorial anchors. Offline export of SoundFont tracks is already silent (renderProject.ts:24-30), so that path is unaffected.

title: Saved guitar/bass/vocal tone is not applied after any reload until each track's Controls tab is opened
evidence: The only callers of adapter.syncChain/loadNamModel in src/daw are the views: GuitarBassView.tsx:550-562 (syncChain), :534-547 (NAM restore) and :499-531 (NAM auto-load); VocalView.tsx:548-563. usePlaybackEngine.ts:446-447 says 'The track is the source of truth for the GM sound and the organ settings, so undo, project load and collab peers land here too'. Its init .then (513-557) applies Oracle Synth, drum pads, organ and Chops state but nothing for GuitarFxAdapter or VocalFxAdapter, which createInstrument builds bare ('return new GuitarFxAdapter()' / 'new VocalFxAdapter()'). A fresh GuitarPedalChain is a straight bypass ('this.inputNode.connect(this.outputNode)', GuitarPedalChain.ts:93-95). Clips are routed through the pedal input ('Schedule audio clips — route through pedal chain', usePlaybackEngine.ts:685-695), and takes are recorded dry: startRecordingStream taps channelGain before the chain. The whole registry is disposed when the editor unmounts (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1187-1191).
impact: After a refresh/crash recovery, opening a cloud project, leaving and returning to /studio/editor, or joining a collab session, every recorded guitar/bass DI and vocal take plays back dry: no NAM amp, pedals, reverb or pitch correction. This lasts until the student opens that track's CONTROLS tab, and even that works only if the engine started first (see live-input-03). Mixing in MASTER view happens on the wrong sound, and students conclude the save lost their tone.
recommendation: Make the store the source of truth, as for Organ and Chops. Add applyPedalChain(adapter, track.guitarChain or vocalChain, bpm) to the instrument-init .then and to the in-place track-sync loop in usePlaybackEngine. It should try updateProcessorParams first and fall back to syncChain, then restore the NAM model from namModelId through a module-level cache of parsed models. The views then only edit store state.
verifierNote: Confirmed: usePlaybackEngine.ts init .then (~513-557) applies OracleSynth/drums/organ/Chops but nothing for GuitarFx/VocalFx, and the only syncChain/loadNamModel callers are the views (GuitarBassView.tsx:554, VocalView.tsx:559-561). A fresh GuitarPedalChain is a bypass (GuitarPedalChain.ts:93-94), and clips are routed through the pedal input (usePlaybackEngine.ts:685-695). The saved chain is still in the store and is reapplied as soon as it is edited, so nothing is lost or corrupted. Under the rubric this is a high reload/persistence bug, not critical.
impactNote: Nothing outside the two views ever calls syncChain or loadNamModel. The only callers are VocalView.tsx:548-563 and GuitarBassView.tsx:499-562, and the adapters just forward (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:333-351, VocalFxAdapter.ts:251-257). The init .then in usePlaybackEngine.ts:513-557 restores Oracle Synth, drum pads, organ and Chops, but has no branch for GuitarFxAdapter or VocalFxAdapter. The in-place sync loop (:446-462) has none either. A fresh GuitarPedalChain is wired straight through (GuitarPedalChain.ts:93-95). Clips play back through the pedal input (usePlaybackEngine.ts:685-695), and takes are recorded dry: startRecordingStream taps channelGain, which sits before the chain (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:218-225, 275-279). So a saved guitar DI plays back with no amp or pedals after a reload. Because of live-input-03, opening Controls does not fix it either; the student has to touch a knob or remount the view. Every project with recorded guitar, bass or vocal will hit this, and a dry DI guitar sounds obviously wrong. That is why I kept it critical.
regressionRisks: (1) The track-sync effect runs on every change to the tracks array, so the new apply has to be idempotent. Compare the guitarChain/vocalChain reference, or try updateProcessorParams first. Otherwise unrelated edits (volume, mute, a collab peer's edit) will rewire the chain mid-playback and cause dropouts. (5) The NAM fetch is async, so load the model with a cancel token in case the track is deleted or its instrument changes first. No data-tutorial-id anchors in these views are affected.

title: Live input silently disconnects after every reload and on any collaborator edit (audioInputChannel not persisted or preserved)

Repo-wide, a non-null value is set only at track creation (tracksSlice.ts:589, :961) and by the views. The UI still shows the device and channel '1', because channelLabel falls back to '1' when the channel is null (VocalView.tsx:716-722, GuitarBassView.tsx:680-686). With no adapter stream, recording falls back to getUserMedia({ audio: audioConstraints }) with no deviceId (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1039-1055).

If the track is armed, the take is recorded from the system default mic instead of the interface input. In collab, any peer edit to any track nulls the local channel; the effect then calls setDevice(null) and cuts the guitarist's or singer's live input mid-performance.

In the views, default null to {mode:'mono',channel:0} instead of disconnecting, and show a 'Not connected — Reconnect' state whenever the adapter has no stream.

The view effects then call setDevice(null) (VocalView.tsx:536-539, GuitarBassView.tsx:474-477). Recording falls back to an unconstrained getUserMedia, i.e. the default mic (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1039-1055). Recording without an adapter stream falls back to the default getUserMedia mic (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1039-1055), so the take silently comes from the wrong input. In a collab session, any remote track change nulls the channel and cuts the live input. Recording is deferred during a take, but monitoring is not. Do not write the field into Yjs, because channel numbers belong to one user's hardware. Merge it per user in applyTracksFromDoc and pullDocIntoStore, as monitoring already is. Turning a null channel into mono 0 in the views means a stream may open on mount, which could trigger a mic prompt. That ties in with live-input-07. title: Docked piano rolls (PIANO ROLL tab, Keyboard controls) misplace every clip that doesn't start at bar 1
evidence: PianoRoll treats `clipStartTick` as the editor origin in clip-relative ticks. Notes are drawn at `x = (ev.startTick - clipStartTick) * pixelsPerTick` (PianoRoll.tsx:657-658), and a click creates a note at `x / pixelsPerTick + clipStartTick` (:1050). `timelineStartTick` is the clip's song position (`songOffset = timelineStartTick + clipStartTick`, :347; documented at :212-214). Events are clip-relative: playback schedules them at `event.startTick + clip.startTick` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:672-682 -> MidiScheduler.ts:28-29). The dock passes the song position for both props: ChannelStrip.tsx:333-335 `clipStartTick={selectedClip?.startTick ?? 0}` and `timelineStartTick={selectedClip?.startTick ?? 0}`. KeyboardView.tsx:331-332 does the same with `clip.startTick`.
impact: Take a clip at bar 5 (startTick 7680) with notes at clip ticks 0-7679. Every note gets a negative x and is drawn off the left edge, where it can't be reached, while the toolbar still reads 'N notes'. A note drawn at the first visible beat is stored at clip tick 7680+, so it plays 4 bars later than shown and may fall outside the clip box. title: Global clip shortcuts fire inside Score and Lead Sheet: deleting a note or chord also deletes the selected arrangement clip, and ⌥R starts recording

title: Chord-region ids restart at cr-1 on every page load, so edits after a reload hit the wrong chord
evidence: prismSlice.ts:45-49 keeps the id counter in module state: 'let _chordIdCounter = 0; ... return `cr-${++_chordIdCounter}`'. Restored regions keep their saved ids (SessionSerializer.ts:788, chordRegions: d.chordRegions). After a refresh the counter is back at 0, so these all mint cr-1, cr-2, ... again: insertChordRegion (1908-1947), setChordRegions tagging (1841), locked-mode slicing (675, 686), the song exporter and the practice builders. Lookups take the first match by id: deleteChordRegion (1949-1971) and renameChordRegion (1973-1984) use findIndex, and markAsMelody (2089-2098) filters out every region with that id. Collab diffs chord regions by id (diffEngine.ts:349-393), and a joining peer's counter also starts at 0.
impact: After a refresh, if a student inserts a chord in the Lead Sheet and then deletes or renames it, a different chord changes instead (often bar 1). Selecting one chord selects two, 'mark as melody' removes several, and duplicate React keys and Yjs entries make peers diverge. The chart is silently corrupted.
recommendation: Use crypto.randomUUID() for chord ids, as commitPrismSuggestion already does. Alternatively, seed the counter from the highest restored numeric id on every load and collab pull. Add a dedupe pass on deserialize to repair existing saves.
verifierNote: The counter is module state starting at 0 (prismSlice.ts:45-49), restored regions keep their saved ids (SessionSerializer.ts:788), insertChordRegion mints with nextChordId (1926, 1937), and delete/rename use findIndex (1952, 1976), so collisions after a refresh are real. However, a collision only happens when a saved id happens to fall in the low counter range that gets re-minted, and the 'often bar 1' and collab-divergence effects are conditional, so this is high rather than certain critical corruption.
impactNote: prismSlice.ts:45-49 holds a module-level counter that restarts at 0 on every page load. Restored autosaves keep their 'cr-N' ids (SessionSerializer.ts:788). insertChordRegion (prismSlice.ts:1926, 1937), locked slicing (675, 686) and the other builders (exportToStudio.ts:244, generatePracticeTrack.ts:358, buildGenrePracticeTrack.ts:341) then mint cr-1, cr-2... again. deleteChordRegion and renameChordRegion use findIndex on the id (1949-1984), and regions are sorted by startTick, so the earlier duplicate is hit. markAsMelody filters out every match (2089-2098). The flow is common: a student returns, the autosave restores, and they insert a chord on the lead sheet and then delete or rename it, so the wrong (earlier) chord changes. The fix is small.
regressionRisks: Switching to crypto.randomUUID changes the id format. Nothing appears to parse 'cr-' ids, but any test snapshots that assert cr-N will break. A dedupe pass on deserialize must also remap references keyed by chord id (melodyOverrides, selectedChordIds, scoreChordHidden if it keys by region id, and Yjs chordRegions entries) or those links will orphan. In collab, a deduped id rewrite on one peer must be pushed to the doc, or the peers diverge.

title: Offline export renders Oracle tracks wrong: the engine schedules against ctx.currentTime and wall-clock timers
evidence:
renderProject.ts:252-270 initializes the adapter on the offline context through asRunningContext. That proxy (89-97) forwards currentTime to the raw OfflineAudioContext. renderProject then applies the patch and schedules MIDI with Tone.Part (MidiScheduler.ts:58-66).

Tone's OfflineContext.render() runs _renderClock(), which emits every tick and so fires every Part callback, before this._context.startRendering() (OfflineContext.js:54-70, 75-80). The raw currentTime is therefore 0 for every engine call.

The engine schedules against ctx.currentTime, not the `time` it receives:
- Each Voice.noteOn calls stopAllSources()/startActiveSources() (Voice.ts:273-275), which runs UnisonEngine.destroyOscillators 'osc.stop(); osc.disconnect()' (UnisonEngine.ts:191-197) and rebuildOscillators 'osc.start()' (167).
- Pitch is set with 'osc.frequency.setValueAtTime(freq, this.ctx.currentTime)' (52-58).
- A steal calls forceStop, which runs 'envGain.gain.cancelScheduledValues(now)' with now = ctx.currentTime (Voice.ts:371-375). The allocator steals a releasing voice before creating a new one (VoiceManager.ts:86-94 vs 96-108).
- Envelope.release starts from 'target.value' (Envelope.ts:61), which before rendering is the initial 0.
- Voices are freed by setTimeout (Voice.ts:346-351, 382-391); those timers fire mid-render and call osc.stop() at an arbitrary render position.
- The arp runs on setInterval (Arpeggiator.ts:228-234).
impact:
File > Export Audio (ExportAudioDialog > exportProjectAudio > renderProject, exportAudio.ts:71-76) produces broken Oracle tracks:
- On each voice, only the oscillators from its last note-on stay in the graph (earlier ones are stopped at 0 and disconnected). They play that last note's pitch from t=0.
- Every steal wipes that voice's whole envelope timeline.
- Releases drop to 0 with no tail.
- Wall-clock timers can stop the surviving oscillators mid-render.

A melodic Oracle part exports as near-silence plus at most the final note per voice, so the bounce does not match what the student heard.
recommendation:
Make the engine schedule from the `time` it is given:
- Pass `time` through allocateVoice, forceStop and Voice.noteOn.
- Start new oscillators with osc.start(time) and set frequency at `time`.
- Fade outgoing sources and stop them with osc.stop(time + fade) instead of stop()/disconnect() now.
- Replace setTimeout voice lifetimes with scheduled stops plus `onended` (or a queue keyed on context time).
- Compute release start levels analytically.
- Schedule arp steps from `time`.

Until this lands, warn about or exclude Oracle tracks in Export Audio. Add an OfflineAudioContext regression test asserting that two sequenced notes each produce energy at their own time and pitch.
verifierNote: renderProject.ts:252-259 initializes the engine on the raw offline context through the proxy. Before startRendering, that context's currentTime is 0, and Tone's render() runs _renderClock first (OfflineContext.js:75-80). Voice.noteOn runs stopAllSources/startActiveSources immediately (Voice.ts:274-275, UnisonEngine.ts:167,193). forceStop cancels from ctx.currentTime (Voice.ts:372-375), and the allocator steals releasing voices first (VoiceManager.ts:86-94), so a sequenced melody collapses to roughly the last note per voice; ExportAudioDialog.tsx:150-169 warns only for SoundFont and amp tracks, not Oracle.
impactNote:
I traced the code and the bug is real. renderProject.ts:186-193 takes ctx from offlineCtx.rawContext, and asRunningContext (89-97) only fakes `state`, so currentTime still comes from the raw OfflineAudioContext. Tone's OfflineContext.render() runs _renderClock(), which fires every Part callback, before it calls startRendering() (OfflineContext.js:54-80), so the raw currentTime is 0 for every note event.

What goes wrong at time 0:
- Voice.noteOn (Voice.ts:273-275) runs stopAllSources/startActiveSources. That ends in UnisonEngine.destroyOscillators calling osc.stop() with no time (UnisonEngine.ts:190-197), so each earlier oscillator set on that voice stops at 0.
- setFrequency uses this.ctx.currentTime (UnisonEngine.ts:52-58).
- forceStop/Envelope.forceStop use ctx.currentTime (Voice.ts:354-376, Envelope.ts:64-69), so a steal wipes the voice's whole envelope timeline from 0.
- Envelope.release reads target.value (Envelope.ts:61), which is the initial value before rendering starts.
- setTimeout-based freeing (Voice.ts:346-351, 382-391) runs on wall-clock time while the render is in progress.
- Arps are additionally driven by setInterval with no time (Arpeggiator.ts:223-234).

Result: File > Export Audio renders Oracle tracks (the most common instrument; tracksSlice.ts uses 'oracle-synth' across the defaults and demos) as mostly silence or the wrong pitch. Students are likely to hand in or share this file, so it is a broken core deliverable.

The recommended fix (thread `time` through, start/stop sources at scheduled times, scheduled stops instead of timers) is sound. Interim guard: warn about Oracle tracks in ExportAudioDialog until the fix lands.
regressionRisks:
- Overlaps heavily with fixes 02, 03 and 05, so these should land together or the live-playback timing will change twice.
- Replacing destroy/rebuild with scheduled osc.stop(time + fade) keeps old oscillators alive a little longer: slightly more nodes at once, and the vibrato/detune bus disconnect (the leak fix in destroyOscillators) must still run, from onended.
- Computing release levels analytically changes the release shape slightly compared with today's live behaviour.
- No impact on saved projects, collab or tutorial anchors (engine-only). Add an OfflineAudioContext regression test as suggested.

title: Voice allocator steals releasing voices before using spare polyphony, and steals hard-stop at 'now' instead of the scheduled time
evidence:
VoiceManager.allocateVoice (79-127) tries, in order:
1. a free voice
2. 'Steal oldest releasing voice' with voice.forceStop() (86-94)
3. only then creates a voice 'if this.voices.length < this.maxVoices' (96-108).

Voices are created lazily, so the pool only grows when no voice is free and none is releasing. Voice.noteOff sets state = 'releasing' at call time even when `time` is in the future (Voice.ts:309-311).

forceStop takes no time argument and ramps from this.ctx.currentTime (354-376). The next call, Voice.noteOn, runs stopAllSources() (273-275). UnisonEngine.destroyOscillators then stops and disconnects the old oscillators immediately (UnisonEngine.ts:190-197), before the 5 ms ramp (ANTI_CLICK_TIME, constants.ts:36) can take effect.

MidiScheduler queues each note's note-off before the next note's note-on at the same tick (MidiScheduler.ts:28-40). Tone dispatches Part callbacks lookAhead 0.1 s plus up to updateInterval 0.05 s early (tone Context.js:80-81; src/audio/core/toneBridge.ts:56 sets no override).
impact:
Live playing: whenever no voice is free, a key played during the previous note's release cuts that tail off with a click. That is the normal case, because melodic playing never grows the pool, so PAD-style melodies never overlap.

Piano roll: at every touching boundary (legato melody, repeated note, block-chord change):
- the outgoing note is faded at 'now', 100-150 ms before its scheduled end
- its oscillators are cut, which clicks
- the new pitch blips for 5 ms
- then there is silence until the new note starts.

The factory BASS, LEAD and WOBBLE presets (voiceCount 1, factoryPresets.ts:447, 579, 832) hit this on every note; chord progressions hit it on every chord change.
recommendation:
- Reorder allocation: free voice, then create a new one while under maxVoices, then steal the oldest releasing voice, then steal the oldest active voice.
- Make steals time-aware: forceStop(time) ramps the outgoing voice to 0 over 5-10 ms ending at `time`, and its sources stop with osc.stop(time) rather than immediately.
- Let the stolen voice's nodes finish fading on a separate list while the new note starts on a clean voice.
- Treat a voice as 'releasing' only from its scheduled release time.
verifierNote: VoiceManager.ts:86-108 steals the oldest releasing voice before creating one. Voice.noteOff sets 'releasing' at call time (Voice.ts:311), and forceStop ramps from ctx.currentTime with no time argument (354-376). noteOn then destroys the old oscillators immediately (Voice.ts:274; UnisonEngine.ts:190-197). MidiScheduler.ts:28-40 pushes each note-off before the next note-on, and the DAW never overrides Tone's 0.1 s lookAhead, so every touching boundary is cut 100-150 ms early with a click.
impactNote:
VoiceManager.allocateVoice (VoiceManager.ts:79-127) steals a releasing voice (step 2) before it creates one under maxVoices (step 3). Voice.noteOff sets state='releasing' as soon as it is called, even when `time` is in the future (Voice.ts:309-311).

MidiScheduler pushes a note's 'off' before the next note's 'on' at the same tick (MidiScheduler.ts:28-40). Tone keeps that order and runs both in the same callback, 0.1-0.15 s early (Tone's default Context lookAhead; toneBridge.ts creates new Tone.Context({context}) with no override).

What happens at each touching note boundary:
- The previous note becomes 'releasing'.
- The new note-on steals it with forceStop(), which ramps from ctx.currentTime (Voice.ts:354-376).
- Voice.noteOn then destroys the old oscillators immediately (Voice.ts:273-275 to UnisonEngine.ts:190-197).

The outgoing note is cut about 100-150 ms before its scheduled end, with a click, a 5 ms blip at the new pitch, and silence until `time`.

Mono/legato presets go through allNotesOff(time) and then the same steal (VoiceManager.ts:36-40). BASS, LEAD and WOBBLE are mono or legato with voiceCount 1 (factoryPresets.ts:446-447, 578-579, 831-832), so every legato bass line in the piano roll is audibly choppy (about 25% of a quarter note at 120 BPM). Poly melodies never grow the pool, so PAD tails are cut on every chord change in live playing too.

This is the main thing students hear in every project, so it fits the user's 'work perfectly' bar. The recommended reorder plus time-aware steal is correct.
regressionRisks:
- Growing the pool before stealing means more voices sound at once (overlapping tails). With unison stacks that is a real CPU increase on Chromebooks: bound it by maxVoices and consider an inaudible-tail cutoff.
- Making forceStop time-aware needs a 'zombie' list so fading nodes aren't reused. Mono/legato glide (setTargetAtTime from currentTime in UnisonEngine.setFrequency) must also move to `time`, or glide will start early.
- The per-voice modulation-matrix connection (SynthEngine.rawNoteOn calls modMatrix.connectVoice) must handle voices that are fading out but no longer allocated.
- No save-format, collab, undo or tutorial impact.

title: Splitting an audio clip discards its uploaded recording and slices the wrong audio
evidence: The scissors tool (Timeline.tsx:1649-1698) and 'Split at Playhead' (1927-1985) both compute splitSample from `offsetTicks = splitTick - clip.startTick` and slice `sliceBuffer(ctx, buffer, 0, splitSample)` / `(splitSample, buffer.length)`, ignoring clip.offsetSeconds, which playback honours (usePlaybackEngine.ts:705-716). They then call removeAudioBuffer on the original and add two clips built as `{ id, startTick, duration, fadeInTicks, fadeOutTicks }`: no assetId, offsetSeconds, gain or original bytes. AudioBufferStore.ts:11-12 says buffers 'Neither survives a page refresh'. Recordings are uploaded the moment recording stops for exactly that reason (upload-pending.ts:112-117), but split halves stay memory-only until an explicit cloud Save, and the cloud serializer drops clips with no assetId (SessionSerializer.ts:437-441). After a refresh, the halves have neither buffer nor assetId, so Timeline.tsx:984-990 paints a seeded random waveform over silence. Undo restores the original clip, but its buffer has already been deleted.
impact: Scenario: a student records a take, splits it to cut a mistake, then the tab reloads or crashes before Save. The recording is gone from the project (the original asset is left orphaned in GCS) while the timeline still shows a convincing fake waveform. Splitting a clip that was already trimmed at the start immediately plays the wrong audio, shifted by the trim. Every split is also re-encoded and re-uploaded on Save, losing quality and doubling storage.
recommendation: Make split non-destructive, the way trims already are. Both halves reuse the same AudioBuffer object and assetId (setAudioBuffer(leftId, buffer); setAudioBuffer(rightId, buffer)). Left half: {startTick, duration: offsetTicks, offsetSeconds: clip.offsetSeconds, gain}. Right half: {startTick: splitTick, duration: clip.duration - offsetTicks, offsetSeconds: (clip.offsetSeconds ?? 0) + offsetTicks / ticksPerSec, gain}. Carry the fades over. Never remove the source buffer during an edit; evict buffers when the project closes. Put this in a single store action (splitClipAt) used by the scissors tool, the context menu and any shortcut, and unit-test it on a trimmed clip.
verifierNote: Timeline.tsx:1659-1698 slices from sample 0 using `offsetTicks = splitTick - audioClip.startTick` and ignores clip.offsetSeconds, which playback passes through (usePlaybackEngine.ts:715). It then calls removeAudioBuffer(audioClip.id) and adds halves with no assetId, offsetSeconds or gain. serializeSession keeps `assetId: c.assetId ?? null` (SessionSerializer.ts:318-321), so after a refresh the halves have neither buffer nor asset and get the seeded fake waveform (Timeline.tsx:984-989). The cloud save drops them (437-441). One detail is overstated: an undo restores the original clip, which still has its assetId, so useCollabAudioLoader (useCollabAudioLoader.ts:24-34) downloads it again. The core data-loss bug holds.
impactNote: Both split paths (Timeline.tsx:1650-1698 scissors, 1927-1985 Split at Playhead) slice from sample 0 using offsetTicks = splitTick - clip.startTick and ignore clip.offsetSeconds. Playback honours offsetSeconds (usePlaybackEngine.ts:715) and so does the waveform (Timeline.tsx:904-906), so splitting a clip that was trimmed at the front immediately plays the wrong audio, shifted by the trim. The new clips are built without assetId, offsetSeconds or gain (1684-1697, 1969-1982). removeAudioBuffer(original) runs straight away (1681, 1966), so Ctrl+Z restores a clip whose buffer is gone and plays silence. That happens without any reload and is very likely after a bad cut. The cloud serializer drops clips with no assetId (SessionSerializer.ts:437-441). The local autosave keeps the halves with assetId null and no bytes, so after a refresh they hit the seeded-random placeholder (Timeline.tsx:984-989) because isLoadingCloudAudio needs an assetId (951). Splitting a take to cut a mistake is a core student flow, and both silent data loss and a fake waveform are severe. The non-destructive fix is right: share the buffer and assetId, adjust offsetSeconds, keep the source buffer.
regressionRisks: AudioBufferStore and resolvePitchBuffer/pitchData are keyed by clip id. Both halves must get their own entries pointing at the same AudioBuffer, and pitch-edit caches need re-keying or invalidating. Deleting one half must not free bytes the other half or the undo history still use, so evict only when the project closes. Halves share one assetId, so check that reconcileMissingAssets and any asset-GC or ref-count logic accept several clips per asset. Collab: halves with an assetId now sync audio to peers, which they didn't before. Check the diffEngine handles two clips with the same assetId. Existing saved projects with already-split, re-encoded halves stay as they are, and no migration is needed. Do both writes through one store action so undo records a single step, not remove + add + add (the 300 ms debounce currently hides this, but collab Yjs undo may record separate steps).

title: Pedal/amp/auto-tune chains only reach the audio graph while that track's CONTROLS view is open: takes play back raw after every kind of reload
evidence: GuitarPedalChain gets processors only through syncChain() (GuitarPedalChain.ts:110-143). With none, it is a straight bypass (ctor line 94: `this.inputNode.connect(this.outputNode)`). Grep finds no DAW caller of syncChain/updateChainParams other than the view effects (GuitarBassView.tsx:549-562, VocalView.tsx:547-563), and nothing engine-side reads track.guitarChain/vocalChain. Those views mount only for the selected track while CONTROLS is active (ChannelStrip.tsx:320 `activeTab === 'controls' && <TrackControlsPanel />`; TrackControlsPanel.tsx:144-161). Recorded DI clips are scheduled into the chain input (usePlaybackEngine.ts:689-699, getNativePedalInputNode). The NAM model is likewise loaded only by GuitarBassView effects (498-547). Both views read the stored chain once, in a useState initializer (GuitarBassView.tsx:428-440, VocalView.tsx:486-495), and write the whole local chain back on every change (GuitarBassView.tsx:565-575, VocalView.tsx:565-575). Phaser BPM sync is injected only by the view (GuitarBassView.tsx:558; PhaserPedal.ts:73 defaults bpm=120). Engines are disposed on editor exit (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1187-1191).
impact: After (a) a refresh or crash-restore, (b) opening a cloud project, or (d) leaving and returning to the editor, every guitar, bass and vocal track plays its takes as raw DI: no amp, NAM, pedals or auto-tune. This lasts until the student selects that track and opens CONTROLS. Tracks not opened in a session stay raw for the whole session. In collab (e), a partner's pedal edits reach the store but never the local audio graph, and the next local knob move overwrites the partner's chain. Changing BPM while the view is closed leaves a synced phaser at the old rate.
recommendation: Make the engine own the chain. A reconciler (in usePlaybackEngine or a hook mounted in DawApp) subscribes to tracks[].guitarChain/vocalChain plus bpm via subscribeWithSelector and calls GuitarPedalChain.apply(desired) on adapter init and on every change, including remote ones. GuitarPedalChain resolves namModelId itself through a cached model loader. The views become pure store editors: they read the chain with a selector and write through setGuitarChain/setVocalChain, with no local copy and no audio side-effects.

title: Post-take 'refined' chord analysis reads the previous take (the first take is never refined)
evidence: On the first 20 Hz tick after recording stops, useAudioChordDetection.ts:232-240 synchronously reads `const lastClip = track?.audioClips[track.audioClips.length - 1]` and schedules `analyzeChords(getAudioBuffer(lastClip.id), …)` 500 ms later (240-251). The new take is committed only after the recorder's async decode: usePlaybackEngine.ts:1098-1118 `recorder.stopRecording(ctx).then(({ buffer }) => { setAudioBuffer(clipId, …); addAudioClip(trackId, { id: clipId, startTick, … }) })`. At the moment lastClip is read, the array still ends with the previous clip, or is empty on the first take.
impact: On the first take of a track, `if (lastClip)` is false, so no refinement runs. On every later take, the 'refined' chords come from the previous take's audio. They are placed at the new take's start and replace the correct live proposal through proposeChordSymbols (264-270). Pressing 'Use Chord Symbols' then writes chords the student didn't play into the chord lane.
recommendation: Trigger refinement from the commit point rather than from transport polling. Have the recording finalizer emit onTakeCommitted({trackId, clipId, buffer, startTick}), or subscribe to the store for the new clip, and analyse that exact clip id. Drop stale jobs by clip id.
verifierNote: useAudioChordDetection.ts:233-234 reads `track?.audioClips[track.audioClips.length - 1]` synchronously on the first tick after the stop is detected. The new clip is only added inside `recorder.stopRecording(ctx).then(...)` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1098-1118), which waits for MediaRecorder stop plus decode. So the first take is skipped (lastClip undefined) and later takes analyse the previous clip's buffer.
impactNote: The race is deterministic. useAudioChordDetection.ts:232-237 reads `track?.audioClips[track.audioClips.length - 1]` on the first tick after isRecording turns false. The new clip is added only after recorder.stopRecording(ctx) resolves its async decode (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1098-1118: setAudioBuffer, then addAudioClip). The 500 ms setTimeout captures the stale lastClip.id, so the delay does not help. On a track's first take lastClip is undefined and nothing is refined. On later takes the previous take's audio is analysed, placed at the new take's start tick (capturedStartTick), and replaces the live proposal through proposeChordSymbols. A student who records a second take and accepts 'Use Chord Symbols' gets chords from the earlier take in the chord lane. The bug lives in a teaching feature, so wrong chords are actively misleading. The impact is gated behind an explicit accept, but it is a plain correctness bug in a learning tool, so high is defensible. The fix (trigger refinement from the commit point with the exact clipId) is small and sound.
regressionRisks: Fixing this makes the expensive offline analysis (audio-analysis-03) run on every take, including first takes, right after stop. Without the worker or performance fix that adds a new main-thread freeze on the first take. Land the two together, or at least run analysis in idle time. Overdub and replace logic trims existing clips in the same .then (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1118+), so pass the committed clipId and buffer directly rather than re-reading the track's last clip. Stale-job cancellation should key on clipId so that undoing a take, or recording again quickly, does not propose chords for a removed clip. Collab: only the local recorder should trigger analysis, not remote addAudioClip events.

title: Offline chord analysis blocks the main thread for seconds after every audio take (twice when Insight analysis is active)
evidence:
analyzeChords runs synchronously inside the hook's setTimeout (useAudioChordDetection.ts:240-251). With FFT_SIZE 32768 and HOP 8192 (lines 80-81) that is about 351 frames per minute at 48 kHz (loop at 727-755). Per frame:
- fftMagnitudeDb calls Math.cos/Math.sin inside the innermost butterfly (247-249): 245,760 butterflies, about 491k trig calls.
- The bit-reversal is recomputed for every index (232-240).
- New real, imag, windowed and magnitude Float64Arrays are allocated, about 0.9 MB per frame (230-231, 262, 273).
- viterbiSmooth is O(T·S²) with S = 38 qualities × 12 roots + silence = 457, i.e. 208,849 inner iterations per frame. Each one does `diatonicPCs.has(TEMPLATES[ps].rootPc)` (471-506), and the caller always passes a key (see -10).

When unisonDoc exists, the same tick then calls analyzeAudio (useAudioChordDetection.ts:272-279). audioToUnison re-runs analyzeChords on the same buffer plus analyzePitch, analyzeTimbre and analyzeMix (audioToUnison.ts:71-76, 90, 143, 146). unisonSlice.ts:229 sets unisonLoading:true and then blocks, so the loading state never paints.

A take at the 5-minute cap can freeze the editor for 10–20+ s right after the student presses stop, exactly when they want to hear the take back. Nothing renders during the freeze, and requestAnimationFrame-driven audio (wah, chord loop) stalls.

Use a precomputed twiddle and bit-reversal table with reusable buffers, or a real-FFT library. Precompute a per-template isDiatonic Uint8Array. Reduce Viterbi to O(T·S): non-self transitions take only 2–3 distinct values, so tracking the best and second-best predecessor per class is enough. Pass the already-computed frames into audioToUnison instead of recomputing them, and show 'Analyzing take…' in Insight.
