title: Autosave can silently drop recent edits, and re-entering the editor restores that stale copy over the newer session
evidence:
useAutosave.ts:19-24 subscribes to every main-store change, and each change clears and restarts a 1500 ms setTimeout that calls writeLocalSession().
(1) Starvation: setPosition fires every 33 ms while playing (useTransport.ts:79-93), and pushLiveChord/setGlobalTuningCents fire every 50 ms while an armed guitar or vocal track is sounding (useAudioChordDetection.ts:175-186). So no autosave can fire during playback, during recording, or while a student plays into an armed track.
(2) Pending write dropped on unmount: the cleanup clears the timer without flushing (useAutosave.ts:27-30). There is no pagehide or visibilitychange flush anywhere in src/daw, although the app already uses one elsewhere (src/features/admin/content/mock/persist.ts:1084).
(3) Synth edits never schedule a write: Oracle Synth knobs write useSynthStore, which useAutosave doesn't subscribe to. serializeSession only picks them up through getTrackSynthState (synthTrackState.ts:190-197) if some later main-store change triggers a write.
(4) Stale restore: on re-entry, the boot effect's default branch calls restoreLocalSessionIfPresent() (DawApp.tsx:428). That deserializes the autosave over the live singleton store, and deserializeSession re-seeds the synth cache from it (SessionSerializer.ts:718-721).
writeLocalSession also swallows quota errors (localSession.ts:15-21), so a large project can keep an arbitrarily old autosave that the next SPA entry restores.
impact: Some edits are lost when a student goes to a lesson and comes back, or after a refresh or crash: anything done while playing (the loop-and-tweak workflow), within 1.5 s of leaving, or only in the synth panel. The loss is silent, with no prompt.
recommendation: Subscribe with content selectors only (tracks, chordRegions, markers, master/returns, project metadata) and also to useSynthStore. Use a debounce with a maxWait (for example 1.5 s idle / 5 s max) so playback can't starve it. Flush synchronously on pagehide, on visibilitychange to hidden, and on unmount. Stamp the autosave with a revision or updatedAt, and on boot restore it only when the in-memory session is empty or older. Show a toast when a write fails on quota. Serialize in requestIdleCallback where possible.
verifierNote: useAutosave.ts:19-24 subscribes to every store change and restarts the 1500 ms timer. useTransport.ts:89 calls setPosition every 33 ms while playing, so the timer can't fire during playback. The cleanup at 27-30 clears the timer without writing, and nothing in src/daw listens for pagehide. Synth knob edits go to useSynthStore, which isn't subscribed. On re-entry, DawApp.tsx:428 calls restoreLocalSessionIfPresent(), which writes the stale autosave over the newer live store, and deserializeSession re-seeds the synth cache (SessionSerializer.ts:721), so synth-only edits are silently rolled back.
impactNote: useAutosave.ts:19-24 debounces on every store change, and useTransport.ts:79-93 calls setPosition every 33 ms while playing, so nothing is written until about 1.5 s after Stop. The cleanup at useAutosave.ts:27-30 clears a pending timer without writing it, and nothing in src/daw listens for pagehide or beforeunload (the only visibilitychange listener is AudioEngine's). On SPA re-entry, DawApp's boot effect falls through to restoreLocalSessionIfPresent() (DawApp.tsx:428), which deserializes the older autosave over the newer in-memory singleton store. localSession.ts:15-21 only logs quota errors, so a failed write leaves an old snapshot that wins on the next entry. Downgraded from critical: in the common case the loss is bounded to edits made during playback or in the last 1.5 s before leaving or refreshing. A student who stops and waits is safe. The quota case is the only unbounded one, and it needs a project bigger than about 5 MB of JSON (audio isn't included).
regressionRisks:
Any of these can cause trouble:
- Flushing on unmount or pagehide could write while the store is mid-reset during a New/Lesson/Template boot. That would persist an empty session, or bring back the project the user just cleared (clearLocalSession runs in the boot branches).
- A content-only selector has to include every persisted field (markers, chordRegions, returns, master, key/mode, timeSignature, projectName, the synth store). Otherwise new fields silently stop autosaving.
- A revision stamp changes the SessionData shape. readLocalSession must tolerate old autosaves that have no stamp.
- Skipping restore when the in-memory store is 'newer' must still restore after a real reload, where the store is empty.
- Don't serialize during collab sessions in a way that fights the Yjs state.
- unsavedStudioSession() relies on canUndo and the autosave contents, so its prompt logic needs re-checking.

title: The [isReady, tracks] effect rewrites every track's whole mixer and FX chain on every edit
evidence:
usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-574 runs on any tracks change. For every existing track (411-471) it calls:
- setVolume
- setAudible(isTrackAudible(track, tracks)), which is O(n) per track, so O(n^2) per edit
- setPan
- updateEffects(track.effects)
- applySends
- applyOrganState, which JSON.stringifies engine and track state twice (209-215)
- applySamplerState
- while playing, reassertAutomationIfPlaying (466-470)

EffectChain.update (EffectChain.ts:1313-1529) is not gated on what changed. It writes dozens of AudioParams, re-assigns WaveShaper curves (crushNode.curve at 1408-1414, saturator at 1484-1486), and ends with this.state = structuredClone(newState) (1529).
setAudible adds a setTargetAtTime event to every track's gain on each pass (TrackEngine.ts:104-110). A second effect (595-605) walks all tracks again for setMonitoring on every edit.
impact: Dragging one fader does a full-chain update for every track about 60 times a second. With 12 tracks that is roughly 720 structuredClones and thousands of AudioParam writes per second, plus WaveShaper curve copies to the audio thread. This load lands on the most common gestures and grows quadratically with track count.
recommendation: Keep a Map<trackId, Track> of the last-applied objects. Zustand keeps unchanged tracks referentially equal, so skip any track whose object is the same. Within a changed track, diff volume, pan, effects, sends, the mute/solo set and instrument settings before touching the engine. Gate each EffectChain.update section by reference, and assign curves only when drive or crush actually changed. Compute anySolo once per pass.
verifierNote: usePlaybackEngine.ts:411-470 calls setVolume, setAudible(isTrackAudible(track, tracks)), setPan, updateEffects, applySends, applyOrganState (JSON.stringify x2 at 211) and reassertAutomationIfPlaying for every existing track on any tracks change. EffectChain.update has no overall gate: it reassigns crushNode.curve unconditionally (EffectChain.ts:1408-1414, including generateCrushCurve(0) when off) and ends with structuredClone (1529). TrackEngine.setAudible schedules a setTargetAtTime on every call (TrackEngine.ts:104-110).
impactNote: The [isReady, tracks] effect (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-574) calls the following for every existing track on any tracks change: setVolume, setAudible(isTrackAudible(track, tracks)), setPan, updateEffects, applySends, applyOrganState (a double JSON.stringify, lines 209-215), applySamplerState and reassertAutomationIfPlaying. EffectChain.update (EffectChain.ts:1313+) only gates the reverb IR. It reassigns crushNode.curve and saturatorShaper.curve each call; the curves come from a cache, but each assignment still copies 4096 floats to the audio thread (EffectChain.ts:1407-1414, 1484-1486). It ends with structuredClone(newState) (line 1529). setAudible queues a setTargetAtTime on every pass (TrackEngine.ts:104-110). A second effect re-walks all tracks for setMonitoring (usePlaybackEngine.ts:594-604). At about 60 fader updates per second times N tracks, this is several ms per frame on Chromebook-class CPUs. That is a real share of drag lag, and it grows with track count.
regressionRisks: Identity-skipping relies on zustand reducers never mutating tracks in place. If any reducer, the collab Yjs bridge or deserialize mutates rather than replaces, sync silently stops. Mute/solo depends on other tracks, so a solo change elsewhere must still re-run setAudible on unchanged track objects (compute an anySolo signature). Engines recreated after an instrument swap or a kit/sampler async load must still get their first full apply. The Map of last-applied tracks must be cleared when the engine is re-initialised or a project is loaded. Gating the curve assignment must still handle enable/disable bypass rewiring.

title: Edits made during playback aren't heard until the transport restarts
evidence:
- The play/stop scheduling effect depends only on [isReady, isPlaying] (usePlaybackEngine.ts:643-744, with the exhaustive-deps lint disabled at 743). It snapshots tracks once (657-662).
- MidiScheduler builds one Tone.Part per clip from a copied event list and captures the TrackEngine instance in its callback (MidiScheduler.ts:57-69). Nothing reschedules on edits; AutomationScheduler.ts:12-17 documents the same limitation.
- When an instrument type changes, the TrackEngine is disposed and replaced (usePlaybackEngine.ts:416-420, 475), but the running Part keeps calling the old engine.
- TrackEngine.dispose doesn't detach the instrument (TrackEngine.ts:205-214).
- A deleted track's Parts keep firing too: lines 388-396 only clear its automation.
impact: A student looping 4 bars who adds, moves or deletes notes or clips keeps hearing the old version. Adding a track, or swapping its instrument while auditioning sounds, leaves it silent until Stop then Play. Ableton, Logic, BandLab, Soundtrap and Soundation all apply these edits live, and loop-and-edit is the core beat-making workflow.
recommendation: Make scheduling incremental. Key Parts by clip id plus a content version (or clip object identity). While playing, diff clips on each tracks change and replace only the changed Parts, starting each new Part at the transport's current position. On an instrument swap, rebind the Part to the new TrackEngine. As a quick safety net, check a per-track schedule generation inside the Part callback.
verifierNote: The scheduling effect depends only on [isReady, isPlaying] (usePlaybackEngine.ts:744) and snapshots tracks once (657-662). Each Tone.Part closes over the trackEngine (MidiScheduler.ts:57-65), and nothing reschedules; AutomationScheduler.ts:12-17 documents this. When the instrument type changes, the old engine is disposed (416-420) but its Part keeps calling it. TrackEngine.dispose (TrackEngine.ts:188-190) disposes the instrument without nulling it, so line numbers in the finding are off but the behaviour holds.
impactNote: The scheduling effect depends only on [isReady, isPlaying] (usePlaybackEngine.ts:643-744, exhaustive-deps disabled at 743). MidiScheduler builds Tone.Parts from copied events and closes over the TrackEngine instance (MidiScheduler.ts:28-66). handleLoop (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-905) only reschedules audio clips and automation, never MIDI Parts, so even loop laps replay stale notes. The instrument-swap path disposes and replaces the TrackEngine (416-420), but running Parts keep calling the old one. A deleted track only gets allNotesOff, dispose and automation clear (388-396); its Parts keep firing into a disposed engine. AutomationScheduler.ts:12-17 documents the same limitation. Loop-and-edit in the piano roll is the core student workflow, and changes are inaudible until Stop then Play.
regressionRisks:
Incremental Part replacement mid-play has to avoid:
- double-triggering notes at the replacement boundary
- orphaned note-offs (call allNotesOff for the old Part's sounding notes, or keep note-offs)
- breaking loop laps (Part start and loop interplay)
Collab peers editing at 60 Hz could cause Part churn, so throttle or key by clip content identity. Count-in and recording (MidiRecorder punch-in) timing must stay intact. renderProject.ts also uses scheduleSequence, so keep the offline path unchanged.

title: Seeking while playing desyncs audio clips and can leave notes hanging
evidence:
seekTo (useTransport.ts:11-16) only sets Tone.getTransport().ticks and the store position. It is called during playback from the ruler and playhead drag (Timeline.tsx:2065, 2296, 2309), the piano roll (PianoRoll.tsx:1478, 1528) and skip back/forward (TransportBar.tsx:212-257). Nothing in usePlaybackEngine reacts, because the scheduling deps are [isReady, isPlaying].

In AudioClipScheduler:
- Sources that have already started keep running. Only cancelAll stops them (AudioClipScheduler.ts:94-114).
- Clips the playhead starts inside use startSourceNow, which is not tied to the transport.
- Future clips are transport events, which fire again when the playhead passes them a second time.

Tone Part note-offs that the seek jumps over are never delivered.
impact:
Clicking the ruler while playing causes four kinds of wrong audio:
- Audio that was playing carries on from the old position.
- Jumping into the middle of a clip leaves that clip silent.
- Jumping back before a clip that is already playing starts a second, offset copy (doubled, flamming audio).
- Held synth notes whose note-off was skipped drone until Stop.
recommendation: Treat a seek during playback as stop-and-reschedule. Subscribe to lastSeekPosition, which seekTo already writes. While playing, run cancelAll and panic, then rebuild the schedule from the new tick. Alternatively, do pause, seek and start in one step.
verifierNote: seekTo (useTransport.ts:11-16) only sets transport.ticks and the store. It is called mid-play from Timeline.tsx:2065/2296/2309, PianoRoll.tsx:1478/1528 and TransportBar.tsx:228/243/257. lastSeekPosition is only read by stop() (transportSlice.ts:160), and nothing in usePlaybackEngine reacts to a seek. AudioClipScheduler only stops running sources in cancelAll (94-114), and mid-clip starts use startSourceNow, which isn't tied to the transport.
impactNote: seekTo (useTransport.ts:11-16) only sets Transport ticks and the store position. Nothing subscribes to lastSeekPosition apart from stop()'s return-to-seek (transportSlice.ts:160). AudioClipScheduler keeps already-started sources (only cancelAll at 94-114 stops them). Mid-clip starts use startSourceNow, which isn't transport-bound. Future clips are transport.schedule events, so seeking into a clip skips its start (silent), and seeking back before a playing clip starts a second copy. Callers that run while playing include the Timeline ruler/playhead drag (Timeline.tsx:2065), the PianoRoll (1478, 1528), and skip back/forward (TransportBar.tsx:212-257). AutomationScheduler.ts:12-17 acknowledges the same gap. Clicking the ruler during playback is extremely common.
regressionRisks: Stop-and-reschedule on every seek during a playhead drag (pointermove) would thrash scheduling and could click. Debounce, or reschedule only on pointerup or when the seek delta exceeds a threshold. panic() on seek cuts sustain tails and reverbs abruptly. The loop handler and count-in must not double-schedule. Recording in progress must not be restarted or re-anchored by a seek, or the take offset breaks. TransportBar's stop+seekTo(0) path already stops first; keep it.

title: Audio clips started mid-clip or on loop laps play ~100 ms ahead of MIDI and the metronome, and loop laps ignore the clip trim
evidence:
useTransport starts the transport with transport.start() (useTransport.ts:63-64). That means Tone's now(), which is currentTime + 0.1 s lookAhead (node_modules/tone/build/esm/core/context/Context.js:329-331; the lookAhead is not overridden, src/audio/core/toneBridge.ts:56).

In the same commit, the play effect schedules clips that the playhead is inside (currentTick >= startTick, AudioClipScheduler.ts:47-69) through startSourceNow. This includes a clip that starts exactly at the playhead, such as after the auto-rewind at usePlaybackEngine.ts:1139. startSourceNow starts at the native ctx.currentTime (AudioClipScheduler.ts:215-216, 257-261), so these clips start about 100 ms before the transport reaches them.

The loop handler (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-905) ignores the loop event's time argument. Tone emits 'loop' up to one lookAhead early (Clock.js:200-225, Transport.js:119-127). So cancelAll() stops sources immediately, cutting the tail before the loop point, and clips that span loopStart restart at currentTime.

The loop path also drops the trim. The play path passes clip.offsetSeconds ?? 0 (line 715). The loop call at 881-891 stops after clip.fadeInTicks and clip.fadeOutTicks, so the trim offset defaults to 0 (AudioClipScheduler.ts:35).
impact: Recorded or imported audio flams against the drums depending on where Play was pressed. The last ~100 ms before every loop point is chopped. Front-trimmed clips play their trimmed-away start on every lap after the first. Practice mode loops by default (DawApp.tsx:332), so any audio there is affected on every lap.
recommendation: Start the transport at an explicit time t0 and start mid-clip sources at t0 with the computed offset. Use the loop event's time for both stop and start (source.stop(time), then source.start(time, offset)). Pass clip.offsetSeconds in the loop path. Better still, have both paths use one shared scheduling helper.
verifierNote: startSourceNow starts at the native ctx.currentTime (AudioClipScheduler.ts:216, 257-261), while useTransport.ts:64 calls transport.start() at now() (+0.1 s lookAhead; no lookAhead override found in src). The loop handler (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-905) ignores the event's time, calls cancelAll() with an immediate source.stop(), and its scheduleClip call (881-891) stops at clip.fadeOutTicks, omitting clip.offsetSeconds, unlike the play path at 715.
impactNote: Tone 15.0.4's Context defaults to lookAhead 0.1 (Context.js:80) and now() = currentTime + lookAhead (Context.js:329-331). toneBridge creates new Tone.Context({context: shared}) without overriding it. useTransport calls transport.start() with no time (useTransport.ts:63-64), so tick X sounds at currentTime+0.1. Meanwhile startSourceNow starts at native ctx.currentTime (AudioClipScheduler.ts:216, 258-261), so mid-clip audio leads MIDI and the metronome by about 100 ms. Clips that start exactly at the playhead take this path too (currentTick >= startTick, line 47). The loop path at usePlaybackEngine.ts:881-891 omits clip.offsetSeconds, so it defaults to 0 at AudioClipScheduler.ts:35 and front-trimmed clips replay their trimmed head on every lap. That trim bug is unambiguous and visible in Practice mode, which loops by default.
regressionRisks: Starting the transport at an explicit t0 shifts every transport-relative calculation. That includes the MidiRecorder lookAhead compensation (MidiRecorder.ts:60-79), the count-in timer and countInStartedAt display, the playhead rAF, and recording start-tick anchoring (finding 13). They must all move together, or MIDI takes will shift. Using the loop event's time for source.stop/start must keep fades correct. Passing offsetSeconds in the loop path changes what saved trimmed projects sound like (a fix, but users may notice).

title: Level meters re-render whole track headers, mixer strips and the FX panel every frame
evidence:
useMeterLevel calls setLevel(Math.round(peak)) on every rAF with no throttle (useMeterLevel.ts:24-46). useCompressorMeters calls setMeters with a new object every 33 ms, even in silence, so React can never bail out (useCompressorMeters.ts:49-75).

The hosts are large components:
- TrackHeader (540 lines) calls useMeterLevel at its top level, once per track (TrackHeader.tsx:91-93).
- MasterTrackHeader has two meters (MasterTrackHeader.tsx:50-51).
- Also Mixer/ChannelStrip.tsx:149, StudioView MixingStrip (616) and MasterStrip (762-763).
- EffectsPanel hosts useCompressorMeters (EffectsPanel.tsx:192) and passes new inline closures to its children on every render (229-252).

Decay is applied per frame (PEAK_DECAY 0.9, useMeterLevel.ts:3), so meters fall twice as fast on 120 Hz displays. The analysers are 256 samples (TrackEngine.ts:29-30, AudioEngine.ts:55-60), so each frame sees about 5 ms out of every 16 ms of audio and misses transients.
impact: During playback with 10 tracks, the arrange view re-renders about 12 full headers 60-120 times a second. The FX tab re-renders the entire effects editor 30 times a second for as long as it is open, even when stopped. This is a major share of playback jank, and the meters under-read peaks, which misleads students in gain-staging lessons.
recommendation: Replace state-driven meters with a single MeterBus. One rAF runs only while audio is active. It reads each registered analyser once, applies time-based (dt) peak-hold and decay, and writes straight to DOM refs (transform: scaleY) or one canvas. Meters become small leaf components that register a ref. Use analysers of at least 1024 samples, or an AudioWorklet peak meter. As an interim fix, move useMeterLevel into a small TrackMeter leaf and skip setState when the value hasn't changed.
verifierNote: useMeterLevel.ts:44 calls setLevel every rAF; it only bails out when the value is unchanged (e.g. silence). TrackHeader reads the analyser and calls useMeterLevel at its top level (TrackHeader.tsx:91-93), so the whole memo'd header re-renders while audio plays. useCompressorMeters.ts:66-70 sets a new object every 33 ms, so EffectsPanel (EffectsPanel.tsx:192) re-renders 30 times a second even in silence. The analysers are 256 samples (TrackEngine.ts:30, AudioEngine.ts:56/60), and decay is per frame.
impactNote: useMeterLevel calls setLevel on every rAF with no throttle (useMeterLevel.ts:24-46). React bails out only when the rounded value repeats, which is rare while audio plays. Each TrackHeader (memoized, but internal state still re-renders the whole 540-line header) hosts one meter (TrackHeader.tsx:91-93), so 10-12 tracks means 600-1400 header renders per second at 60-120 Hz. useCompressorMeters creates a new object every 33 ms (useCompressorMeters.ts:71-75), so EffectsPanel (EffectsPanel.tsx:192) re-renders 30 times a second even in silence. Decay is per frame (PEAK_DECAY 0.9), so it is frame-rate dependent. The 256-sample analysers (TrackEngine.ts:29-30) under-read transients. Of the per-frame costs during playback, this is likely the largest.
regressionRisks: A DOM-ref MeterBus must keep any visual hooks the tutorial uses (data-tutorial-id on meter containers) and the existing MeterSegments look. A larger fftSize raises per-frame analyser read cost, so read once per frame centrally. Stopping the rAF when audio is inactive must still show live-input monitoring (armed guitar or mic with transport stopped). For useCompressorMeters, skip setState only when the values are equal; don't break GR display.

title: MIDI export writes a file that plays 3.75x slower, with flattened dynamics, every clip stacked at bar 1, and wrong channels
evidence:
- PPQ: exportMidiFile ignores seq.ticksPerQuarterNote and passes the DAW's 480-PPQ ticks straight to midi-writer-js as startTick and as a 'T'-prefixed duration (MidiFileIO.ts:75-87). midi-writer-js 2.1.4 writes a 128-ticks-per-quarter header (node_modules/midi-writer-js/build/index.js:19, HEADER_CHUNK_DIVISION [0x00, 0x80]).
- Velocity: values in 0-127 go into an API that expects 1-100 and clamps (convertVelocity, index.js:323-327).
- Clip positions: both callers flatten clip events without adding clip.startTick (FileMenu.tsx:338, useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:198), but events are clip-relative (MidiScheduler.ts:28-29).
- Channels: both callers use the track index as the channel (sequences.set(i + 1, ...) at FileMenu.tsx:341 and useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:200). The 10th track lands on GM drum channel 10, and channel 17 or higher produces status bytes 0xA0/0x90 (index.js:693-696, 755-758).
- Download: downloadMidiBlob revokes the object URL right after click() on an anchor that was never added to the document (MidiFileIO.ts:101-108).
impact: A student who exports to GarageBand, MuseScore or Logic gets a slow-motion file with every clip stacked at bar 1, every velocity of 100 or more flattened to 127, and possibly a melody playing as drums. In practice the export flow is broken.
recommendation: Write the file with @tonejs/midi, which is already a dependency for import and supports header.ppq, tempos and 0-1 velocities, at 480 PPQ. Add clip.startTick and honour clip length and trim. Map drum-machine tracks to channel 10 and assign melodic tracks to channels that skip 10. Include time signature and track names. Keep the anchor in the DOM and revoke the URL on a timeout.
verifierNote: exportMidiFile passes 480-PPQ ticks as startTick and 'T' durations (MidiFileIO.ts:78-85), while midi-writer-js 2.1.4 hard-codes a 128 PPQ division (index.js:19, 1625). Its convertVelocity clamps input above 100 (index.js:324-327). Both callers flatten clip.events without adding clip.startTick and use the track index as the channel (FileMenu.tsx:338-341; useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:198-200). downloadMidiBlob revokes the URL straight after click() on an anchor that was never attached (MidiFileIO.ts:101-108).
impactNote:
The export path is wrong in several ways:
- exportMidiFile passes 480-PPQ ticks as startTick and 'T'+durationTicks (MidiFileIO.ts:75-87) into midi-writer-js 2.1.4, whose header is fixed at 128 ticks per beat (index.js:19, HEADER_CHUNK_DIVISION 0x80). Playback is 3.75x slower.
- convertVelocity clamps at 100 and scales by 127/100 (index.js:323-327), so velocities of 100 and above become 127.
- Both callers flatten clip.events without adding clip.startTick (FileMenu.tsx:338, useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:198), which stacks every clip at the start.
- Both callers use the track index as the channel (FileMenu.tsx:341, useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:200), so track 10 lands on the drum channel.
Any student who exports to GarageBand or MuseScore gets a broken file. The anchor-not-in-DOM and immediate-revoke issues are minor in Chrome.
regressionRisks: Switching to @tonejs/midi changes the output format details (track 0 tempo track, names). Any tests that snapshot bytes will need updating. Honour clip trim and loop/length semantics so clips aren't exported past their visible length. Channel mapping must handle more than 15 melodic tracks, for example by reusing channels per track. The FileMenu and Cmd+E paths differ (all tracks versus MIDI-only), so unify them in one helper.

title: After opening or restoring a project, live MIDI and recorded takes are pinned to the first MIDI track
evidence:
- Both deserializers force firstMidi.monitoring = true and firstMidi.recordArmed = true (SessionSerializer.ts:601-606 for cloud projects, 744-751 for local restore).
- Routing prefers monitored tracks over the selection (useMidiInputRouting.ts:12-19, 106-123).
- Arming neither routes input nor disarms other tracks (tracksSlice.ts:646-653).
- A MIDI take goes to the first armed MIDI track in list order (useMidiRecording.ts:36-38), and the live overlay is drawn there too (55).
impact: A student selects their piano track (track 3) and plays, but hears track 1's bass. If they arm track 3 and record, the clip lands on track 1. Ableton, Logic, BandLab and Soundtrap all route a MIDI keyboard to the selected or armed track.
recommendation: Make input follow selection: auto-monitor the selected MIDI track, with explicit monitoring only adding extra layers. Make arming exclusive by default, with shift-click to arm several. Record into the armed track(s) the user chose, not the first in list order. Remove the forced monitoring and arming from the deserializers, and show the current input target in the track header.
verifierNote: deserializeCloudProject forces firstMidi.monitoring/recordArmed = true (SessionSerializer.ts:601-606), and local restore does the same when nothing is monitored (744-751). loadProjectTemplate also arms the first MIDI track (tracksSlice.ts:983-993). Routing prefers monitored tracks over the selection (useMidiInputRouting.ts:12-19, 106-123), toggleRecordArm isn't exclusive (tracksSlice.ts:646-653), and takes go to the first armed MIDI track (useMidiRecording.ts:36-38).
impactNote: The cloud deserializer unconditionally sets firstMidi.monitoring = true and recordArmed = true (SessionSerializer.ts:601-606). title: Post-recording chord analysis analyses the wrong take and blocks the main thread
evidence:
When the detector sees recording stop (useAudioChordDetection.ts:211), it immediately captures lastClip as the track's last audio clip (236-238). But the new take is only added after MediaRecorder stop, the blob read and decodeAudioData have all resolved (AudioRecorder.ts:43-55, then usePlaybackEngine.ts:1099-1120).

So on a track's first take there is no clip and no refinement. On later takes, the previous take is analysed, stamped at the new take's start tick (capturedStartTick, 233), and then replaces the live proposal via proposeChordSymbols (264-270).

The 500 ms timer then runs analyzeChords synchronously (246-251). That is a loop of 32,768-point FFTs every 8,192 samples over the whole buffer (OfflineChordAnalyzer.ts:80-81, 727-755): about 1,050 FFT frames for a 3-minute 48 kHz take. It may also run the UNISON analyzeAudio (273-279).
impact: Students are offered chord symbols from the wrong recording, which is a serious error for a theory-teaching app. Stopping a long take also freezes the editor right when they want to listen back.
recommendation: Have the recorder emit a finished-take event ({trackId, clipId, startTick, buffer}) and run refinement on that event. Move analyzeChords into a Web Worker, transferring a copy of the channel data, and show an 'Analysing chords...' state in Insight.
verifierNote: On the recording-stop edge the detector immediately reads track.audioClips[last] (useAudioChordDetection.ts:236-238). The new clip is only added after the async MediaRecorder stop, blob read and decodeAudioData (AudioRecorder.ts:43-55, usePlaybackEngine.ts:1120). So it captures the previous take, or nothing on the first take, stamped at the new take's start tick. analyzeChords then runs synchronously in the 500 ms timeout with FFT_SIZE 32768 and HOP 8192 (OfflineChordAnalyzer.ts:80-81, 727-755).
impactNote: When recording stops, useAudioChordDetection.ts:236-238 synchronously reads track.audioClips[last]. The new take is only added after MediaRecorder stop, blob read and decodeAudioData (AudioRecorder.ts:43-55, then usePlaybackEngine.ts:1099-1120). On the first take there is no refinement. On later takes, the previous take is analysed and stamped at the new take's capturedStartTick (233, 254-259), and that result replaces the proposal (264-270). analyzeChords then runs synchronously on the main thread over the whole buffer, so a multi-second freeze on long takes is plausible on Chromebooks. Wrong chord suggestions are a serious problem for a theory app, though the user still has to accept them in Insight.
regressionRisks: A finished-take event needs to run after overwriteAudioRegion, which may split or trim clips and change ids. Key refinement by the new clipId. Moving analysis to a Worker needs a bundler worker setup and a transfer of copied Float32Array data. UNISON analyzeAudio (the store action) may also need to be async-safe. If the user re-records quickly, results arriving late must be dropped (generation check).

title: Audio takes land off the beat with no latency compensation, and the mic-fallback path starts late and never releases the mic
evidence:
The take is anchored at the store position when the effect runs (startTickForLimit at usePlaybackEngine.ts:955, recordStartTickRef at 971). The transport only reaches that tick one lookAhead later (useTransport.ts:63-64, now() + 0.1 s).

Capture starts immediately for instrument adapters (1039-1043). For tracks without an input device, startRecordingStream returns null (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:270-275), and capture starts only after an async getUserMedia resolves (1050-1055).

The audio path compensates for nothing: no lookAhead, baseLatency or outputLatency. The MIDI path compensates for both lookAhead and event delay (MidiRecorder.ts:60-79).

The fallback stream is never kept or stopped. AudioRecorder.stopRecording only stops the MediaRecorder (AudioRecorder.ts:36-56), and the cleanup only disconnects the analyser source (usePlaybackEngine.ts:928-940).
impact: Vocals and guitar sit late against the beat by roughly 100 ms plus the device round trip (more on Bluetooth). On the fallback path they sit early by the getUserMedia or permission delay. Alignment also differs depending on where Play is pressed (see engine-hooks-06). The browser's mic-in-use indicator stays on after recording, and each take opens another live stream.
recommendation:
Build a small recording service:
- Keep one persistent input stream per device.
- Capture with an AudioWorklet on the shared context, so the first frame has a known context time.
- Start the transport at an explicit time t0.
- Offset the take by (t0 - captureStart) + baseLatency + outputLatency + a user calibration value, set by a Soundtrap/BandLab-style latency test in Settings.
- Stop all stream tracks when the take is finalized or the track is disarmed.
verifierNote: recordStartTickRef is set to the store position (usePlaybackEngine.ts:955, 971), and capture starts immediately for adapters (1039-1043), while the transport only reaches that tick one lookAhead later. There's no latency compensation, unlike MidiRecorder.ts:60-68. The getUserMedia fallback (1050-1055) never keeps or stops the stream: AudioRecorder.stopRecording only stops the MediaRecorder, and the cleanup only disconnects the analyser source (928-940).
impactNote: The take anchor is the store position at effect time (usePlaybackEngine.ts:955, 971). Tone's transport reaches that tick at currentTime+0.1 (useTransport.ts:63-64 with the default 0.1 lookAhead), and capture starts immediately for adapters (1039-1043), so takes land about 100 ms late, plus the device round trip. There is no baseLatency or outputLatency compensation, unlike the MIDI path (MidiRecorder.ts:60-79). The fallback getUserMedia path (1050-1055) starts capture after an async delay. That stream is never stored or stopped: AudioRecorder.stopRecording only stops the MediaRecorder (AudioRecorder.ts:36-56). So the mic indicator stays on, and a new stream opens on every take. Vocal and guitar takes that drift visibly off the grid are noticed immediately.
regressionRisks: Changing the take offset shifts all new recordings. Existing saved clips are unaffected, but users who manually nudged clips to compensate will see new takes behave differently. Calibration UI and settings need persistence. Stopping stream tracks must not kill the GuitarFxAdapter's live monitoring stream (only stop streams the recorder opened). This must be coordinated with the t0 transport start change in finding 06, and with the count-in path. An AudioWorklet capture adds a module-loading dependency.

title: In collab sessions every peer presence update re-renders the whole editor

The selector returns a new object and no equalityFn is set (541-549), so the listener calls awareness.setLocalState with lastActiveAt: Date.now() (551-560) on every setPosition tick (30 a second while playing) and every chord-bus write.

The listen-store subscription runs apply() on every activity update (useStudioMonitor.ts:97-115). setPeerGain jumps gain.value without a ramp (StudioRtcManager.ts:127-130).

In CollabProvider, pass equalityFn: shallow and bump lastActiveAt only on real user actions, throttled. Ramp peer gains with setTargetAtTime.

Its selector returns a new object and there is no equalityFn, so Object.is fires the listener on every store change, including setPosition 30 times a second while playing. title: Mixer meters re-render whole strips every display frame during playback
evidence:
useMeterLevel (useMeterLevel.ts:11-55) runs an unthrottled requestAnimationFrame loop per analyser. Each frame it scans `analyser.fftSize` bytes and calls `setLevel(Math.round(peak))` (44-45).

Each MixingStrip calls it at the top level (StudioView.tsx:614-616). During playback the whole memoised strip (Radix Slider 667-696, PanKnob, two send RotaryKnobs 709-730, DbReadout/FixedDigits) therefore re-renders at 60-120 Hz. MeterBar then calls `setPeakPct` inside `useEffect([pct])` (444-455), adding a second render per meter per frame. Each strip also draws the same mono level twice (663-665, 698-700).

MasterStrip (759-763) and LufsMeter (191-195) each start their own two loops on the same master analysers. LufsMeter also animates 20 segment divs with CSS transitions (209-229).
impact: With the 10-track maximum at 60 Hz, the MASTER view does roughly 600 strip renders and about 1,200 MeterBar renders per second, on top of the transport's 30 Hz updates. On 120 Hz displays the counts double. This main-thread time is taken from fader and knob drags and from Tone's scheduling. It is the most likely cause of mixer lag on school Chromebooks and iPads.
recommendation: Replace per-component meter state with one module-level meter loop. Run it at 30 Hz or less, and pause it when the transport is stopped and all levels are 0. The loop reads the registered analysers and writes `transform: scaleY()` or CSS variables to meter elements through refs, with no React state. Do time-based peak hold inside the loop. Draw one bar for a mono analyser, or split real L/R with a ChannelSplitter.
verifierNote: useMeterLevel calls setLevel every rAF with no throttle (useMeterLevel.ts:44-45). React only skips identical values, so the whole memoised MixingStrip re-renders while levels change during playback (StudioView.tsx:614-616). MeterBar adds a second state update inside useEffect([pct]) (444-455). MasterStrip (759-763) and LufsMeter (191-195) each run their own loops on the same master analysers.
impactNote: useMeterLevel (useMeterLevel.ts:11-55) runs an unthrottled rAF loop and calls setLevel each frame. While audio plays the rounded level changes almost every frame, so each memoised MixingStrip re-renders at display rate (StudioView.tsx:614-616 calls the hook at the strip's top level, above the Radix Slider, PanKnob and send knobs). MeterBar's useEffect([pct]) calls setPeakPct (440-455), adding a second render per bar, and the strip draws the same mono level twice (663-665, 698-700). MasterStrip and LufsMeter each run their own loops on the same analysers. When stopped, the level settles at 0 and React bails out, so the cost applies only during playback. During playback it is real main-thread load on Chromebooks and competes with fader drags. MeterBar's peak hold also decays per pct change rather than per unit of time, a small extra bug.
regressionRisks: A ref-driven module meter loop must handle analysers appearing and disappearing when tracks are added or removed, or when an instrument change recreates the TrackEngine; register and unregister them on mount and unmount. Pausing when stopped has to let the meters decay to zero first, or they freeze lit. If L/R becomes a real stereo split, the ChannelSplitter nodes must be disconnected and disposed with the track, or they leak audio nodes. The fix doesn't affect persistence, collab or undo. The meters themselves carry no tutorial anchors, so it's safe as long as the strip DOM wrappers keep their data-tutorial-id.

title: Every knob, fader, pan or send drag step does work proportional to the whole project
evidence:
Controls write to the store on every pointermove (e.g. EffectsPanel.tsx:649-651 `onUpdate(trackId, { compressor: { ...comp, ratio: v } })`, and StudioView.tsx:675 and 725). Each write then does four things:
1. Undo's handleChange runs `watched()` first (undoMiddleware.ts:223). That JSON-stringifies all tracks and chordRegions and structuredClones 13 mark keys (194-205, 64) before the cheap identity check.
2. DawAppInner re-renders. usePlaybackEngine, called at DawApp.tsx:80, subscribes to `tracks`, `masteringEffects`, `masterVolume` and `returns` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:363-376). That re-renders the non-memoised StudioView, LibraryPanel, TimelineWithHeaders and dock.

4. In collab, the whole effects object is re-serialised (diffEngine.ts:171-175, 470-480).
impact: The cost of a drag grows with the project (notes, clips, automation), not with the one parameter being moved. Knob and fader drags get steadily laggier in real songs. Every drag step is an undo diff, a full engine re-sync and, in collab, a full-object network message.

Keep the dragged value in local state or a ref, write the AudioParam directly (setTargetAtTime) each frame, and commit to the store once on pointerup: one undo entry, one collab op, one autosave. In undoMiddleware, compare references before building JSON. Move usePlaybackEngine's store reads to `useStore.subscribe` listeners so DawAppInner doesn't re-render, and sync only the changed track or slot.

title: Mixer edits made while the transport is playing are not autosaved until it stops
evidence: useAutosave subscribes to every store change and restarts a 1,500 ms debounce each time (useAutosave.ts:18-26). During playback, useTransport writes `position` about every 33 ms (useTransport.ts:80-93). The timer is reset about 30 times a second and never fires while playing.
impact: Mixing is usually done with a loop running. A student who balances faders, sends and FX for ten minutes and then hits a crash or refresh before pressing stop loses all of it; crash recovery restores the state from before playback started.
recommendation: Subscribe autosave only to persisted keys (tracks, returns, mastering, chordRegions …), or at least ignore `position`. Add a maximum wait so it flushes at least every 10 s while there are unsaved changes.
verifierNote: useAutosave's unfiltered useStore.subscribe resets a 1500ms timer on every store write (useAutosave.ts:18-26). useTransport writes position about every 33ms while playing (useTransport.ts:80-93). There is no beforeunload or pagehide flush in src/daw, so edits made during playback are lost if the tab closes or crashes before stop. That makes it a persistence bug, which the rubric rates high.

title: Browser refresh restores only part of the project: time signature, markers, mastering, Score/Lead Sheet marks and pitch edits are lost
evidence: SessionData.data (SessionSerializer.ts:186-247) and serializeSession (274-337) store transport {bpm, position, metronome, loop}, tracks, prism (with mode), chordRegions, returns and masterAutomation. They do not store timeSignatureNumerator/Denominator (default 4/4, transportSlice.ts:108-109), markers, masteringStyle/FxChain/Effects, masterVolume, leadSheetSections/Repeats, score articulations/slurs/spellings/breaks/text marks/slash notes, measureRowSizes or pitchData. deserializeSession also spreads freshProjectHarmony() before restoring (782). Pitch edits are read by playback (usePlaybackEngine.ts:315).
impact: After a refresh or a Chromebook tab discard: a 6/8 song comes back in 4/4, so Timeline, Score, Lead Sheet and exports all re-bar. Markers and the mastering chain built in MASTER are gone. Lead Sheet sections and repeats and all Score engraving work vanish. Vocal pitch corrections no longer play.
recommendation: Use the same projectState codec as ia-flows-01 for the local autosave. Bump SESSION_SCHEMA_VERSION to 3 with a v2 migration.
verifierNote: SessionData.data and serializeSession (SessionSerializer.ts:186-247, 274-337) leave out timeSignature, markers, mastering*, masterVolume, leadSheetSections/Repeats, score marks, measureRowSizes and pitchData. A grep for timeSignature, markers or mastering under src/daw/persistence and src/lib/studio-projects finds nothing. deserializeSession spreads freshProjectHarmony() before restoring, and nothing else in src/daw writes these keys to localStorage.
impactNote: SessionData.data and serializeSession (SessionSerializer.ts:186-247, 274-337) contain transport{bpm,position,metronome,loop}, tracks, prism+mode, chordRegions, returns and masterAutomation only. A grep of src/daw/persistence and src/lib/studio-projects finds no timeSignature, markers, mastering*, masterVolume, leadSheetSections or pitchData. deserializeSession spreads freshProjectHarmony() (782), so Lead Sheet and Score marks reset to empty. A Chromebook tab discard or a refresh therefore silently turns a 3/4 or 6/8 piece into 4/4 and drops the master chain and Score engraving work. It stays high rather than critical because most student projects are 4/4 with no mastering, but for those who use these features it is real data loss.
regressionRisks: Bump SESSION_SCHEMA_VERSION to 3 and keep v1 and v2 readers. Defaults for missing keys must match the slice initial state. localStorage quota: pitchData (per-frame pitch curves) can be large, and a quota error makes writeLocalSession fail entirely (localSession.ts:14-22). Consider storing pitch segments compactly or leaving them out of autosave. Undo: readMarks (undoMiddleware.ts:62-72) tracks these marks, so restore before resetUndoHistory().

title: Autosave never runs while the transport plays and is dropped on unmount or unload
evidence: useAutosave subscribes to every store change and restarts a 1,500 ms timer each time (useAutosave.ts:19-25). During playback, useTransport writes position about every 33 ms (useTransport.ts:72-98), so the timer can't fire until playback stops. The cleanup clears a pending timer without writing (useAutosave.ts:27-30). Nothing flushes on pagehide or visibilitychange; there is no such listener in src/daw or src/lib/studio-projects. UI-only changes (zoom, scroll, selection, panel toggles) still trigger a full serializeSession + JSON.stringify + localStorage.setItem (localSession.ts:14-22).
impact: Nothing is autosaved during looping practice, lesson playback or recording takes until the transport stops. A crash, refresh or tab discard mid-loop loses everything since Play was pressed. Leaving the editor within 1.5 s of an edit also loses that edit (worsened by ia-flows-05).
recommendation: Subscribe with a selector over project keys only; exclude position, live-recording buffers and UI state. Write at most once every 2–3 s (throttle) instead of only after 1.5 s of inactivity. Flush on pagehide, on visibilitychange to hidden, and on unmount. Serialize in requestIdleCallback.
verifierNote: useAutosave subscribes to every store change and restarts a 1,500 ms timeout each time (useAutosave.ts:19-25). useTransport calls setPosition about every 33 ms while playing (useTransport.ts:72-98), so the save can't fire until playback stops. The cleanup clears the timer without writing (27-30). The only pagehide/visibilitychange listener in src/daw is AudioEngine's audio-context handler (AudioEngine.ts:97), which doesn't save.
impactNote: useAutosave subscribes to every store change and restarts a 1500 ms debounce (useAutosave.ts:16-25). During playback, useTransport's rAF loop calls setPosition about every 33 ms (useTransport.ts:72-98), so the timer never fires until the transport stops. Cleanup clears the pending timer without writing (27-30). The only visibilitychange listener in src/daw is AudioEngine's audio-resume handler, and there are no pagehide/beforeunload handlers. Students loop while they edit in the piano roll, which is a core flow, and a crash, refresh or tab discard mid-loop loses all of it.
regressionRisks: Throttled writes during playback do a full serializeSession + JSON.stringify + localStorage.setItem on the main thread, which can stall rAF and Tone scheduling (audio glitches on Chromebooks). Use a project-only selector, run in requestIdleCallback, and skip while the transport is playing unless the project changed. Flushing on unmount must not run after a reset path has cleared the session: e.g. ?new=1 calls clearLocalSession, and a late flush of the old store would resurrect the old project. Order the flush before boot or key it to a session id. A flush on pagehide must be synchronous (localStorage is).

title: Returning to the editor by SPA navigation overwrites the live session with the autosave
evidence: The comment at DawApp.tsx:101-105 notes that the store survives SPA navigation. Even so, the boot path with no URL params always ends in restoreLocalSessionIfPresent() (DawApp.tsx:425-428). That calls deserializeSession (localSession.ts:43-47), which spreads freshProjectHarmony() (SessionSerializer.ts:782) and calls resetUndoHistory() (794).
impact: Every Learn ↔ Studio round trip, and the dashboard's 'Continue last session' tile, does three things: wipes undo history; clears Lead Sheet sections/repeats, Score articulations/slurs/slash notes, measure layout and melody overrides; and replaces the last 1.5 s of in-memory edits with the stale autosave.
recommendation: Mark the store as hydrated (for example a sessionLoadedAt value set by every load or reset path) and skip the localStorage restore when it is set. Restore from localStorage only on a cold page load.
verifierNote: With no URL params (OpenInStudioButton.tsx:39, StudioNewProject 'Continue last session' :55, ActivityFlow.tsx:1687), boot falls through to restoreLocalSessionIfPresent() (DawApp.tsx:428). That runs deserializeSession, which spreads freshProjectHarmony() (clearing leadSheetSections/Repeats, scoreArticulations/Slurs/SlashNotes, measureRowSizes, melodyOverrides) and calls resetUndoHistory(). The unmount cleanup in useAutosave also drops any write still pending.
impactNote: DawApp's boot effect runs again on each mount (bootedRef is per-instance). With no URL params and no collab room it falls through to restoreLocalSessionIfPresent() (DawApp.tsx:425-428), even though the comment at 101-105 says the store survives SPA navigation. deserializeSession resets freshProjectHarmony() (SessionSerializer.ts:782) and calls resetUndoHistory() (794). Every Learn to Studio round trip therefore wipes undo, clears the unserialized Lead Sheet and Score marks, and replaces any edits from the last ≤1.5 s, or from the whole time playback ran (ia-flows-04), with the stale autosave.
regressionRisks: The 'hydrated' flag must be set by every load path (cloud open, demo, template, song seed with ?seeded=1, collab join, jam import), or a cold-load restore could be skipped wrongly. useSongActions' unsavedStudioSession treats a non-empty undo stack as 'edited'; keeping undo across navigation is correct but changes when that prompt appears. The collab rejoin branch (DawApp.tsx:398-404) must still come first. Audio buffers live in AudioBufferStore (a module singleton), so skipping the restore must not skip reloading pending audio when the store holds clips whose buffers were never decoded.

title: Global Cmd/Ctrl shortcuts hijack text fields and the browser's page zoom
evidence:
Modifier shortcuts run before the editable-target check (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:42-292 vs 296-301; the code comment says 'always active, even in inputs').
- Cmd/Ctrl+Z always calls preventDefault and smartUndo (59-68).
- Cmd+A always calls preventDefault (177-189).
- Cmd+C copies the selected clip (70-91).
- Cmd+V pastes clips at the playhead whenever the DAW clipboard is non-empty (93-131).
- Cmd+= / Cmd+- / Cmd+0 call preventDefault and zoom the timeline (242-261).
impact:
Affected fields: the chat box (ChatPanel.tsx:136-146), project name, BPM, Lead Sheet chord editor and Score text.
- Ctrl+A doesn't select text.
- Ctrl+Z undoes a musical edit instead of the typing.
- Ctrl+V drops a MIDI clip into the arrangement, synced to collaborators, instead of pasting text.
- Ctrl+C copies the clip instead of the text.
Students also can't use Ctrl +/- to enlarge the page (WCAG 1.4.4); this is new beyond A11Y#5.
recommendation: Return early for editable targets (input, textarea, select, contenteditable) for everything except Cmd+S. Limit clipboard, undo and duplicate to the focused editor region. Drop the Cmd+=/-/0 overrides and use Alt/Ctrl+scroll and on-screen zoom instead.
verifierNote: The modifier shortcuts sit above the input check (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:42 says 'always active, even in inputs'; the input check is at 296-301). Cmd+Z always calls preventDefault and smartUndo (59-68), and Cmd+A always calls preventDefault (177-180). Cmd+C/Cmd+V take over when a clip is selected or the clipboard is non-empty (70-131), and Cmd+= / Cmd+- / Cmd+0 call preventDefault (242-261). ChatPanel's onKeyDown only handles Enter and doesn't stop propagation (ChatPanel.tsx:50-58).
impactNote: In useKeyboardShortcuts.ts all Cmd/Ctrl handlers run before the input check at 296-301, and that check also misses contenteditable and select elements. Cmd+Z always calls preventDefault and smartUndo (59-68), so Ctrl+Z inside the project name, BPM or chat undoes a musical edit. Cmd+A always calls preventDefault (177-189), so select-all never works in any text field. Cmd+C intercepts whenever a clip is selected (70-91), and Cmd+V pastes clips whenever the DAW clipboard is non-empty (93-131), which in collab inserts a clip for everyone. Cmd+=/-/0 call preventDefault (242-261) and block browser page zoom on Chromebooks, a WCAG 1.4.4 problem.
regressionRisks: Students may rely on Ctrl+Z working while focus sits on a slider or button (not editable), so keep it global for non-text targets. Radix Slider thumbs are role=slider, not input, so they stay unaffected. Removing the Cmd+= timeline zoom loses a shortcut that may be documented in tutorials or the shortcut sheet, so update those. Keep Cmd+S global.

title: Single-key, Delete and arrow shortcuts act across views and collide with computer-keyboard note input
evidence:
The global window listener is registered first (at DawApp mount) and doesn't know which view is showing.
- Digits 1–4 set the arrange tool (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:15-20, 303-309), while Score uses 2–7 for note durations (noteEditor.ts:28-35).
- Delete/Backspace remove selectedClipId and the arrow keys nudge it (311-345, 385-405) in every view. setCurrentView never clears it (uiSlice.ts:378-382), and Score and Lead Sheet run their own Delete handlers (useScoreEditing.tsx:721-727; LeadSheetView.tsx:697-742).
- KeyL toggles loop and KeyM the metronome (366-378), but the computer-keyboard note maps use 'l' (KeyboardView.tsx:33-45 → D4; oracle-synth/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:10-38 → D5) and 'm' (synth → B3).
- The two maps disagree (a = C3 vs a = C4), and they only exist while KeyboardView/SoundFontView or the synth pop-out is mounted.
impact:
- Select a clip in Create, switch to Score, delete a note: the whole clip is deleted and that part empties.
- Pressing '3' to pick a 16th note silently switches the timeline to Scissors.
- Playing D on the computer keyboard toggles the loop; on the synth, B3 toggles the metronome.
- Computer-keyboard playing stops working when the dock shows FX or Piano Roll.
recommendation: Use a scoped keymap. Global keys cover only transport, views and save; editing keys go to the focused region (canvas, track list, notes editor, score). Clear the clip selection on view change. One computer-keyboard note service with a single map and an explicit on/off toggle that suspends letter shortcuts while on.
verifierNote: TOOL_KEYS maps Digit1-4 to tools (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:15-20, 303-309), while Score durations use keys 2-7 (noteEditor.ts:28-35). Delete/arrow handling acts on selectedClipId in any view (311-405); setCurrentView doesn't clear it (uiSlice.ts:378-382), and Score adds its own window Delete listener (useScoreEditing.tsx:719-737), so both fire. KeyL/KeyM toggle loop and metronome, colliding with the QWERTY maps (KeyboardView 'l'=62; synth 'l'=74, 'm'=59). The two maps differ ('a'=48 vs 'a'=60).
impactNote: The global handler has no view awareness and never checks defaultPrevented. Delete/Backspace remove selectedClipId (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:385-405), and setCurrentView doesn't clear the selection (uiSlice.ts:378-382). Score's own window keydown (useScoreEditing.tsx:720-737) also deletes notes, so deleting a note in Score while a clip from Create is still selected also deletes that whole clip. Digit2-4 switch the arrange tool (15-20, 303-309), which collides with Score durations '2'-'7' (noteEditor.ts:28-35). KeyL/KeyM toggle loop and metronome (366-378) while KeyboardView maps 'l' to D4 (KeyboardView.tsx:33-45) on its own window listener (159), so playing D also toggles the loop. Undo can recover the deletion, but the student won't realise what happened.
regressionRisks: A scoped keymap changes muscle memory, so tutorials that teach shortcuts (Space/R/L/M) need checking. Clearing the clip selection on view change may affect Lead Sheet melody mode and PianoRollModal, which read editingClipId (a separate field). Keep that one. One shared computer-keyboard map changes octave for whichever surface switches (C3 vs C4), and any tutorial step that says 'press A' must match. Suspending letter shortcuts while note input is on needs a visible indicator.

title: The editor root re-renders the whole tree on every track, fader or loop edit
evidence:
DawAppInner calls useTransport, usePlaybackEngine and useCollabAudioLoader (DawApp.tsx:79-85). Together they subscribe to:
- tracks, transport flags, count-in, metronome, time signature, loop, masteringEffects, masterVolume, masterAutomation and returns (usePlaybackEngine.ts:363-376)
- tracks (useCollabAudioLoader.ts:24)
- bpm and loop range (useTransport.ts:26-35)
DawAppInner renders every region (DawApp.tsx:481-538), and of those only TransportBar is memoized. TimelineWithHeaders, Timeline (Timeline.tsx:340), LibraryPanel/InsightContent, ChannelStrip and its active panel, PianoRollModal, PitchEditorModal and the global prompts are plain functions. 28 places also subscribe to the whole tracks array (e.g. TransportBar.tsx:201, ChannelStrip.tsx:115, ChordAnalysisPrompt.tsx:89, ExportAudioDialog.tsx:139).
impact: Every pointer move on a track volume slider, the master or return fader, a loop-region drag, or a recorded note re-renders the 3,058-line Timeline, the active dock panel and Insight from the root. This is the 'sliders feel sticky' lag on Chromebooks.
recommendation: Move the engine hooks into a sibling <EngineHost/> that renders nothing, or use useStore.subscribe inside effects. Memoize every region. Replace whole-array subscriptions with useTrackIds() + useTrack(id), which MixingStrip already does (StudioView.tsx:593-616).
verifierNote: DawAppInner does subscribe to tracks and the engine fields (usePlaybackEngine.ts:363-376; useCollabAudioLoader.ts:24), and only TransportBar (TransportBar.tsx:142) and MixingStrip are memoized. However, Timeline (Timeline.tsx:415), ChannelStrip (:115), InsightContent (:69) and LibraryPanel (:394) each subscribe to the whole tracks array themselves. They would re-render on every fader step even without the root, so moving the hooks out only removes part of the cost; per-track selectors are the bigger fix.
impactNote: Confirmed: DawAppInner calls usePlaybackEngine (subscribes to tracks, masteringEffects, masterVolume, masterAutomation, returns etc., usePlaybackEngine.ts:363-376) and useCollabAudioLoader (tracks, useCollabAudioLoader.ts:24), so any tracks change re-renders the root and every unmemoized child (DawApp.tsx:481-538). TrackHeader's volume slider writes to the store on every pointer move (TrackHeader.tsx:497), so a fader drag re-renders the whole tree. Partial: Timeline and many children also subscribe to the whole tracks array themselves, so moving the engine hooks alone buys less than claimed. Most of the win needs the useTrackIds/useTrack(id) migration. The '3,058-line Timeline' cost on Chromebooks is plausible but not measured.
regressionRisks: Moving engine hooks into a sibling EngineHost changes effect ordering relative to useTransport, useKeyboardShortcuts and the boot effect. The engine must still be initialised before the boot loads a project and audio. React.memo on regions with inline callbacks gives no benefit unless props are stable. Per-track selectors must handle collab Yjs updates that replace the tracks array identity, or meters, faders or remote edits could stop updating. Data-tutorial-id anchors are unaffected.

title: Undo tracking serializes the whole project on every change and adds duplicate subscriptions on every editor visit
evidence: DawApp.tsx:97-99 calls initUndoTracking() on every mount. It adds 15 store subscriptions with no unsubscribe and no init guard (undoMiddleware.ts:219-265). The handler first calls watched() (195-208), which JSON.stringify's tracks, chordRegions and readMarks() (itself a structuredClone of 13 mark arrays, 62-72). Only after that does it run the reference comparison it actually relies on (223-230).
impact: Every tracks change (fader step, clip drag, note draw) serializes all MIDI events on the main thread. After N visits to the editor in one SPA session, N handlers each do it.
recommendation: Make initUndoTracking idempotent and return an unsubscribe for the effect cleanup. Compare references without JSON. Stringify only inside the 300 ms debounce. Expose a 'dirty since save' flag for the save chip (ia-flows-18).
verifierNote: initUndoTracking() runs on every DawApp mount (DawApp.tsx:97-99). It registers 2 + 13 MARK_KEYS subscriptions that are never unsubscribed and has no guard against running twice (undoMiddleware.ts:255-264). handleChange calls watched() first, which JSON.stringifies tracks, chordRegions and the structuredClone'd readMarks() (195-208), and only then runs the reference check (223-230). So each handler serializes the whole project on every tracks change, and there is one handler per editor visit.
impactNote: DawApp.tsx:97-99 calls initUndoTracking() on every mount. initUndoTracking (undoMiddleware.ts:219-265) registers 15 selector subscriptions, never unsubscribes and has no guard. handleChange calls watched() first (195-208), which JSON.stringify's all tracks and chordRegions plus readMarks() (a structuredClone of the mark arrays, 62-72), before the cheap reference check. Every tracks change, such as each pointer move of a fader (TrackHeader.tsx:497) or each note drawn, therefore serialises the whole project, N times after N editor visits. Duplicate handlers don't create duplicate undo entries (module-level lastRefs makes the extra handlers exit early), but they still pay the stringify cost.
regressionRisks: Making init idempotent and returning an unsubscribe must keep the module-level baseline (lastJson). Re-mount should call rebaseline(), not create a second subscription, or the first edit after navigation records a bogus undo step. Deferring the stringify to the 300 ms debounce is safe because the 'before' snapshot is lastJson from the previous settle. Collab mode uses the Yjs UndoManager (smartUndo), so make sure the snapshot tracking doesn't double-record there. The dirty flag needs a reset on save and on load.

title: Export MIDI puts every clip at bar 1 and drops the time signature
evidence: FileMenu.handleExport (FileMenu.tsx:323-352) and the Cmd+E handler (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:191-211) flatten track.midiClips.flatMap((clip) => clip.events) without adding clip.startTick. Events are clip-relative: PianoRollModal.tsx:87-89 says 'Events are clip-relative', and TransportBar.tsx:252 adds clip.startTick. exportMidiFile writes only tempo and track name (MidiFileIO.ts:61-96), and the file is always named 'prism-session.mid'. The two exporters disagree on which tracks they include (all tracks vs type 'midi'). An empty project exports nothing and shows no message (FileMenu.tsx:348).

recommendation: Use one exportProjectMidi(state) for both the menu and the shortcut. Offset events by clip.startTick, write the time signature and key, name the file after the project, and show a toast when there's nothing to export.
verifierNote: FileMenu.handleExport (FileMenu.tsx:339) and the Cmd+E handler (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:198) use track.midiClips.flatMap(clip => clip.events) without adding clip.startTick. Events are clip-relative (PianoRollModal.tsx:87; TransportBar.tsx:252 adds clip.startTick). exportMidiFile writes only tempo and track name (MidiFileIO.ts:61-96). The file is always 'prism-session.mid'. The menu exports all tracks while Cmd+E filters to type 'midi', and an empty project returns silently.

Even a single-clip export comes out 3.75x too slow. title: MASTER (Mix) view leaves the mixer about 68 px tall on a 1366x768 screen
evidence: MasteringSection has a fixed height (shrink-0, StudioView.tsx:287-294) and holds a 180 px spectrum (170-182) plus an FX-chain block. MixingSection is flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-hidden (1083-1102), so it only gets what's left. In a11y-studio-MASTER.png (1440x900) the mastering block spans y≈104–672 and the strip labels are cut off at the bottom edge. At 768 px the editor box is about 712 px. After the 48 px top bar and the ≈568 px block, the mixer gets about 96 px including its 28 px header. A strip needs more than that: dB readout, Mute/Solo, fader, a 32 px pan knob, send knobs and its name. The R&B lesson's mix steps target the mixer sends and the master strip (tutorials.ts:676-745).

title: Three piano rolls with three targeting rules; the docked one often edits the wrong thing
evidence:
1. The dock's Piano Roll tab shows selectedClip, which can come from any track. With no clip selected it shows a blank roll that creates a clip at tick 0 on the selected track (ChannelStrip.tsx:132-138, 160-175, 330-341). addMidiClip just appends (tracksSlice.ts:664-671). The dock header names the selected track (259-280), which can differ from the clip's track.
2. KeyboardView embeds its own roll that always edits track.midiClips[0] (KeyboardView.tsx:75-85, 328-332).
3. PianoRollModal opens on clip double-click and has an editor loop and 'Analyze in Insight' (PianoRollModal.tsx:23-31, 50-78), which the dock lacks.
The dock content is 33vh (ChannelStrip.tsx:318). a11y-studio-bottom-piano-roll.png shows only A3–A4 and '0 notes' for Rhodes, which has a clip.
impact: Students see an empty roll for a track that has notes. They draw into it and stack a second clip at bar 1, so both play. Or they edit the Bass clip while the dock says 'Rhodes'. The better editor sits behind a double-click nobody discovers.
recommendation: Use one Notes editor bound to the selected track. Selecting a track focuses its clip under the playhead (else its first clip). Drawing on a blank roll creates a clip only in empty space at the playhead. A 'Maximize' button on the same instance replaces the modal. Remove the roll embedded in KeyboardView.
verifierNote: The dock roll edits selectedClip from selectedClipTrackId, which can differ from the selected track shown in the header. With no clip selected it creates a clip at startTick 0 on the selected track (ChannelStrip.tsx:134-138, 160-172). KeyboardView always edits track.midiClips[0] (KeyboardView.tsx:75-85). The dock content is fixed at 33vh (ChannelStrip.tsx:318).
impactNote: The dock roll edits selectedClip from any track (ChannelStrip.tsx:134-138), while the header and audition use the selected track (132, 148-151). With no clip selected and a MIDI track selected, the first drawn note creates a new clip at startTick 0 on that track (160-175), even if the track already has clips, so it stacks onto bar 1 and both play. KeyboardView's embedded roll always edits track.midiClips[0] (KeyboardView.tsx:75-85). PianoRollModal is a third editor reached only by double-click. Students get confused about which notes they're editing, and the stacked duplicate clip is a concrete defect. The full three-into-one unification is M effort, but focusing the track's clip on selection is a small targeted fix.
regressionRisks: Auto-selecting a clip when a track is selected changes what Delete/arrow keys act on (ia-flows-08). A student selecting a track could then delete a clip by pressing Backspace, so combine with scoped keys. Removing PianoRollModal affects its editor loop (getPlaybackLoop reads the editor loop, useTransport.ts:31-33) and 'Analyze in Insight'. Tutorial steps that target piano-roll anchors in the modal or KeyboardView must be re-pointed.

title: No save status: Cmd+S is silent, there is no unsaved indicator, and Undo/Redo buttons exist only in Score
evidence: Cmd+S calls saveCurrentProjectToCloud(...).catch(err => console.error(...)) and shows no toast. If the user isn't signed in, it only logs console.warn (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:46-57). File > Save does show toasts and advertises Cmd+S (FileMenu.tsx:153-177, 441-455). TransportBar (357-952) shows no saved, saving or unsaved state. On-screen Undo/Redo is wired only through useScoreEditing (2415-2424), which covers Score and the Lead Sheet's melody mode. Create, Mix and the chord chart rely on Cmd+Z alone (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:59-68).
impact: The most-used save path gives no confirmation, and a failed save looks the same as a successful one. Students leave thinking their work is saved. Beginners have no on-screen undo after a destructive Prism Create, a clip delete or a track delete.
recommendation: Add a save-state chip next to the project name (Saved / Saving... / Unsaved changes / Couldn't save - Retry), driven by a dirty flag. Route Cmd+S through the same handler as File > Save. Add Undo/Redo buttons to the top bar in every view.
verifierNote: Cmd+S only logs console.warn when signed out and .catch(console.error) on failure (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:46-57). saveCurrentProjectToCloud shows no success toast (api.ts:262-340), while File > Save calls showSuccess (FileMenu.tsx:163). The only on-screen undo is in Score (useScoreEditing.tsx, NoteEditorBar.tsx), and TransportBar has no saved/saving/unsaved state.
impactNote: Cmd+S (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:46-57) calls saveCurrentProjectToCloud with only console.error on failure and console.warn when signed out, and shows no toast. File > Save shows success and error toasts and handles PartialUploadError (FileMenu.tsx:153-177). TransportBar has no save-state indicator, and grep finds smartUndo used in components only by Score/useScoreEditing.tsx, so Create, Mix and the chord chart have no on-screen undo. Collab non-hosts saving their own copy use the nameOverride path, so preserve it. A dirty flag must reset on load and save and ignore UI-only changes. Base it on the undo tracker (ia-flows-10), not the autosave subscription. Undo buttons in collab must call smartUndo (Yjs) so they don't undo peers' edits. title: Live meters re-render track headers and mixer strips on every animation frame
evidence: useMeterLevel runs a rAF loop and calls setLevel(Math.round(peak)) on every frame (useMeterLevel.ts:23-46). It is used inside TrackHeader (TrackHeader.tsx:90-93), MasterTrackHeader (47-52), MixingStrip (StudioView.tsx:614-616), MasterStrip (759-763) and LufsMeter (191-195). MeterBar adds another effect→setState on each level change (444-455). SpectrumAnalyzer loops at 60 fps whenever the engine is ready, allocates a points array and two gradients each frame, and sizes its canvas only once (55-60, 82-131, 166-168).
impact: With 8 tracks playing, track headers re-render about 500 times a second, and each one contains a Radix Slider, a Popover and 6 motion buttons. That comes on top of the Timeline's 30 Hz render and causes jank during playback on Chromebooks. The loops keep running when playback is stopped.
recommendation: Use one shared MeterBus rAF loop that runs only while playing, recording or monitoring. It writes levels straight into refs (transform: scaleX/scaleY) instead of React state. Draw the spectrum only while audio is flowing, reuse its buffers, and resize it with a ResizeObserver.
verifierNote: useMeterLevel calls setLevel(Math.round(peak)) on every rAF frame (useMeterLevel.ts:23-46) and is used in TrackHeader (:93), MasterTrackHeader (:50-51) and StudioView (194-195, 616, 762-763). TrackHeader's memo doesn't help because the state is internal. React bails out of the render when the level stays at 0 while silent, but the rAF loops and the SpectrumAnalyzer gradients (createLinearGradient each frame) keep running.
impactNote: Confirmed: useMeterLevel runs a rAF and calls setLevel(Math.round(peak)) every frame (useMeterLevel.ts:23-46). It is used per TrackHeader (TrackHeader.tsx:90-93), MasterTrackHeader, MixingStrip, MasterStrip and LufsMeter. During playback every track header (Radix Slider, Popover, motion buttons) re-renders at about 60 Hz, which is about 480 renders/s with 8 tracks, on top of the 30 Hz playhead updates. That is a real source of playback jank on 4-core Chromebooks. Partial: the claim that re-renders continue when stopped is wrong. Once the peak decays to 0, setLevel(0) bails out, so only the cheap rAF and analyser read keep running. SpectrumAnalyzer's per-frame allocation is real but limited to the Master view.
regressionRisks: Writing levels directly into refs or the DOM bypasses React, so meters must still clear when tracks are deleted or engines rebuilt (analyser node replaced on instrument change). Look the analyser up lazily on each tick. A playing-only loop must still meter during monitoring and recording count-in and for remote collab activity (useRemoteTrackActivity). Peak-hold decay behaviour should look the same.
