title: The detected-key bus goes stale and overrides the user's key for vocal pitch correction, chord detection and synth snap
evidence:
unisonSlice.ts:209-219 calls `setDetectedKey(..., 'unison-offline')` only when `key.confidence > 0.5`. That confidence is the detector's own, even when the user set the key (sessionToUnison.ts:178-191 spreads `...detected`). analyzeSession only runs while InsightContent is mounted (InsightContent.tsx:73-84).

Nothing resets the bus:
- `clearDetectedKey` (musicIntelligenceSlice.ts:108-116) has no callers.
- freshProjectHarmony (SessionSerializer.ts:512-544) does not include the bus fields.
- `keySource: 'manual'` is never set; setRootNote and setMode (prismSlice.ts:1419-1495) do not touch the bus.

Consumers prefer the bus over the session key:
- VocalView.tsx:469-472 uses `const globalRootNote = busKeyRootPc ?? prismRootNote`. It copies that into the pitch-correction block (`updateBlockParam(pcBlockId, 'rootNote', ...)`, :581-613), which is saved through setVocalChain (:565-575).
- useAudioChordDetection.ts:127-133 uses `effectiveRoot = busRoot ?? rootNote`.
- DawSynthLayout.tsx:56-66 and useStoreBridge.ts:85-103 snap the synth to the bus key.
impact: The previous key sticks in three cases: the student changes the key while the Insight panel is closed, detection confidence is 0.5 or lower, or another project is opened in the same tab or collab room. Vocal auto-tune, the live chord detector and 'snap to song key' keep using the old key. VocalView also writes that wrong root and scale into the track's saved vocal chain. Students hear correction to the wrong scale with no visible cause.
recommendation: Make the session key authoritative. Inside setRootNote and setMode, set keySource 'manual' and update the bus key. Reset the bus in freshProjectHarmony and resetSessionToEmpty. Let detection fill the bus only when rootNote is null. Better still, derive an `effectiveKey` with a selector instead of storing a copy.
verifierNote: The bus is only set when key.confidence > 0.5 inside analyzeSession (unisonSlice.ts:211-219), and analyzeSession only runs automatically while InsightContent is mounted. clearDetectedKey has no callers, and neither freshProjectHarmony nor resetSessionToEmpty (SessionSerializer.ts:512-544, 649-678) resets the bus fields. VocalView.tsx:469-472 and useAudioChordDetection.ts:127-133 use the bus key before the session key, so a stale bus key overrides the user's key.
impactNote: The mechanism is real, but the stale cases are narrower than stated. resolveKey (sessionToUnison.ts:180-193) returns the user's rootNote and mode with the detector's confidence. So while Insight is mounted (panel open, Insight tab is the default) and confidence is above 0.5, a key change does reach the bus within about 500 ms (unisonSlice.ts:209-219). Confirmed gaps: clearDetectedKey is never called, and keySource 'manual' is never set (grep finds only useLiveUnisonAnalysis reading it). freshProjectHarmony does not touch the bus fields, so opening another project keeps the previous project's bus key. VocalView.tsx:469-472 uses busKeyRootPc ?? prismRootNote. So when the bus is stale (low confidence, panel closed, or a different project), the key picker inside VocalView (setGlobalRootNote at :1296/:1917) has no visible effect on pitch correction. The sync effects at :581-613 then write the bus key into the saved vocal chain. useAudioChordDetection.ts:127-133 has the same preference. Auto-tune correcting to the wrong scale is audible. It affects fewer users (those using the vocal chain or the chord detector), but it is hard for them to diagnose.
regressionRisks: Making the session key authoritative changes useLiveUnisonAnalysis behaviour (it skips when keySource is 'manual' or 'unison-offline'). Live key detection for projects with no key set must keep working. Resetting the bus on load changes pitch-correction params on existing vocal chains the first time they render, because VocalView writes globalRootNote into the block and persists it via setVocalChain. Saved projects that hold a wrong root will be rewritten, which is desired but a visible change. Collab: rootNote syncs but the bus is local, so derive effectiveKey with a selector rather than syncing bus fields. The audio worklet scale bitmask (activeNotesBitmask) must be recomputed when the bus resets, or there may be a brief stale correction.

title: Guitar/Bass/Vocal tone, input device and NAM model are applied only while that track's Controls view is open
evidence: The adapters start with an empty chain (direct bypass `this.inputNode.connect(this.outputNode)`, GuitarPedalChain.ts:93-94) and no input stream. The saved track.guitarChain / vocalChain (persisted by SessionSerializer and Yjs) reaches the engine only from view effects: `adapter.syncChain(...)` (GuitarBassView.tsx:549-562), `adapter.setDevice(globalInputDeviceId)` (GuitarBassView.tsx:470-482), NAM auto-load (GuitarBassView.tsx:498+), and the same in VocalView.tsx:532-562. Those views mount only for the selected track, and only on the CONTROLS tab (`activeTab === 'controls' && <TrackControlsPanel />`, ChannelStrip.tsx:320; renderView, TrackControlsPanel.tsx:133-162). The engine's post-init hook applies Oracle, drum pad, organ and Chops state but nothing for guitar or vocal (usePlaybackEngine.ts:508-559). Recording falls back when no device is attached: startRecordingStream returns null without a channelGain (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:275-276), and the engine then calls `getUserMedia({ audio: audioConstraints })` with no deviceId (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1039-1055).
impact: This happens after a refresh or crash recovery, after opening a cloud project, after returning to the editor, or when a collaborator edits the chain. Recorded DI guitar/bass/vocal clips, which play through getNativePedalInputNode() (usePlaybackEngine.ts:685-696), then play dry: no amp, NAM, overdrive or pitch correction until the student selects that track and opens CONTROLS. With two guitar tracks, only the inspected one gets its tone back. Arming and recording such a track records the laptop's default mic instead of the chosen interface channel. Export bounces these tracks dry too (renderProject.ts:33-37).
recommendation: Make the engine the only place that applies this state. Give the input adapters an applyTrackState(track, globalInput) covering chain (updateProcessorParams/syncChain), NAM model id, channel config and monitoring, and call it from usePlaybackEngine's init `.then` and per-track sync, as applyOrganState and applySamplerState already work. Views then only write the store. Open the input stream when the student shows intent (record-arm or monitor-on), not when a view mounts, and show an 'input not connected' state on the track.
verifierNote: The only DAW callers of syncChain, updateChainParams and setDevice are GuitarBassView.tsx:475-478 and 554, and VocalView.tsx:537-561. The init `.then` in usePlaybackEngine.ts:508-559 applies Oracle, drum, organ and Chops state but nothing for guitar or vocal. These views mount only under `activeTab === 'controls' && <TrackControlsPanel />` (ChannelStrip.tsx:320). With no device, startRecordingStream returns null (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:275-276), and recording falls back to a getUserMedia call with no deviceId (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1043-1050).
impactNote: syncChain, setDevice and loadNamModel are only ever called from GuitarBassView.tsx:475-554 and VocalView.tsx:537-561 (grep finds no other callers in src/daw). Those views only render through TrackControlsPanel.renderView (TrackControlsPanel.tsx:144-160), and that only renders when activeTab === 'controls' (ChannelStrip.tsx:320). The engine's post-init `.then` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:510-555) applies Oracle, drum, organ and Chops state, but nothing for guitar or vocal. DI clips are routed through getNativePedalInputNode (usePlaybackEngine.ts:685-696), so after a reload or project open every guitar/bass/vocal track plays dry through an empty chain until its Controls view has been opened once. Once synced, the adapter keeps the chain, which limits this to tracks not inspected since load. That still covers every non-selected guitar track. The record fallback that calls getUserMedia with no deviceId (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1043-1050) is also real. The dry export is a documented known limitation (renderProject.ts:33-37) and isn't caused by this bug.
regressionRisks: Moving NAM model loading into the engine means remote model fetches at project load (bandwidth, and concurrent loads across several tracks). Load lazily or on first play. Opening getUserMedia from the engine at load would trigger permission prompts without a user gesture, so the device should only attach on arm or monitor, as recommended. The views must stop applying the chain themselves, or the chain gets applied twice (rebuilt, with possible audio glitches). Collab peer edits to guitarChain need the same engine-side sync path. Keep any data-tutorial-id anchors in GuitarBassView and VocalView unchanged.

title: Live drum pad and MIDI drum hits sound ~100 ms late (Tone.now() instead of Tone.immediate())
evidence: `noteOn(note, velocity, time?) { const t = time ?? Tone.now();` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:202-203). Tone's now() is `this._context.currentTime + this._lookAhead` (node_modules/tone/build/esm/core/context/Context.js:329-331), lookAhead defaults to 0.1 (Context.js:79-80), and nothing in src overrides it. Live pad taps pass no time: `state.trackEngine.noteOn(note, 100)` (DrumMachineView.tsx:317-323). Every other adapter deliberately uses the raw clock for live input: PianoSampler.ts:71-76, SamplerInstrument.ts:62-67 and ChopsSampler.ts:112-117 (with the comment 'Live playing passes no time; Tone would default to now() + lookAhead'), and EightOhEightInstrument.ts:28-32.
impact: Every on-screen pad tap and MIDI drum hit is delayed by 100 ms plus output latency. That is clearly perceptible when finger-drumming, makes live drum recording hard (students learn to play early), and feels inconsistent next to the instant piano and synth tracks.
recommendation: Use `time ?? Tone.immediate()` in DrumMachineEngine.noteOn; the choke and velocity-gain writes reuse `t`, so they follow. Add a test that live calls land at context.currentTime.
verifierNote: DrumMachineEngine.ts:203 has `const t = time ?? Tone.now();`. Tone's now() is currentTime + lookAhead, and the 0.1 default is never overridden in src/daw. Pad taps call `state.trackEngine.noteOn(note, 100)` with no time (DrumMachineView.tsx:317-321), while PianoSampler.ts:71-76 deliberately uses Tone.immediate() for live input.
impactNote: DrumMachineEngine.ts:203 uses `time ?? Tone.now()`. The pad tap in DrumMachineView.tsx:317-321 calls `trackEngine.noteOn(note, 100)` with no time, and src never overrides lookAhead (grep only finds it in learn/ and tests). Tone.Player.start at immediate() can occasionally clip the first few samples, which is negligible for drums.

title: Load failures are silent and often permanent: PianoSampler can hang forever, and a SoundFont failure is cached for the session
evidence: PianoSampler.init resolves only from `onload` and passes no `onerror` (PianoSampler.ts:19-65). Tone's buffer onerror defaults to noOp (ToneAudioBuffer.js:26-39), so a single failed file among the 30 CDN MP3s leaves the promise pending forever, with nothing logged; SamplerInstrument already rejects in this case (SamplerInstrument.ts:44-52). SoundFont: `if (!synthInitPromise) synthInitPromise = initSharedSynth(ctx); await synthInitPromise;` (SoundFontAdapter.ts:77-80). A rejection (worklet timeout or SF2 fetch failure) stays cached at module scope (SoundFontAdapter.ts:30-32), so every later SoundFont track fails at once until a full page reload; SPA navigation doesn't reset it. The worklet 'processorerror' listener is an empty function despite its 'surface errors' comment (SoundFontAdapter.ts:238-242). Init errors only reach console.error (usePlaybackEngine.ts:560-565), even though showError is imported at line 3. SoundFontView keeps polling and spinning forever when the instrument never attaches (SoundFontView.tsx:68-90).
impact: One CDN hiccup or blocked domain leaves a piano or GM track silent for the rest of the session, showing either an endless spinner or nothing at all. Students can't tell whether to wait, retry or reload.
recommendation: Make every adapter reject on any load error (add onerror to PianoSampler, or fold it into SamplerInstrument). Clear synthInitPromise on rejection so the next attempt retries, with backoff. Show an error status with a Retry action in the track header and the Controls view, and a toast via showError. Have processorerror mark the synth as failed and notify. Use timeouts that cover the body download, not just the headers.
verifierNote: PianoSampler.init's Promise resolves only in `onload` and has no onerror (PianoSampler.ts:18-63), unlike SamplerInstrument.ts:44-52. `if (!synthInitPromise) synthInitPromise = initSharedSynth(ctx)` caches a rejection at module scope (SoundFontAdapter.ts:76-79). The processorerror listener is `(_e: Event) => {}`. Init failures only reach console.error (usePlaybackEngine.ts:560-565), and SoundFontView polls forever.
impactNote: PianoSampler.init (PianoSampler.ts:18-65) resolves only through onload and has no onerror. If any of the 30 MP3s from tonejs.github.io fails (school firewalls often block github.io), the promise stays pending forever and the piano is silent with no error. Piano is the most common track type, which makes this a likely school scenario. synthInitPromise is cached at module scope (SoundFontAdapter.ts:32, 77-80) and is never cleared on rejection, so one SF2 or worklet timeout disables GM for the whole session. The processorerror handler is empty (SoundFontAdapter.ts:238-242). Init errors only reach console.error (usePlaybackEngine.ts:560-565). Students get silent tracks with no feedback.
regressionRisks: If the PianoSampler rejects on any single missing sample, a piano that is mostly playable fails outright. Consider resolving with partial samples and a warning instead. Resetting synthInitPromise on failure must also reset sharedSynth and synthReady, and avoid creating duplicate WorkletSynthesizers or calling addModule twice (addModule on the same URL is fine, but the old synth node must be disconnected). Toasts per track on a project load where a whole domain is blocked could spam the user, so de-duplicate per cause. Retrying while the transport is running could cause audio pops.

title: Global DAW shortcuts change hidden timeline clips while you edit the lead sheet
evidence:
useKeyboardShortcuts is mounted in every view (DawApp.tsx:81) and never checks currentView:
- Delete/Backspace removes state.selectedClipId and calls removeAudioBuffer (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:385-405).
- ←/→ nudge the selected clip (313-345).
- ⌘V pastes clipboardClips at the playhead (93-131).
- ⌘D duplicates the selected clip (133-175).
- Escape calls state.stop() (380-383).

setCurrentView only sets currentView and libraryOpen (uiSlice.ts:378-381), so a clip selected in CREATE stays selected in LEAD SHEET. LeadSheetChartView adds its own window keydown listener for the same keys (LeadSheetView.tsx:640-745): Delete clears chords, ⌘V pastes chords, Escape clears the selection. Neither handler checks e.defaultPrevented or stops propagation, and the global listener is registered first, so it always runs first. The lead sheet's focus exclusion covers only INPUT and TEXTAREA (642-648), so a focused SELECT (for example in the Send dialog) still triggers both handlers.
impact: Pressing Delete to remove a chord also deletes the last clip clicked in the arrange view. For an unsaved audio recording the buffer is destroyed, so undo brings back a silent clip. Arrow keys, a natural way to move around a chart, shift a MIDI or audio clip by a beat on each press. ⌘V drops a previously copied clip onto the song at the playhead. Escape, pressed to drop a selection, stops playback. None of this is visible from the lead sheet.
recommendation: Scope shortcuts to views. Clip and timeline shortcuts (Delete, arrows, ⌘C/⌘V/⌘D/⌘A, Escape→stop) should run only when currentView === 'arrange'; Space, R, M and L can stay global. Notation views should handle their keys in a capture-phase listener on their own container and call preventDefault, and the global hook should bail out when e.defaultPrevented is set. Clear selectedClipId on view switch. In both handlers, treat SELECT, contentEditable and an open dialog as text entry.
verifierNote: useKeyboardShortcuts is mounted unconditionally (DawApp.tsx:81) and never reads currentView. Its only input guard is the e.target instanceof Input/TextArea check (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:296-301), so Escape→stop(), arrow nudges and Delete→removeAudioBuffer+removeAudioClip all run against state.selectedClipId. setCurrentView (uiSlice.ts:378-381) does not clear that selection, and the lead sheet's own listener (LeadSheetView.tsx:640-745) is registered later and never stops propagation.
impactNote: useKeyboardShortcuts is mounted for every view (src/daw/DawApp.tsx:81) and never reads currentView. Delete/Backspace removes selectedClipId and calls removeAudioBuffer (src/daw/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:385-405). When it does fire, it is invisible from the lead sheet, which makes it serious.

title: A browser refresh restores chords but loses the roadmap, layout and time signature
evidence: serializeSession (SessionSerializer.ts:274-337) writes the project ids and names, transport {bpm, position, metronome, loop}, tracks, prism {rootNote, rhythmName, genre, swing, mode}, chordRegions, returns and masterAutomation. It does not write leadSheetSections, leadSheetRepeats, measureRowSizes, measureRestMap, measureFermatas, scoreSlashNotes, leadSheetShowMelody, leadSheetChordFormat or timeSignatureNumerator/Denominator. deserializeSession (762-793) spreads ...freshProjectHarmony() and restores only chordRegions. Library songs set exactly the lost fields: seedStudioFromSong.ts:35-46 calls setTimeSignature, setMeasureRowSizes, setLeadSheetSections, setMeasureRestMap and setMeasureFermatas. Separately, useAutosave.ts:19-25 restarts a 1.5 s debounce on every store change. Because position changes about 30 times a second during playback, nothing is written while the transport runs.
impact: After a refresh or crash, every rehearsal mark, repeat, system break, multi-bar rest and fermata is gone. A 3/4 or 6/8 song comes back in 4/4, so regionToMeasures re-bars every chord at 1,920 ticks and the chart stops making sense. Chord edits made while a loop plays, which is common when writing over a groove, are not saved until playback has been stopped for 1.5 s.
recommendation: Bump SESSION_SCHEMA_VERSION to 3. Serialise one leadSheet object (sections, repeats, rowSizes, restMap, fermatas, slashNotes, chordFormat, showMelody, melodyTrackId) plus transport.timeSignature, and restore it after freshProjectHarmony. In useAutosave, subscribe with a selector that ignores position and isPlaying (the store already uses subscribeWithSelector) so edits still save during playback.
verifierNote: serializeSession (SessionSerializer.ts:274-337) writes chordRegions and prism.mode but none of leadSheetSections, leadSheetRepeats, measureRowSizes, measureRestMap, measureFermatas, scoreSlashNotes or the time signature. deserializeSession restores only chordRegions after ...freshProjectHarmony(). useAutosave.ts:19-25 restarts its 1.5 s timer on every store change, and useTransport.ts:79-90 writes position about every 33 ms, so nothing is saved while playback runs.
impactNote: serializeSession (src/daw/persistence/SessionSerializer.ts:274-337) writes chordRegions and prism.mode, but not leadSheetSections, leadSheetRepeats, measureRowSizes, measureRestMap, measureFermatas, scoreSlashNotes, chord format, show-melody or time signature. deserializeSession (~762-793) restores only chordRegions on top of freshProjectHarmony(). src/features/songs/seedStudioFromSong.ts:35-46 sets exactly those lost fields, so every 'Open in Studio' song in 3/4 or 6/8 comes back in 4/4 after a refresh, with sections and rests gone. The autosave starvation is real too. useAutosave (src/daw/hooks/useAutosave.ts:19-25) resets on any store change, and useTransport calls setPosition about every 33 ms while playing (src/daw/hooks/useTransport.ts:78-93), so nothing is written during playback. A refresh is less common than a cloud reopen, but this is the crash-recovery path, so high is justified.
regressionRisks: Bumping SESSION_SCHEMA_VERSION to 3 is risky. deserializeSession rejects any version other than 1 or the current one (SessionSerializer.ts:683), so an older cached tab or bundle would drop a v3 session completely. Adding optional fields under v2, and reading them defensively, is safer. Restoring the time signature must happen before chordRegions are re-barred, and must call the same setter the transport uses, or the metronome and grid will disagree. For the autosave selector, the subscription has to ignore position and isPlaying but still fire for other transport-adjacent changes, such as loop range. Writing during playback costs a serialisation on the main thread. Keep the debounce so a 4-core Chromebook doesn't glitch audio, and avoid serialising large MIDI every 1.5 s while playing if possible.

title: 'Update the Set List chart?' can overwrite a set's page with a blank or degraded chart
evidence: SetListUpdatePrompt is always mounted (DawApp.tsx:532). It builds the chart from the live store (SendToSetList.tsx:259), and on every cloud save (event dispatched at api.ts:313-318) it asks whenever staleFor(chart) is non-empty (264-269). staleFor compares fingerprints only (useSetLists.ts:313-320). After a cloud reopen, chordRegions is [] (leadsheet-01). After a refresh, the sections, rows and metre are gone (leadsheet-03). Either way the fingerprint differs, so the dialog says 'the copy there is the one you sent before these edits. Send the new version?', with a teal primary Update button (334-340). update() calls replaceProjectChart for every stale entry (286-289), which overwrites the chart and the title with no guard (setListsStore.ts:1064-1086).
impact: A normal sequence breaks it: send a chart to a set list, save, reopen later, press ⌘S. The prompt then invites the user to replace the gig chart with four empty bars, or with a version stripped of its sections, and it also resets the entry's title. The set list was the only place the chart survived, so this destroys the last copy.
recommendation: Don't offer an update when the new chart has no chords, or has fewer bars or sections than the stored copy. Show a short before/after summary in the dialog (bars, sections, key). Make 'Keep' the primary action. Preserve the entry's own title. Fixing leadsheet-01 and leadsheet-03 removes the main triggers.
verifierNote: SetListUpdatePrompt (SendToSetList.tsx:251-297) builds the chart from the live store and asks whenever staleFor(chart) finds a differing fingerprint (useSetLists.ts:313-320). There is no guard against an empty or shrunk chart. update() calls replaceProjectChart(…, chart, chart.title), which overwrites both the chart and the title (setListsStore.ts:1064-1086). Update is the teal primary button, so after the reopen-loss in leadsheet-01 or leadsheet-03 it invites replacing the gig copy with blank bars.
impactNote: SetListUpdatePrompt (src/daw/components/LeadSheet/SendToSetList.tsx:251-341) builds the chart from the live store and asks after every save whenever staleFor(chart) is non-empty (264-269). staleFor is a plain fingerprint comparison (src/features/setlists/useSetLists.ts:313-320). update() calls replaceProjectChart for every stale entry (286-289), which overwrites the chart unconditionally and also the title when one is given (src/features/setlists/setListsStore.ts:1064-1086). The dialog's wording assumes the new version is an improvement, and Update is the teal primary button. Combined with 01 (a reopened cloud project has no chords) and 03 (a refresh loses sections and metre), the normal flow 'send, save, reopen, ⌘S' invites the user to wipe the only surviving copy. Note that the save event fires from every save path (src/lib/studio-projects/api.ts:313-318).
regressionRisks: Suppressing the prompt when the new chart has fewer bars or sections would also block legitimate shortening edits. Better to change the wording ('This version has 0 chords; the set list has 32 bars') than to block. Keeping the entry's own title changes the current behaviour, where renaming a project propagates its title; decide deliberately. Making 'Keep' the primary button is a UX-only change and safe. Fixing 01 and 03 removes most triggers, but older set-list copies will still differ by fingerprint after the fix.

title: Multi-bar rests shift every later bar index: sections, rests, fermatas, playhead and edits
evidence:
Two index spaces get mixed:
- **Visible-slot index:** the chart drops the bars a rest swallows (LeadSheetView.tsx:170-181) and indexes systems by position in that filtered array (184-222). LeadSheetStaff uses globalIdx = startIndex + i for sections.find, repeats, measureRestMap?.[globalIdx], measureFermatas?.includes(globalIdx) and the bar number (LeadSheetStaff.tsx:122-160; LeadSheetMeasure.tsx:557-566).
- **Real-bar index:** the rest map, fermatas and section marks are keyed by real bar (exportToStudio.ts:211-220 records restMap[barIndex], then advances barIndex += restBars).
- **Mixed uses:** the playhead compares the real index Math.floor(position / ticksPerMeasure) against the filtered ranges (LeadSheetView.tsx:225-240). Copy, paste, ⌘K and Delete convert the filtered measureIndex back to ticks with measureIndex * ticksPerMeasure (412-421, 527-540, 664-676, 717-731). toSetListChart repeats the mix (barFrom idx at 112-119; sectionStarts uses real measureIdx at 127-138).

203 song files contain restBars of 2 or more.
impact:
For any library song with an intro or stop rest:
- Every label after the rest is drawn n−1 bars late.
- A second rest is drawn over a bar that has chords, and those chords disappear because isMultiBarRest skips them (LeadSheetMeasure.tsx:214).
- The playhead runs ahead of the music and the bar numbers are wrong.
- Paste, clear and ⌘K write chords into the wrong bars.

The set-list copy carries the same misplacement.
recommendation: Use one index space. Build the visible slots once as {realIndex, restBars} in a selector shared with toSetListChart. Pass realIndex as measureIndex everywhere (selection, roadmap, ticks) and use slot position only for layout. Number bars by real index, the way MuseScore numbers around a multi-bar rest. Add a test with two rests and a section after them.
verifierNote: exportToStudio.ts:211-218 keys restMap, fermatas and section marks by real barIndex. LeadSheetView.tsx:170-181 filters out swallowed bars, and LeadSheetStaff.tsx:123-150 then looks up sections, repeats, measureRestMap[globalIdx] and fermatas by the filtered slot index (startIndex + i). The playhead (LeadSheetView.tsx:228) and the paste and clear tick maths (419, 540, 675) use slot × ticksPerMeasure, so every mark after the first multi-bar rest is offset.
impactNote: LeadSheetView filters out the bars a rest swallows (src/daw/components/LeadSheet/LeadSheetView.tsx:170-181) and builds systems from positions in the filtered array (184-222). LeadSheetStaff then uses globalIdx = startIndex + i, a filtered position, to look up sections, repeats, measureRestMap and fermatas, and to number bars (src/daw/components/LeadSheet/LeadSheetStaff.tsx:122-160; LeadSheetMeasure.tsx:565). exportToStudio records restMap, fermatas and section runs at the real barIndex and then advances by restBars (src/curriculum/songLibrary/exportToStudio.ts:204-220). After the first rest of n bars, every later lookup is n−1 bars off, and the playhead compares a real index against filtered ranges (LeadSheetView.tsx:225-240). A rest at bar 0, the typical intro, lines up correctly, but everything after it does not. Many library song files contain multi-bar rests, so the 'Open in Studio' flow shows misplaced section letters and wrong bar numbers. It is user-visible on a core flow.
regressionRisks: Changing measureIndex to the real index affects selection keys, clipboard measureOffset, system breaks and rowSizesFromBreaks (measureCount currently counts filtered slots), the barline targets, and the toSetListChart output. Already-sent set-list charts were built with the mixed indexing and won't be migrated. Any persisted leadSheetSections or rows created by hand in the Studio, which today are keyed by filtered position, would shift by n−1 when interpretation changes. Songs from the library re-seed correctly, but user-edited projects with rests (local sessions) need care. Tutorial anchors keyed on data-selected-measure values could change.

title: The lead-sheet print stylesheet stays loaded and blanks other pages' printouts
evidence:
leadsheet-print.css is imported by the lead-sheet views (LeadSheetView.tsx:39) and becomes global once the DAW chunk loads. These rules then apply to every print in the SPA:
- body *:not(:has(.leadsheet-container)):not(.leadsheet-container):not(.leadsheet-container *) { display: none !important } (leadsheet-print.css:130-135)
- html, body { background: white !important } (125-128)
- @page { size: letter; margin: 0.75in } (8-11)

The set-list print page is reached by in-app navigation (SetListWorkspace.tsx:1013-1016). It shows itself only through visibility (setlist-print.css:33-39), and display:none !important wins over that.
impact: Send a chart to a set list from the Studio, open the set list, press Print, and you get blank pages. Any other in-app print after visiting /studio/editor behaves the same until a full page reload. The lead sheet's @page margin also fights the set list's 0.6 in margin.
recommendation: Put the rules under a body class that the editor adds in a beforeprint handler and removes in afterprint (for example body.ma-print-leadsheet ...). Never use bare 'body *'. Apply the same treatment to the Score's named page.
verifierNote: leadsheet-print.css:125-135 contains unscoped @media print rules: html/body white, and 'body *:not(:has(.leadsheet-container))…{display:none !important}'. It is imported by LeadSheetView, LeadSheetScoreView and ScoreView, so it stays global once loaded. setlist-print.css:33-39 reveals the set-list page only via visibility, which cannot beat display:none !important, and SetListWorkspace.tsx:1013-1016 reaches the print page by SPA navigate().
impactNote: src/daw/components/LeadSheet/leadsheet-print.css is imported by LeadSheetView.tsx:39, LeadSheetScoreView.tsx:14 and ScoreView.tsx:7, and once injected it stays global for the SPA session. Its bare rule `body *:not(:has(.leadsheet-container)):not(.leadsheet-container):not(.leadsheet-container *) { display:none !important }` (~130-135) hides every element on any page without a .leadsheet-container. src/features/setlists/print/SetListPrintPage.tsx has no such class and relies on visibility (src/features/setlists/print/setlist-print.css:33-39), which cannot override display:none. The set-list Print button navigates in-app (src/features/setlists/pages/SetListWorkspace.tsx:1013-1016) and auto-prints (SetListPrintPage.tsx:42). The flow 'send chart from Studio, open the set list, Print' therefore produces blank pages, and so does Ctrl+P on any page, until a full reload. Teachers printing set lists is a core action, and the bug is deterministic once the editor has been visited.
regressionRisks: Scoping the rules under a body class added in beforeprint has two traps. ⌘P from the browser menu fires beforeprint too, so the handler must check that the lead-sheet or score view is actually mounted, and must remove the class in afterprint (Chrome fires both reliably, but check that the class doesn't leak if the view unmounts mid-print). Do the same for the Score's named @page and score-print-root, and test that Score printing still yields one engraved page per sheet. The @page {size: letter; margin: 0.75in} rule inside @media print is also global and will still override other pages' @page margins unless it is scoped. @page cannot be scoped by a selector, so use a named page.

title: +/− Measure assumes 4/4, leaves the roadmap and melody behind, and can't add bars at the end
evidence: The toolbar calls insertMeasure(idx + 1) and deleteMeasure(idx) (LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:98-106). With nothing selected it inserts after bar 1. The store shifts chordRegions only, by a constant 1,920 ticks (prismSlice.ts:2037-2085: insertTick = measureIdx * 1920, delStart = measureIdx * 1920). Sections, repeats, measureRowSizes, the rest map, fermatas and the melody clip are not touched. The chart's length comes from the last chord's end (leadSheetUtils.ts:77-78), so inserting after the last bar, or in an empty chart, changes nothing. A double-clicked chord is created one quarter note long (prismSlice.ts:1935-1943, endTick: tick + 480). moveChordRegion snaps to 480 ticks whatever the metre (2019).
impact: In 3/4, an inserted bar is 1⅓ bars long and pushes every later chord off its downbeat. After any insert or delete, every section letter, repeat and system break after the edit sits one bar off. In melody mode the chords slide away from the melody. A student writing a 12-bar blues from scratch cannot add bar 5 with '+ Measure' at the end; the button silently does nothing. The only workarounds are pasting a block past the end or dragging a chord off the right edge.
recommendation: Replace both store actions with one metre-aware command (ticksPerBar(num, den)) that also shifts sections, repeats, breaks, rests and fermatas, and shifts the melody clip events when a melody is shown. Store an explicit bar count, or an end marker, so empty bars can be appended. With nothing selected, '+ Measure' should append at the end. New chords should last until the next chord, and moves should snap to the metre's own beat.
verifierNote: insertMeasure and deleteMeasure (prismSlice.ts:2037-2085) shift chordRegions only, by a hard-coded 1920 ticks. Sections, repeats, row sizes, rests and fermatas are not touched. regionToMeasures derives the bar count from the maximum endTick (leadSheetUtils.ts:77-78), so inserting after the last chord changes nothing. handleInsertMeasure uses (selectedMeasureIdx ?? 0)+1 (LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:98-101), and insertChordRegion with no overlap uses tick+480 (prismSlice.ts:1935-1943).
impactNote: insertMeasure and deleteMeasure hard-code 1920 ticks (src/daw/store/prismSlice.ts:2037-2085) and shift only chordRegions, leaving sections, repeats, row sizes, rests, fermatas and the melody clip in place. The toolbar inserts at (selectedMeasureIdx ?? 0) + 1 (src/daw/components/LeadSheet/LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:98-101). The chart length comes from the last chord's endTick, with a minimum of 4 bars (src/daw/midi/leadSheetUtils.ts:77-78), so inserting at or after the end changes no region and nothing appears. A student writing a 12-bar blues cannot add bar 5 with '+ Measure'. That is a very visible authoring blocker, and 3/4 inserts misalign every later chord. New chords are 480 ticks long (prismSlice.ts:~1937) and moves snap to 480 (~2019), which is plausible but a lesser issue (480 is a quarter note, so 6/8 snapping is off).
regressionRisks: Adding an explicit bar count or end marker is new persisted state that must go into both serializers (ties to 01 and 03), into collab sync, and into the set-list chart's bar count. Shifting the melody clip's events touches MIDI on a track, which changes audio playback, and must be a single undo step together with the chord shift (today each setter may produce its own undo entry). With nothing selected, appending at the end changes current behaviour (insert after bar 1), which may matter to any tutorial step that uses '+ Measure'. Check tutorials.ts. Changing new chords to 'last until the next chord' changes the playback lane for typed charts.

title: Views never re-apply device or chain when the engine becomes ready after they mount (always the case on reload)
evidence: The engine starts only on a user gesture ('Call initEngine() from a click / keydown handler', useAudioEngine.ts:6). Adapters are registered inside DawApp's effect (usePlaybackEngine.ts:380 'if (!isReady) return', :568 audioMap.set), and child effects run before it. ChannelStrip auto-opens CONTROLS when tracks load (ChannelStrip.tsx:122-131). So getAdapter() returns null and the views' effects bail. VocalView subscribes to engine-ready with the comment 'Re-render when instrument finishes async init' (VocalView.tsx:513-514), but the device effect's deps are [trackId, globalInputDeviceId, audioInputChannel] (:533-543) and the chain effect's are [chain, trackId, bpm] (:548-563), so the re-render never re-runs them. GuitarBassView is the same (:471-481, :550-562). Its NAM restore effect does re-run on readyVersion (:534-547), but GuitarPedalChain.loadNamModel returns silently when there is no nam-amp processor yet ('if (!proc) return', GuitarPedalChain.ts:168-172), because syncChain never ran. It therefore re-fetches and re-parses the 280–410 KB .nam file on every readyVersion bump (one per instrument init) and loads nothing until the first knob change.
impact: Even a student who already has the vocal or guitar Controls open gets no input and no tone after a reload until they change the device or channel or touch a knob. Repeated .nam downloads and JSON parses on project load waste bandwidth and main-thread time.
recommendation: Short term: add readyVersion, or a per-track adapter-ready token, to the deps of the engine-facing effects in both views. Long term: move engine application out of the views entirely (live-input-01).

title: Modal origin mixes song and clip ticks: emptying a clip at bar > 1 makes new notes land bars late
evidence: PianoRollModal.tsx:90-92 computes `clip.events.reduce((min, e) => Math.min(min, e.startTick), clip.startTick)`. This seeds a minimum over clip-relative event ticks with a song tick, so with no events it returns clip.startTick. The result is passed as clipStartTick (:191) and added again in songOffset (PianoRoll.tsx:347) and in the notation's first bar (StudioNotationView.tsx:83-85). An unsized clip extends from clip tick 0 to its last note (Timeline.tsx:650-670).
impact: Erase every note in a clip at bar 9 (startTick 15360), or open the empty half of a scissors split. The grid silently re-anchors, and the next note drawn at the left edge is stored at clip tick 15360+, which is bar 17 in the song. The clip box stretches 8 bars, or for a sized clip the note sits outside the box but still plays. Playhead, loop and notation bar numbers are 8 bars off. On reopening, the origin equals the new note, so the editor looks normal and hides the damage. Also, when a clip starts before its first note (e.g. the clip starts on beat 2 and the first note is on beat 3), the start of the clip is unreachable and bar lines begin mid-bar.
recommendation: Use origin 0, or `Math.min(0, floorToBar(minEventTick))` if negative ticks are ever possible. Never mix clip.startTick into the origin. This is folded into the pianoroll-01 API change once PianoRoll owns the origin.
verifierNote: PianoRollModal.tsx:90-92 seeds `clip.events.reduce((min,e)=>Math.min(min,e.startTick), clip.startTick)` with a song tick. With no events it returns clip.startTick, which is then added again in songOffset (PianoRoll.tsx:347) and in the note-creation math (:1050). StudioNotationView.tsx:83-85 adds it into firstBar as well. The comment at :87-89 shows the author meant to handle front-trims, but mixing tick spaces breaks empty clips.
impactNote: PianoRollModal.tsx:90-92 seeds a minimum over clip-relative event ticks with the song tick clip.startTick. That value becomes clipStartTick (:191) and is added again in songOffset (PianoRoll.tsx:347) and in the notation's first bar (StudioNotationView.tsx:83-85). Empty clip at bar > 1: origin = clip.startTick, so the next note is stored that many ticks late, and the unsized clip box stretches to include it (Timeline.tsx:650-664). The second case is more common than the finding suggests. For any clip with startTick > 0 whose first note isn't at clip tick 0, the origin becomes the first note's tick. Grid bar lines are drawn from x=0 as if that were a downbeat (PianoRoll.tsx:619-634), so the grid is misaligned with the real bars and the clip's leading rest can't be reached. Students will notice when notes land in the wrong bar and bar lines don't match the timeline. The recommendation (origin 0; trims already clamp events to >= 0, Timeline.tsx:2395-2398) is sound and folds into the -01 fix.
regressionRisks: If any legacy or imported data has negative event ticks, origin 0 would hide them, so keep a Math.min(0, floorToBar(minTick)) guard. The comment at PianoRollModal.tsx:87-89 shows someone added this to handle front trims, so check the trim, scissors split and recording paths (recordedClip.ts) to confirm they always produce >= 0 clip-relative ticks. Initial auto-scroll (initialScrollDone) may need to target the first note, since the view no longer starts on it. Notation bar numbers will change for existing clips. That is correct, but it is a visible change.

title: Keys pressed in the piano roll edit the timeline behind it: arrows move the clip, Cmd+C/V/D duplicate it, Backspace in the dock deletes it
evidence:
The global shortcuts are a window keydown listener with no editor or modal guard (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:38-409). PianoRoll handles only V/D/E, and Delete/Backspace when notes are selected (PianoRoll.tsx:1311-1342), and stops propagation only in the Delete case. The modal stops only Delete/Backspace (PianoRollModal.tsx:119-124). Double-clicking first selects the clip (Timeline.tsx:1520-1524), so selectedClipId is the clip being edited. Consequences:
- Left/Right arrows move the whole clip by one beat via `updateMidiClip(..., { startTick: newStart })` (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:313-345).
- Cmd+C copies the clip, Cmd+V pastes a copy at the playhead, Cmd+D duplicates it (:71-175).
- Cmd+A selects the track's first clip instead of all notes (:178-189).
- Escape also stops the transport and deselects the clip (:380-383).
- R starts recording; L toggles a project loop the editor loop overrides (:359-378).
- In the dock there is no Delete guard: with no notes selected, Backspace reaches `removeMidiClip(selectedClipTrackId, selectedClipId)` (:385-404), which is the clip being edited.
impact: Students naturally try the arrow keys to nudge notes and Cmd+C/V/D to copy notes. Instead they move or clone the clip out of sight behind the overlay, and the modal's ruler and playhead shift for no visible reason. In the dock, deleting a note clears the selection (PianoRoll.tsx:1338), so a second Delete removes the whole clip.
recommendation: Give the editor its own keymap. While focus is in the editor or editingClipId is set, the global hook should ignore everything except transport keys (Space). The editor should implement note-level keys: arrows nudge by the grid or transpose by a semitone (Shift for bar/octave); Cmd+A/C/V/D act on notes; Delete removes only notes; Escape clears the selection. Call stopPropagation for every key it handles.
verifierNote: The window keydown handler in useKeyboardShortcuts.ts has no editingClipId or editor guard; only an input/textarea check exists at :297-298. Arrows call updateMidiClip startTick (:313-345), Cmd+A selects the first clip (:178-189), Escape stops and deselects (:380-383), and Delete removes the selected clip (:385-404). PianoRoll's handleKeyDown (:1316-1344) calls stopPropagation only for Delete when notes are selected (:1333-1335), and the modal stops only Delete/Backspace (PianoRollModal.tsx:119-124). In the dock, a second Backspace therefore deletes the clip.
impactNote: useKeyboardShortcuts.ts is a window keydown listener whose only guard is input/textarea for non-Cmd keys (:296-300). It has no modal or editor guard. PianoRoll handles only V/D/E, plus Delete when notes are selected (PianoRoll.tsx:1311-1342). The modal only stops Delete/Backspace (PianoRollModal.tsx:119-124). Opening the editor selects the clip (Timeline.tsx:1524). So ArrowLeft/Right move the edited clip by a beat (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:313-345), and in the modal that shifts the ruler and playhead because timelineStartTick changes. Cmd+C/V/D copy, paste or duplicate the clip behind the overlay. Cmd+A selects a clip (:178-189). Escape also stops the transport and deselects (:380-383). In the dock, Backspace with no notes selected deletes the clip (:385-404). Students will very likely try arrows and Cmd+C/V to edit notes, and those edits happen out of sight. Undo recovers the damage, so it isn't critical, but high is justified.

Radix Dialog handles Escape itself, so the editor's Escape (clear selection) should call preventDefault to keep the first Escape from closing the modal, or the close behaviour must be deliberate. In the dock, the guard has to be focus-based (the PianoRoll tabIndex div, PianoRoll.tsx:1723), not editingClipId. title: Note edits made while playing aren't heard until playback is restarted
evidence: MIDI is scheduled once per Play. The effect at usePlaybackEngine.ts:642-744 (deps `[isReady, isPlaying]`) reads a store snapshot and builds one Tone.Part per clip (:672-682; MidiScheduler.ts:13-70). The loop handler re-schedules only audio clips and automation (:836-905), and nothing re-schedules when midiClips change. Yet the modal sets up an editor loop for exactly this edit-while-looping workflow (PianoRollModal.tsx:23-31).
impact: A student loops two bars, drags a wrong note to the right pitch, and keeps hearing the wrong note on every pass. Newly drawn notes stay silent until Stop and Play. This breaks the core edit-and-listen loop that BandLab, Soundtrap, Ableton and Logic all support, and makes the editor feel broken.
recommendation: While playing, watch the edited clip's events and rebuild only that clip's Part from the current transport position (or add and remove the changed events). Combined with pianoroll-04 this happens once per committed gesture.
verifierNote: MIDI is scheduled only in the `[isReady, isPlaying]` effect (usePlaybackEngine.ts:642-744), using a getState snapshot (:657-682). The loop handler (:836-905) reschedules only audio and automation. A grep finds no other scheduleSequence or reschedule path, and Tone.Part copies its events when the Part is created (MidiScheduler.ts:58-69).
impactNote: The MIDI scheduling effect has deps [isReady, isPlaying] (usePlaybackEngine.ts:643, :744) and reads a store snapshot once. MidiScheduler.scheduleSequence is called only there (:673), and nothing reschedules MIDI when tracks or midiClips change. The loop handler (:837 onward) re-schedules only audio and automation. Yet the modal sets up an editor loop specifically for edit-while-looping (PianoRollModal.tsx:23-31). A student who loops a phrase and fixes a note keeps hearing the old note, and newly drawn notes stay silent until Stop and Play. This breaks the core edit-and-listen workflow and makes the editor seem broken. The same applies to collaborators' remote MIDI edits during playback. High is justified.
regressionRisks: Rebuilding a Part mid-playback can leave stuck notes. Any sounding note whose event is removed or moved needs an explicit noteOff, and the old Part must be disposed without cutting releases. It can also double-trigger at the current transport tick and miss notes when rebuilding right at a loop boundary. Each clip needs its own rebuild (MidiScheduler currently only has cancelAll). Without the -04 commit-on-release change this would rebuild about 60 times/s during a drag, so do -04 first or throttle. Recording overdub and count-in paths share the scheduler and must not be cancelled.

title: Practice keyboard is MIDI-only; clickable keys play a different piano and are never recorded
evidence: ScaleKeyboard renders `<PianoKeyboard gaming ... hintNotes={litKeys} playingNotes={playedKeys} />` (ScaleKeyboard.tsx:286-293) without overriding `enableClick = true` / `useContextNotes = true` (PianoKeyboard.tsx:49-50). A click calls `playNote(note)` (77-105) from the app-wide PianoProvider (AppContext.tsx:58; PianoContext.tsx:21-56), which plays the lesson piano sampler at a fixed 0.3 s through '@/audio/pianoSampler', not through the student's track instrument. Takes come only from Web MIDI: useMidiInputRouting.ts:144 calls hwNoteOn, and useMidiRecording.ts:55 records the recordArmed track. A clicked key lights with the default classes `bg-zinc-300` / `bg-orange-700` (PianoKeyboard.tsx:208, 242) instead of the in-scale/off-scale colours. The copy says 'Play along on your MIDI keyboard' (PracticeTrackView.tsx:425-429), and the screen has no MIDI status, because this view replaces the TransportBar and its 'MIDI: Unavailable — use Chrome/Edge' indicator (TransportBar.tsx:840-876; DawApp.tsx:487-495).
impact: Students on iPads/Safari, or on Chromebooks without a MIDI keyboard, can't do the screen's one job (play over the track and record a take), and nothing tells them why. Because the keys look playable and make sound, 'Record take' appears broken: no take, and takeNotes stays 0. Black keys also flash orange, off-brand. This extends A11Y#2 (lessons are MIDI-only) to the Practice Track.
recommendation: Route on-screen key presses (pointer down/up) and a QWERTY note map into the DAW's hw note path (hwNoteOn/hwNoteOff plus recording), so they sound through the student's track and are captured in takes. Until then, pass enableClick={false} and useContextNotes={false}. Add a MIDI status chip in the practice header that points to the computer-keyboard fallback.
verifierNote: ScaleKeyboard.tsx:286-293 leaves enableClick and useContextNotes at their defaults (true), so a click calls PianoContext's playNote, which plays the 0.3 s lesson piano sampler (PianoContext.tsx:21-56). Takes come only from MidiRecorder, fed by the Web MIDI routing (useMidiInputRouting.ts:41, 144); there is no pointer or QWERTY path into it. The only explanation is the line 'Play along on your MIDI keyboard' (PracticeTrackView.tsx:425-429), and there is no MIDI status because the TransportBar is replaced on this screen. Routing pointer events into hwNoteOn/hwNoteOff needs pointerup, pointerleave and pointercancel handling (plus releasing on blur or unmount), or notes get stuck in recording and live synths. It must respect the recordArmed and monitoring tracks, and collab presence, if hw notes are broadcast. title: A running lesson carries over into unrelated projects (no boot path ends it)
evidence: quitTutorial is only called from the lesson UI (TutorialLayer.tsx:112, 135, 174). None of the boot branches clear activeTutorialId: `?project=`, `?template=`, `?demo=`, `?song=`, `?practiceGenre=`/`?practiceMode=`, `?collab=`, `?new=1` or the default restore (DawApp.tsx:131-428). resetSessionToEmpty doesn't touch it either (SessionSerializer.ts:649-678). Steps can then auto-complete against unrelated content. For example, House 'add-drums' passes on any project with a drum track (tutorials.ts:567), which can cascade into a false Completed badge.

Quitting while a 950 ms completion timer is pending is handled: the effect cleanup clears the timer when status or tutorial changes.

title: Suggestions ignore the key's mode: an A-minor project gets A-major progressions
evidence: The graph is written relative to the parent major key. prismSlice voices graph names from `parentRoot = rootMidi - getModeOffset(mode)` (prismSlice.ts:463-472) and stores mode-relative labels (`degreeKey: ionianToModeLabel(known, mode)`, 561/585). The suggestion engine does neither. extractGraphSeed ignores `_rootNote`/`_mode` (suggestionEngine.ts:164-169) and looks up those mode-relative degreeKeys (186-188) in the parent-major graph. degreeNameToChord ignores `_mode` (256-265; its comment says 'degreeMidi is relative to the mode root') and uses `rootMidi = (rootNote ?? 0) + 48` (318). SuggestionChordPill.tsx:31-33 already notes that 'the suggestion engine voices degrees from the mode tonic' and only patches the label. Example: in A Aeolian an empty chord lane makes getFirstChords pick '1 major', voiced A-C#-E, and the 'Most Common' walk is A maj, B min, C# min, D maj. An existing Am region carries degreeKey '1 minor', which is not a graph key, so its context is silently dropped. In D Dorian, a G-major region becomes '4 major', which collides with a real graph key and continues in D major.
impact: Affects any Suggest Chords in Dorian, Phrygian, Lydian, Mixolydian, Aeolian or Locrian, including the EDM lesson, which tells students to pick Aeolian (tutorials.ts:487-495). The suggestions contain C#, F# and G# in A minor, show in 'out of key' colours, and Commit writes them to the chord lane. Meanwhile the Prism palette in the same session correctly offers Am, Dm, Em, F, G and C.
recommendation: Do what prismSlice does: convert seeds with modeToIonianLabel(degreeKey, mode) before graph lookups, voice chords from rootMidi - getModeOffset(mode), and store degreeKey = ionianToModeLabel(graphDegree, mode). The helpers already exist in naming.ts:17-112. Better still, add one shared helper for this key conversion and use it in both slices, with tests for Aeolian and Dorian.
verifierNote: generateSuggestions uses `rootMidi = (rootNote ?? 0) + 48` (suggestionEngine.ts:318), and degreeNameToChord ignores `_mode` (256-265). prismSlice instead voices chords from `parentRoot = rootMidi - getModeOffset(mode)` (prismSlice.ts:463-472). extractGraphSeed ignores `_mode` and feeds mode-relative degreeKeys into the parent-major graph (164-188). In A Aeolian the suggestions come out in A major, and SuggestionChordPill.tsx:31-33 already notes the mismatch.
impactNote: Confirmed. generateSuggestions sets rootMidi = rootNote + 48 (suggestionEngine.ts:318). degreeNameToChord ignores _mode (256-265), so '1 major' in A Aeolian is voiced A-C#-E. prismSlice, by contrast, voices from parentRoot = rootMidi - getModeOffset(mode) (prismSlice.ts:463-472). extractGraphSeed ignores _rootNote and _mode (164-169) and feeds the mode-relative degreeKeys that prismSlice stores (ionianToModeLabel at 561/585) straight into the parent-major graph, so 'minor' seeds miss and fall back to getFirstChords. The getChordColor call at suggestionEngine.ts:358 passes mode, and remapChordForMode (colorSystem.ts:48-) then reads the graph name as mode-relative, so the colours come out as out-of-key. SuggestionChordPill.tsx:31-33 shows the authors already knew about the tonic-voicing problem and only patched the label. A minor key is a very common student choice, and the preview plays audibly wrong notes (C#, F#, G# in A minor), so a user notices immediately. It is still context-menu-only (Timeline.tsx:1858-1862), and the EDM lesson only asks for Aeolian (tutorials.ts:487-495) without using Suggest Chords, so the 'including the EDM lesson' impact is overstated. The remaining claims hold.
regressionRisks: Commit writes degreeKey: chord.degree (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:177). After the fix this becomes mode-relative, which is the convention chordRegionNotation.ts:14-24 documents. Already-saved regions committed under the old behaviour in non-Ionian projects have parent-major-style degreeKeys and could be misread as seeds. That is minor, and reconcile and relabel logic may already overwrite them. Keep the graph lookups in Ionian space and convert only at the edges. Converting twice (seed -> Ionian -> mode) can double-shift if prismSlice's helpers are reused carelessly. A shared helper with Aeolian and Dorian tests reduces the risk. No collab, undo or tutorial-anchor impact.

title: Prism 'Create' silently deletes the selected track's clips and the whole chord lane
evidence:
generateToTracks (prismSlice.ts:1568-1623) works in four steps once the worker replies:
- `currentState.clearMidiClips(trackId)` (1599) sets `midiClips: []` for the whole track (tracksSlice.ts:763-770).
- It adds one clip at `startTick: 0, durationTicks: 7680` (1601-1608).
- It replaces the entire chord lane with `set({ chordRegions: deriveChordRegions(...) })` (1611-1618), bypassing reconcile and chordRecordMode.
- The Create button (PrismStudio.tsx:206-223) shows no pending state, confirmation or result.

The worker itself:
- A new module Worker is constructed on every click (1579-1582); it imports the `@prism/engine` barrel, about 8.5k lines.
- It has only `onmessage`: no `onerror` and no timeout.
- `terminate()` runs only on success (1621).

With no key chosen it silently generates in C (`rootMidi = (rootNote ?? 0) + 48`, 1577).

- Lessons: DawApp.tsx:206-214. The step 'Click G on the Circle of Fifths' checks `s.rootNote === 7` (tutorials.ts:141-150).

title: Suggestion-modal hotkeys also fire the global DAW shortcuts (R records, Space plays, arrows move clips)

- The modal adds a bubble-phase listener only while open (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:341-405). It calls `e.preventDefault()` but never stopPropagation or stopImmediatePropagation.

- 'R': the modal re-rolls (377-381), as its own title 'Re-roll (R)' promises (497). The global `state.record()` also runs (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:359-364), setting `{ isRecording: true, isPlaying: true }` (transportSlice.ts:169-175). Loading a project auto-arms the first MIDI track (SessionSerializer.ts:601-606, 744-752).
- Space: preview, plus the global play()/pause() (350-357).
- ArrowLeft/ArrowRight: previous/next suggestion, plus `updateMidiClip` nudging the selected clip ±480 ticks (313-345). The right-click that opens the modal does not clear the clip selection (Timeline.tsx:1812-1826).
- Digits 1–4: jump to a suggestion, plus `setActiveTool` (305-309, TOOL_KEYS 15-20).
- Escape: close, plus `stop()` (380-383).

- Browsing suggestions with the arrow keys moves the student's selected clip one beat per press.
- Space starts song playback on top of the preview.
- A keyboard user who tabs to Cancel and presses Enter commits instead.

- Listen in the capture phase and call stopPropagation(), the pattern PopOutOverlay.tsx:31-58 already documents.
- Or use Radix Dialog and have useKeyboardShortcuts bail when `e.defaultPrevented` is set or a dialog-open flag is on.

- insertChordRegion (1926, 1937)

- markAsMelody filters out every match (2095).

title: Every edit rebuilds every part and re-engraves the whole score, blocking paint
evidence:
Chain of work after one edit:
- The scoreParts memo is keyed on the whole `tracks` array (ScoreView.tsx:75-90), so buildScoreParts rebuilds every part.
- StaffView re-engraves in a useLayoutEffect keyed on `parts` (StaffView.tsx:1533-1572). render() clears the host (809), then builds and formats every measure of every part twice: once for minimum widths (812-814 via measureMinWidth 558-577) and again to draw (1163-1176). It calls getComputedTextLength() for each rest in the middle of drawing (1203-1205), forcing a layout each time.
- onLayout then triggers setLayout (1574-1589), which re-runs tieCandidates (a tracks/clips/events `find` per drawn note, useScoreEditing.tsx:978-1001) and `marks` (filters all notes and re-parses all articulations for each mark, 1135-1155).
- Each edit makes 3+ store writes (392-400). For each one, the undo watcher calls watched(), which JSON.stringifies and structuredClones the project before its identity check (undoMiddleware.ts:194-206, 222-224).
- In collab, any remote track change, even a fader move, rebuilds every track object (yjsToZustand.ts:126-144), so every peer on SCORE re-engraves.
impact: Edit latency scales with the size of the whole score, not the edit. Moving one note in a 6-part, 64-bar song builds and formats about 384 part-measures twice, synchronously, on every arrow-key press. In class collab, other people's mixer moves freeze your score.
recommendation: Cache each track's NotationScore by midiClips reference, and make yjsToZustand reuse unchanged track and clip objects. Cache buildMeasure and minimum width per (part, measure-content hash). Draw each system into its own group and redraw only dirty systems. Engrave visible pages first and the rest at idle. Batch an edit into one store set. Replace the tieCandidates and marks scans with Maps built once per layout.
verifierNote: The scoreParts memo is keyed on the whole tracks array (ScoreView.tsx:75-86). The engrave useLayoutEffect depends on parts (StaffView.tsx:1533-1572), render() clears the host and computes measureMinWidth for every measure before drawing (809-814), and it calls getComputedTextLength while drawing (1203-1204). handleChange calls watched(), which JSON.stringifies the project and structuredClones the marks before the identity check (undoMiddleware.ts:194-206, 222-230). yjsToZustand rebuilds every track object on any remote change (yjsToZustand.ts:130-144).
impactNote: The chain is real. scoreParts is memoized on the whole `tracks` array (ScoreView.tsx:75-86), and buildScoreParts maps every track and clip (scoreParts.ts:90-115). StaffView's useLayoutEffect re-runs render() for all parts whenever `parts` changes (StaffView.tsx:1533-1572), synchronously before paint, and every writeEdit changes tracks. In collab, applyTracksFromDoc rebuilds every Track object on any remote track event (src/daw/collab/yjsToZustand.ts:126-144), so a peer dragging a fader triggers a full re-engrave on every peer viewing Score, possibly dozens of times a second. That's the most serious part. The undo-watcher point is weaker. It only subscribes to tracks, chordRegions and the MARK_KEYS (undoMiddleware.ts:257-260), so it doesn't run per frame, and stringify plus clone of MIDI data is cheap next to VexFlow. The ~384-measures-twice figure is an estimate, not a measurement. Keeping high because arrow-key nudges and collab fader moves will visibly freeze a multi-part score on a Chromebook. The recommended fix is large.
regressionRisks: A per-track NotationScore cache keyed by midiClips reference only works if yjsToZustand and every slice action preserve references for unchanged clips. Otherwise you get stale notation, which is worse than slow notation. Reusing Track objects in yjsToZustand has to keep merging the per-user mute/solo/arm/monitoring fields correctly, and could change downstream audio-graph diffing that currently expects fresh objects. Partial per-system redraws risk mismatched layout coordinates for the overlay, hit-testing and print/PDF output. Batching an edit into one store set changes undo granularity and the collab diff (which is fine, but check smartUndo).

title: Returning to the editor overwrites the live session with an older autosave, losing lead-sheet/score layout, recent edits and undo
evidence: When the URL has no boot link, DawApp.tsx:425-428 always calls restoreLocalSessionIfPresent(). title: Undo tracking adds another set of store listeners on every editor visit, and each one serialises the whole project on every edit

title: Autosave never runs during playback, writes on UI-only changes, and never flushes on close or navigation
evidence: useAutosave.ts:19-25 calls useStore.subscribe(() => { clearTimeout; setTimeout(write, 1500) }), which fires on every store change, including setPosition every 33 ms during playback (useTransport.ts:80-90). Selection, zoom and panel toggles also schedule a full serializeSession() + JSON.stringify + localStorage.setItem on the main thread (localSession.ts:14-21). Quota errors only reach console.warn. The cleanup (useAutosave.ts:27-29) clears the pending write instead of flushing it. Nothing in src/daw, layouts or studio-projects handles pagehide, visibilitychange or beforeunload (grep).

verifierNote: useAutosave.ts:19-25 resets a 1.5 s timer on every store change, and useTransport.ts:80-90 writes position about every 33 ms during playback, so nothing is written while playing. title: Global shortcuts ignore focus and context: ⌘Z/⌘A/⌘C/⌘V hijacked in text fields, Space/Delete/Escape act behind open dialogs, browser zoom overridden
evidence:
Every ⌘ shortcut runs before the text-field check (296-301):
- ⌘Z always calls preventDefault and runs smartUndo/smartRedo (60-68).
- ⌘A always calls preventDefault (178-189).
- ⌘C/⌘V call preventDefault whenever a clip is selected or the clip clipboard is non-empty (71-131).
- ⌘=/⌘−/⌘0 replace browser zoom (243-261).
- ⌘N (222-240) is reserved by Chrome for a new window, so it never fires.

The text-field check covers only HTMLInputElement and HTMLTextAreaElement, not buttons, selects, or anything inside a Radix dialog or menu:
- Space (350-357) toggles playback and blocks the focused button from activating.
- Delete/Backspace (385-404) deletes the selected clip behind an open dialog.
- Escape (380-383) stops playback or recording whenever a dialog or menu is dismissed.

There is no e.repeat guard. R, M, L and 1–4 are single-character shortcuts that can't be turned off or remapped.
impact: Pressing ⌘Z to fix a typo in the project name, BPM, a track name or collab chat undoes the student's last musical edit instead. ⌘A/⌘C/⌘V don't work on text while a clip is selected. Keyboard users can't press dialog buttons with Space. Closing Settings with Escape stops the take. Low-vision users lose ⌘+/− page zoom. This fails WCAG 2.1.4 Character Key Shortcuts (Level A), which the A11Y audit doesn't cover.

impactNote: ⌘Z, ⌘A, ⌘C/⌘V, ⌘= / ⌘−/⌘0 and ⌘N are all handled before the text-field check (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:46-292 vs 296-301). ⌘Z always calls preventDefault and runs smartUndo (60-68), so fixing a typo in the project name or BPM field undoes a musical edit instead. ⌘A always calls preventDefault (178-189), which breaks select-all in every text field. ⌘+/− page zoom is overridden (243-261), which matters for low-vision students on 1366x768. Chrome never delivers Ctrl/⌘+N to pages, so that binding is dead. The Space, Escape and Delete claims are lower impact: Space-to-play over a focused button is common DAW behaviour, though Delete behind an open dialog is a real hazard. Users may rely on ⌘+/- for timeline zoom, so provide an alternative such as ⌥+wheel and update any help or tutorial copy that mentions it. title: Autosave never fires while playing, recording or collaborating, never flushes, and ignores synth edits
evidence:
useAutosave.ts:19-25 subscribes to the whole store and restarts a 1500 ms timer on every set(). Several sources write continuously:
- During playback, useTransport.ts:72-96 calls setPosition about every 33 ms.
- While recording, usePlaybackEngine.ts:1009-1022 writes setLiveAudioRecording every 66 ms (copying the whole peaks array each time).
- Live-input chord detection writes setAudioActiveNotes, pushLiveChord and setGlobalTuningCents (useAudioChordDetection.ts:171-186).
- In collab, presence writes _setRemoteUsers on every awareness change (CollabProvider.tsx:375-386).
The timer cannot elapse until all of these stop. Nothing in src/daw flushes on pagehide, visibilitychange or beforeunload; the comment at useAutosave.ts:5-7 only assumes a tab close 'usually persists'. Oracle Synth edits live in useSynthStore (synthTrackState.ts:11-18) and are only captured when serializeSession happens to run (SessionSerializer.ts:67-68); nothing subscribes to useSynthStore for autosave.
impact: A student who loops playback while editing in the piano roll (the normal workflow), records several takes, or works in a collab room can go many minutes without a crash-recovery copy. A crash or accidental refresh loses all of it. Tweaking a synth patch and then refreshing loses the patch.
recommendation: Trigger autosave from a document version counter, not from every store write. Debounce by 1 s with a maxWait of about 5 s so it still fires during playback. Flush on pagehide, on visibilitychange to hidden, and on editor unmount. Bump the document version when useSynthStore patches change. Keep high-rate transient state (position, peaks, meters, presence) out of the persisted store, or at least out of the autosave trigger.
verifierNote: useAutosave restarts a 1500 ms timer on every store set (useAutosave.ts:19-25). There is no pagehide, visibilitychange or beforeunload flush anywhere in src/daw (the only visibilitychange listener is in AudioEngine), and nothing subscribes to useSynthStore for autosave.
impactNote: useAutosave.ts:19-25 restarts a 1500 ms timer on every store set. useTransport.ts:72-96 calls setPosition about every 33 ms while playing, and usePlaybackEngine.ts:1009-1022 writes setLiveAudioRecording every 66 ms while recording, so the timer never elapses during loop playback, which is the normal piano-roll workflow. src/daw has no pagehide or beforeunload flush; the only visibilitychange listener is in AudioEngine.ts:97 for audio resume. regressionRisks: A maxWait flush during playback runs serializeSession plus JSON.stringify on the main thread, which could cause an audible glitch on a 4-core Chromebook if the project is large. Prefer requestIdleCallback, or flush only on bar boundaries or pauses. Removing position and peaks from the main store affects many subscribers (Timeline playhead, recording waveform), so a document-version counter is the safer change. title: Undo auto-capture serializes the whole project to JSON on every edit frame and leaks subscriptions on each editor visit
evidence: watched() (undoMiddleware.ts:194-206) runs JSON.stringify({tracks, chordRegions, marks: readMarks()}), and readMarks (62-79) structuredClones 13 arrays. handleChange calls watched() before the cheap identity check (222-229), so the full stringify runs on every tracks, chordRegions or mark change. When the 300 ms debounce fires it stringifies again and JSON.parses the previous copy (235-247). initUndoTracking registers 15 subscriptions (257-264) and returns no unsubscribe function. DawApp.tsx:97-99 calls it in a mount effect with no cleanup or guard, so each visit to the editor adds another full set (the StrictMode double effect adds two in dev). Fader and knob drags write tracks on every pointer move (ChannelStrip.tsx:185, onValueChange -> updateTrack), and clip and note drags do the same. The header comment 'High-frequency updates (position, volume drags) are excluded' (undoMiddleware.ts:15) is not true for volume.
impact: Each fader, knob or clip-drag frame stringifies the entire project (all MIDI events, effects and automation) once per accumulated registration. On a Chromebook a mid-size project costs several ms per stringify, so drags stutter, and the cost grows each time the student leaves and returns to the editor. Memory holds up to 50 full parsed snapshots plus the last JSON string.
recommendation: Short term: make initUndoTracking idempotent (a module flag, or return and call the unsubscribe), compute the JSON only inside the debounced callback, and drop the structuredClone in readMarks. Long term: replace snapshot diffing with patch/command undo (immer patches or per-action inverse operations), grouped per gesture from pointerdown to pointerup, so a drag costs nothing until it ends.
verifierNote: handleChange calls watched() before the identity check (undoMiddleware.ts:222-229), and watched() runs a full JSON.stringify plus a structuredClone through readMarks (194-206, 62-79). initUndoTracking registers 15 subscriptions and returns no unsubscribe (257-264), and DawApp.tsx:97-99 calls it in a mount effect with no cleanup, so subscriptions pile up on each editor visit. title: Track roles become undefined after a refresh, which breaks chord analysis

title: The key lock survives a reset, so the next song or practice track opens without its key
