title: Arpeggiator runs on setInterval and discards the scheduled time, so it never locks to the transport
evidence: SynthEngine.noteOn/noteOff drop `time` when the arp is on (SynthEngine.ts:390-404). Arpeggiator.noteOn calls rebuildAndRestart, which calls restartTimer() and then tick() immediately (Arpeggiator.ts:156-163, 188-194). restartTimer is 'setInterval(() => this.tick(), ms)' with ms derived from bpm (223-234). tick calls outputNoteOff/outputNoteOn with no time (236-251), and those are wired to rawNoteOn/rawNoteOff (SynthEngine.ts:268-272).
impact:
- In sequenced playback the MIDI scheduler delivers note-on 100-150 ms early (Tone lookAhead 0.1 s, updateInterval 0.05 s). The first arp step therefore sounds immediately, about a 1/16 note early at 120 BPM.
- Every later step inherits that offset plus setInterval jitter from the busy main thread (the DAW re-renders about 30 times a second during playback).
- Each new held note restarts the timer, so a 3-note chord retriggers the first step three times, each through the steal path (synth-engine-02), which clicks.
- Background tabs throttle the interval to 1 s or more while Tone keeps other tracks playing.
- In export, ticks fire on wall-clock time during Tone's pre-render loop (synth-engine-01).
recommendation:
- Drive the arp from the transport: compute step times from the note-on `time` and the Tone transport (a Tone.Loop or a lookahead scheduler on context time), and call rawNoteOn/rawNoteOff with an explicit `time`.
- Coalesce notes that arrive within a few ms before restarting.
- Quantize the first step to the next grid division.
verifierNote: SynthEngine.ts:391-392 and 399-400 drop `time` when the arp is on. Arpeggiator.ts:188-194 restarts the setInterval and ticks immediately on every noteOn, and restartTimer is a wall-clock setInterval (228-234). tick calls the outputs with no time (236-251), which are wired to rawNoteOn/rawNoteOff without a time (SynthEngine.ts:269-272).
impactNote:
The scheduled time is dropped:
- When the arp is on, SynthEngine.noteOn/noteOff discard `time` (SynthEngine.ts:390-404).
- Arpeggiator.noteOn calls rebuildAndRestart, which runs restartTimer() and then tick() immediately (Arpeggiator.ts:156-163, 188-194).
- restartTimer is a plain setInterval (223-234).
- The arp callbacks call rawNoteOn/rawNoteOff with no time (SynthEngine.ts:268-272).

In piano-roll playback the first step therefore sounds 100-150 ms early (Tone lookAhead), every later step is phase-locked to that early start, and each note of a chord restarts the timer and retriggers step 1.

This affects the factory presets that ship with the arp on: SEQUENCE, CHORDS and STAB (factoryPresets.ts:1343, 1467, 1565). An arp running visibly off the drum grid is obvious to students, and it gets worse under main-thread load and in background tabs. In export, ticks run on wall-clock time while Tone is still pre-computing the schedule, so arps don't export correctly (ties to 01).

The recommendation (a transport/context-time lookahead scheduler, coalescing chord arrivals, quantizing the first step) is correct.
regressionRisks:
- A transport-driven arp must still work for live keyboard playing with the transport stopped: it needs a free-running context-time scheduler, not just a Tone.Loop tied to the transport.
- It must stop and clear on transport stop, loop wrap and allNotesOff, or it will leave stuck notes.
- The chord-aware rebuild (setChordContext) must stay in-place.
- Changing first-step quantization changes the live 'feel' that existing users are used to.
- No save-format change: arp params stay the same.

title: Oracle LFOs and arps ignore the project tempo after reload, on unselected tracks, and in export
evidence: applySynthStateToEngine takes the tempo from the patch: 'engine.setBPM(s.bpm)' (synthTrackState.ts:241). `bpm` is saved with every patch (SYNTH_STATE_KEYS, lines 49 and 73) and defaults to 120 in the synth store (globalSlice.ts:30). Nothing writes the project BPM into it. The only path from DAW tempo to an engine is the mounted panel's effect 'engine.setBPM(dawBpm)' (useStoreBridge.ts:73-79). SynthEngine.setBPM sets the LFO bar lengths and the arp rate (SynthEngine.ts:505-510).
impact:
- After a refresh, project open or export, Oracle LFOs (4-bar shapes) and arps in a 90 BPM project run at 120 BPM until that track's panel is opened.
- Changing the project tempo only retimes the selected Oracle track, so the others drift.
- The stale 120 is saved again with the patch, so the problem returns on every reload.
- Exports use the stale tempo.
recommendation:
- Treat tempo as host state, not patch state: pass the project BPM into applySynthStateToEngine and ignore the patch's bpm.
- Have usePlaybackEngine push BPM changes to every Oracle adapter, as it already does for track volume and pan.
- Drop `bpm` from SynthTrackState, or overwrite it when the patch is captured.
verifierNote: applySynthStateToEngine calls engine.setBPM(s.bpm) from the patch (synthTrackState.ts:241). The only path from DAW tempo to an engine is the mounted bridge (useStoreBridge.ts:73-79), and usePlaybackEngine has no setBPM. synthTrackStateFromPreset seeds the project bpm only at creation (99-111), so later tempo changes and panel-created patches (store default 120, globalSlice.ts:30) go stale.
impactNote:
applySynthStateToEngine calls engine.setBPM(s.bpm) from the patch (synthTrackState.ts:241). The synth store's bpm defaults to 120 (globalSlice.ts:30), and nothing writes the DAW tempo into it. useStoreBridge only pushes dawBpm directly to the mounted engine (useStoreBridge.ts:73-79), so captureSynthState keeps saving the stale value. Only demo seeding passes a real tempo (demoSynthPresets.ts:28 via synthTrackStateFromPreset). usePlaybackEngine never calls setBPM on adapters.

What users hear:
- In any project not at 120 BPM, after a reload or project open, or for unselected tracks after a tempo change, Oracle arps run at the wrong tempo. SEQUENCE, CHORDS and STAB have the arp on.
- Tempo-synced LFOs (PAD and WOBBLE have LFO routes, factoryPresets.ts:333-342) run at the wrong rate.
- Exports also use the wrong tempo.

A wobble or arp off the beat is immediately audible. The recommendation (tempo as host state, pushed to all Oracle adapters) is correct.
regressionRisks:
- Keep the `bpm` field in SynthTrackState for saved-project compatibility (normalizeSynthTrackState and old saves), and ignore it on apply rather than deleting it.
- Pushing BPM to every adapter on each tempo change triggers a full LFO buffer re-render per LFO per track (see 10). Debounce tempo-input changes or fix 10 first, or dragging the BPM field will stall.
- Each re-render restarts LFO phase, so LFOs jump audibly on a tempo change.
- No collab or undo impact.

title: Pack wavetables aren't registered on reload, so tracks silently fall back to a basic waveform
evidence:
Pack table URLs are registered only by loadOraclePacks (packLoader.ts:29-43). Its only caller is the panel hook, fire-and-forget (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:25).

The same effect's initial sync calls ensureWavetables right away (305-310), before the manifest fetch resolves. ensureFramesLoaded skips names with no registered URL ('unknown table — caller falls back', wavetableImport.ts:194-196), and nothing re-runs it when the registry fills; the engine never uses subscribeTableRegistry (180-183).

applySynthStateToEngine's 'void engine.ensureWavetables(...)' (synthTrackState.ts:225-228) has the same problem on load and export. Oscillator.applyWavetablePosition then falls back to setOscType(this.params.waveform) (Oscillator.ts:299-313) without telling the UI.
impact: After a refresh or project open, an Oracle track whose patch uses a pack wavetable plays a basic saw or square instead. Pack presets use S2/* tables; 'S2/Default Shapes' alone is referenced 37 times. The wrong sound persists even after the user opens the track's panel, until they touch an oscillator control or remount the panel. Exports can render the fallback. No loading or error state tells the student why the sound changed.
recommendation:
- Register the pack manifest once at DAW/engine startup and await it before applying patches.
- Have SynthEngine subscribe to the table registry and call ensureWavetables for its current tables whenever new names register.
- Expose a per-oscillator 'loading' or 'fallback' flag the UI can show.
verifierNote: loadOraclePacks is called only from useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:25, fire-and-forget, and ensureWavetables runs in the same effect (305-310) before the manifest fetch resolves. ensureFramesLoaded skips unregistered names (wavetableImport.ts:196), and nothing outside OscillatorModule's picker list subscribes to the registry. Oscillator.applyWavetablePosition then silently falls back to setOscType (Oscillator.ts:299-313). The pack has 24 preset files with 37 references to 'S2/Default Shapes'.
impactNote:
loadOraclePacks has a single caller, the panel hook, and is fire-and-forget (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:25). It registers URLs only after the manifest fetch resolves (packLoader.ts:29-43).

The same effect calls ensureWavetables synchronously in its initial sync (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:305-310). ensureFramesLoaded skips unregistered names (wavetableImport.ts:194-196). SynthEngine never subscribes to the registry; only OscillatorModule does, for UI listing.

applySynthStateToEngine (synthTrackState.ts:225-228) runs at init and in export before any panel exists, so pack tables are never resolved there.

What users hear:
- After a reload, a track built from a pack preset plays a basic fallback waveform. That is a clearly different sound with no indication why.
- Other tracks recover once their panel is mounted, because the registry is filled by then.
- The first panel opened in the session stays wrong until it is remounted or an oscillator control is touched.
- Exports in a session where no panel was opened render the fallback.

'The project sounds different after I reopen it' is exactly the reload-correctness problem the user asked about. The fix is small and sound: load the manifest once at DAW start and await it before applying patches, plus a registry subscription in the engine.
regressionRisks:
- Awaiting the manifest before applying patches delays first sound on project open. Apply the patch immediately and refresh wavetables when they register, rather than blocking init.
- With no pack installed (404), the code must still resolve quickly.
- A registry subscription per engine must be unsubscribed in dispose, or it will leak listeners and engines.
- Large wavetable WAV fetches at startup would cost bandwidth on school networks, so fetch only the tables the project uses.
- No save-format impact.

title: LFO edits re-render the whole 4-bar buffer at audio rate, 36-40 times per engine init or panel mount
evidence:
How a render happens:
- LFO.setBPM, setBarNodes and setBarSmooth each destroy the source and rebuild the whole buffer (LFO.ts:51-81).
- createSource renders 4 bars at ctx.sampleRate, (240/bpm) s each (87-104).
- buildBar allocates a new Float32Array per bar and, for every sample, rescans the node list from index 0 ('let nodeIdx = 0; while ...', LFOWaveformBuilder.ts:21, 35-42). The smoothing filter adds two more passes (59-70).
- buildBuffer allocates a fresh AudioBuffer (89-96).
- LFOs are already running from init (SynthEngine.ts:194-200), so every set* call re-renders.

What calls it:
- applySynthStateToEngine makes 16 setLFONodes + 16 setLFOSmooth calls plus setBPM, which hits 4 LFOs (synthTrackState.ts:241-247).
- The panel's initial sync repeats the same (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:323-329), and useStoreBridge then calls setBPM again (73-79).
- The SMOOTH knob calls setLFOBarSmooth on every pointer move (LFOArea.tsx:169-173, 314-323; Knob.tsx:136-147).
impact:
At 120 BPM and 48 kHz, one render is 384,000 samples and about 3 MB of allocations. Each engine init (project open, refresh, track creation, export) and each panel mount does 36-40 renders: about 14 M samples and about 110 MB of short-lived garbage per Oracle track.

Panel mounts happen when the student selects an Oracle track, returns to the dock's CONTROLS tab (ChannelStrip.tsx:320) or opens the pop-out. The pop-out keeps a second bridge on the same engine (synthTrackState.ts:159-161), which doubles every render.

Slower tempos scale the cost up. Students on Chromebooks see load-time and track-selection stalls plus GC pauses, and dragging SMOOTH stutters.
recommendation:
- Render only the bar that changed into a persistent buffer, or keep per-bar buffers.
- Render at a low LFO sample rate (createBuffer allows sample rates down to 3 kHz; the source resamples).
- Walk the node index forward instead of rescanning per sample.
- Batch the 32 per-bar calls into one setLFO(index, bars, smooths).
- Skip updates where nothing changed, and throttle SMOOTH to rAF or pointer-up.
verifierNote: LFO.setBPM, setBarNodes and setBarSmooth each destroy and rebuild the full 4-bar buffer at ctx.sampleRate (LFO.ts:51-81, 87-104), allocating a new Float32Array per bar plus an AudioBuffer (LFOWaveformBuilder buildBar and buildBuffer). applySynthStateToEngine makes 32 bar calls plus setBPM across 4 LFOs (synthTrackState.ts:241-247). The panel's initial sync repeats this (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:323-329), and the bridge calls setBPM again (useStoreBridge.ts:78), giving 36-40 renders of about 384k samples each at 120 BPM and 48 kHz.
impactNote:
How the re-renders happen:
- Every setBPM, setBarNodes or setBarSmooth on a running LFO destroys its source and rebuilds the full 4-bar buffer (LFO.ts:51-81, 87-108).
- buildBuffer allocates an AudioBuffer at ctx.sampleRate, and buildBar allocates a Float32Array per bar and rescans the node list from index 0 for every sample (LFOWaveformBuilder.ts:21-42, 89-96).
- applySynthStateToEngine makes 32 per-bar calls plus setBPM, which hits all 4 LFOs (synthTrackState.ts:241-247). That is about 36 full renders per engine init.
- Panel mount repeats them (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:323-329), and useStoreBridge then calls setBPM again (73-79).

The cost: at 120 BPM and 48 kHz, each render is 384k samples and about 3 MB of allocations, so roughly 110 MB of short-lived garbage and tens to hundreds of ms of main-thread work per Oracle track on a Chromebook. That hits project open (multiplied by the number of Oracle tracks) and every time the student selects an Oracle track, which is exactly the lag the user wants removed.

Each rebuild also calls source.start() fresh, so LFO phase resets on every edit and drifts off the transport. That is an extra audible side effect.

All the fixes listed are sound and low risk: batch per-LFO updates, skip unchanged values, use a low LFO sample rate, walk nodes incrementally, and throttle the SMOOTH knob.
regressionRisks:
- Rendering at a low sample rate (for example 3 kHz) softens very sharp steps or square LFO edges a little, so compare stepped shapes.
- Keeping persistent per-bar buffers means the source must be swapped without a phase jump; schedule the new source at the old source's phase offset.
- Skipping unchanged values needs deep equality on node arrays, or edits may be missed.
- If tempo changes start reaching every adapter (fix 07), this cost multiplies, so land 10 before or with 07.
- No save-format, collab or tutorial impact.

title: Synth-only edits never trigger the crash-recovery autosave, so a refresh silently loses sound design
evidence: useAutosave.ts:19 `const unsub = useStore.subscribe(() => {` subscribes to the MAIN store only. Every synth setter writes the separate store created at store/index.ts:23 (`export const useSynthStore = create<SynthStore>()(`), which nothing in the autosave path observes. The live patch reaches localStorage only incidentally, when some later main-store change runs writeLocalSession, then serializeSession, then trackSettings, then `getTrackSynthState(t.id)` (SessionSerializer.ts:67-68). The full-screen synth makes zero main-store writes while a student designs and auditions: DawSynthLayout handleNoteOn only calls `engine.noteOn(...)` plus a local `setActiveNotes` (DawSynthLayout.tsx ~80-86). There is no pagehide or beforeunload flush anywhere in src/daw (grep). localSession.ts:62-65 decides 'unsaved' from `canUndo()`, which synth edits never touch.
impact: A student builds a patch in the pop-out, or tweaks knobs in the strip, then refreshes, closes the tab, or the tab crashes. Crash recovery restores the project with the previous patch and the work is gone, with no warning. Starting a lesson, template or demo from the dashboard (which clears the autosave) doesn't treat synth-only work as unsaved, so it isn't protected either.
recommendation: Also subscribe the autosave to useSynthStore's patch keys (debounced, same 1.5 s), and add a pagehide/visibilitychange flush of writeLocalSession. Count synth edits in unsavedStudioSession (a patch revision counter). Structural fix: store per-track patches in the main store so autosave, undo and collab cover them automatically (see proposal).
verifierNote: Confirmed: useAutosave.ts:19 subscribes only to useStore, and no code anywhere subscribes the autosave to useSynthStore (the only useSynthStore.subscribe callers are useSyncStoreToEngine and the dirty watcher). There is no pagehide or beforeunload flush in src/daw; the only visibilitychange listener is AudioEngine.ts:97. DawSynthLayout handleNoteOn (~80-86) only calls engine.noteOn and local state. The patch reaches localStorage only through SessionSerializer.ts:67-68 when some unrelated main-store change happens. I lowered it to high: this is the crash-recovery slot only, so explicit cloud saves still capture the live patch, and any later main-store write (transport, selection, edits) flushes it incidentally.
impactNote: The mechanism is real. useAutosave.ts:19 subscribes only to useStore. Synth setters write useSynthStore. Nothing in src/daw listens for pagehide or beforeunload; the only visibilitychange listener is in AudioEngine.ts:97, and it does not save. The pop-out open state is local React state (TrackControlsPanel.tsx:69), so closing it doesn't trigger a save either. However, 'critical' and 'silently loses' overstate it. The main store changes very often (transportSlice.ts:201 setPosition during playback, track selection, tab changes, etc.). Any later DAW interaction runs writeLocalSession, which serializes getTrackSynthState(activeTrackId) = captureSynthState() (synthTrackState.ts:196). So the loss window is narrow: synth-only edits followed directly by a refresh, close or crash, with no other DAW interaction. The more serious part is unsavedStudioSession (localSession.ts:62-65). When live tracks exist and canUndo() is false, it returns null, so starting a lesson, template or demo discards synth-only sound design without any prompt. Students who design sounds and then audition through the synth keyboard can hit this. High, not critical.
regressionRisks: Subscribe only to patch keys (the SYNTH_STATE_KEYS list). The store also holds pitchBend, modWheel, activeNotes and isDirty, which change on every gesture and would cause constant serialize work during play. serializeSession is a whole-session serialization, so keep the 1.5 s debounce and don't run it per knob tick. A pagehide flush must be synchronous: localStorage is fine, an async cloud save is not. A synth revision counter in unsavedStudioSession will show 'unsaved work' prompts more often, including after the follow-project-key mirror (useStoreBridge.ts:96). Exclude machine-driven writes. Moving patches into the main store is the right long-term fix, but it would fill undo history with every knob move unless coalesced per gesture. It would also flood collab diffs, and it needs a migration that keeps settings.oracleSynth readable. Tutorial synthCheck reads useSynthStore (useTutorialDetection.ts:53), so the store must keep mirroring the live patch.

title: applySynthStateToEngine never applies REVERB, so loaded projects and every export play Oracle tracks dry
evidence: synthTrackState.ts:257-263 calls setDriveParams, setChorusParams, setPhaserParams, setDelayParams, setCompressorParams, setRouting and setArpParams. There is no `engine.setReverbParams(s.fx.reverb)`, although the panel's own initial sync has it (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:335). Effects start bypassed (FXProcessor.ts:17 `protected enabled = false`). applySynthStateToEngine is the ONLY patch application for: every Oracle track at instrument init after any load or refresh (usePlaybackEngine.ts:516-521), and every Oracle track in the offline render (renderProject.ts:256-259). 17 of the 82 SERUM pack presets ship with reverb enabled.
impact: After a refresh or opening a project, an Oracle track whose patch uses reverb plays dry until its synth panel is opened, then reverb suddenly appears. Bounced or exported audio never contains Oracle reverb, even for the track being edited, so the export doesn't match what the student hears.
recommendation: Add setReverbParams, and make useSyncStoreToEngine's initial sync call applySynthStateToEngine(engine, captureSynthState()) so only one apply list exists. Add a test that spies on every public SynthEngine setter and asserts each is called by the apply function.

Normalize fx first.

title: Pack wavetables register only when a synth panel mounts, so 81 of 82 SERUM presets play basic waveforms after reload and in exports
evidence: loadOraclePacks is called from exactly one place: useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:25 (`void loadOraclePacks();`), which runs only when a panel mounts with an engine. On load, applySynthStateToEngine fires `void engine.ensureWavetables([...])` (synthTrackState.ts:225-228). That reaches ensureFramesLoaded, which skips unregistered names: wavetableImport.ts:196 `if (!url) continue; // unknown table — caller falls back to basic waveform`. Nothing retries for engines that already fell back, even though subscribeTableRegistry exists (wavetableImport.ts:180). packLoader.ts:30-31 sets `loadAttempted = true` before the fetch succeeds, so one network blip disables packs for the whole session. packLoader.ts:45-54 fires 82 preset fetches at once through Promise.all. Data check: 81 of 82 pack presets reference pack wavetables ('S2/...').
impact: Students mostly pick pack presets (82 of the 93 factory and pack menu items). After any reload or cloud open, those tracks sound like plain saw or square waves until the student opens each track's synth. Exports do the same. Opening one track's panel does not fix the other tracks.

Have each engine subscribe to the table registry and re-run ensureWavetables on registration. Set loadAttempted only on success, with retry/backoff. title: Oracle LFO/arp tempo is frozen per patch: synth-store bpm is never updated, and only the open engine follows the DAW tempo

That clearly drifts against the drums and the grid. The EDM wobble lesson depends on this.
regressionRisks: Ignoring patch bpm changes how existing non-120 projects sound in exports, which is the intended fix. Demos set bpm through synthTrackStateFromPreset(preset, bundle.bpm) (demoSynthPresets.ts:28), so drop or ignore that field consistently, but keep it in the type so old saves still parse. Pushing bpm to every Oracle engine on each tempo change rebuilds 4 LFO buffers per engine (see 09). Debounce it, because a tempo-knob drag would otherwise rebuild buffers on every frame and restart LFO phase. Tempo automation, if supported, needs the same path. The synth-store bpm subscription (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:175) can currently override dawBpm when a demo-seeded patch is restored, so remove it along with the patch bpm.

title: Unopened Oracle tracks have no patch and inherit whatever the singleton store last held; the store and cache are never reset
evidence: restoreCachedSynthState returns false and leaves the store untouched when nothing is cached (synthTrackState.ts:181-186). useStoreBridge.ts:47-49 calls it, then the initial sync (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:302-342) pushes the leftover patch into the new track's engine. This contradicts the docstring 'or defaults are used for first visit' (useStoreBridge.ts:20-22). New tracks are never seeded: addTrack (tracksSlice.ts:564-608) and loadProjectTemplate (tracksSlice.ts:933-979) create Oracle tracks without a patch. The templates hold 8 unseeded Oracle tracks named Bass, Pad and Synth (projectTemplates.ts:40,74,86,114,120,126,154,166), although BASS, PAD and LEAD factory presets exist. Only demos are seeded (DawApp.tsx:180-182). resetSessionToEmpty (SessionSerializer.ts:649-678) and both deserializers touch only useStore, and there is no stateCache.clear() or delete anywhere. An unopened track saves no patch: getTrackSynthState returns undefined (synthTrackState.ts:193-198), so `oracleSynth` is dropped (SessionSerializer.ts:67-68), and before it is opened the engine plays its constructor default (usePlaybackEngine.ts:517-521). The lesson check is tutorials.ts:467 `synthCheck: (sy) => sy.presetName === 'WOBBLE'`, and it auto-advances when already true (useTutorialDetection.ts:45-48).
impact: A new or template track plays INITIALIZE from the timeline, then changes to a copy of the previously opened patch (named e.g. 'WOBBLE *') the moment it's selected. After a reload, its sound depends on which track was opened first. Patches leak across projects, templates and lessons within one SPA session. Re-running 'EDM — Design the drop' silently skips the 'load WOBBLE' step. The cache keeps every patch ever opened.
recommendation: Seed every Oracle track at creation: INITIALIZE by default, and role-matched factory presets for templates via synthTrackStateFromPreset. Reset the store to INITIALIZE when no cache entry exists. Add resetSynthSession(), which clears the cache, resets the store and clears the active track, and call it from resetSessionToEmpty and both deserializers. Prune cache ids that are absent from the new project.
verifierNote: When nothing is cached, restoreCachedSynthState returns false without touching the store (synthTrackState.ts:181-186), so the bridge (useStoreBridge.ts:47-49) and the initial sync push the leftover patch into the new engine. The cache is only ever set and never cleared or deleted (synthTrackState.ts:142-209). resetSessionToEmpty (SessionSerializer.ts:649-678) resets only useStore. The templates have 8 unseeded oracle-synth tracks (projectTemplates.ts:42-168). The tutorial check `sy.presetName === 'WOBBLE'` (tutorials.ts:467) auto-advances when it is already true on arrival (useTutorialDetection evalSynth with celebrate=false).
impactNote: restoreCachedSynthState returns false and leaves the store untouched when there's no cache entry (synthTrackState.ts:181-186). useStoreBridge.ts:47-53 then marks the track active, and the initial sync pushes the leftover patch into the new engine. Nothing in src clears stateCache: the only Map writes are set() at :177/:208, and there is no clear() or delete. setTrackSynthState is called only from the deserializers (SessionSerializer.ts:556, :721) and the demo path. The tutorial step 'load-wobble' (tutorials.ts:467) auto-advances on arrival if the store still holds presetName 'WOBBLE' (useTutorialDetection.ts:45-48), so re-running the lesson in one SPA session skips that step. Sound changes on selection, sound leaking between projects, and a broken lesson step are all user-visible.
regressionRisks: Seeding INITIALIZE (or role presets) onto existing saved projects whose Oracle tracks were never opened changes their sound if the SynthEngine constructor default differs from the INITIALIZE preset. Seed only at creation time, not on load, or verify the two match. Role-matched template presets change what the templates sound like, which is a product decision. resetSynthSession must run BEFORE the deserializers seed the cache (deserializeCloudProject calls setTrackSynthState inside its map at SessionSerializer.ts:556; DawApp.tsx:180 calls resetSessionToEmpty before deserializeCloudProject). Otherwise it wipes the freshly seeded patches. Clearing activeTrackId while a bridge is mounted (mountedBridges>0) can desync the bridge counter. Resetting the store fires every synth subscription, which means a full LFO rebuild on the live engine (see 09). Tutorial lessons that rely on a fresh store should still pass, but re-check the EDM steps that follow load-wobble.

title: Every patch application rebuilds full-sample-rate LFO buffers ~36-40 times (track select, tab return, pop-out, load, preset switch)
evidence: LFO.setBPM, setBarNodes and setBarSmooth each destroy and recreate the source (LFO.ts:51-82), and all 4 LFOs always run (SynthEngine.ts:198 `lfo.start()`). Each rebuild calls buildBuffer at ctx.sampleRate over 4 bars (LFOWaveformBuilder.ts:83-107). At 120 BPM and 48 kHz that is 384,000 samples (a 1.5 MB AudioBuffer plus four 384 KB temporary arrays), with a per-sample node scan (35-55; pack bars have up to 60 nodes) and two IIR passes when smooth > 0 (59-70). applySynthStateToEngine runs setBPM (4 rebuilds, line 241) plus 16 setLFONodes and 16 setLFOSmooth (242-247), so 36 rebuilds per Oracle track on load or render. A panel mount runs the initial sync (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:323-329, 36 rebuilds) plus the dawBpm effect (useStoreBridge.ts:76-79, 4 rebuilds). Mounts happen on every Oracle track selection (TrackControlsPanel.tsx:79 `key={track.id}`), on every return to the CONTROLS tab (ChannelStrip.tsx:320), and again when the pop-out opens (OracleSynthView.tsx:22). The pop-out's second bridge also duplicates all ~45 subscriptions, so every later edit hits the engine twice. A preset switch clones all bars (presetSlice.ts:65), so all 16 per-bar subscriptions (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:180-196) fire. The SMOOTH knob commits on every pointer move (Knob.tsx:147), causing one full rebuild and an LFO phase restart per move.
impact: Expect a main-thread stall and roughly 60-120 MB of short-lived buffer allocation each time a student clicks onto an Oracle track or returns to CONTROLS. Turning SMOOTH is janky and makes the modulation stutter. Loading a project with several Oracle tracks freezes the UI, and a busy main thread can delay Tone.js scheduling during playback. Timings were not measured; confirm with a Performance trace on a Chromebook.
recommendation: Add engine.applyPatch(patch) or LFO.setState({bars, smooths, bpm}) that rebuilds each LFO once (4 rebuilds instead of 36-40), or coalesce rebuilds with a dirty flag and queueMicrotask. Build LFO buffers at a control rate (createBuffer with a 2-4 kHz sampleRate is about 12-24x less work). Commit knob changes at most once per animation frame for LFO params. Ref-count engine subscriptions per engine rather than per bridge.
verifierNote: Each LFO.setBPM, setBarNodes or setBarSmooth destroys and recreates the source (LFO.ts:51-82). buildBuffer builds 4 bars at ctx.sampleRate (LFOWaveformBuilder.ts:83-107), and buildBar re-scans nodes from index 0 on every sample (lines 35-41), so cost is O(samples x nodes). applySynthStateToEngine and the initial sync each do 4 + 16 + 16 = 36 rebuilds, plus 4 from the dawBpm effect. Panels remount per track (TrackControlsPanel key=track.id), and the pop-out adds a second bridge (OracleSynthView.tsx:22). The bar subscriptions have no equality function, so a preset clone fires all 16 of them. The timings are estimates, but the rebuild count and allocation size are accurate.
impactNote: Every LFO setter destroys and rebuilds the source (LFO.ts:51-82). applySynthStateToEngine calls setBPM (4 rebuilds) plus 16 setLFONodes and 16 setLFOSmooth (synthTrackState.ts:241-247), which is 36 full rebuilds. The panel initial sync (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:323-329) does the same, plus 4 more from the dawBpm effect (useStoreBridge.ts:76-79). Panels remount on every track selection (TrackControlsPanel.tsx:79 key=track.id) and every return to CONTROLS (ChannelStrip.tsx:320). The pop-out adds a second useStoreBridge (OracleSynthView.tsx:22). The per-sample segment search in LFOWaveformBuilder.buildBar restarts at nodeIdx = 0 for every sample, so the cost is O(samples × nodes). At 48 kHz and 120 BPM that is 384k samples × up to 60 pack nodes per rebuild, times 36. This is on the main thread, and preset switches (16 bar subscriptions fire, :180-196) and SMOOTH knob drags (Knob.tsx onChange per pointer move) hit the same path. A clear stall on track select or project load is very likely on a 4-core Chromebook, even though it wasn't profiled. That's the exact lag the user asked about.
regressionRisks: Coalescing via a dirty flag plus queueMicrotask/rAF delays parameter application by up to one frame, which is fine for LFOs. Make sure the offline render path, which applies and then schedules synchronously, flushes before scheduling MIDI. Low-rate buffers: Chrome's createBuffer accepts sampleRate ≥3000 Hz, and resampling smooths sharp gate edges slightly, so use 4-8 kHz for gate-heavy presets. Ref-counting subscriptions per engine must still handle the inline strip and the pop-out unmounting in either order (acquireSynthBridge/releaseSynthBridge semantics, synthTrackState.ts:162-173). Today each rebuild restarts LFO phase. Reducing rebuilds changes phase-reset behavior, which is better for users, but tests asserting a phase restart could break. Throttling SMOOTH knob commits must still record the final value so isDirty and the autosave see it.

title: Saved synth patches replay without reverb and at a stale tempo after reload and in exports
evidence: applySynthStateToEngine (synthTrackState.ts:218-264) pushes drive, chorus, phaser, delay and compressor (257-261) but never calls engine.setReverbParams. The live initial sync does (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:335). Effects start disabled (FXProcessor.ts:17 `protected enabled = false`). This helper is the only patch path at instrument init after a project or autosave load (usePlaybackEngine.ts:513-521) and in offline export (renderProject.ts:255-259). Tempo: it calls engine.setBPM(s.bpm) (synthTrackState.ts:241) with the synth store's bpm. That value defaults to 120 (globalSlice.ts:30) and is never written by the DAW: the store's setBPM (globalSlice.ts:46) has no callers. DAW tempo reaches an engine only through useStoreBridge.ts:74-79, i.e. only while that track's synth panel is mounted.
impact: After a refresh (crash recovery), opening a cloud project, or returning to the editor, a synth track whose patch uses reverb plays dry. Tempo-synced LFOs and the arp (e.g. the tutorial's WOBBLE) run at the stale 120 BPM until the student happens to open that track's synth panel, at which point the sound jumps. Exports are always dry and at the stale tempo. Tempo changes made while a synth's panel is closed never reach it.
recommendation: Generate one applyPatch(engine, patch) from a single parameter table and use it for the initial sync, project load and export, including reverb. Add a test that every SynthTrackState key is applied. Make tempo engine-owned: push the DAW bpm to every OracleSynthAdapter on init and on every change (usePlaybackEngine and renderProject). Drop `bpm` from the patch, or override it at apply time.
verifierNote: applySynthStateToEngine (synthTrackState.ts:257-261) sets drive/chorus/phaser/delay/compressor but never calls setReverbParams; the only other callers are useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:247 and :335. FXProcessor.ts:17 starts with enabled=false. It sets engine.setBPM(s.bpm) at :241, and nothing ever writes the synth store's bpm: the only setBPM callers are the engine/LFO/arp methods, and DAW tempo reaches an engine only through useStoreBridge.ts:74-79. Both the instrument-init path (usePlaybackEngine.ts:513-521) and export (renderProject.ts:255-259) go through this helper.
impactNote: Verified. applySynthStateToEngine (src/daw/oracle-synth/synthTrackState.ts:256-261) applies drive, chorus, phaser, delay and compressor but never calls setReverbParams. The only setReverbParams callers are useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:247 and :335, both of which need the panel to be mounted. FXProcessor.ts:17 starts every effect disabled, so on reload a patch with reverb plays dry. Both load paths use this helper: usePlaybackEngine.ts:516-521 and renderProject.ts:255-258. Tempo: synthTrackState.ts:241 calls setBPM(s.bpm), and globalSlice.ts:30 sets that to 120. The store's setBPM has no callers in src, so the DAW tempo reaches the engine only through useStoreBridge.ts:74-79 while the panel is mounted. LFO.ts:89 (barDuration = 240/bpm) and Arpeggiator.ts:225 both read that value, so synced LFOs and the arp run at 120 BPM in any project not at 120, and exports always do. Students will notice: reverb that vanishes after a refresh, and a wobble that runs at the wrong speed in exports. That is a concrete reload and export bug, so high is justified.
regressionRisks: Applying reverb at load turns on a convolver/reverb graph for every synth track whose patch has it enabled. That costs CPU on 4-core Chromebooks and makes offline renders slower, so measure with several synth tracks. Existing projects will start to sound different (correctly), which teachers may notice. When pushing the DAW bpm, the bridge's effect and the initial sync both call setBPM, so order them so the stale 120 never wins. Do not remove `bpm` from SynthTrackState without a normalize/migration default, because old saved patches and presets contain it. Renderers must use the project's bpm (with tempo automation, if any), not the store's current bpm.

title: Wavetable-position/blend modulation never runs in the DAW (50 of 82 bundled pack presets use it)
evidence: The matrix can't drive these targets ('wtPos/blend are absent: they are not AudioParams', ModulationMatrix.ts:210). The only driver is the UI hook useWtPosModulation, and the only caller is the standalone SynthLayout.tsx:48. Neither DAW host calls it: DawSynthLayout.tsx imports at 12-30, OracleSynthInline.tsx at 1-15, and useStoreBridge.ts:71 mounts only useSyncStoreToEngine. 50 of the 82 presets in public/daw-assets/oracle-packs/serum2/presets contain `"param": "wtPos"` routes, e.g. 'PD - EMOTIONS.json':844-852 (LFO 1 → osc1 wtPos). ModulationSlot's OSC_PARAM_OPTIONS (70-74) has no wtPos or blend, so effectiveParam (116-121) falls back to 'level' and the slot displays OSC 1 → LEVEL for these routes.
impact: Most pack presets lose their defining wavetable sweep: in the editor, during playback with the panel closed, and in exports. The matrix then labels the route LEVEL, so a student who edits it changes something else entirely.
recommendation: Move control-rate WT-position/blend modulation into SynthEngine, using an engine-owned timer or AudioWorklet that reads LFO, macro and mod-wheel values; run it in offline render as well. Delete the UI hook. Add WT POS and BLEND to the matrix targets. Delete the standalone SynthLayout so the two layouts can't drift again.
verifierNote: useWtPosModulation is called only in SynthLayout.tsx:48, which is imported only by the standalone oracle-synth/App.tsx. DawSynthLayout and OracleSynthInline never call it. ModulationMatrix.ts:210 confirms the matrix has no wtPos/blend targets. A grep finds `"param": "wtPos"` in 50 of the 82 pack presets, and OSC_PARAM_OPTIONS (ModulationSlot.tsx:70-74) has no wtPos, so effectiveParam falls back to 'level'.
impactNote: Verified. The only caller of useWtPosModulation is SynthLayout.tsx:48, which is used only by oracle-synth/App.tsx, and nothing in src imports App.tsx, so the code is dead in the DAW. DawSynthLayout.tsx:9-30 imports no such hook. ModulationMatrix.ts:210 explicitly excludes wtPos/blend. I counted 50 of the 82 pack presets with wtPos routes, and the EMOTIONS example at :844-852 checks out. ModulationSlot.tsx:70-74 has no wtPos option, and effectiveParam (116-121) falls back to 'level', so the slot shows LEVEL for these routes. If a student touches the param dropdown, the route is rewritten to a real LEVEL target. The missing sweep is subtle for students who never heard the original, but the mislabeled route is something they will see, and most of the pack is affected, including exports. High is reasonable.
regressionRisks: An engine-owned timer per SynthEngine adds main-thread work for every synth track. A rAF loop is throttled in background tabs, so use the audio clock (or a worklet) and run it only while routes exist. Offline render needs a deterministic, sample-time-based driver: a setTimeout poller will not work in OfflineAudioContext, so effort is closer to M-L. Reading LFO values from AnalyserNodes is approximate, and per-voice sources still won't work. Adding WT POS/BLEND to OSC_PARAM_OPTIONS changes what existing routes display; that is correct, but snapshot tests may need updates. Deleting the standalone SynthLayout/App is safe only if no route or dev page uses them (none was found in src).

title: The LFO node editor maps the pointer wrongly in the scaled pop-out
evidence: The editor's size comes from ResizeObserver contentRect (LFONodeEditor.tsx:53-58), which ignores CSS transforms, and that size sets drawW/drawH (69-70). fromSvg subtracts getBoundingClientRect() (80-82), which is post-transform, then divides by the untransformed drawW/drawH (84-85). The pop-out renders the whole layout under `transform: translate(..) scale(scale)` (DawSynthLayout.tsx:123-127), with scale = min(w/1440, h/932) (useContainerScale.ts:28).
impact: On a 1440×900 laptop the pop-out scale is about 0.75-0.8. Dragged nodes drift away from the cursor, and click-to-add can't place a node in roughly the last fifth of a bar or the bottom fifth of the range: the node lands short. On large monitors (scale above 1) nodes overshoot. The dock has no transform and works, so the bug shows only in the full-screen editor that students use for detailed shaping.
recommendation: Convert using the rendered rect: x = (clientX - rect.left) * (width / rect.width), and the same for y; or use svg.getScreenCTM().inverse(). Add a unit test with a scaled container. Dropping the transform-scaled canvas (synth-ui-08) removes this class of bug entirely.
verifierNote: The size comes from ResizeObserver contentRect (LFONodeEditor.tsx:53-58), which ignores ancestor transforms. fromSvg subtracts getBoundingClientRect (80-82), which is post-transform, then divides by the untransformed drawW/drawH (84-85). DawSynthLayout.tsx:123-127 applies scale(scale). On a ~820px viewport, (820-24-40)/932 ≈ 0.81, so the mismatch is real.
impactNote: Verified. LFONodeEditor.tsx:53-58 takes the size from ResizeObserver contentRect, which is the untransformed layout size, and computes drawW/drawH from it (69-70). fromSvg (80-85) subtracts the post-transform getBoundingClientRect origin, then divides screen-space pixels by the untransformed drawW/drawH, and PAD is also subtracted unscaled. The pop-out applies scale() at DawSynthLayout.tsx:123-127 with scale = min(w/1440, h/932) (useContainerScale.ts:28). At a typical scale of 0.64-0.78, a node lands at roughly 64-78% of the cursor position and cannot reach the right or bottom edge. The full-screen editor is where students do detailed LFO drawing, and the mismatch is obvious the moment they drag, so high is justified.
regressionRisks: Low. Using rect.width/height or getScreenCTM().inverse() is self-correcting at scale 1, so the dock is unaffected. Check that the curve-drag path (curveDragStartY, which uses a raw clientY delta) is scaled the same way, or curve bending will feel too fast or slow in the pop-out. Grid snap and the hover/hit-test radius should use the same conversion.

title: The preset workflow loses student work: same-name saves become unreachable, and INIT or a preset switch wipes edits with no confirm or undo
evidence: SAVE pre-fills the current preset name (PresetSelector.tsx:72-76) and saves it upper-cased (86-92). loadPreset searches factory presets first, then pack, then user (presetSlice.ts:189-208). Factory names are upper-case ('PAD', 'BASS', 'LEAD', factoryPresets.ts:217, 369, 473). So load PAD → tweak → SAVE → SAVE creates a user 'PAD' that the USER list can never load: clicking it loads the factory PAD. savePreset silently overwrites any user preset with the same name (presetSlice.ts:210-218). INIT (PresetSelector.tsx:148-154), styled identically to SAVE (PresetSelector.module.css:43-58), and any preset pick (78-84) replace the patch immediately, even when isDirty. The synth store has no undo (store/index.ts:23-42) and isn't on the DAW undo stack. User presets live only in localStorage (presetSlice.ts:16-31).
impact: The default save flow produces a preset the student can never load again. One mis-click on INIT or a preset name destroys a patch for good. Presets don't follow students across school devices.
recommendation: Key presets by id and source. On a clash with a factory or pack name, auto-suffix (e.g. 'PAD (MINE)') or warn. Confirm, or offer an undo toast, before INIT or loading over a dirty patch. Add undo to useSynthStore (temporal middleware), or route synth edits into the DAW's undo stack. Store user presets in the student's account.
verifierNote: loadPreset checks FACTORY_PRESETS first (presetSlice.ts:189-193), and factory names are upper-case ('PAD' at factoryPresets.ts:217). SAVE pre-fills presetName (PresetSelector.tsx:72-76) and upper-cases it (86-92), so a user 'PAD' can never be loaded. savePreset filters out same-name entries silently (presetSlice.ts:210-218). INIT is wired directly to initPreset (PresetSelector.tsx:148-154) with no dirty check. User presets are stored only in localStorage (presetSlice.ts:16-31).
impactNote: Verified. PresetSelector.tsx:72-76 pre-fills the save name with presetName, and :86-92 upper-cases it. loadPreset (presetSlice.ts:189-208) checks FACTORY_PRESETS first by name, so a user preset named 'PAD', 'BASS' or 'LEAD' can never load, and the default save flow creates exactly that. savePreset (210-218) silently overwrites a same-named user preset. INIT (PresetSelector.tsx:148-154) calls initPreset directly with no isDirty check, sits next to SAVE in the same actionButton style, and the synth store has no undo. One mis-click loses a patch. The track's last-saved project copy is a partial safety net, but autosave (see synth-ui-04) will soon overwrite it with the INIT state. Cross-device preset storage is a valid but separate, larger feature request and shouldn't drive the severity.
regressionRisks: Changing preset identity from name to id+source needs a localStorage migration ('oracle-synth-presets' entries have no id). The project-saved presetName and the tutorial check (tutorials.ts synthCheck presetName === 'WOBBLE') compare by name, so keep presetName semantics. Suffixing names like 'PAD (MINE)' must not collide with the upper-casing. A confirm dialog must not block the tutorial's 'load WOBBLE' step when the patch is dirty; prefer an undo toast. Temporal/undo middleware on useSynthStore must exclude high-frequency UI fields (modWheel, pitchBend, activeNotes) or it will flood memory. Routing synth edits into the DAW undo stack risks interleaving with collab ops. Account-backed presets need backend work and an offline fallback.

title: QWERTY playing in the pop-out changes focused dropdowns and toggles the metronome and loop
evidence: The synth key handler skips only input and textarea targets (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:51-55) and never calls preventDefault. Dropdown is a native <select> (Dropdown.tsx:16-25) that keeps focus after a choice, so the browser's type-to-select changes it on letter keys. With the filter type focused, 'a' → ALL PASS and 'h' → HIGH PASS; with a mod SOURCE focused, 'e' → ENV AMP; with the Key Lock key focused, 'd' → D♭/D (FilterModule.tsx:17-26, ModulationSlot.tsx:18-37, KeyScaleBar.tsx:14-17). The DAW's global handler also acts on KeyM (toggleMetronome) and KeyL (toggleLoop) (src/daw/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:366-378); in the synth map those keys are B3 and D5 (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:26, 37). Cleanup (81-84) never releases held notes. Callers pass inline callbacks (DawSynthLayout.tsx:102-111), so the listeners are re-bound on every layout render. The synth map puts 'a' at C4, while KeyboardView puts 'a' at C3 and does release held notes on cleanup (KeyboardView.tsx:33-45, 161-169).
impact: While a student performs, the patch changes without notice (filter type, mod source, scale-lock key), and the metronome or loop toggles. Closing the pop-out mid-note leaves a stuck note. Musical typing maps to different octaves on different instruments.
recommendation: Use one shared musical-typing hook across instruments. Ignore keys whose target is a select, button, [role=slider] or contentEditable, or blur dropdowns after a change. Consume note keys (preventDefault and stopPropagation), and suspend the DAW's single-letter shortcuts while an instrument keyboard is active. Release all notes on cleanup, blur and visibilitychange. Use one octave map with Z/X for octave shift.
verifierNote: The synth handler skips only input and textarea targets (oracle-synth/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:51-55), never calls preventDefault, and its cleanup (81-84) doesn't release held notes. Dropdown is a native <select> (Dropdown.tsx:16-25). The DAW handler only skips input/textarea (hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:296-301) and toggles the metronome and loop on KeyM/KeyL (366-378), while the synth maps m→59 and l→74. KeyboardView maps a→48 and releases held notes on cleanup (KeyboardView.tsx:34-45, 161-168), whereas the synth maps a→60.
impactNote: Verified. The synth handler (oracle-synth/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:51-55) only skips input and textarea targets and never calls preventDefault or stopPropagation. Dropdown.tsx:16-25 is a native <select>, which keeps focus after a mouse choice in Chrome, so letter keys type-select options (for example 'a' → ALL PASS on a focused filter type). The DAW global handler (src/daw/hooks/useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:295-300 guards only input/textarea) is also bound on window. KeyM toggles the metronome and KeyL the loop (366-378), and those are B3 ('m', line 37) and D5 ('l', line 26) in the synth map. Space also toggles play. Any student playing a melody with QWERTY in the pop-out will hear the metronome or loop flip. Cleanup (81-84) does not release held notes, and callbacks are inline (DawSynthLayout.tsx:102-111), so the listeners rebind on every activeNotes change. That rebind is what can strand notes mid-press.
regressionRisks: Suppressing DAW single-letter shortcuts while the synth keyboard is active must not break Space (play/pause) or Escape, which students expect everywhere. Decide explicitly, and scope suppression to when the pop-out or instrument has focus. Blurring selects after change hurts keyboard accessibility; prefer ignoring keys when the target is a select or button. Unifying the octave map ('a' = C3 vs C4) changes what existing users muscle-remember, and any tutorial text that names keys must be checked. Releasing notes on cleanup must also clear activeNotes and DAW hwActiveNotes, so chord detection (useLiveChordColor) doesn't keep stale notes.

title: The pop-out is a fixed 1440×932 canvas scaled to fit, so its 8-10px labels render at about 5-7px

title: The scissors tool compares clip-relative MIDI note ticks with an absolute split tick
evidence: MIDI events are clip-relative (comments at Timeline.tsx:314-315 and 655-658; playback schedules clip.events at clip.startTick, usePlaybackEngine.ts:672-682). The scissors branch compares them with the absolute split tick: `clipEnd = … events.reduce(…, midiClip.startTick)` (1613-1618), `leftEvents = events.filter(ev => ev.startTick < splitTick)` / `rightEvents … >= splitTick` (1621-1626). The right clip keeps its events un-rebased at `startTick: splitTick` (1638-1644). Zoom-to-fit repeats the same `reduce(…, clip.startTick)` mistake (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:274-282).
impact: For an unsized clip that doesn't start at bar 1 (most clips), clipEnd collapses to clip.startTick, so every cut silently does nothing. For sized clips, all notes stay in the left half and still play past its new right edge (the scheduler ignores durationTicks), while the right half is empty or plays its notes shifted late. Students see a cut that doesn't cut. Zoom-to-fit can also leave content off-screen.
recommendation: Add midiClipLength(clip) and splitMidiClip(clip, absTick) helpers. Compute rel = absTick - clip.startTick; the left clip keeps events with e.startTick < rel (trimming the duration of notes that straddle the cut); the right clip gets events with e.startTick >= rel, shifted by -rel; split ccEvents the same way. Use the helpers in the scissors tool, a MIDI 'Split at playhead', zoom-to-fit and computeProjectLengthTicks. Unit-test clips that start at non-zero ticks.

The scissors branch seeds the reduce with midiClip.startTick (1613-1618) and filters on ev.startTick < splitTick, an absolute tick (1621-1626). For an unsized clip that starts after its own content length (any clip not near bar 1), clipEnd = startTick, so the guard at 1619 returns and the cut silently does nothing. For sized clips, all events usually land in the left half and the right half (1638-1644) gets no rebasing. computeProjectLengthTicks (310-330) does this correctly, which confirms the scissors code is wrong. Otherwise Score and Lead Sheet notation may change unexpectedly. ccEvents must be split and rebased the same way, or the sustain state at the cut is lost. Consider inserting a pedal-off or pedal-on at the boundary. Selection state (selectedNotes) refers to the old clip id, so clear it. title: Every redraw rescans raw audio samples, and almost any edit triggers a full redraw
evidence: draw() calls computePeaks(buffer, clipWidth/2, offset, end) for every visible audio clip (Timeline.tsx:944-983). computePeaks scans every sample of the clip's played window and caches nothing (AudioBufferStore.ts:101-140). Redraws are triggered by: the draw callback, which is memoised on the whole `tracks` array (Timeline.tsx:1339); the redraw effect (1342-1366), which also fires on every zoom or scrollLeft change; every wheel event, which writes scroll or zoom to the store (2536-2566); every vertical scroll frame (1369-1388); live recording peaks, which arrive every 66 ms as a fresh array copy (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1010-1022); every TrackHeader volume step (TrackHeader.tsx:497); and every automation-drag mousemove (AutomationLaneEditor.tsx:237-245). Each such `tracks` replacement also reaches 28 hooks and components that subscribe to the whole array, and the undo watcher JSON.stringifies the whole project before its identity check (undoMiddleware.ts:194-206, 222-223). draw also calls getComputedStyle on every pass (Timeline.tsx:520), and draws are never coalesced into one per frame.
impact: A 3-minute 48 kHz clip is about 8.6 million samples scanned on the main thread per redraw. With a backing track plus a vocal, every wheel tick, fader step, FX-knob turn or automation drag costs tens of milliseconds, which shows up as jank while scrolling and zooming. While recording, about 15 full redraws a second compete with audio scheduling. Low-end Chromebooks are hit hardest.
recommendation: Compute a min/max peak pyramid once per AudioBuffer (in setAudioBuffer or a worker, keyed by buffer identity) and pick the right resolution at draw time. Feed the renderer from a narrow geometry selector (clip start, length, events reference, colour, offset, fades) with custom equality, so mixer, FX and automation edits don't repaint the arrangement. Coalesce all redraws through one requestAnimationFrame dirty flag. Split the canvas into layers: static grid and rulers, clips, overlays. Cache CSS token values and refresh them only on theme change. In undoMiddleware, run the identity check before serialising.

The redraw effect depends on tracks, zoom and scrollLeft (1342-1366). The fader writes tracks on every step (TrackHeader.tsx:497), automation drags write on every mousemove (AutomationLaneEditor.tsx:237-245), and live peaks are copied every 66 ms (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1009-1022). getComputedStyle runs on every draw (Timeline.tsx:520). The undo watcher JSON.stringifies tracks before its identity check (undoMiddleware.ts:194-206, 222-223).

The redraw effect (1342-1366) fires on every tracks, zoom or scrollLeft change. The wheel handler writes scroll or zoom to the store on every event (2536-2559), the TrackHeader slider writes tracks on each step (TrackHeader.tsx:497), automation drag writes on each mousemove (AutomationLaneEditor.tsx:237-245), and recording pushes a fresh peaks array every 66 ms (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1009-1022). undoMiddleware.watched() JSON.stringifies tracks, chordRegions and structuredClone'd marks before the identity check (undoMiddleware.ts:194-206, 222-223), so every fader step serialises the whole project. getComputedStyle runs on every draw (Timeline.tsx:520). A backing track plus a vocal means millions of float reads per wheel tick, which is noticeable jank on a Chromebook. High is justified. Note that the peak cache and moving the undo identity check first are each small changes that capture most of the gain. The full L-sized layering can come later.

title: Clip moves, trims and the note marquee show no visual feedback while the transport is playing
evidence: Drag previews are held only in refs (dragTickRef, dragEndTickRef, dragTrackRef) and appear only when draw() runs. The move handlers call it only `if (!state.isPlaying)` (Timeline.tsx:2171-2173 move, 2183 left trim, 2193 right trim; the marquee at 2123 and 2470). `position` isn't a redraw dependency (1342-1366), and nothing redraws per frame during playback. handleWindowMouseMove ignores dragRef entirely (2465-2501), so a clip drag also freezes whenever the pointer leaves the canvas.
impact: The most common student workflow is to loop four bars, leave it playing, and nudge or trim clips. While it plays, the clip stays frozen under the cursor and then jumps on release. It feels broken and leads to misplaced edits.

title: The pedal layer is realtime-only, so exports bounce guitar/bass/vocal tracks raw
evidence:
renderProject.ts:33-37 documents that Guitar/Bass/Vocal-FX tracks bounce DRY because 'replicating that offline needs the chain params applied to an offline adapter plus remote NAM model loading'. The pedal layer can't be rendered offline as built:
- WahPedal drives its filter from requestAnimationFrame (WahPedal.ts:149-178), which can't run inside an OfflineAudioContext render.
- PitchCorrectionNode's module-loaded flag is module-global rather than per context (PitchCorrectionNode.ts:97-114), so a second context would skip addModule and `new AudioWorkletNode` would throw.
- NamWorkletNode.init resumes the context and calls addModule per instance (NamWorkletNode.ts:19-26).
- Turning a NAM model id into a loaded model happens in GuitarBassView effects (498-547), not in the chain.
impact: Students hear amped guitar and tuned vocals in the editor, but the exported file contains raw DI and untuned voice. This is the most audible gap between the editor and the export, and it hits exactly the tracks students record themselves.
recommendation: Make processors context-agnostic. Accept BaseAudioContext, register worklets per context with a WeakMap from context to Promise, and remove rAF control loops (see -09). Give GuitarPedalChain a static async build(ctx, descriptors, modelCache) that both the live adapter and renderProject use, preloading NAM models from a module-level cache. Until then, warn in the export dialog as is already done for SoundFont tracks.

However, this is a documented, deliberate limitation, and the finding's own recommendation is already implemented: ExportAudioDialog.tsx:152-167 counts these tracks and warns 'N guitar/bass/vocal tracks bounce dry (without amp/pedal FX)'. impactNote: The gap is real: renderProject.ts:33-37 documents that Guitar/Bass/Vocal-FX tracks bounce dry. The technical blockers cited are accurate. Pitch-correction worklet registration is module-global (PitchCorrectionNode.ts:97-114). NamWorkletNode.init calls resume() and addModule per instance (NamWorkletNode.ts:19-26). Model resolution lives in the view. The finding's fallback recommendation, though ('warn in the export dialog'), is already implemented: ExportAudioDialog.tsx:153-169 counts unmuted guitar/bass/vocal tracks with clips and shows '…tracks bounce dry (without amp/pedal FX)'. Per-context worklet registration through a WeakMap<BaseAudioContext, Promise> must not break the live context's existing registration. title: Each knob pointermove rewires the whole guitar chain, re-applies every pedal's parameters with no ramps, and writes the chain to the store and collab
evidence:
RotaryKnob calls onChange on every pointermove (RotaryKnob.tsx:106, 144). That goes to updateBlockParam, which builds a new chain (GuitarBassView.tsx:600-611), and the effect at 550-562 calls adapter.syncChain(all blocks). GuitarBassView never uses the parameter-only path that VocalView uses (VocalView.tsx:558-562; GuitarPedalChain.updateProcessorParams 202-213).

syncChain calls setEnabled() and updateParams(all params) on every processor, then wireChain(), which disconnects and reconnects every edge (GuitarPedalChain.ts:129-131, 142, 226-253). Re-applying everything has side effects:
- OverdrivePedal re-assigns shaper.curve, a 44,100-float copy, whenever any knob of any pedal moves (77-82).
- NamAmpPedal posts two worklet messages per change (154-161).
- PitchCorrectionPedal.setEnabled has no early return, so it re-posts 'bypass' and reconnects its bypass edge each time (42-57, 142-165).

All parameter writes are instantaneous `.value =` jumps (for example OverdrivePedal.ts:78-87, NamAmpPedal.ts:148-176, ChorusPedal.ts:69-78, PhaserPedal.ts:145-161). Bypass toggles hard-switch the graph (ChorusPedal.ts:56-64 and the other pedals). The same tick persists the whole chain (GuitarBassView.tsx:565-575), which creates a new tracks array, re-renders TrackControlsPanel (it subscribes to all tracks) and, in collab, JSON.stringifies the chain (diffEngine.ts:195-198).
impact: Dragging any knob rewires the graph about 60 times a second and steps gains and filter frequencies at pointer rate. That causes zipper noise and risks clicks or dropouts: Chromium's WaveShaper outputs a silent quantum if its curve is being replaced. Toggling a pedal clicks. Every tick also re-renders the controls twice and, in a collab session, broadcasts a chain per pointermove.
recommendation: Make GuitarPedalChain.apply() diff internally: if the structure is unchanged, update parameters only and skip wireChain. Give each processor a setParam that skips unchanged values and uses `param.setTargetAtTime(v, ctx.currentTime, 0.01)`. Re-set shaper curves only when drive changes, and crossfade bypass toggles over about 10 ms. Keep audio live during a drag (coalesced to one update per frame) but commit to the store, undo and collab once on pointerup.

title: Loading a NAM model stalls the audio thread; concurrent loads race on a single resolver; no loading or error feedback
evidence:
The engine is built and prewarmed inside the worklet's port.onmessage, i.e. on the audio rendering thread (nam-processor.js:467-518). The WaveNetEngine constructor calls _prewarm (284-303), which runs processSample for the whole receptive field: Σd·(k−1) = 4,092 full-network samples for the bundled configs.

NamWorkletNode keeps one _loadResolve/_loadReject pair, and each loadModel() call overwrites it (lines 12-13, 62-69). 'model-loaded' resolves whichever pair is current (41-45), and each call's 30 s timeout rejects whatever is pending (72-78). Concurrent loads are routine:
- GuitarBassView's restore effect fires again on every chain or readyVersion change while isNamLoaded() is false (534-547).
- The amp picker has no in-flight guard, loading state or catch (656-670, 924-931).

fetchBundledModel has no cache or de-duplication (NamModelStore.ts:259-274). Failures are only console.warn'd (GuitarBassView.tsx:522-529, 546).
recommendation: Give each load a request id (a Map from id to {resolve, reject, timer}) and add a 'latest wins' guard like Learn's GuitarAmpRig (wantedModelId plus disposed). Cache parsed models at module level and de-duplicate in-flight promises. Build the engine without prewarm and warm it over successive process() calls while the previous engine keeps sounding, then crossfade. Show a spinner on the chosen amp, an inline retry on error, and use a clean fallback.
verifierNote: NamWorkletNode keeps a single `_loadResolve/_loadReject` pair that each loadModel overwrites (NamWorkletNode.ts:12-13, 64-67), and 'model-loaded' resolves whichever pair is current (41-45). title: The wah's envelope follower runs on main-thread requestAnimationFrame: zipper noise, frame-rate-dependent timing, and it freezes on jank
evidence: The constructor starts a requestAnimationFrame loop (WahPedal.ts:64-66, 149-151) that runs until dispose (130). Every frame it reads the analyser and writes `filter.frequency.value` and `filter.Q.value` (173-175). When bypassed, the analyser is disconnected (setEnabled 75-85, wireEnabled 193-196) but the loop keeps running. Attack and decay coefficients assume exactly 60 frames per second (`const framesPerSec = 60`, 143-147). Recorded clips play through the chain (usePlaybackEngine.ts:689-699).
impact: The sweep is stepped at the display frame rate, which causes zipper noise that is very audible with Q up to 35. It runs twice as fast on 120 Hz displays and slower on throttled devices. It freezes whenever the main thread is busy (for example during the offline analysis in -03) or the tab is hidden. Each wah keeps a rAF callback alive while bypassed, and a take played through the wah can sound different from run to run.
recommendation: Move the follower to the audio thread. Either use an AudioWorklet that outputs a control signal connected to filter.frequency and filter.Q (sample-accurate, with attack and decay in seconds), or a native chain: WaveShaper |x| → low-pass Biquad → Gain → filter.frequency. Remove the rAF loop and stop work while bypassed.
verifierNote: WahPedal starts a rAF loop in its constructor (WahPedal.ts:65-66, 149-151) that writes filter.frequency.value and Q.value each frame (173-175) with no enabled check, and assumes `framesPerSec = 60` (143-147). rAF stops in hidden tabs and stalls during main-thread blocking, so the behaviour depends on frame rate, as described.

title: Audio chord proposals assume C major when no key is set; the live detector keeps a stale 'detected' key across projects
evidence:
The offline refinement uses `const effectiveRoot = rn ?? 0; const modeIntervals = m ? ALL_MODES[m] : undefined;` (useAudioChordDetection.ts:243-251), and the proposal made at stop uses `(rootNote ?? 0) + 48` (222-228). rootNote defaults to null (prismSlice.ts:1389) but mode is always a string ('ionian' on load, SessionSerializer.ts:512-524). So with no key, the analyzer gets C-major diatonic priors: a 1.25× boost for C D E F G A B roots (OfflineChordAnalyzer.ts:718-721, 387-389) and boosted diatonic Viterbi transitions (438, 495-499). Insight labels the result 'Analysis: N chords in C Major' (ChordSymbolsSection.tsx:180-185).

The live detector prefers `detectedKeyRootPc ?? rootNote` (useAudioChordDetection.ts:127-134). setDetectedKey runs after any UNISON analysis (unisonSlice.ts:213, 246). clearDetectedKey is never called anywhere, and freshProjectHarmony doesn't reset the bus fields (SessionSerializer.ts:512-544).
impact: A student with no key set who plays in E or B♭ gets chords biased toward C-major roots (an F♯m can lose to a D chord), presented as 'in C Major'. Within a session, the live detector's prior silently follows the key of a previously analysed project or an old analysis, not the key the student just chose. The Oracle Synth's follow-key mirror reads the same stale value.
recommendation: With no key, pass no prior, as the live path already does. Alternatively, estimate the key from the take's summed chroma and mark it as detected. Show chords without a key label until a key is chosen. Reset the bus fields in freshProjectHarmony, and make a manual key change override or clear detectedKey (keySource 'manual').

ALL_MODES[m] : undefined` (useAudioChordDetection.ts:243-244), and mode is always 'ionian' after load (SessionSerializer.ts:522), so C-major diatonic priors apply (OfflineChordAnalyzer.ts:387-389). audioChordAnalysis gets rootNote 0, so Insight renders the key as C (ChordSymbolsSection.tsx:180-185). clearDetectedKey is defined but never called (grep finds only musicIntelligenceSlice.ts:108), and freshProjectHarmony does not reset detectedKeyRootPc.

title: Offline chord timing is early and measured from the take start, not the project's bars
evidence:
Each frame is stamped with the start of its 32,768-sample window (`timeMs = offset / sampleRate * 1000`, OfflineChordAnalyzer.ts:735). The window is about 683 ms at 48 kHz, so its Hann-weighted content is centred about 341 ms later.
- quantizeToBeats subtracts another 5% of a beat (535, 545, 585) and snaps to a beat grid counted from the buffer start (586-588).
- optimizeDownbeatAlignment counts bars from the buffer start and shifts every chord by 0–3 whole beats to maximise 'downbeat' hits (650-703, 798-805).
- The start tick it receives is the transport position sampled by the 20 Hz loop when recording was first noticed (useAudioChordDetection.ts:206-209), not the committed clip's startTick (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1112-1115).
- The final segment end hard-codes 48000 (577).
impact: At typical tempos (≳75 BPM), a chord change played on a beat is stamped about 0.37 s early and rounds to the previous beat. Whether the global 0–3-beat shift happens to undo that depends on the progression. Any take that doesn't start on a bar line gets its 'downbeats' in the wrong place, so audio-derived chord symbols land early or off the bars.
recommendation: Stamp frames at the window centre (offset + FFT_SIZE/2). Quantise against the project's bar grid using the clip's real startTick and the tempo, not buffer time. Remove the global shift heuristic, or limit it to ±1 beat behind a confidence threshold. Use the buffer's own sample rate throughout.
verifierNote: Frames are stamped at the window start, `timeMs = (offset / sampleRate) * 1000` (OfflineChordAnalyzer.ts:735), although the 32768-sample Hann window is centred about 341 ms later. quantizeToBeats subtracts another 5% of a beat and snaps to a grid counted from the buffer start (586-588), and the final segment end hard-codes 48000. optimizeDownbeatAlignment applies a global 0-3 beat shift measured from the buffer start (650-703, 798-805). The start tick comes from the polled transport position (useAudioChordDetection.ts:206-209), not the committed clip.startTick.

title: The offline analyzer has no tuning compensation at twice the FFT resolution, and duplicates about 300 lines of the live detector that have already diverged
evidence: The offline analyzer doubles the FFT to 32,768 (1.46 Hz bins at 48 kHz, line 80) but keeps the live detector's ±2-bin search (line 23). It has no tuning estimate: analyzeFrame uses fixed NOTE_FREQUENCIES (316-330). AudioChordDetector estimates a cents offset and applies it (estimateTuning 335-394; tuningMultiplier 400, 425). ±2 bins is ±2.9 Hz, which is about ±10 cents in the top analysed octave (C5–B5) and ±19 cents in C4–B4. CHORD_PRIOR, TIER1_QUALITIES, TONE_WEIGHTS, template building, chroma, harmonic suppression and the parsimony rule are copied between the files (OfflineChordAnalyzer.ts:19-223 and 289-418 vs AudioChordDetector.ts:39-157, 398-565 and 707-789).

title: The live detector writes to the store about 40 times a second while a student strums, mostly unchanged values

Every analysed frame (about 20 Hz) with confidence > 0.5 calls pushLiveChord, and setGlobalTuningCents whenever |tuning| > 1 cent (useAudioChordDetection.ts:174-186).
- pushLiveChord copies the array on every call (musicIntelligenceSlice.ts:118-131). MAX_LIVE_CHORDS = 30, documented as '~30 seconds at ~1 chord/sec' (61-62), actually holds about 1.5 s of near-identical entries.
- setGlobalTuningCents has no equality check (133-135), and the smoothed tuning value changes every frame.
- useLiveUnisonAnalysis, the consumer the bus was built for, is never mounted: grep finds only its definition.
- useStoreBridge re-renders its host and calls engine.setArpChordContext on every push (useStoreBridge.ts:108-129).
- TunerDisplay subscribes to globalTuningCents at its top level (TunerDisplay.tsx:192). It is always mounted in GuitarBassView (878-882) but shows the value only while its own tuner is active (328-336).
- In collab, every set also runs the store diff (collabMiddleware.ts:97-108).

title: Gate and sidechain ducker run as main-thread timer loops: late and jittery live, missing or random in exports
evidence: The gate is a `window.setInterval` every 16 ms that reads a 256-sample analyser (EffectChain.ts:745-800); the ducker polls every 12 ms (1231-1269). At 48 kHz each read covers about 5.3 ms of each poll interval. The gate only opens after a poll sees the transient (776-780), and the hold and envelope maths assume perfectly regular intervals (786 `gateHoldRemaining -= POLL_MS / 1000`, 1262). Any long main-thread task delays the polls. renderProject.ts:22-25 says gating is simply absent from the bounce, but TrackEngine's constructor starts the gate loop (TrackEngine.ts:43) and update() keeps it running for gate-enabled chains (EffectChain.ts:1535-1536) throughout the export. While instruments load (renderProject.ts:285), the offline analyser reads zeros, so the loop closes the gate to minus the range (default −40 dB) at offline time 0. Later polls toggle it at whatever render position the main thread happens to sample. Offline there is no key-track lookup, so the ducker does nothing. The export dialog only warns about SoundFont and amp tracks (ExportAudioDialog.tsx:161-169).
impact: Gated drums and vocals lose their attacks, and the 'Make it pump' ducker wobbles whenever the UI is busy. Exported files have no pump, and gated tracks can come out nearly silent or chopped differently on each export, with no warning.
recommendation: Move the gate and ducker into AudioWorkletProcessors: a sample-accurate detector with a short lookahead, and a ducker that takes the key track as a second input. Worklets behave the same live and in an OfflineAudioContext, which is how openDAW and Audiotool work. Until then, stop gate loops on offline chains and warn in the export dialog.

The TrackEngine constructor starts the gate loop (TrackEngine.ts:43), and update keeps it running when gate.enabled (EffectChain.ts:1535-1536), including on offline chains in renderProject. The renderProject.ts:22-25 comment says gating is simply absent. In fact the timer keeps scheduling gate ramps against the offline graph's currentTime, so the result is nondeterministic, and the export dialog warns only about SoundFont and amp tracks (ExportAudioDialog.tsx:161-169).
impactNote: The mechanics are as described. The gate polls a 256-sample analyser every 16 ms via window.setInterval (EffectChain.ts:745-800) and opens only after a poll sees a transient. The ducker polls every 12 ms (1231-1269). In the bounce, the gate loop runs on the offline chains for gate-enabled tracks (TrackEngine.ts:43, EffectChain.ts:1535-1536), closes the gate while the analyser reads silence during `await Promise.all(inits)`, and then toggles at random render positions. The ducker has no key resolver offline, so the export has no pump, and the ExportAudioDialog warnings (161-169) don't mention it. However, the gate is off by default and rarely used. Live, the ducker's 12 ms one-pole with a 4 ms setTargetAtTime gives an acceptable pump on a mostly idle main thread, and wobble only appears under heavy UI load. The export gap is real and affects the 'House — Make it pump' lesson (tutorials.ts:555), but the code already documents it (renderProject.ts:22-25). Medium is the right level: the quick fixes (stop gate loops on offline chains, warn in the export dialog) are small, while the worklet rewrite is effort L and can be scheduled later.
regressionRisks: Moving to AudioWorklets changes the gate and duck sound (sample-accurate instead of polled), which will audibly change existing projects and the 'Make it pump' tutorial's tuned defaults. Worklet modules must load on both the live and offline contexts before chains are built, which adds async init to renderProject. The ducker's key routing needs an extra connection per keyed track. Watch collab sync of ducker params. The gate's UI meters, which read the analyser taps, would need new data sources.

title: Every change to the tracks list re-applies every track's whole effect chain (twice while playing), and automation re-anchoring briefly snaps automated controls to their fader values
evidence: The sync effect depends on [isReady, tracks]. For every existing track it calls setVolume, setAudible, setPan and updateEffects (usePlaybackEngine.ts:423-426) and applySends (462). While playing it also calls reassertAutomationIfPlaying (466-470), which runs clearTrack, then applyStaticTrackParams (a second setVolume, setPan and updateEffects, 179-182), then scheduleTrack. EffectChain.update never checks what changed: it rewrites about 70 AudioParams, reassigns the crush curve on every call (EffectChain.ts:1407-1414) and the saturator curve when it is enabled (1484-1486), and structuredClones the whole state (1529). Any knob, fader or note edit replaces `tracks` (tracksSlice.ts:716-725). AutomationScheduler cancels and anchors at `Tone.getContext().now()`, i.e. currentTime + lookAhead (AutomationScheduler.ts:76, 92-93, 149-150), while the static fader writes land at currentTime (TrackEngine.ts:99 `.value =`). So after each re-assert the fader value holds for about 0.1 s.
impact: One knob or fader drag (about 60–120 events per second) triggers N full chain updates per event, or 2N while playing. That main-thread work grows with track count and competes with the 30 Hz playhead re-renders, and the frequent WaveShaper curve copies can cause audio dropouts. Tracks with automation jump to their fader value for about 100 ms on every edit made during playback. In collab sessions, where other people's edits keep changing `tracks`, this happens constantly.
recommendation: In EffectChain.update, compare each slot with the previous state and only touch what changed; reassign curves only when drive or crush changes. In the sync effect, skip tracks whose effects, volume, pan, sends and automation are unchanged. In AutomationScheduler, clear and anchor at ctx.currentTime using cancelAndHoldAtTime, and re-anchor only the track that was edited.

It then calls reassertAutomationIfPlaying, which runs applyStaticTrackParams again (179-182, 192-195). EffectChain.update has no diff: it unconditionally reassigns the crush curve (EffectChain.ts:1407-1414) and structuredClones the state (1529). AutomationScheduler anchors at `Tone.getContext().now()` (AutomationScheduler.ts:76,92-93), while TrackEngine.setVolume writes `.value` at currentTime (TrackEngine.ts:97-100). That leaves the lookAhead gap where the fader value holds.

The sync effect calls setVolume, setAudible, setPan, updateEffects and applySends for every existing track on every `tracks` change (usePlaybackEngine.ts:423-426, 462). While playing it also calls reassertAutomationIfPlaying (466-470), which re-applies the static params (179-182).
