The audible part is real: AutomationScheduler cancels and anchors at Tone.getContext().now() = currentTime + lookAhead (AutomationScheduler.ts:76, 92-93), while the static .value writes take effect at currentTime. Automated params therefore jump to the fader value for about 100 ms whenever any track changes during playback, including peers' edits in collab. The performance cost is overstated: AudioParam .value writes and a 4096-float curve copy are microsecond-scale, so 'audio dropouts' is speculative. The main-thread cost is mostly a scaling concern with many tracks. Medium overall.

Skipping unchanged tracks needs a reliable identity or shallow compare. Immer or structured clones from undo produce new references, so compare by value or slice. title: The crush stage is not neutral when off: every track, return and master passes through a tanh soft-clipper (+2.4 dB) that hard-clips at 0 dBFS
evidence: generateCrushCurve(0) sets `drive = 1 + crush * 20` (so 1) and `curve[i] = Math.tanh(drive * x) / norm` with `norm = Math.tanh(drive)` (EffectChain.ts:397-405). Near zero the slope is 1/tanh(1) ≈ 1.31 (+2.4 dB), squashing to 1.0 at full scale. The node is always in the signal path (buildChain 875-876 `compressor → crushNode → makeupGain`) with 2x oversampling (559). update() reassigns this same curve whenever crush is 0 or the compressor is off (1407-1414), even though the comment says 'Default: linear (no crush)' (560). A WaveShaperNode maps any input beyond ±1 to the curve's end values, which is a hard clip.
impact: Every project plays and exports louder (+2.4 dB per stage, about +4.7 dB for a track plus the master) and softly distorted, even with every effect off. Anything above 0 dBFS inside a chain (EQ boosts, hot samples, the summed mix inside the master chain before its effects) is hard-clipped. Students hear distortion they didn't add and can't find, and every chain pays for an oversampled waveshaper.
recommendation: When crush is 0, take the crush node out of the path (connect compressor straight to makeup, as the other effects already do), or use a straight-line curve with oversample 'none'. Only switch to a tanh curve when crush is above 0, and scale it so quiet signals keep a gain of 1.
verifierNote: generateCrushCurve(0) gives drive = 1 and `curve[i] = Math.tanh(drive * x) / norm` (EffectChain.ts:397-405), whose slope at zero is 1/tanh(1) ≈ 1.31 (+2.4 dB) with soft saturation toward ±1. The node is always wired compressor → crushNode → makeupGain (875-876) with `oversample = '2x'` (559), and the `// Default: linear (no crush)` comment at 560 is wrong. update sets the same curve when crush is 0 (1413).
impactNote: generateCrushCurve(0) gives drive = 1 and curve = tanh(x)/tanh(1) (EffectChain.ts:397-405), a soft clipper with a small-signal gain of 1/tanh(1) ≈ 1.31 (+2.4 dB) that saturates to ±1. buildChain wires compressor → crushNode → makeupGain unconditionally (EffectChain.ts:875-876) with 2x oversampling (559), and update() reassigns the same curve whenever crush is 0 or the compressor is off (1407-1414), despite the 'linear (no crush)' comment (560). Every track, return and master chain therefore adds about +2.4 dB, mild third-harmonic saturation on hot signals, and a hard clamp beyond ±1 (for example after EQ boosts or on the summed mix inside the master chain). The facts are correct, but users won't perceive it as a bug: it's how the DAW has always sounded, and the distortion only becomes noticeable on hot mixes. It's a real fidelity defect, not a high-severity user-facing break.
regressionRisks: Making the stage linear changes the loudness and tone of every existing saved project and template: each track gets about 2.4 dB quieter, and the master as well, about 4-5 dB end to end. Demos, templates, tutorial expectations and student mixes balanced against the old gain staging will sound quieter and slightly different, and the auto-makeup and meter calibration may have been tuned around it. Consider a one-off level compensation, or ship the fix with a mastering limiter or level match. Removing the node from the path needs safe reconnect logic, like the other true-bypass helpers, to avoid clicks during playback.

title: The de-esser doesn't target a frequency: its band filter is never connected, so FREQUENCY does nothing and the whole vocal gets compressed
evidence: deEsserFilter is created and its frequency is set (EffectChain.ts:594-597, 1449), but it is only ever disconnected (940, 955, 1574). When enabled, the code wires `deEsserMerge → deEsserCompressor → deEsserWetGain` plus a dry path (978-986). The comment at 931 describes a sidechain, but DynamicsCompressorNode has no sidechain input. EffectsPanel.tsx:1132-1145 still shows a FREQUENCY knob (2–16 kHz). A secondary issue: the blend adds the compressor output to an undelayed dry signal. Browsers build DynamicsCompressorNode with a fixed look-ahead delay (6 ms in Chromium and WebKit), so in-between Amount settings comb-filter. The multiband (OTT) Depth control uses the same parallel layout (1211-1220).
impact: A student trying to tame harsh 's' sounds gets a full-band compressor that ducks loud vowels and leaves the sibilance. Turning FREQUENCY changes nothing, a dead control in a teaching UI, and middle Amount settings can sound hollow or phasey.
recommendation: Build a real split-band de-esser (crossover, compress only the high band, sum back), or a worklet with a band-passed detector. Delay-compensate the dry paths here and in the multiband. Hide FREQUENCY until it works.
verifierNote: deEsserFilter is created and its frequency set (EffectChain.ts:594-597, 1449), but it is only ever disconnected (940, 955, 1574). The enabled wiring is `deEsserMerge → deEsserCompressor → deEsserWetGain → reverbMerge` plus a dry path (978-985), so the FREQUENCY control has no audible effect.

title: Recording failures are silent, and the microphone is never released
evidence: AudioRecorder.ts:17 sets `this.recording = true` before `new MediaRecorder(stream, { mimeType })` (23), which throws when the browser can't record WebM. The fallback format (19-21) is just another WebM type; audio/mp4 is never tried. The caller neither awaits nor catches startRecording (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1042, 1053). stopRecording's async onstop handler (43-53) has no try/catch, so a decode failure never rejects and the promise hangs. Failures that do reach the caller only produce `console.warn` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1163-1165), and there is no onerror handler. Neither dispose (63-69) nor the caller stops the getUserMedia tracks; the cleanup only disconnects the analyser source (usePlaybackEngine.ts:928-940). Every take requests a new stream (1050-1052).
impact: Where WebM recording isn't available, or decoding fails, a student records a whole take and ends up with nothing, with no message. After recording, the browser's 'microphone in use' indicator stays on, which is a privacy worry on school devices, and each take leaves another capture stream open.
recommendation: Negotiate the format (WebM/Opus, then MP4/AAC, otherwise the browser default) and set `recording` only after start succeeds. Wrap onstop in try/catch and reject on error, add onerror, and show failures with showError. Own the stream lifecycle: stop its tracks on stop/dispose, or keep one stream per armed track.
verifierNote: AudioRecorder.ts:17 sets `this.recording = true` before `new MediaRecorder(stream, { mimeType })` (23), and the fallback is just 'audio/webm' (19-21). startRecording is called without await or catch (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1042,1053). onstop is async with no try/catch (AudioRecorder.ts:43-52), so a decode error leaves the promise unresolved. The getUserMedia stream's tracks are never stopped: there is no getTracks().stop() in usePlaybackEngine or AudioRecorder, and only the adapter path calls stopRecordingStream (1094).

title: Faders, sends and effect parameters jump with no smoothing, and changing reverb Decay rebuilds impulse responses on the main thread
evidence: TrackEngine.setVolume, setPan and setSend assign `.value` directly (TrackEngine.ts:97-100, 112-115, 185). EffectChain.update does the same for delay time (1467), feedback and wet/dry (1470-1474), reverb wet/dry (1341-1342), EQ frequency/gain/Q (1371-1373), the compressor (1397-1401), and the saturator and multiband gains. Only setAudible (104-110), return volume (AudioEngine.ts:168-177) and master volume use ramps. Changing reverb type or decay assigns a new convolver buffer (EffectChain.ts:1296, 1299-1307), which restarts the reverb tail. When no real IR is decoded yet (before it loads, or if the pack is missing), generateImpulseResponse builds each IR with Math.random and Math.exp per sample on the main thread, for every 0.1 s decay step, and caches every one forever (312-379; irCache is never evicted). The Decay knob goes up to 10 s while the manifest isn't loaded (EffectsPanel.tsx:632-634). With the real IR, applyDecayEnvelope runs Math.exp per sample (reverbIR.ts:128-137).
impact: Fader and knob drags produce zipper noise, and dragging delay time clicks and warbles. Dragging Decay cuts the reverb tail and causes main-thread spikes. On the synthetic path, sweeping the Decay knob through its range can keep hundreds of MB of IRs in memory.
recommendation: Send continuous changes through setTargetAtTime (5–20 ms) or short linear ramps, calling cancelAndHoldAtTime first so automation is respected. Crossfade between two convolvers when swapping IRs. Generate IRs off the main thread and limit irCache to the most recent entries, as processedCache already does. Apply Decay on release, or debounce it.
verifierNote: TrackEngine.setVolume and setPan assign `.value` directly (TrackEngine.ts:97-100,112-115), as does EffectChain.update for the reverb wet/dry (EffectChain.ts:1341-1342) and the compressor params (1397-1401). Only setAudible ramps (104-110). On the synthetic path, the IR is generated per sample on the main thread and cached forever in irCache (EffectChain.ts:312-377, no eviction), with a new convolver buffer assigned per decay change (1296-1307). Memory growth is limited to the window before the real IR loads.

title: The playhead runs about 100 ms (plus output latency) ahead of what students hear, and live drum pads add the same delay
evidence: useTransport.ts:81 pushes `Tone.getTransport().ticks` into the store. Transport.ticks returns Clock.ticks = `Math.ceil(this.getTicksAtTime(this.now()))` (Clock.js:138), where now() = currentTime + lookAhead (ToneWithContext.js:35-37; default 0.1 s, Context.js:80). AudioEngine.init never tunes lookAhead and offers no output-latency or display-offset API (AudioEngine.ts:24-27, 188-190). Drum tracks play live input at `time ?? Tone.now()` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:203), and auditionNote calls `engine.noteOn(note, velocity)` without a time (auditionNote.ts:31).
impact: The playhead, piano-roll highlights and score cursor run ahead of the sound by about 110–140 ms on wired output and 250 ms or more on Bluetooth, which is clearly out of sync for a student reading along. Drum pads and drum-lane previews feel sluggish.
recommendation: Expose audioEngine.getVisualLatency() (lookAhead plus the native outputLatency) and compute the displayed position with transport.getTicksAtTime(ctx.currentTime - outputLatency), or from getOutputTimestamp. Trigger live input with Tone.immediate(). Evaluate lowering lookAhead to 0.05 s with the worker clock.
verifierNote: useTransport.ts:81 reads `Tone.getTransport().ticks`, which is `Math.ceil(this.getTicksAtTime(this.now()))` (Clock.js:137-139), where now() includes lookAhead. No src code tunes lookAhead or compensates for output latency. DrumMachineEngine.ts:203 uses `time ?? Tone.now()`, and auditionNote.ts:31 calls noteOn without a time.

title: Every track builds a ~64-node effect graph and keeps 8 EQ filters, a compressor and an oversampled waveshaper in the signal path even with all effects off
evidence: The EffectChain constructor (EffectChain.ts:504-659) always creates reverb (7 nodes), 8 EQ filters, gate, compressor, crush, two meter analysers, delay (5), presence, de-esser (5), saturator (5), 22 multiband nodes and the duck gain. TrackEngine adds gain, panner, mute gain, analyser and one send gain per return (TrackEngine.ts:19-44, 159-186). buildChain always wires input → 8 EQ filters → EQ makeup → gate → DynamicsCompressor → 2x-oversampled WaveShaper → makeup (859-879); turning EQ or the compressor off only sets neutral values (1359-1375, 1402-1405). All of this is built synchronously for every track in the first sync after the first click (usePlaybackEngine.ts:475-479).
impact: About 70 nodes per track (roughly 1,100 for 16 tracks, plus the master and two returns) and always-on processing on every track. This eats CPU headroom on Chromebooks and iPads so dropouts start sooner, slows the first-click start-up, and adds the compressor's look-ahead latency to instruments being played live.
recommendation: Split EffectChain into per-effect modules that are created on first enable, and take EQ, compressor and crush fully out of the path when off, as the other effects already are. Keeping an ordered list of effect modules also makes reorderable effects possible, as in Ableton and Logic.
verifierNote: buildChain always wires input → all EQ filters → eqMakeup → gate → compressor → crush → makeup (EffectChain.ts:859-876). Disabled EQ and compressor only get neutral values (e.g. 1402-1405 sets threshold 0 and ratio 1 but leaves the node in the path). The exact node count is approximate, but the always-in-path DynamicsCompressor and 2x-oversampled WaveShaper on every chain are real.

title: Export is slow and gives little feedback, and the result differs from playback in ways the dialog doesn't mention
evidence: renderProject creates and initialises a fresh instrument for every track on each export (renderProject.ts:245-279); for example, PianoSampler.init fetches 30 samples from tonejs.github.io every time (PianoSampler.ts:24-57). The render step reports no progress (exportAudio.ts:75-76), and WAV encoding runs synchronously on the main thread (80-82). A fixed 2 s tail (renderProject.ts:74-76) cuts off longer reverbs (IRs up to 3.7 s) and high-feedback delay. Pitch-editor edits are ignored: the export uses getAudioBuffer (renderProject.ts:38-39, 338), while playback uses resolvePitchBuffer (usePlaybackEngine.ts:700-704). The dialog warns only about SoundFont and amp tracks (ExportAudioDialog.tsx:161-169). Export doesn't stop playback, and while the offline render waits for instruments to load, Tone's global context is the offline one, so live transport-scheduled clips are created on the wrong context (AudioClipScheduler.ts:132-135) and fail.
impact: Students watch an indeterminate 'Rendering…' bar, the UI freezes during encoding, song endings are cut off abruptly, and pitch-corrected vocals export uncorrected. Playing while an export runs glitches the live audio.
recommendation: Preload and reuse instrument sample buffers, and stop the transport before rendering. Size the tail from the longest reverb IR and delay feedback, and fade it out. Export the pitch-corrected buffers. Encode in a worker with real progress and a Cancel button, and add the missing warnings.
verifierNote: The render stage reports only pct 0 (exportAudio.ts:75-76), and WAV encoding runs synchronously (80-82). TAIL_SECONDS = 2 (renderProject.ts:75) is shorter than the hall IR's decaySeconds of 3.46 in the manifest. scheduleTrackClips uses getAudioBuffer (renderProject.ts:338) rather than resolvePitchBuffer, unlike playback (usePlaybackEngine.ts:700-704). Live clip callbacks would call Tone.getContext() (AudioClipScheduler.ts:132) while the offline context is installed. Those failures are caught and logged, not crashes.

title: The output-device picker can never appear, because supportsOutputSelection checks the wrapper context, which has no setSinkId
evidence: AudioEngine.ts:192-209 checks for and calls `setSinkId` on `this.ctx`, which is Tone's rawContext (27): the standardized-audio-context wrapper. That class exposes baseLatency (node_modules/standardized-audio-context/build/es2019/factories/audio-context-constructor.js:79), but setSinkId appears nowhere in its es2019 build. recommendation: Get the native context once (`_nativeContext ?? ctx`) and use it for setSinkId, outputLatency and getOutputTimestamp. Re-apply the saved output device when the engine starts.
verifierNote: AudioEngine.ts:27 sets `this.ctx = Tone.getContext().rawContext`, the standardized-audio-context class (audio-context-constructor.js:4 `class AudioContext extends ...`, not a Proxy). supportsOutputSelection and setOutputDevice check `this.ctx.setSinkId` (AudioEngine.ts:192-209), and grep finds no setSinkId anywhere in standardized-audio-context's es2019 build, so the check is always false.

title: The 1.13 MB editor chunk is only requested after auth bootstrap and the songs bundle, behind a dashboard-shaped skeleton
evidence: The editor route is `<ContentGate needs={['songs']}><DawApp /></ContentGate>` (ClassroomPages.tsx:441-449, with the comment "DawApp resolves a song by id when opened with ?song="). The DAW reads songs only in that branch (`getSong(songParam)`, DawApp.tsx:223-236). ContentSuspender throws before rendering children (ContentGate.tsx:50-61), and React.lazy starts `import('@/daw/DawApp')` (ClassroomPages.tsx:191-195) only when <DawApp/> first renders. That happens only after ProtectedPage stops returning <FullScreenLoading/> (ProtectedPage.tsx:43-45 and the !appUser branch) and after songs hydrate. The bundled songs fallback chunk alone is 3.5 MB raw / 350 KB gzip. The DAW chunk is 1,133,817 B (286 KB gzip -9) in the 2026-09-30 dist. Meanwhile the fallback is DashboardContentSkeleton, which renders null for 1 s and then a header/filter/cards skeleton (DashboardContentSkeleton.tsx:5-18), not the editor's layout.
impact: Every cold load of /studio/editor pays for auth, then songs, then the DAW chunk download and parse, in series. That covers browser refresh (crash recovery, reload a), classroom deep links and ?project= links (b). On school networks the DAW chunk alone is roughly 0.5–1.5 s that could have overlapped auth. Going from blank, to the wrong skeleton, to the DAW also means two visible layout jumps.
recommendation: Drop the route-level gate; in the ?song= branch set bootedRef, then `await ensureSongContent()` before getSong. Start the chunk early with a memoised preloadDaw(), used by the lazy() factory and called during route-module evaluation when location.pathname starts with /studio/editor, so it downloads alongside Auth0/me. Give the editor route a DAW-shaped fallback: 48 px transport row, header column, ruler, three lane placeholders, 32 px dock, on the #101012 base with white/6 fills, white/8 hairlines and aria-busy.

The route wraps lazy DawApp in `<ContentGate needs={['songs']}>` (ClassroomPages.tsx:441-449), so `import('@/daw/DawApp')` (:191-195) only starts after ProtectedPage's loading gate (ProtectedPage.tsx:43-45) and songs hydration. The fallback is DashboardContentSkeleton, which renders null for 1 s and then a dashboard skeleton (ContentGate.tsx:79-82). Medium fits better than high.
impactNote: The serial chain is overstated. AppContext.tsx:26-29 already starts ensureSongContent() at app boot, in parallel with auth, so in most cases the ContentGate (ClassroomPages.tsx:441-449, ContentGate.tsx:50-61) resolves from an already-warm promise and adds little. One part is accurate: the lazy DawApp import (ClassroomPages.tsx:191-195) starts only once the route renders past ProtectedPage's FullScreenLoading (ProtectedPage.tsx:43-45). Its fallback, DashboardContentSkeleton (lines 5-18), renders nothing for 1 s and then a dashboard-shaped skeleton. That costs a few hundred ms to about 1 s and causes layout jumps, which is noticeable but cosmetic next to -01 through -05.
regressionRisks: Removing the route-level ContentGate means the ?song= branch must await ensureSongContent() before calling getSong. Otherwise it reports 'That song could not be found'. Other DAW code that reads songs (song-seeding helpers, Insight or any getAllSongs consumer) must also be audited, since songStore.ts warns that mutation does not re-render. Calling preloadDaw() at route-module evaluation adds about 1 MB of parse work to any page whose pathname matches, so make the match exact. A DAW-shaped skeleton must not carry data-tutorial-id attributes, or tutorial anchors could resolve against placeholder nodes.

title: MeshGradientBg redraws four full-viewport gradients every frame, hidden behind an opaque background
evidence: draw() runs on every requestAnimationFrame for as long as the editor is mounted: `ctx!.clearRect(0, 0, w, h)`, then four createRadialGradient + `ctx!.fillRect(0, 0, w, h)` calls on a canvas sized `w * dpr` × `h * dpr` (MeshGradientBg.tsx:22-31, 73-98). It never pauses while playing, idle or covered. It is the first child of .daw-root (DawApp.tsx:482-486), which has an opaque `backgroundColor: 'var(--color-bg)'` and no position or z-index, while the canvas is `absolute` with `zIndex: -1` (:107-113). By CSS painting order a negative-z positioned child is painted before its non-positioned parent's background, so the canvas is covered; the editor screenshots (a11y-studio-create.png, a11y-studio-MASTER.png) show flat #101012. Its purple/teal/pink/blue orbs (:38-71) are also off the Music Atlas palette, where colour is reserved for musical meaning.
impact: A permanent full-screen gradient fill at display refresh rate (60–120 Hz) and device-pixel resolution. It competes with the playhead, meters and the transport/track-header .glass-panel backdrop blur, and nothing is visible as a result.
recommendation: Remove <MeshGradientBg/> from DawApp and keep the flat #101012 landing-look base. If a wash is wanted elsewhere, use a static CSS gradient, or draw once and redraw only on resize.
verifierNote: MeshGradientBg.tsx:73-98 clears and fills four full-canvas radial gradients on every rAF at DPR resolution, and nothing pauses it. It is rendered at DawApp.tsx:486 with `zIndex: -1` (:112) inside .daw-root, which is non-positioned and has an opaque `backgroundColor: var(--color-bg)` (#101012). evidence: The chunk was DawApp-B2B4m2Eo.js at 982.02 kB / 260.88 kB gzip on 2026-06-10 (build.log). In the 2026-09-30 dist it is DawApp-BACIKhSK.js at 1,133,817 B (+15%). The only dynamic imports under src/daw are spessasynth_lib (SoundFontAdapter.ts:234) and upload-pending. Static imports put every secondary surface in the chunk: ScoreView, LeadSheetView, PracticeTrackView, StudioView, PitchEditorModal, PrismSuggestionModal, SettingsModal and TutorialLayer (DawApp.tsx:4-21). Every instrument view comes in through TrackControlsPanel.tsx:5-14: VocalView 101 KB src, DrumMachineView 68 KB, CrystalIcons 64 KB of amp SVG paths used only by GuitarBassView, GuitarBassView 54 KB, OrganView, SamplerChopsView, and the Oracle Synth UI at 128 KB. Also included: the ChannelStrip tabs (ChannelStrip.tsx:16-21), FileMenu → ExportAudioDialog/renderProject/encoders, and collab (CollabProvider.tsx:17-20: yjs, y-indexeddb, y-partykit, awareness; 175 KB src). title: No caching policy for 67 MB of DAW assets; engines and decoded samples are thrown away every time the editor is left
evidence: vercel.json contains only `redirects` and `rewrites` (:2-46) and no `headers`. Hashed /assets/*.js and /daw-assets/** therefore fall back to platform defaults. By du, /daw-assets/** holds 30 MB of SF2, 20 MB of samples, 7.5 MB of NAM models, 6.7 MB of Oracle packs and 2.3 MB of IRs. Nothing uses a service worker or Cache Storage for samples. On unmount, usePlaybackEngine disposes every TrackEngine and clears the registry (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1169-1191), and Tone has no decoded-buffer cache. Returning to the editor (reload d) therefore re-fetches and re-decodes every instrument after the next click. By contrast, reverbIR.ts keeps module-level nativeCache/processedCache (reverbIR.ts:42-47), and the SoundFont synth is a module singleton.
impact: Large assets are revalidated or re-downloaded depending on browser heuristics, and every return to the editor repeats the full first-interaction cost.
recommendation: Add headers: `/assets/(.*)` → `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`; `/daw-assets/(.*)` → a long max-age plus stale-while-revalidate, with versioned filenames so assets can be marked immutable. Add a bounded module-level decoded-buffer cache keyed by URL, shared across instruments and remounts, and keep the SF2 in Cache Storage. Consider keeping instrument engines alive across SPA navigation while the project is unchanged.
verifierNote: vercel.json has only redirects and rewrites, with no headers block. The unmount effect in usePlaybackEngine.ts:1169-1191 disposes every TrackEngine and clears the map. useAudioEngine re-inits isReady=false on every mount, so returning to the editor needs another click and a full re-fetch and re-decode. title: Every remote change rebuilds every track, defeating all memoization downstream
evidence: yjsToZustand.ts:112-115 says 'Any change ... rebuilds the full tracks array'. applyTracksFromDoc (126-145) maps every Y track through yMapToTrack, which re-creates every clip and note object, JSON.parses effects, chains and automation, and structuredClones DEFAULT_EFFECTS for each track (YjsDocManager.ts:263-337, 299-302). A peer's volume drag writes once per pointer move (TrackHeader.tsx:497 `onValueChange={([v]) => updateTrack(track.id, { volume: v / 100 })}`).
impact: Each remote edit replaces every Track, clip and events reference, so memoized TrackHeader rows and every track/clip subscriber re-render. The TrackEngine sync re-applies volume, pan, effects, sends and automation to every track (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-472). useCollabAudioLoader's DawApp-level `useStore((s) => s.tracks)` (useCollabAudioLoader.ts:24) re-renders the whole editor. The solo undo tracker JSON.stringifies the whole project on each change (undoMiddleware.ts:194-206, 222-231) even though collab uses Yjs undo. initUndoTracking also adds a fresh set of subscriptions that is never removed on every editor mount (DawApp.tsx:97-99, undoMiddleware.ts:257-264), so after N visits that stringify runs N times. With 60 Hz remote fader or knob drags, listeners carry a continuous main-thread load, seen as timeline jank during playback.
recommendation: Apply remote changes incrementally. Use the observeDeep event paths to find the touched track and keys, rebuild only that track, and reuse the previous objects for untouched tracks and clips (structural sharing). Cache parsed JSON per Y.Map key. Skip solo undo capture while collab undo is active, and make initUndoTracking idempotent. Make the TrackEngine sync skip reference-equal tracks.

Any remote change therefore replaces every track reference. initUndoTracking adds 15 subscriptions that are never removed on each mount (undoMiddleware.ts:257-264, DawApp.tsx:97-99). watched() JSON.stringifies the whole project before its identity check (194-206), so N mounts means N stringifies per tracks change. Mitigating factor: DawAppInner already re-renders on every tracks change via usePlaybackEngine, so the cost is not unique to collab, but it is multiplied by remote write rates.

However, MAX_TOTAL_TRACKS = 10 (tracksSlice.ts:36) limits the rebuild cost, and the re-render storm described is mostly caused by collab-02. TrackEngine sync re-applies volume and effects per track (usePlaybackEngine.ts:~411-430), but there is no evidence it causes audio glitches. The jank is real during a remote fader drag but moderate. Any reuse of previous objects must still carry local-only fields (see collab-08) and the deferred-while-recording logic (yjsToZustand.ts:~146-155). Making initUndoTracking idempotent must keep rebaseline on project load. Skipping solo undo capture during collab must not lose history when the session ends.

title: Socket status is treated as session membership: every blip looks like the session ended and re-enables destructive actions

When !isCollabActive: DawApp.tsx:504-509 and 523-528 unmount UserList and ChatPanel; CollabToolbar.tsx:52-59 and 217-272 hide chat, invite and leave and show 'Start Collaboration'; FileMenu.tsx:426 and 466-478 re-enable New Project and Open; TransportBar.tsx:189-191 re-enables renaming for non-hosts. deserializeCloudProject writes via raw useStore.setState (SessionSerializer.ts:611), which collabMiddleware doesn't intercept (it only wraps the slice set, store/index.ts:48-68). So Open during a blip makes the store diverge from the doc, and the next local track edit deletes every shared track not in the local list (diffEngine.ts:141-146).

title: Refresh and navigation: hosts end the room with no warning, joiners can't get back, and stale room identity triggers unwanted rejoins

Explicit boots don't clear it: the ?project= branch returns first (DawApp.tsx:131-155), and resetSessionToEmpty leaves roomId, collabRole and chatMessages alone (SessionSerializer.ts:649-678). There is no beforeunload or route-leave guard anywhere in src/daw (grep). _setRoomInfo doesn't clear chatMessages or unreadChatCount (collabSlice.ts:116-124). The IndexedDB copy `collab-${roomId}` (CollabProvider.tsx:321-323) is never read after a refresh.
impact: (a) On refresh, a joiner drops out with no way back except retyping a code they may not have, and lands in a solo copy (or an empty project, since autosave is starved per collab-02). A host's refresh, or an SPA navigation such as clicking Learn in the sidebar, closes the room for everyone with no confirmation. (b)/(d) A joiner who leaves the editor, opens their own project via ?project=, then returns through a plain link is silently rejoined to the old room, and pullFromYjs replaces the project they had open; projectId still points at theirs, so Cmd-S then overwrites it. (e) Old chat and unread counts carry into the next session.

Add a host beforeunload and route-leave confirm ('Leaving ends the session for 3 people'). Clear chat in _setRoomInfo. Either use the IndexedDB copy for recovery or remove it.

title: Deletions are inferred as 'in the doc but not in my store', so peers' tracks get deleted when the two are out of sync
evidence: diffTracks deletes every Y track whose id isn't in the local nextTracks (diffEngine.ts:141-146), rather than only tracks removed between prev and next. Clips, regions and markers use the same pattern (250-255, 306-311, 359-364, 419-424). The store is deliberately behind the doc while recording, because remote track changes are deferred (yjsToZustand.ts:146-154).
impact: While student A records, student B adds a track. If A touches any track before stopping (e.g. nudges a fader), A's diff deletes B's new track from the shared doc for everyone.
recommendation: Compute deletions as prevIds − nextIds and additions as nextIds − prevIds. Never infer a deletion from the doc's contents.
verifierNote: diffTracks deletes any Y track whose id is not in nextIds (diffEngine.ts:141-146), and clips use the same pattern (250-255). Deletions are therefore inferred from the doc's contents, not from prev minus next. Remote track changes are deferred while the local user is recording (yjsToZustand.ts:146-154), so the local store can lag the doc, and any local track edit during that window deletes the peer's new tracks.

title: Partial field diffs: chord-region edits and MIDI CC changes never reach peers

title: Selecting a track locks it indefinitely, and the host has no moderation controls
evidence: setSelectedTrackId refuses a track any peer has selected (prismSlice.ts:1820-1836), guardTrack blocks every edit on it (tracksSlice.ts:62-88), and TrackHeader greys it out with pointer-events none (TrackHeader.tsx:70-80). title: WebRTC setup can deadlock when a joiner hasn't clicked yet
evidence: Only the peer with the lower clientID sends an offer, once, when it adds the peer (StudioRtcManager.ts:227-230). Recovery only triggers on 'disconnected' or 'failed' (213-221). studioRealtime doesn't buffer messages (studioRealtime.ts:104-108). The RTC manager and MIDI subscribers exist only after the audio engine is ready (useStudioMonitor.ts:41-43, 68-77), which waits for a first click or keypress (DawApp.tsx:437-448).
impact: A joiner arriving via a link who hasn't clicked yet drops the offer from a lower-id peer. When their manager later creates its side, it waits as answerer forever, and the offerer never reaches 'failed'. That pair never hears each other's live audio, with no indication; roughly half of such pairs are affected.
recommendation: When the answerer creates a peer, have it send 'request-offer'. Add a negotiation timeout that re-offers if no answer arrives within ~5 s, or buffer studio:rtc messages until the manager starts.
verifierNote: The offer is sent once, and only by the lower clientID (StudioRtcManager.ts:227-235). title: Dragging a volume fader re-renders 24 store subscribers and redraws the Timeline canvas on every pointer move
evidence: TrackHeader.tsx:497 and StudioView.tsx:675 call updateTrack() on every Radix onValueChange, i.e. every pointer move. 24 components subscribe to the whole s.tracks array (grep), so each step re-renders all of them. Timeline.tsx:415: draw depends on tracks (1339) and the redraw effect runs on it (1342-1366), so every clip and note is redrawn per pointer move. TransportBar.tsx:201: used only inside handleSkipForward (248-256). ChannelStrip.tsx:115 plus whichever dock panel is open. InsightContent.tsx:69, whose effect (73-84) re-runs analyzeSession 500ms after every volume change. Each LibraryItemRow (LibraryPanel.tsx:394). Always-mounted ChordAnalysisPrompt.tsx:89, PianoRollModal.tsx:17, PitchEditorModal.tsx:14 and AutomationLaneEditor.tsx:37. Granular selectors already exist (store/index.ts:73-85 useTrack/useTrackIds/useTrackCount), and MixingSection uses them.
impact: The most common mixing gesture does arrangement-scale work at pointer rate. Jank grows with track and clip count and happens while audio plays. A volume change also triggers a harmony re-analysis whose result cannot change.
recommendation: Give the Fader primitive a transient/commit contract. During a drag, write gain straight to the track engine and to a ref-driven readout; commit to the store on release, or throttle commits to once per animation frame. Keep mix parameters (volume, pan, mute, solo, sends) in a map separate from arrangement data. Replace s.tracks subscriptions with id/field selectors (useShallow), and read via getState() inside handlers. Trigger Insight analysis only from note and chord data.
verifierNote: TrackHeader.tsx:497 and StudioView.tsx:675 call updateTrack on every Radix onValueChange. That fires on each 1% step rather than literally every pointer move, but it is still many times per drag. updateTrack (tracksSlice.ts:619-625) maps a new tracks array, which re-renders the roughly 24 `useStore((s) => s.tracks)` subscribers. Timeline's draw has `tracks` as a dependency (Timeline.tsx:1339, 1342-1366), so the canvas fully redraws each step. InsightContent.tsx:73-84 also re-schedules analyzeSession whenever `tracks` changes.
impactNote: The mechanism is right. TrackHeader.tsx:497 and StudioView.tsx:675 call updateTrack on every Radix onValueChange, and updateTrack (tracksSlice.ts:619-626) replaces the tracks array. 28 call sites subscribe to `s.tracks`. Timeline.tsx:1339 puts `tracks` in draw's deps, and the effect at 1342-1366 redraws the whole canvas on each step. InsightContent.tsx:73-84 re-arms analyzeSession on every tracks change (debounced 500ms, so it fires once after the drag, not per move). The finding misses something worse: usePlaybackEngine.ts:363-420 re-runs its whole TrackEngine sync loop over all tracks per pointer move. Parts are overstated. TrackHeader is wrapped in memo (TrackHeader.tsx:51) and TrackList passes stable per-track objects, so only the dragged header re-renders, not all of them. Many of the 28 subscribers (ScoreView, LeadSheetView, the PianoRoll/PitchEditor modals' inner content, Effects panels) only matter when that view is mounted. Undo is already coalesced by a 300ms debounce (undoMiddleware.ts:233-253). Impact on a typical student project of 4-8 tracks with modest clip counts is unmeasured; it plausibly shows as fader stutter on Chromebooks with large arrangements. Medium rather than high.
regressionRisks: A transient/commit split for faders is the riskiest part. Volume syncs to collaborators (diffEngine.ts:60 lists 'volume'). Committing only on release means peers see jumps instead of a smooth ramp, and a dropped pointerup (tab switch, pointer capture loss) could leave the engine gain and the store/collab state out of sync. Use onValueCommit plus a cleanup path. Writing gain straight to the TrackEngine while usePlaybackEngine also applies track.volume from the store can double-apply or snap back. Use a single ramped setter (setTargetAtTime) to avoid zipper noise. Track locks (lockedStyle / guardTrack) must still block remote-locked tracks during the transient phase. Splitting mix params into a separate map changes the Track shape. Saved-project serialization, collab Yjs schema, undo snapshots (which JSON.stringify state.tracks) and migrations all assume volume/pan/mute live on Track, so this is far more than 'M' effort. Prefer selector fixes (useShallow, getState() in handlers, narrowing the Timeline draw deps to clip/note data) first. Insight analysis should depend on note/chord data only, otherwise it would miss track-type changes.

title: Token values have three sources of truth; the inline runtime copy overrides daw.css, so the A11Y#7 fix as written would not take effect
evidence: themes.ts:7-9: 'Applied as inline styles on .daw-root by useTheme, which is the authoritative runtime source (overrides daw.css)'. useTheme.ts:8-10 calls setProperty() inline. A11Y#7 tells implementers to change the token at daw.css:13. That edit has no runtime effect, because the inline '#6b6b80' wins. THEMES.dark (themes.ts:10-27) holds 18 tokens; daw.css defines 33. Values are also hard-coded in components: #7ecfcf ×70 plus rgba(126,207,207,…) ×39; #6b6b80 ×20 (OrganView.module.css ×5, PianoRoll.tsx ×5, DrumMachineView.tsx ×4, PopOutOverlay.tsx:103 and others); #101012 ×15; #1a1a1a ×17. The same --color-* names are redefined in dashboard.css:7-16, learn.css:5-14 and settings.css:5-14, with --color-bg #191919 instead of the DAW's #101012. Four tokens are used but defined nowhere: --color-surface-1 (LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:154, so that toolbar's background is silently transparent), --color-text-secondary (CircleOfFifths.tsx:329; VocalView.tsx ×4), --color-bg-elev and --color-warning (AudioMidiSourcePanel.tsx:72 and 127). Delete useTheme/THEMES. Codemod --color-* to --daw-* and literals to tokens. Define or remove the four phantom tokens. Add a lint rule banning colour literals in src/daw/components, with an allowlist for the music-colour module.

evidence:
- onNoteOn sends to the monitored tracks, or the selected track, at the moment the key is pressed (useMidiInputRouting.ts:106-123).
- releaseNote recomputes the targets at release time (73-83).
- Sustain-held notes are released to whatever is targeted when the pedal lifts (207-216).
- On input hot-plug, the cleanup clears sustainHeldNotes without releasing them (239-244).
- The same release-time lookup is relayed to collaborators (86-96, via liveMidiTargets at 12-19).
- The receiver keys held notes by trackId (useStudioMonitor.ts:48-63) and never releases the notes of a peer who leaves (80-94).

Downgraded to medium: the mismatch only happens when the selected-track fallback is in use (no monitored MIDI track) and the selection changes mid-note, or monitoring flags change mid-note. regressionRisks: Tracking per-note targets has to cover re-strikes of the same note (sustainHeldNotes.delete on re-strike) and overlapping note-ons to different targets, so use a refcount or Set. Releasing everything on target change can cut notes the user intends to sustain. Collab relay message shapes must stay compatible with older clients during rollout. The hwNoteOn/hwNoteOff visual keyboard must stay in sync.

title: Any edit while playing makes automated parameters jump to their fader value for ~100 ms
evidence:
While playing, reassertAutomationIfPlaying (usePlaybackEngine.ts:190-207) runs for every existing track on every tracks change (466-470). It does three things in order:
1. Calls automationScheduler.clearTrack, which runs cancelScheduledValues at Tone.getContext().now().
2. Calls applyStaticTrackParams. Its setVolume and setPan write .value (TrackEngine.ts:97-115), which takes effect at the AudioContext's currentTime.
3. Calls scheduleTrack, which anchors the automated value at Tone.getContext().now() (AutomationScheduler.ts:76, 91-94).

In Tone 15, now() is currentTime + lookAhead (Context.js:329-331), with the default 0.1 s lookAhead left in place (toneBridge.ts:56). So each reassert leaves the static fader value in force for about 100 ms before the automation resumes.
impact: While a loop plays, many ordinary actions make every automated volume, pan, send or FX parameter flutter between its fader value and its automated value. Triggers include dragging another track's fader, moving a note, renaming a track, or receiving a collaborator's edit. The result is audible pumping on fades and filter sweeps.
recommendation: Re-assert only tracks whose automation or static values actually changed (see engine-hooks-03). When re-asserting, don't write .value on automated params. Anchor with Tone.immediate(), or schedule the static write at the same time as the anchor, or skip static writes entirely for params that have a lane.
verifierNote: reassertAutomationIfPlaying (usePlaybackEngine.ts:190-207) runs for every track on every tracks change while playing. It clears, then applyStaticTrackParams writes .value (TrackEngine.ts:97-115, which per spec is setValueAtTime at currentTime) plus updateEffects writes. scheduleLanes then cancels and anchors at Tone.getContext().now() (AutomationScheduler.ts:76, 91-94), which is currentTime plus 0.1 s. So the static value holds for about 100 ms on every edit.
impactNote:
reassertAutomationIfPlaying (usePlaybackEngine.ts:190-207) runs for every track on every tracks change while playing (466-470). It does three things in order:
1. clearTrack: cancelScheduledValues at Tone now(), which is currentTime+0.1.
2. applyStaticTrackParams: writes .value, effective at currentTime (TrackEngine.ts:97-115).
3. Re-anchors at now() (AutomationScheduler.ts:76, 91-94).
That leaves the static value in force for about 100 ms. During a continuous drag on another track this repeats every frame, so automated params can sit at their static value for the whole drag. The mechanism is sound. Downgraded to medium because it only affects projects with automation lanes, an advanced feature students use less often.
regressionRisks: Skipping static writes on params that have lanes must still restore the static value when a lane is deleted mid-play (the comment at 185-189 relies on this). Anchoring with Tone.immediate() or currentTime must not clash with transport-scheduled segment events already queued inside the lookahead window. The master automation effect (608-624) has the same pattern and should be fixed the same way.

title: Missing audio is invisible after a reload: failed downloads retry on every edit, and un-uploaded takes come back as a fake waveform
evidence:
useCollabAudioLoader runs on every tracks change (useCollabAudioLoader.ts:24-41). Its 'hasPending' guard is true for any clip that has an assetId, loaded or not (30-33), so it calls loadPendingClipAudio on every edit. The sampler-sample branch works the same way.

A failed download is only logged and removed from the in-flight set (load-audio.ts:47-55). So every later edit requests a new signed URL and fetches again, up to once per drag frame per failed clip, while the Timeline shows 'Loading...' indefinitely (Timeline.tsx:949-972).

Takes are only uploaded when a token exists (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1145-1160), and the local autosave holds no audio. After a refresh, a clip without an assetId has no buffer. The Timeline draws it as a seeded random placeholder waveform (Timeline.tsx:984-985) that plays silent.
impact: On a flaky network or with an expired token, the editor hammers the assets API during every drag. Students see 'Loading...' forever, or a convincing waveform for audio that no longer exists. Nothing tells them they need to re-record or re-save.
recommendation: Keep a per-clip load status (loading, failed or missing) in a small store. Back off failed clips (for example 2 s, 10 s, then 60 s) and retry when the browser comes back online or the tab becomes visible. Trigger loads from a diff of clip ids rather than every tracks change. Render explicit 'Audio unavailable, retry' and 'Not saved to cloud' states. Warn before a leave or refresh when takes are still waiting to upload.
verifierNote: hasPending is true for any clip with an assetId, loaded or not (useCollabAudioLoader.ts:30-33), so the loader runs on every tracks change. loadClipAudio only logs a failure and removes the clip from in-flight (load-audio.ts:47-55), so it refetches on the next edit, while Timeline keeps drawing 'Loading...' (Timeline.tsx:953-972). Clips without an assetId and with no buffer render a seededRandom placeholder waveform (Timeline.tsx:984-988), and an upload only happens when a token exists (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1145).
impactNote: useCollabAudioLoader runs on every tracks change (useCollabAudioLoader.ts:24-41). It calls loadPendingClipAudio whenever any clip has an assetId. That function filters to clips missing a buffer and skips ones in flight (load-audio.ts:36-37, 65-75). A failed download is just logged and removed from in-flight (47-55), so later edits retry indefinitely, with no backoff, while the Timeline shows 'Loading...' (Timeline.tsx:949-972). Clips with no assetId and no buffer draw a seeded random waveform (Timeline.tsx:984-988). Both are real, but each needs a failure first: an expired token, an asset 404, or an upload failure, and the upload path already shows a toast (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1153-1159). Edge-case impact, so medium.
regressionRisks: Per-clip status needs clearing when a collaborator re-uploads, which gives a new assetId. Key status by clipId+assetId. Backoff must not delay first-time loads of collaborator clips arriving over Yjs. A beforeunload warning should only fire for genuinely pending uploads, or it will annoy users. Changing the placeholder rendering affects how freshly recorded clips look before the decode lands, if any path renders before setAudioBuffer.

title: The tuner runs heavy YIN pitch detection every frame and can never show an error
evidence:
Performance: the tuner calls yinDetectSingle on a 4,096-sample buffer on every requestAnimationFrame (useTuner.ts:173-225). With minFreq 27 Hz, the difference function is about 1,778 lags x 2,048 samples, roughly 3.6 M multiply-adds per frame. Each call also allocates two Float32Arrays (YinCore.ts:265-281). The tuner then sets 2-4 React states per frame.

Errors never show: stop() resets error to null (useTuner.ts:126), and both error paths call setError(...) then stop() (159-164, 226-229). So TunerDisplay's red error text (TunerDisplay.tsx:200-218) can never appear. With no device and no analyser, start() returns silently (144), but TunerDisplay has already reported the tuner as active (227-235).

Unmount race: if the component unmounts during await getAudioStream (146-147), the stream, the AudioContext and the rAF loop all start after cleanup has run, and nothing ever stops them.

Input quality: standalone mode gets a stream with the browser's echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain left on (AudioInputEnumerator.ts:66-70). The guitar adapter deliberately avoids this (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:21-22).
impact: While a note is sounding, pitch detection takes several ms of JS per frame, worse on 120 Hz screens and Chromebooks. That janks the whole editor. A blocked mic or unplugged interface just shows 'Off' with no explanation. Noise suppression can swallow sustained notes, and a leaked tuner keeps the mic indicator on.
recommendation: Throttle detection to ~20-30 Hz and reuse buffers, or move YIN into an AudioWorklet or Worker using FFT-based autocorrelation. Separate setting the error from the reset, for example stop({ keepError: true }). Guard start() with a cancelled flag or AbortController. Request raw audio in getAudioStream (echoCancellation, noiseSuppression and autoGainControl all false). Show 'Choose an input' when there is no device.
verifierNote: The code matches the finding. yinDetectSingle runs every rAF on a 4096-sample buffer with an O(tauLimit x 2048) difference loop and allocates two Float32Arrays per call (useTuner.ts:173-225, YinCore.ts:266-281). stop() resets error to null (useTuner.ts:126) after setError at 159-164/226-229, start() returns silently with no deviceId (144), and getAudioStream leaves echo cancellation, noise suppression and auto gain on (AudioInputEnumerator.ts:66-70). Severity is lower than claimed because the tuner is opt-in and usually used while the transport is stopped.
impactNote: yinDetectSingle on a 4096-sample buffer runs every rAF with no throttle (useTuner.ts:173-225). That is an O(tau x N/2) difference function, about 3.6M multiply-adds, with two Float32Array allocations per call (YinCore.ts:267-281), and the RMS gate skips it in silence. stop() calls setError(null) (useTuner.ts:126), and both error paths call setError then stop() (159-164, 226-229), so error text can never render. With no deviceId, start() returns before setActive (144). An unmount during await getAudioStream leaks the stream and context. All confirmed. Downgraded because the cost only applies while the tuner is open on Guitar/Bass/Vocal views and a note is sounding, which is usually a dedicated tuning moment rather than editing. The silent-error UX bug is real but low impact.
regressionRisks: Throttling to 20-30 Hz changes needle responsiveness, and NOTE_HOLD_FRAMES and CENTS_ALPHA are frame-count based, so they need retuning. Turning off echo cancellation and noise suppression in getAudioStream affects any other consumer of AudioInputEnumerator.getAudioStream. Integrated mode shares the DAW analyser, so don't change its fftSize.

title: A zero-length loop is passed to Tone unchecked and fires the loop handler on every tick
evidence:
useTransport writes loop points straight to Tone (useTransport.ts:47-53). Tone doesn't validate them (Transport.js:350-361), and it loops whenever ticks >= loopEnd, checked on every tick (Transport.js:119-127, Clock.js:223-225).

toggleLoop fits the loop to a selected MIDI clip's last note end (transportSlice.ts:227-237). For an empty clip that end is 0, so loopEnd equals loopStart. setLoopRange and updateEditorLoop don't enforce end > start either (transportSlice.ts:251-257).

Each 'loop' event runs handleLoop: allNotesOff on every track, plus cancelling and rescheduling all audio clips and automation (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-905).
impact: Select a freshly created empty clip, press Loop, then Play: handleLoop can run about 960 times a second at 120 BPM. The editor freezes and audio stops.
recommendation: In useTransport, enable Tone looping only when end - start is at least one beat; otherwise disable the loop or extend it to one bar. Fit loops to the clip's own length rather than its last note. Clamp the range in setLoopRange and updateEditorLoop.
verifierNote: For a MIDI clip, toggleLoop sets loopEnd = startTick + the last note end (transportSlice.ts:227-237), so an empty clip gives loopEnd == loopStart. setLoopRange doesn't enforce end > start (251-252), and useTransport.ts:48-53 passes the values straight to Tone. Tone's _processTick loops whenever ticks >= loopEnd (Transport.js:119-127), at PPQ 480 (AudioEngine.ts:83), and each loop event runs the full handleLoop rescheduling.
impactNote: toggleLoop fits loopEnd to the selected MIDI clip's last note end (transportSlice.ts:227-237), which equals loopStart for an empty clip. setLoopRange (251-252) and updateEditorLoop don't enforce end > start. useTransport writes loop points to Tone unchecked (useTransport.ts:47-53). Tone's _processTick loops whenever ticks >= loopEnd (Transport.js:119-127), so with loopEnd == loopStart, 'loop' fires on every tick (PPQ 480, so about 960 per second at 120 BPM). Each one runs handleLoop: allNotesOff, audio cancel and reschedule, and automation reschedule (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-905). The playhead sticks and playback stalls. A hard freeze is plausible but unverified; the user can recover by toggling Loop off. The trigger is narrow (empty clip selected, then Loop, then Play), so medium. The fix is trivial.
regressionRisks: Clamping or extending the range changes what Loop does for a clip-selected toggle. Fitting to clip length instead of the last note changes existing loop behaviour users may rely on (fitting to note content). The editor loop (piano roll) and project loop share getPlaybackLoop, so clamp both. Saved projects with a degenerate loop range should be sanitised at deserialize.

title: The chord detector writes to the store ~40 times a second, and its intended consumer is never mounted
evidence:
On every 50 ms frame with confidence > 0.5 the detector calls pushLiveChord, and on every frame with a result it calls setGlobalTuningCents, with no check for change (useAudioChordDetection.ts:174-186). pushLiveChord copies the array each time (musicIntelligenceSlice.ts:118-131). The 30-entry window was sized for '~30 seconds at ~1 chord/sec' (61-62) but in practice holds about 1.5 s of duplicates.

useLiveUnisonAnalysis, the main consumer of the stream, is not called anywhere; a search finds only its definition. So liveAnalysis and the 'unison-live' key source are dead.

useStoreBridge subscribes the synth panels to the stream unconditionally (useStoreBridge.ts:108) and re-applies the arp mask on each push (111-129).
impact: While a student plays into an armed guitar or vocal track, OracleSynthInline and OracleSynthView re-render 20 times a second, autosave never fires, and collab presence is rebroadcast 40 times a second (see engine-hooks-01 and -15). All of this is for data that nothing reads.
recommendation: Push only when the chord's root or quality changes, and only for tuning changes over 1 cent. Make the stream window time-based. Either mount useLiveUnisonAnalysis deliberately or delete it. In useStoreBridge, subscribe to a derived 'last chord' key, and only when arpChordAware is on.
verifierNote: pushLiveChord and setGlobalTuningCents are called on every 50 ms frame with no change check (useAudioChordDetection.ts:175-186). Zustand set always notifies, and pushLiveChord copies the array (musicIntelligenceSlice.ts:118-131). A grep shows useLiveUnisonAnalysis is never called outside its definition. useStoreBridge subscribes to liveChordStream unconditionally (useStoreBridge.ts:108).

title: Instruments that finish loading after their engine was replaced are leaked
evidence:
usePlaybackEngine.ts:496-559 creates the instrument, then instrument.init(ctx, trackEngine.getInputNode()).then(...) attaches it with setInstrument. Nothing can cancel this.

The TrackEngine is disposed while the instrument is still unattached if any of these happen before init resolves:
- the track's instrument type changes (416-420)
- the track is deleted (388-396)
- the editor unmounts (1187-1191)

TrackEngine.dispose only disposes an attached instrument (TrackEngine.ts:205-206, this.instrument?.dispose()), so it can't reach this one. The .then later attaches the instrument to the dead engine and bumps engineReadyVersion.
impact: Clicking through instruments to audition sounds leaves behind a loaded sampler (sample buffers and a Tone graph) for each one that was still loading. Memory grows over a session, especially on Chromebooks and iPads.
recommendation: Track a per-track init token or AbortController. In the .then, if the engine was disposed or the token changed, dispose the instrument and return. Let TrackEngine.dispose also take care of a pending instrument.
verifierNote: instrument.init(...).then(() => trackEngine.setInstrument(instrument)) has no cancellation (usePlaybackEngine.ts:508-511). If the engine is disposed first (416-420, 388-396, 1187-1191), TrackEngine.dispose only disposes an attached instrument (TrackEngine.ts:189), so the late instrument leaks and is attached to a dead engine.

title: Components read the engine registry during render, so meters bind to missing or disposed analysers
evidence:
TrackHeader reads the analyser via getTrackAudioState(track.id) during render (TrackHeader.tsx:91-93). EffectsPanel memoizes the effect chain on selectedTrackId only (EffectsPanel.tsx:185-190).

TrackEngines are created or replaced in a passive effect that runs after that render (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-574), and their creation isn't observable: engineReadyVersion only bumps when an instrument finishes init (557-558).

So after the first audio unlock, after adding a track, or after an instrument swap, the memoized header keeps a null or disposed analyser until something else happens to re-render it.
impact: Track meters and compressor gain-reduction meters stay dead after a student adds a track or changes its instrument, until they happen to change the selection. The mixer looks broken.
recommendation: Make the registry observable. Add subscribeTrackEngine(trackId) and a useTrackEngine(trackId) hook built on useSyncExternalStore, with a per-track version bumped on create, replace and dispose. Meters should subscribe by track id instead of holding node references.
verifierNote: TrackHeader is memo'd and reads getTrackAudioState during render (TrackHeader.tsx:91-93), and the engine is only created in the later passive effect (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-574). Nothing makes TrackHeader re-render once the engine exists; it doesn't subscribe to engineReady (only VocalView, OrganView, GuitarBassView and useOracleSynthInstance do). EffectsPanel memoizes the chain on selectedTrackId only (EffectsPanel.tsx:185-190).

title: The first downbeat after a count-in lands late
evidence:
Count-in clicks are scheduled on the audio clock (usePlaybackEngine.ts:793-809). The transport start, though, goes through a chain of main-thread steps:
1. a setTimeout (813-818)
2. the _startAfterCountIn store write
3. a React render of the whole DawApp tree, since isPlaying is subscribed there (see engine-hooks-02)
4. useTransport's passive effect
5. transport.start() at 'now' (useTransport.ts:56-64)
impact: Timer jitter plus a full editor render and effect flush delay bar 1 relative to the last click. Players who come in on the downbeat are early against the recording, and there is an audible hiccup between the count-in and the song.
recommendation: At count-in start, compute t0 = clickStart + totalBeats x beatDuration and call transport.start(t0) directly, arming recording at t0 too. Use the timer only to flip UI state.
verifierNote: Count-in clicks are scheduled on the audio clock from Tone.now() (usePlaybackEngine.ts:793-809). The transport start goes through setTimeout, then _startAfterCountIn (813-818), then a store write that re-renders DawAppInner (isPlaying is subscribed via useTransport.ts:26), then the useTransport passive effect calling transport.start() at now() (63-64).

title: Leaving and re-entering the editor leaves the shared transport running and audio off until the next click
evidence:
On leaving:
- useTransport has no unmount cleanup (useTransport.ts:55-70).
- usePlaybackEngine's unmount cleanup cancels schedulers and disposes engines, but neither pauses Tone.Transport nor resets isPlaying (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1170-1194).
- The transport is an app-wide singleton that curriculum features also use; for example useMetronome.ts:108 starts it without resetting loop.

On returning:
- useAudioEngine starts with isReady false even though audioEngine is already initialized (useAudioEngine.ts:10; lines 14-17 only run via initEngine).
- DawApp only calls initEngine on the next click or keydown (DawApp.tsx:435-447), so no TrackEngines exist until then. MIDI input is dropped, meters are dead, and the synth panel says 'Synth engine not available'.

No retry: the init promise is cached even if it rejects (useAudioEngine.ts:18-21), and the once-only listeners don't re-arm, so a failed init can't be retried.
impact: A student coming back from a lesson finds a silent editor until they click something. If they left mid-playback, the transport is still running with the DAW's loop and BPM underneath other features.
recommendation: Initialise isReady from audioEngine.getIsInitialized() (useState(() => ...)). On unmount, pause the transport and set isPlaying to false; if background playback is wanted instead, keep the engines alive. Clear initPromise on rejection and re-arm the listeners.
verifierNote: useTransport has no unmount pause (useTransport.ts:56-70), and the usePlaybackEngine unmount cleanup (1170-1194) disposes engines but doesn't pause Tone.Transport or reset isPlaying. useAudioEngine starts with useState(false) even when audioEngine is already initialized (useAudioEngine.ts:10), so engines are only rebuilt after the next click or keydown (DawApp.tsx:435-447). A rejected init promise stays cached (18-21).

title: The on-screen playhead runs ahead of what students hear
evidence: useTransport pushes Math.round(Tone.getTransport().ticks) to the store (useTransport.ts:82). Transport.ticks reads the clock at this.now() (Clock.js:137-139), which is currentTime + 0.1 s lookAhead (Context.js:329-331), and output latency isn't subtracted. MidiRecorder already compensates for exactly this lead: its comment says 'transport.ticks is ahead of audible position' (MidiRecorder.ts:65-68).
impact: The playhead, score and lead-sheet highlighting, and the practice view all lead the audio by about 100 ms plus device latency. On Bluetooth earbuds the lead is much larger. At 120 BPM that is close to a full 16th note early, which undermines play-along teaching.
recommendation: Derive the displayed tick from transport.getTicksAtTime(Tone.immediate() - ctx.outputLatency), clamped to at least 0. Share it with the playhead channel in engine-hooks-25.
verifierNote: useTransport.ts:82 publishes Math.round(Tone.getTransport().ticks). Those ticks are evaluated at now() (currentTime plus lookAhead), which MidiRecorder.ts:65-68 explicitly compensates for ('transport.ticks is ahead of audible position'). There's no outputLatency correction anywhere.

title: The 30 fps playhead goes through the main store and wakes every whole-store listener
evidence:
useTransport.ts:79-93 calls setPosition every 33 ms while playing. Besides the components that select position, every whole-store listener runs on each write:
- useAutosave restarts its debounce (useAutosave.ts:19-24).
- CollabProvider rebroadcasts presence (CollabProvider.tsx:541-562).
- An active lesson re-evaluates its step check (useTutorialDetection.ts:51).
impact: The cost of playback grows with every new store listener. This is the root cause of the autosave starvation (engine-hooks-01) and the collab presence storm (engine-hooks-15).
recommendation: Keep the authoritative position in the transport. Publish the audible tick on a separate small external store or event emitter, consumed by playhead and score components through useSyncExternalStore or direct DOM transforms. Write the main store's position only on pause, stop and seek.
verifierNote: setPosition fires every 33 ms while playing (useTransport.ts:79-93). Whole-store subscribers run on each write: useAutosave (useAutosave.ts:19), CollabProvider presence (whose selector always returns a new object, CollabProvider.tsx:542-560), and useTutorialDetection (useTutorialDetection.ts:51).

title: Always-on polling loops run while the editor is idle
evidence:
- useAudioChordDetection keeps a rAF loop alive for the life of the editor, and scans tracks every 50 ms even with nothing armed (useAudioChordDetection.ts:60-106, 290).
- useGuitarMidiDetection runs a 300 ms setInterval plus a rAF flush loop even with no Guitar-to-MIDI binding (useGuitarMidiDetection.ts:102-114, 178-180).
- useStudioMonitor runs a rAF even outside collab (useStudioMonitor.ts:118-138).
- Each meter keeps its own rAF and analyser reads while stopped and silent (useMeterLevel.ts:24-48).
- usePitchInfo polls at 20 Hz while the vocal view is open, whether or not there is audio (usePitchInfo.ts:12-21), although PitchCorrectionNode already offers a push callback (PitchCorrectionNode.ts:145-149, 181-183).
impact: A dozen or more timers wake the main thread every frame with nothing to do. That drains battery and adds input latency on the school Chromebooks students use, and adds jank when the editor is busy.
recommendation: Create one 'engine clock' service with explicit activation conditions: playing, recording, an armed input, peers present, or meters visible. It starts and stops the shared rAF work. Make guitar-MIDI reconciliation event-driven by subscribing to audioMidiSource and input changes. Pause everything while document.hidden.

title: Device status misleads: red 'MIDI unavailable, use Chrome/Edge' with no keyboard plugged in, and a blocked mic looks like 'no device'
evidence:
MIDI status:
- useMidiDevices sets 'unavailable' whenever there are zero inputs (useMidiDevices.ts:22) and on any init failure (39-44).
- MidiDeviceManager.init swallows the error reason (MidiDeviceManager.ts:46-47).
- TransportBar renders this as a red 9 px 'MIDI' pill with the tooltip 'MIDI: Unavailable — use Chrome/Edge' and hard-coded #22c55e/#ef4444 (TransportBar.tsx:840-877).

Before the first click:
- No TrackEngines exist yet (useAudioEngine.ts:10; DawApp.tsx:435-447).
- MIDI notes are dropped, with console-only warnings for the first three (useMidiInputRouting.ts:121-141).

title: A new Oracle Synth track opens with the previous synth track's patch
evidence:
useStoreBridge's comment says the new track's state is restored 'or defaults are used for first visit' (useStoreBridge.ts:19-22). On a switch, though, it only calls restoreCachedSynthState(trackId) (47-49), which leaves the shared store untouched when the track has no cache entry (synthTrackState.ts:179-186).

Cache entries are only seeded on project load (setTrackSynthState is called only at SessionSerializer.ts:556 and 721) or when leaving a track. setActiveSynthTrack(trackId) (53) then makes the inherited patch the new track's saved patch, and useSyncStoreToEngine pushes it into the new engine (71).
impact: A student adding a second synth (for example bass plus pad) gets a copy of the first one's sound and preset name, contrary to the hook's documented behaviour. The copy is saved, so it is still there after a reload.
recommendation: On a track's first visit, restore a default patch or the track's chosen preset via synthTrackStateFromPreset, and seed the cache when the track is created. If copying a sound is wanted, make it an explicit 'Duplicate sound' action.
