The only seeding is in SessionSerializer.ts:556/721 and in bridge switch/unmount (useStoreBridge.ts:39, 64), so a new synth track inherits the live store patch. setActiveSynthTrack (53) then makes it that track's saved patch, contrary to the comment at 19-22.

title: Synth panels re-render on every edit and say 'not available' while the synth is just loading
evidence: useOracleSynthInstance subscribes to the whole tracks array just to read one track's instrument and name (useOracleSynthInstance.ts:14-24). So OracleSynthInline, OracleSynthView and OracleSynthPanel re-render on every note or fader edit anywhere. engine is null both before audio is unlocked and while the instrument initialises (26-35), and OracleSynthInline shows 'Synth engine not available' in both cases (OracleSynthInline.tsx:41-48).
impact: The heaviest instrument UI re-renders during unrelated drags, and a normal loading moment reads as an error to students.
recommendation: Select primitives instead: the selected track's instrument and name, or a memoized selector. Return a status of 'audio-locked', 'loading' or 'ready', and render 'Click anywhere to enable audio' or a loading skeleton to match.
verifierNote: useOracleSynthInstance subscribes to the whole tracks array (useOracleSynthInstance.ts:15) to read one track's instrument and name. Its engine is null both before unlock and during init (26-35), and OracleSynthInline renders 'Synth engine not available' for either case (OracleSynthInline.tsx:42-48).

title: MIDI import drops tempo, time signature, sustain pedal and instruments
evidence: importMidiFile maps only track.notes (MidiFileIO.ts:29-52). It discards @tonejs/midi's header tempos and time signatures, track.controlChanges (including the CC64 sustain pedal) and track.instrument (GM program and percussion flag). FileMenu then creates every imported part as an Oracle Synth track (FileMenu.tsx:294-299) and leaves the project BPM unchanged.
impact: An imported song plays at the project's tempo instead of its own, without its sustain pedal, with drums as pitched synth notes and every part on the same patch. Students conclude the import is broken. GarageBand, Logic and BandLab-style imports adopt the file's tempo and instruments.
recommendation: Return tempo, time signature and per-sequence program, percussion flag and CC events from importMidiFile. Offer 'Use the file's tempo (92 BPM)?' when importing into a session. Map percussion to the drum machine and GM programs to the SoundFont instrument. Import CC64 into clip.ccEvents, which MidiScheduler already supports.
verifierNote: importMidiFile maps only track.notes (MidiFileIO.ts:33-48) and drops the header tempos, time signatures, controlChanges and instrument. FileMenu creates every part as 'oracle-synth' (FileMenu.tsx:294-299) and never touches BPM.

title: Synth pop-out text shrinks to 5-7 px, and the panel flashes at half size on open
evidence: useContainerScale scales a fixed 1440x932 design canvas uniformly, with scale = min(w/1440, h/932) (useContainerScale.ts:5-6, 27-31), applied as a CSS transform (DawSynthLayout.tsx:123-127). The oracle-synth component CSS has many small labels: font-size 8px x3, 9px x14, 10px x9, 11px x12. A 600 px-tall overlay gives a scale of about 0.64, so 9 px labels render at about 5.8 px. The initial state is scale 0.5, and the measurement runs in useEffect after paint (17-21, 23-43), so the first frame is drawn at the wrong scale.
impact: On 1366x768 Chromebooks the full-screen synth is barely legible and its controls are tiny targets, which compounds A11Y#19. The panel also visibly jumps when it opens.
recommendation: Measure in useLayoutEffect, or keep the panel hidden until measured. Clamp the minimum scale (for example 0.85) and let the layout scroll or reflow below that. Longer term, make the synth layout responsive using the app's text scale.
verifierNote: useContainerScale applies min(w/1440, h/932) uniformly (useContainerScale.ts:5-6, 27-31) via a CSS transform (DawSynthLayout.tsx:123-127), and the synth CSS has 3x8px, 14x9px, 9x10px and 12x11px labels, so text gets tiny. The half-size flash claim is weaker: the initial scale is 0.5 and the measurement is in useEffect, but React 18 flushes passive effects synchronously for click-triggered renders, so a visible first frame is not guaranteed.

title: The 'LUFS' readout is the peak level rescaled, not a loudness measurement
evidence: LufsMeter (StudioView.tsx:190-244) averages two useMeterLevel values (0-100 = peak sample deviation, useMeterLevel.ts:22-44). It then prints `lufs = avg > 0 ? -14 + (avg / 100) * 14 : -Infinity` with two decimals (198-199). There is no K-weighting, gating or time integration. The MASTER screenshot (docs/ux-research/accessibility-evidence/a11y-studio-MASTER.png) shows a master peak of '-18.1 dB' next to '-12.25 LUFS'. Both come from the same value (avg ≈ 12.5), just relabelled.
impact: Anything audible reads between -14 and 0 'LUFS'. A quiet mix peaking at -30 dBFS shows about -13.6, which looks like it is at a streaming loudness target. On an education platform this teaches the wrong loudness concept and the wrong mastering target, and the two-decimal precision makes it look authoritative.
recommendation: Either implement real loudness (BS.1770 K-weighting filters with 400 ms momentary and 3 s short-term windows in an AudioWorklet, plus an Integrated value that resets on play), or rename it 'Level' and show honest dBFS peak or RMS. Only add target markings (e.g. -14 LUFS) once the measurement is real.
verifierNote: LufsMeter averages two peak values from useMeterLevel and prints `-14 + (avg/100)*14` (StudioView.tsx:196-199), with no weighting, gating or integration. The screenshot is consistent: avg 12.5 gives -18.1 dB on the strip and -12.25 'LUFS'.
impactNote: In StudioView.tsx:190-199, LufsMeter averages two peak values from useMeterLevel (peak sample deviation, 0-100; useMeterLevel.ts:22-44). It then maps them linearly to -14..0 and prints two decimals. There is no weighting, gating or integration. The screenshot shows a master peak of -18.1 dB next to -12.25 'LUFS'. The claim is correct, but students rarely act on this number, and the harm is teaching the wrong concept rather than a broken workflow. That is medium, not high. The cheap fix of renaming it and showing honest dBFS takes minutes.
regressionRisks: Low. Renaming the label or changing the scale doesn't touch audio or persistence. A real BS.1770 AudioWorklet adds an audio-thread node on the master. That path needs careful loading and teardown (Chromebook CPU, worklet module loading under Tone's context). If the meter's markup changes, check that no tutorial step anchors on it; mastering-section is the anchor.

title: Undo ignores mastering and return-bus edits, so Cmd+Z undoes an unrelated earlier edit
evidence: Solo undo captures and restores only `tracks`, `chordRegions` and MARK_KEYS (undoMiddleware.ts:45-59, 111-127), and subscribes only to those keys (257-264). `pushUndo` (130) has no callers. masteringFxChain, masteringEffects, masteringBypass, masterVolume and returns are not among them. Collab undo tracks only the tracks, chordRegions and markers Y.Arrays (278-286).
impact:
Undo only reverts track and score edits. After any of these changes, Cmd+Z restores the previous track snapshot instead, and the mastering or return change stays:
- adding or removing a mastering or return effect
- turning a mastering knob
- moving the master or return fader

That can undo the student's last note edit or track-fader move from minutes earlier. Per-track FX are undoable but master and return FX are not, even though they use the same rack UI.
recommendation: Add the mastering and returns keys to the undo snapshot (capture, restore and watched) and to the collab UndoManager scope, for example through a Y.Map for the mastering doc. Combine this with the commit-on-release drag model from fx-mixer-07 so one knob drag is one undo entry.
verifierNote: capture/restore cover only tracks, chordRegions and MARK_KEYS (undoMiddleware.ts:45-59, 111-127). The subscriptions cover only those keys (257-264), and the collab UndoManager scope is tracks, chordRegions and markers (278-286). Mastering and returns edits never create a snapshot, so Cmd+Z reverts the previous track or score edit instead.
impactNote: Undo captures, restores and subscribes only to tracks, chordRegions and MARK_KEYS (undoMiddleware.ts:45-59, 194-205, 257-264). masterAutomation is included, but masteringFxChain, masteringEffects, masteringBypass, masterVolume and returns are not. After a mastering or return edit, Cmd+Z silently reverts the previous track or score snapshot instead. That is confusing and can quietly undo a note edit the student wanted to keep. Redo exists, and many users won't use Cmd+Z in MASTER, so I'd rate this medium rather than high. It's still worth fixing alongside fx-mixer-01, since both need the same mastering snapshot shape.
regressionRisks: Adding masteringEffects and returns to the JSON snapshot increases the per-change cost in fx-mixer-07, so do the reference-check reorder first. Restoring a mastering snapshot rebuilds the EffectChain through usePlaybackEngine. Restores during playback could click, especially the reverb true-bypass rewiring. Collab undo needs the Y 'mastering' map in UndoManager scope, and it currently holds fxChain and effects as JSON strings, so undo granularity is whole-object. Snapshot restore must keep fxChain and the enabled flags consistent. Tutorial checks comparing `now.effects !== before.effects` (tutorials.ts:712-715) could be satisfied or un-satisfied by an undo.

title: The FX chain is drawn in the order effects were added, but the audio runs in a fixed order
evidence:
FxChainRow maps `activeEffects` in insertion order between an 'In' and an 'Out' block joined by a connection line (EffectsPanel.tsx:302-314, 344-405). Adding an effect appends it (tracksSlice.ts:790 `[...t.activeEffects, effectType]`, masteringSlice.ts:160).

The engine wires a fixed graph: EQ → gate → compressor/crush/makeup (EffectChain.ts:859-879) → presence → de-esser (921-924, 977) → reverb → delay (1041-1052) → saturator (1097-1103) → OTT (1150-1156) → sidechain (1208-1220, 656). Only `track.effects` is synced (usePlaybackEngine.ts:426). The header comments at EffectChain.ts:7 and 825 each list yet another order, and there is no reorder UI.
impact: Add Saturator, then Reverb, and the rack shows 'In → Saturator → Reverb → Out' while the audio actually runs Reverb → Saturator, distorting the reverb tails. For a product that teaches signal flow, the picture contradicts what students hear, and lessons can't discuss insert order.
recommendation: Short term: draw the blocks sorted by a shared ENGINE_ORDER constant and say 'Effects run left to right in a fixed order'. Longer term: make the order real by rebuilding the chain from activeEffects order, and add drag-to-reorder like Ableton and openDAW device chains.
verifierNote: addActiveEffect appends in insertion order (tracksSlice.ts:790) and FxChainRow maps activeEffects in that order (EffectsPanel.tsx:357+). EffectChain.buildChain wires a fixed graph (EffectChain.ts:859-924+), and no audio file reads activeEffects. The header comments at lines 7 and 825 also disagree with each other.

title: Meters and the EQ spectrum lock onto audio nodes at render time and go dead after an engine is created or rebuilt
evidence:
EffectsPanel memoises `getTrackAudioState(selectedTrackId)?.trackEngine.getEffectChain() ?? null` with deps `[selectedTrackId]` only (EffectsPanel.tsx:185-190). MixingStrip reads `getTrackAudioState(trackId)?.trackEngine.getAnalyserNode()` during render (StudioView.tsx:614-616) and is React.memo'd on trackId.

TrackEngines are created in a useEffect after the store update (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-574) and recreated when a track's instrument changes (416-420), and no store change follows. `subscribeEngineReady` and `getEngineReadyVersion` already exist (94-106) and OrganView, VocalView and GuitarBassView use them, but these components don't.

ReturnFxRack hard-codes `gr={0} inLevel={0} outLevel={0} analyserNode={null}` (StudioView.tsx:1053-1056), although FxBrowser only hides the ducker on returns (FxBrowser.tsx:32-43), so a compressor or EQ can be added there.
impact:
Each of these leaves the compressor gain-reduction and IN/OUT meters, the EQ spectrum and the mixer strip meters flat until the student reselects the track or touches that strip's fader:
- adding a track while the FX tab is open
- changing a track's instrument
- opening a project or joining a collab session while in MASTER

Students read that as 'my compressor isn't doing anything'.
recommendation: Add a `useTrackEffectChain(trackId)` / `useTrackAnalyser(trackId)` hook that re-resolves through `useSyncExternalStore(subscribeEngineReady, getEngineReadyVersion)`, and bump that version whenever a TrackEngine is created or replaced. Expose the return-bus chains from AudioEngine and pass real meters to ReturnFxRack, or hide the meters there.
verifierNote: EffectsPanel memoises the chain on [selectedTrackId] only (EffectsPanel.tsx:185-190). MixingStrip resolves the analyser during render (StudioView.tsx:614-616), but TrackEngines are created or replaced in a later effect (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-420) and neither component subscribes to subscribeEngineReady (94-106), so a strip mounted before its engine keeps null. ReturnFxRack hard-codes meters to 0/null (StudioView.tsx:1053-1056), although only the ducker is hidden on bus racks (FxBrowser.tsx:32-43).

title: The docked rack is a wall of knobs; the visualizers are only behind an unlabelled pop-out
evidence:
FxControlsPanel shows only FxKnobs inline (EffectsPanel.tsx:544-552). The curve and meter views (CompressorCurve, GraphicEQ, ReverbDecay, DelayTaps, GateCurve) are rendered only inside PopOutOverlay (554-588). That opens from an icon-only Maximize2 button with no label or title (519-529).

The inline EQ is 8 bands × 5 controls (band tab, FREQ, GAIN, curve-type cycler, Q) plus MAKEUP: 41 controls and no curve (811-913). It sits in a dock fixed at 33vh (ChannelStrip.tsx:318) whose chain row already takes 110 px (EffectsPanel.tsx:300). FxShared's InlineViz (372-395) exists but nothing uses it.

From CREATE, the Master FX are already in a 70vw×70vh pop-out (MasterTrackHeader.tsx:214-221), so pressing Maximize opens a second pop-out of the same size on top.
impact: The views that make effects understandable, such as watching the EQ curve move or seeing gain reduction on the transfer curve, are hidden by default. The default EQ is the hardest representation for a beginner. Students scroll a small dock to reach knobs, and the nested pop-out is confusing.
recommendation:
Show a compact inline visualizer for the selected effect:
- EQ: the graph with draggable nodes as the main control, with knobs for the selected band only.
- Compressor: curve plus a gain-reduction meter.
- Reverb and delay: their sketches.

Turn the pop-out into a labelled 'Expand' button. Remove the nested pop-out by opening the master rack in the dock or detail area.
verifierNote: FxControlsPanel shows only FxKnobs inline. FxVisualizer is rendered only inside PopOutOverlay (EffectsPanel.tsx:544-588), opened by an icon-only Maximize2 button with no label (519-529). The dock is 33vh (ChannelStrip.tsx:318), no file imports InlineViz, and MasterTrackHeader already opens MasterFxPanel inside a PopOutOverlay (214-221), so maximising nests a second pop-out.

title: The mixer has no way to reach a track's effects
evidence: The dock that hosts EffectsPanel (`<ChannelStrip />`, DawApp.tsx:511) is only rendered in the arrange branch (496-514). The MASTER branch renders just StudioView and LibraryPanel (519-523). MixingStrip (StudioView.tsx:593-752) has no insert list, no FX button and no click handler that selects the track.
impact: To EQ or compress a track while balancing the mix, a student has to leave MASTER, find the track in CREATE, open the dock and the FX tab, then come back, losing the mixer context each time. Channel strips in Logic, Ableton, Soundation and BandLab expose the inserts and open them in place.
recommendation: Show a compact insert list (effect names with power dots) on each strip. Clicking it selects the track and opens that track's FX rack in the MASTER view's detail area, using the same component as the master and return racks.
verifierNote: ChannelStrip (the dock with EffectsPanel) is only rendered in the arrange/practice branch (DawApp.tsx:496-514), and the studio branch renders StudioView plus LibraryPanel (519-523). MixingStrip (StudioView.tsx:593-752) has no FX button, insert list or select handler.

title: The master fader's dB readout is wrong and disagrees with the CREATE view
evidence: The master gain is set to the linear fader value (`gain.gain.setTargetAtTime(vol, …)`, usePlaybackEngine.ts:234-241; default 0.8, masteringSlice.ts:91). MasterStrip prints `masterVolume === 80 ? '0 dB' : (levelToDb(masterVolume) + 1.9).toFixed(1) + ' dB'` (StudioView.tsx:845-853). That labels -1.94 dB as '0 dB' and unity gain as '+1.9 dB'. MasterTrackHeader prints `20 * Math.log10(masterVolume)` (MasterTrackHeader.tsx:207-209). So the same fader reads '0 dB' in MASTER and '-1.9' in CREATE.
impact: Students learning gain staging are told the master is at unity when it isn't, and the two views contradict each other.
recommendation: Use one formatter for every fader: true 20·log10(gain), with '-∞' at 0. Alternatively, switch to a dB-scaled fader law with a marked unity detent. Show the fader value on every strip.
verifierNote: MasterStrip prints '0 dB' when masterVolume===80 and otherwise `levelToDb(masterVolume)+1.9` (StudioView.tsx:845-853), so the actual -1.94 dB reads as 0 and unity reads as +1.9. MasterTrackHeader prints `20*log10(masterVolume)` (MasterTrackHeader.tsx:207-209), so the two views disagree.

title: Strip readouts and labels are unclear: peak shown instead of fader value, fake stereo meters, unlabelled sends, return strips without meters
evidence:
The most prominent text on each strip is the live peak (DbReadout, 11 px bold, green/yellow/red: StudioView.tsx:424-434, 631). It is not the fader value, and track strips have no fader readout.

Two MeterBars show the same mono analyser on either side of the fader (663-665, 698-700). TrackEngine has a single AnalyserNode tapped after the panner (TrackEngine.ts:29-31, 40).

Sends are 26 px knobs labelled 'A'/'B' with unitless 0-100 values; the bus name is only in a hover title (709-730), yet the tutorial asks for 'past 25%' (tutorials.ts:691-704). 'Mute All' only mutes and doesn't show or reverse its state (774-778, 794-804). Return strips have no meter and no mute, and are selected by clicking anywhere on a div, hinted only by a 9 px '1 FX' (886-889, 951-953).
impact: Students can't see the level they set. They read the duplicate pair as stereo, which is misleading when learning panning. On touch devices they can't find out what A and B are. They can't hear or mute a return on its own.
recommendation: On each strip: show the fader value in dB under the fader, and one meter (or real L/R). Label sends by return name with % units. Make Mute All a real toggle or remove it. Give return strips a meter, a mute and an explicit 'FX' button.
verifierNote: DbReadout shows the live peak (StudioView.tsx:631) and the track strip has no fader readout. Both MeterBars receive the same liveLevel from the single post-panner analyser (663-665, 698-700; TrackEngine.ts:29-40). Sends are RotaryKnobs labelled 'A'/'B' with the bus name only in a hover title (709-730). Mute All only mutes (774-778), and ReturnStrip has no meter or mute (886-956).

title: Spectrum analyser never resizes, redraws everything every frame, and retunes the shared meter analysers
evidence:
SpectrumAnalyzer measures its container once, when isReady changes (StudioView.tsx:55-60; deps `[isReady]` at 168), with no ResizeObserver. LibraryPanel beside it animates its width from 0 to 200 on mount and toggle (LibraryPanel.tsx:87-93).

The draw loop (95-164) runs every frame, playing or not, and reads only the left channel. Each frame it re-strokes the dB grid, builds a roughly 1,000-point array, creates two gradients, fills twice and redraws the labels.

It also sets `analyserL.fftSize = 2048; smoothingTimeConstant = 0.85` (62-63) on the master meter analyser. AudioEngine created that analyser at 256 / 0 for metering (AudioEngine.ts:55-61), and the change is never undone. GraphicEQ does the same to the pre-compressor analyser that feeds the IN meter (GraphicEQ.tsx:383-384). In the EQ pop-out, 'IN' and 'OUT' are actually the post-EQ/gate and post-compressor taps (EffectsPanel.tsx:1542-1556; EffectChain.ts:867-879).
impact: Toggling the library or resizing the window clips the spectrum, cutting off the high-frequency labels, or leaves a blank band. Entering MASTER with the library open measures the canvas mid-animation. The constant full redraw uses frame time even when stopped. After MASTER has been visited, the left master meter peaks over a 2,048-sample window and the right over 256, so L reads hotter than R on centred material. The EQ's 'IN' meter is not the EQ input.
recommendation: Use a ResizeObserver and DPR handling, as GraphicEQ already does. Draw the grid and labels once to an offscreen layer, and pause the loop when stopped. Give the spectrum its own L and R AnalyserNodes instead of retuning the metering taps. Relabel the EQ meters 'Post-EQ' and 'Out', or tap the true EQ input.
verifierNote: SpectrumAnalyzer measures once with deps [isReady] and has no ResizeObserver (StudioView.tsx:55-60, 168), while LibraryPanel animates its width 0→200 (LibraryPanel.tsx:87-93). The rAF redraw runs unconditionally (95-164). It sets analyserL.fftSize=2048 permanently (62-63) on the analyser AudioEngine created at 256 (AudioEngine.ts:55-61). Because the meter hooks run after it and allocate their buffer from fftSize, the L meter peaks over 2048 samples and R over 256. GraphicEQ retunes preCompAnalyser the same way (GraphicEQ.tsx:383-384).

title: Knob drags on touch screens are likely to scroll the panel instead of turning the knob
evidence: RotaryKnob's svg has `cursor-ns-resize select-none` but no `touch-action: none` (RotaryKnob.tsx:139-147). The knobs sit inside an `overflow-y-auto` container (FxControlsPanel, EffectsPanel.tsx:487-490). PanKnob (StudioView.tsx:549) and the GraphicEQ svg (GraphicEQ.tsx:491) also lack it. `preventDefault()` in onPointerDown does not stop touch panning, and RotaryKnob ends the drag on pointercancel (146). The Radix faders do set `touch-none` (StudioView.tsx:668).
impact: On iPads, which the accessibility audit notes districts use, a vertical drag on a knob in a scrollable rack is likely to scroll the panel and cancel the drag. Effect parameters are then hard to set by touch.
recommendation: Add `touch-none` to every drag surface: knobs, pan and EQ nodes. Consider a tap-to-open larger control on coarse pointers.
verifierNote: The RotaryKnob svg has `cursor-ns-resize select-none` and no touch-action (RotaryKnob.tsx:142). It ends the drag on pointercancel (146) and sits inside the overflow-y-auto FxControlsPanel (EffectsPanel.tsx:487-490). PanKnob also has no touch-none (StudioView.tsx:549), and grep finds no touch-action anywhere in the Effects or Controls knobs. Only the Radix faders set touch-none.

title: Reverb DECAY isn't clamped when the type changes, and the reverb plot puts filter frequencies on its time axis
evidence:
Once the IR manifest loads, the DECAY knob's maximum becomes the impulse response's native length (EffectsPanel.tsx:620-634, `getReverbIrMeta(effects.reverb.type)?.decaySeconds || 10`). The TYPE select only writes `type` (926-935), so the stored decay is never clamped. The default is hall at 2.0 s (EffectChain.ts:148-151), the Room IR is 1.06 s long (public/daw-assets/reverb-irs/manifest.json), and IRs can only be shortened, not lengthened (reverbIR.ts:109-125).

ReverbDecay maps the high-pass and low-pass frequencies (Hz, log2 scale) onto the same x-axis that tToX uses for seconds (ReverbDecay.tsx:114-188).
impact: Switch from Hall to Room and the knob shows '2.0s' with its arc over-rotated past the end. The pop-out draws a 2 s tail while the engine plays the native 1.06 s IR, and the first touch makes the value jump to 1.06. The reverb sketch also draws red 'filtered' regions over time, suggesting the early or late tail is cut.
recommendation: Clamp decay to the new maximum when the type changes, both in the UI and in the store action, and clamp RotaryKnob's angle. Draw the filter band as a separate small frequency strip, or drop it, instead of overlaying it on the time axis.
verifierNote: reverbDecayMax comes from the IR's decaySeconds (EffectsPanel.tsx:632-634), but the TYPE select only writes `type` (926-935). Hall defaults to 2s (EffectChain.ts:148-151) and the Room IR is 1.06s (manifest.json). valueToT is unclamped (RotaryKnob.tsx:23-33), so the arc over-rotates. ReverbDecay maps HP/LP frequencies onto the time-axis plot width (ReverbDecay.tsx:114-188).

title: The FX list can be dragged but nothing accepts the drop, and the 5-effect cap is silent
evidence:
FxRow is `draggable` and puts its payload on DRAG_MIME (FxBrowser.tsx:124-131, 141). No drop handler accepts `kind: 'audio-effect'`: grep finds that string only in FxBrowser and libraryItems. Timeline's handleDrop only handles instrument, template, drum-sample and midi-loop, then returns (Timeline.tsx:2578-2675).

The STAGE 5 lesson step tells students to 'drop a **mastering effect** … onto the master chain' (tutorials.ts:719-723). At MAX_EFFECTS = 5 the rows just fade to 40% opacity with no message (FxBrowser.tsx:13, 28, 115, 147). Clicking an effect already in the chain does nothing (117-122).
impact: Students follow the lesson wording, drag an effect onto the chain, and nothing happens. At the cap, effects look broken. Clicking an existing effect doesn't take them to it.
recommendation: Either make FxChainRow (and track headers) a drop target that inserts at the drop position, or remove `draggable` and change the lesson copy to 'click'. At the cap, show 'Max 5 effects — remove one to add another'. Clicking an effect that's already in the chain should select it.
verifierNote: FxRow is draggable with a DRAG_MIME payload (FxBrowser.tsx:124-141), but outside FxBrowser 'audio-effect' only appears in libraryItems' metadata loop, so no drop target accepts it. At MAX_EFFECTS the rows only fade to 0.4 opacity (115, 147), and handleClick returns early for active effects (117). The tutorial copy says 'drop a mastering effect' (tutorials.ts:719-723).

title: Collab sends whole effect and return objects on every drag step, so simultaneous edits overwrite each other
evidence: Any change to a track's effects runs `yTrack.set('effects', JSON.stringify(nextTrack.effects))` (diffEngine.ts:171-173). Mastering does `yM.set('effects', JSON.stringify(next.masteringEffects))` (472-473), and returns do `yM.set('returns', JSON.stringify(next.returns))` (479-480). These run on every store write, which is every knob or fader pointermove (fx-mixer-07), and the receiving side replaces the whole object.
impact: If two students tweak different master effects at the same time, or one moves a return's volume while another edits its reverb, one person's change is lost. Each of these Y.Map values is last-writer-wins. Every drag step also broadcasts the full effects JSON (ten effect slots, eight EQ bands) to every peer.
recommendation: Store effects as nested Y.Maps per slot and parameter, and returns as a Y.Array of Y.Maps. Send committed values on pointerup, or throttle to about 10 Hz during drags.
verifierNote: diffEngine writes `yTrack.set('effects', JSON.stringify(...))` on any reference change (diffEngine.ts:171-173), and does the same for mastering effects (472-473) and returns (479-480). There is no throttle in src/daw/collab, so every drag step sends the whole object and peers resolve it last-writer-wins.

title: Prism 'Create' silently replaces the track's clips and the song's chord lane
evidence: generateToTracks (prismSlice.ts:1568-1623) calls clearMidiClips(trackId) (1599). It then adds one clip at startTick 0 with durationTicks 7680, commented '4 bars (4 x 4 x 480)' (1601-1606), and replaces chordRegions wholesale (1611-1618). The Create button calls it directly, with no confirmation (PrismStudio.tsx:98-100, 206-223).
impact: A student who recorded or drew a part on a track and then tries Prism on it loses that part, plus every chord symbol elsewhere in the song, with one click. In 3/4 or 6/8 the new clip is the wrong length. Undo is only available as Cmd+Z (ia-flows-18).
recommendation: Insert into a new clip at the playhead or selected bar, and never delete existing clips. Merge chord regions only over that range. Show an 'Added 4 bars — Undo' toast. Compute clip length with ticksPerBar(ts).
verifierNote: generateToTracks calls clearMidiClips(trackId), adds a clip at startTick 0 with durationTicks 7680 (commented '4 bars (4 × 4 × 480)'), and overwrites chordRegions with set() (prismSlice.ts:1597-1618). handleGenerate calls it directly with no confirmation (PrismStudio.tsx:98-100).

PrismStudio's Create (98-100) calls it with no confirmation. Partial: Prism is an iterative generator. The lessons' 'experiment' then 'create' steps (tutorials.ts:181-197) expect Create-again to replace the previous take, so 'never delete existing clips' would stack takes and break that loop. regressionRisks: Changing replace into insert-at-playhead breaks the tutorial flow that expects regeneration, and the Prism clip colour mode. A safer fix: replace only the previously generated Prism clip (tag it) and confirm if the track has other content. Merge chordRegions only over the generated range. Computing length with ticksPerBar must match deriveChordRegions and the worker's output length.

title: Vocal pitch analysis blocks the main thread for seconds
evidence: PitchEditorModal runs analyzeBuffer(buffer) in a setTimeout on the main thread (PitchEditorModal.tsx:35-48). analyzeBuffer steps every 512 samples (PitchAnalyzer.ts:75-91) and calls yinDetectOffline, whose difference function is a 1024 x 1024 nested loop per frame (YinCore.ts:332-347). src/daw/workers holds only midiWorker.ts. There is no progress indicator and no cancel.
impact: One minute of 48 kHz audio is about 5,600 frames x about 1 million multiply-adds. That means several seconds of frozen UI per minute of vocal, up to the 5-minute take cap. Playback scheduling stalls meanwhile.
recommendation: Run the analysis in a worker (transfer the channel data), stream progress with a Cancel button, use an FFT-based difference function, and persist the results in pitchData (ia-flows-03).
verifierNote: PitchEditorModal runs analyzeBuffer synchronously inside setTimeout(…, 50) on the main thread (PitchEditorModal.tsx:42-47). analyzeBuffer hops 512 samples with FRAME_LENGTH 2048 (PitchAnalyzer.ts:62-63, 75-91), and yinDetectOffline runs a 1024x1024 nested difference loop per frame (YinCore.ts:332-347). The only worker is midiWorker.ts. One nuance: a static 'analyzing' state renders (line 140), but it freezes and there is no progress or cancel.
impactNote: PitchEditorModal runs analyzeBuffer in a setTimeout on the main thread (PitchEditorModal.tsx:35-48). analyzeBuffer uses FRAME_LENGTH 2048 and HOP 512 (PitchAnalyzer.ts:62-63, 75-91), and yinDetectOffline's difference function is a 1024x1024 nested loop (YinCore.ts:332-347). One minute at 48 kHz is about 5,600 frames x 1M ops, so several to tens of seconds frozen on a Chromebook, and a 5-minute take can trigger Chrome's 'Page unresponsive'. It is downgraded because the vocal pitch editor is a niche, opt-in flow, it runs once per clip per session (cached in pitchData), and playback is usually stopped while the modal is open.
regressionRisks: A worker needs the channel data transferred or copied, and transferring detaches the AudioBuffer's Float32Array, so copy it. Results must arrive keyed to the clip id even if the modal closed. Cancel on close. An FFT-based difference function changes detection numerically, so retune thresholds and re-check existing pitch-correction output. Persisting pitchData has quota implications (see ia-flows-03).

title: No readiness model: sounds load only after the first click, Play doesn't wait, and early notes are silently dropped
evidence: Instruments are created only once `isReady` is true (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-381). isReady flips only after the first click or keydown runs audioEngine.init() (DawApp.tsx:437-448; useAudioEngine.ts:13-23). Play runs `if (!isReady) onInit(); action();` without awaiting (TransportBar.tsx:193-199). An adapter is attached to its TrackEngine only when its async init resolves (`instrument.init(...).then(() => trackEngine.setInstrument(instrument))`, usePlaybackEngine.ts:508-512); until then `this.instrument?.noteOn(...)` does nothing (TrackEngine.ts:73-75). The interface has no ready or status member (InstrumentAdapter.ts:6-49), and DrumMachineEngine.isLoaded() (lines 123-125) has no UI caller. KeyboardView has no loading state. SoundFontView polls the registry every 200 ms (SoundFontView.tsx:68-90) and shows a bare 'Loading SoundFont...' with no progress for a 31 MB file (SoundFontView.tsx:176-188). Unmounting disposes every instrument (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1187-1191) and isReady starts false again, so each return to the editor repeats the load.
impact: After a refresh or opening a project, the first Play often has missing parts: piano, drums (19 MB) and GM tracks come in one at a time mid-phrase with no explanation. Keys pressed on a piano that is still loading make no sound. Students read this as Studio being broken or laggy.
recommendation: Give each adapter a status (idle/loading/ready/error), a progress value and a ready promise, and publish per-track status to a small store slice. Show a ring on the track header and a 'Loading sounds 3/5' chip next to Play. Hold the transport (or count-in) until audible tracks are ready, with a 'play anyway' option. Start loading when the editor mounts rather than on the first click: an AudioContext can be created suspended, and decodeAudioData and addModule work while suspended. That means removing the `await ctx.resume()` from init paths (SoundFontAdapter.ts:222-224; oracle SynthEngine.ts:124-126) and resuming only on the gesture.

The adapter attaches only in the init `.then` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:508-510), and TrackEngine.noteOn is `this.instrument?.noteOn` (TrackEngine.ts:73-75). isLoaded() has no UI caller. SoundFontView polls every 200 ms and shows a bare 'Loading SoundFont...' (SoundFontView.tsx:68-90, 176-188).

Instruments are created only once isReady is true (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-380), isReady flips on the first document click or keydown (DawApp.tsx:437-447), withInit does not await (TransportBar.tsx:193-196), and notes are dropped until the async init attaches the adapter. In practice, though, any click (selecting a track, opening a menu) starts loading, so the 'first Play misses parts' case only happens when Play is the first click or the assets are slow (piano from the tonejs.github.io CDN, 19 MB drums). That is a noticeable but intermittent first-session annoyance, not a broken flow, so I've downgraded it. Part of the recommendation is sound: a per-track status, a 'loading sounds' indicator, and holding the transport. Preloading before the gesture, by removing the `await ctx.resume()` calls, is a riskier and separate change.

Creating or using the Tone context before a gesture triggers Chrome autoplay warnings, and some adapters may assume a running context, for example worklet addModule in the NAM and Oracle paths. title: Sample strategy: no shared buffer cache, a 19 MB padded default drum kit, a 31 MB SoundFont, and full rebuilds on re-entry and export
evidence: Each instance fetches and decodes its own copy: `new Tone.Player(url)` per pad per engine (DrumMachineEngine.ts:167-176), and a new Tone.Sampler per track (PianoSampler.ts:24-62; SamplerInstrument.ts:36-53). Tone keeps no URL cache; ToneAudioBuffer.load runs fetch plus decodeAudioData on every call (node_modules/tone/build/esm/core/context/ToneAudioBuffer.js:301-336). The default kit is 'natural' (DrumMachineEngine.ts:67; tracks are created without drumKit), which is 19 MB of 24-bit/48 kHz stereo WAV in public/daw-assets/samples/drums/natural. Measured: kick, snare and sidestick are 5.00 s files whose content ends at 0.59 s, 0.54 s and 0.35 s, even counting down to 60 dB below each file's own peak. Across the kit about 51% of the 67.7 s is padding by that strict measure, and about 78% is below −60 dBFS. The 808 and House kits are 0.5–0.8 MB of 16-bit audio. Decoded, the natural kit is about 24–26 MB of float PCM per drum-track instance. The SoundFont downloads the whole 31.3 MB GeneralUser_GS.sf2; the 30 s timeout wraps only fetch() (headers), and `await sfResponse.arrayBuffer()` has no timeout and no progress (SoundFontAdapter.ts:246-253). Leaving the editor disposes all instruments (usePlaybackEngine.ts:1187-1191), and every export creates them again (renderProject.ts:245-253). vercel.json sets no Cache-Control for /daw-assets.
impact: The heaviest kit is the default, so the first sound in any drum project costs about 19 MB over school Wi-Fi. A second drum track doubles the download, the decode work and about 26 MB of RAM, which matters on 4 GB Chromebooks. Re-entering Studio or exporting repeats the whole wait.
recommendation: Add a module-level SampleCache (URL → Promise<AudioBuffer>, LRU capped by bytes) used by every adapter and by renderProject; decoded AudioBuffers are not tied to one context. Trim the natural kit's tails (−60 dB relative to peak plus a 10 ms fade) and convert to 16-bit or Opus/OGG, aiming for about 2–4 MB. Load it progressively (kick, snare and hats first) or default new tracks to a light kit. Ship GeneralUser as SF3, which spessasynth decodes, keep it in Cache Storage, and add immutable cache headers with hashed file names for /daw-assets. Show download progress. Desktop DAWs keep one decoded copy per sample file in a shared pool.

GeneralUser_GS.sf2 is 31,281,186 bytes. Each pad does `new Tone.Player(url)` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:172), and ToneAudioBuffer.load fetches and decodes on every call with no cache. The SF2 `arrayBuffer()` call sits outside withTimeout (SoundFontAdapter.ts:252), and vercel.json has no headers or Cache-Control. I did not re-measure the padding percentages.
impactNote: The asset sizes are confirmed: natural kit 19M, 808 780K, house 548K, GeneralUser_GS.sf2 30M (du). The default kit is 'natural' (DrumMachineEngine.ts:67). Each engine instance creates its own `new Tone.Player(url)` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:172), so a second drum track doubles the decode work and PCM memory. The arrayBuffer() call has no timeout (SoundFontAdapter.ts:252). A second concurrent drum instance is also usually served from the HTTP cache. title: Organ disconnects released voices on a wall-clock timer that fires before scheduled note-offs, so sequenced notes are cut short and click
evidence: releaseVoice ramps the voice down at the scheduled `time` (`voice.mixer.gain.setTargetAtTime(0, time, fadeTime)`, oscillators stop at `time + fadeTime*5`). It then tears the voice down after a fixed `setTimeout(..., (fadeTime * 5 + 0.05) * 1000)`, i.e. 90 ms after noteOff is called (TonewheelOrganEngine.ts:681-732). Sequenced note-offs are called ahead of their `time`. Tone's Clock processes events up to now() = currentTime + lookAhead (node_modules/tone/build/esm/core/clock/Clock.js:200-204; Context.js:329-331), with lookAhead 0.1 s and updateInterval = lookAhead/2 = 0.05 s (Context.js:293-296). So callbacks run 50–100 ms before their audio time.
impact: The disconnect lands somewhere between about 40 ms after and about 10 ms before the release starts. For most sequenced organ notes the voice is cut while still loud, giving an audible click at every note end, and some notes end up to about 10 ms short. That is a constant artefact on the organ, a key Jazz and Gospel sound. Live play is unaffected because it uses time = currentTime.
recommendation: Do the cleanup from the audio clock instead: either set `voice.oscillators[0].onended` to disconnect the voice (the oscillators already stop at stopTime), or compute the delay as `(stopTime - ctx.currentTime) * 1000 + 20`. Apply the same fix to the percussion oscillator.
verifierNote: releaseVoice ramps at `time` but disconnects after `setTimeout(..., (fadeTime * 5 + 0.05) * 1000)`, which is 90 ms of wall clock from the call (TonewheelOrganEngine.ts:681-732). MidiScheduler's Tone.Part callbacks call `trackEngine.noteOff(ev.note, time)` 50-100 ms ahead of `time` (MidiScheduler.ts:58-63), so the mixer disconnect can land at or before the release, giving clicks and short notes.
impactNote: releaseVoice (TonewheelOrganEngine.ts:681-732) schedules the gain ramp and the oscillator stop on the audio clock at `time`, but tears the voice down with a wall-clock `setTimeout((fadeTime*5+0.05)*1000)`, 90 ms after the call. noteOff passes the scheduled time straight through (line 382-387). Sequenced note-offs run 50-100 ms ahead of `time`, so the disconnect lands roughly 10 ms before to 40 ms after the release starts, often while the voice is still loud (time constant 8 ms). That causes clicks or truncation on a large share of sequenced organ note ends. The analysis is correct. I'd rate it medium rather than high: it only affects the tonewheel-organ engine, main-thread jitter often delays the timeout (which hides it), and the organ's own key-click character partly masks it. The fix is small and safe.
regressionRisks: Using osc.onended for cleanup is safe. Make sure the voice is disconnected only once (guard against double disconnect), and that allNotesOff or dispose with fadeTime=0 still cleans up straight away. If onended never fires (an oscillator that never started), voices leak, so keep a fallback timeout computed from stopTime - ctx.currentTime. Leslie and overdrive routing downstream of voice.mixer is unaffected.

title: Instruments still loading when their track goes away are orphaned (memory, live graph nodes, leaked SoundFont channels)
evidence: TrackEngine.dispose only disposes an instrument that is already attached (`this.instrument?.dispose()`, TrackEngine.ts:188-189), and attachment happens in the init `.then` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:508-512). Deleting a track, switching instrument type, opening another project or leaving the editor while a load is in flight (usePlaybackEngine.ts:387-396, 416-420, 1187-1191) disposes the TrackEngine but not the adapter. Its downloads carry on, and its decoded buffers stay referenced from the dead graph. The `.then` later attaches it to the disposed engine and connects input adapters' monitor taps to the global bus (usePlaybackEngine.ts:546-556). SoundFontAdapter takes its channel before awaiting (SoundFontAdapter.ts:73-80) and gives it back only in dispose (lines 179-184), so any failed or orphaned init leaks a channel. Each export with SoundFont tracks builds an adapter on the offline context (renderProject.ts:245-253); connecting the live synth to it throws after the channel is taken, so every export leaks one channel per SoundFont track (renderProject.ts:26-32 documents the silence, not the leak). Once all 15 non-drum channels are leaked, allocateChannel hands out channels that are already in use (SoundFontAdapter.ts:49-51).
impact: Clicking through presets or projects while sounds load piles up tens of MB of decoded samples. After a few exports in one session, new SoundFont tracks share channels, and one track's program change silently changes another track's sound.
recommendation: In the init `.then`, check `audioMap.get(track.id)?.trackEngine === trackEngine`; if not, dispose the instrument and return. Let TrackEngine own a pending instrument so dispose covers it. Pass an AbortSignal into init so downloads stop. Release the SoundFont channel in a catch/finally when init fails, and skip SoundFont tracks in renderProject until offline rendering exists.
verifierNote: TrackEngine.dispose only calls `this.instrument?.dispose()` (TrackEngine.ts:188), and the adapter is attached in the async `.then` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:510), which never checks whether the engine is still current. So a pending load survives deletion or instrument swaps and later attaches to a dead engine and the monitor bus. SoundFontAdapter allocates its channel before awaiting (lines 73-79). In renderProject the instrument only gets disposed through te.dispose after setInstrument (renderProject.ts:253-254), so a rejected SoundFont init on the offline context leaks its channel.

title: Drum kit loads wait on every download in flight across the app, and fail if any of them fails
evidence: loadKit creates each pad with `const player = new Tone.Player(url); await Tone.loaded();` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:168-176). Tone.loaded() waits on the global downloads list (`while (ToneAudioBuffer.downloads.length) yield ToneAudioBuffer.downloads[0]`, ToneAudioBuffer.js:357-365), which holds every pending buffer load from every instrument (ToneAudioBuffer.js:93-110). A rejected download in that list makes loaded() throw.
impact: Drum readiness on project open, and kit switching, take as long as the slowest unrelated load (30 CDN piano MP3s, another drum track, an EP). A failed piano or EP sample makes the drum init reject too, so the drum track goes silent with only a console message.
recommendation: Await each pad's own buffer, e.g. `await Tone.ToneAudioBuffer.fromUrl(url)` or a Player with onload/onerror promises, ideally through the SampleCache from instruments-05. Use Promise.allSettled so one missing pad doesn't take down the whole kit.
verifierNote: loadKit does `const player = new Tone.Player(url); await Tone.loaded();` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:172-173). ToneAudioBuffer.loaded() loops `while (ToneAudioBuffer.downloads.length) yield ToneAudioBuffer.downloads[0]`, over a global list every buffer load pushes to, so the drum load waits on every other instrument's downloads and rejects if any of them fails.

title: Changing kit in the Drum view resets custom pad pans in the audio while the knobs and store keep the old values
evidence: When a kit load commits, it overwrites pans with the kit defaults (`chain.panner.pan.value = pan`, DrumMachineEngine.ts:191-197). The store-sync path compensates with `.then(() => applyDrumPads(...))`, but only when `drumEngine.getKit() !== kitId` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:429-444). DrumMachineView.handleKitChange calls setDrumKit and then `state.instrument.setKit(kitId)` directly (DrumMachineView.tsx:287-310). setKit sets currentKit synchronously (DrumMachineEngine.ts:106-111), so the sync sees the kit already matching and never re-applies the pads. The view's own pad effect depends only on `track?.drumPads` (DrumMachineView.tsx:273-285). The init path also applies pads from the stale closure `track` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:525-527), whereas organ and Chops re-read the store.
impact: After a kit change, panned hats or toms jump to the new kit's default positions while the pan knobs still show the student's settings. On reload the saved pans come back, so the mix changes again — a confusing 'reload changes my sound' bug.
recommendation: Have the engine keep per-pad overrides: loadKit applies kit defaults only to pads without a stored override, and setPadPan records overrides. Alternatively, call applyDrumPads after setKit in the view and re-read the store in the init `.then`.
verifierNote: handleKitChange calls setDrumKit and then `state.instrument.setKit(kitId)` (DrumMachineView.tsx:289-302). setKit sets currentKit synchronously (DrumMachineEngine.ts:109), so the store sync's `drumEngine.getKit() !== kitId` check (usePlaybackEngine.ts:431) is false and applyDrumPads never runs. loadKit then overwrites pans with the kit defaults (lines 191-197), while the view's pad effect depends only on `track?.drumPads` (DrumMachineView.tsx:273-285).

title: SoundFont stop/panic leaves the sustain pedal latched and channel controllers dirty
evidence: `allNotesOff(): void { if (sharedSynth) sharedSynth.controllerChange(this.channel, 123, 0); }`, and panic() just calls allNotesOff (SoundFontAdapter.ts:171-177). In spessasynth, CC123 calls stopAllNotes(), which runs release envelopes; CC120 calls stopAllNotes(true), an immediate kill. Neither resets controllers, and note-off sustains while `_midiControllers[sustainPedal] >= 8192` (spessasynth_processor.min.js). Recorded clips schedule CC64 (MidiScheduler.ts:42-56). On dispose the channel is released with its state still set (SoundFontAdapter.ts:179-184) and handed to the next track (allocateChannel, lines 41-52). By contrast, the Tone samplers reset sustain in allNotesOff (PianoSampler.ts:102-106), and the interface promises that panic will 'Immediately silence all notes' (InstrumentAdapter.ts:44-45).
impact: Stopping during a pedalled passage leaves that GM track's pedal down. The next live notes, or the next play from a later bar, smear until a pedal-up event arrives, and a new track that inherits the channel can start out sustained. Stop also lets GM release tails ring on, unlike the organ.
recommendation: On panic, send CC120, CC121 (reset all controllers) and a centred pitch wheel (8192). On allocate and on release, send CC121 and a programChange. Consider re-sending the latest CC64/CC7/CC11 values from before the playhead when playback starts.
verifierNote: allNotesOff sends only `controllerChange(this.channel, 123, 0)` and panic just delegates (SoundFontAdapter.ts:171-177). In the bundled processor, `case f.allNotesOff:this.stopAllNotes();break;` does not reset _midiControllers, so a CC64 scheduled by MidiScheduler.ts:42-63 stays latched, and the channel is released dirty in dispose.

title: Input adapters don't recover from a device unplug and can race when the device is switched
evidence: On the track's 'ended' event the adapter only calls stopStream() (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:196-205; VocalFxAdapter.ts:166-174). deviceId keeps the old id, so a later setDevice(sameId) hits `if (deviceId === this.deviceId) return;` (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:169). The views' device-effect dependencies don't change on replug (GuitarBassView.tsx:470-482), and the 'devicechange' listener only re-lists devices (GuitarBassView.tsx:454-466). setDevice assigns this.deviceId before `await this.nativeCtx.resume()` and `await getUserMedia(...)` and never checks it again afterwards (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:169-194). A slow earlier request can therefore overwrite a newer one; the orphaned stream is never stopped, and its old source, splitter and channelGain stay connected to the analysers, mute gate and monitor send.
impact: After a USB interface or headset drops out, a sleep/wake, or a permission revoke, guitar or vocal input stays dead until the student picks another device or reloads, with only a console warning. Switching devices quickly can double the input or leave the mic open, with the OS mic indicator still on.
recommendation: Clear deviceId on 'ended' and listen for devicechange to re-open the configured device. Give each setDevice call a request token and stop any stream that resolves after a newer request or after dispose. Expose an input state (connected / disconnected / denied) for the UI.
verifierNote: setDevice returns early on `deviceId === this.deviceId`, assigns this.deviceId before awaiting resume and getUserMedia, and never re-checks it afterwards (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:169-194). The 'ended' handler only calls stopStream, which doesn't clear deviceId (lines 196-205, 415-433). VocalFxAdapter.ts:166-174 is the same, and the view's device effect deps don't change on replug (GuitarBassView.tsx:471-482).

title: Drum pads are monophonic with hard cuts (cymbal and tom tails chopped, clicks)
evidence: Every hit runs `player.stop(t); player.start(t);` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:219-223), and the hi-hat choke runs `openHat.stop(t)` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:207-211). Tone.Player defaults to `fadeOut: 0` (node_modules/tone/build/esm/source/buffer/Player.js:44-57), and `_stop` stops every active source at that time (Player.js:169-171). The natural kit's crash, ride and toms ring for 2–6 s (measured in instruments-05).
impact: In a ride or crash pattern each new hit cuts the previous ring at full level. There is no cymbal wash, and 8th-note rides and tom fills click audibly, so the default kit sounds less realistic than its samples allow.
recommendation: Give cymbals, toms and the open hat a small voice pool (2–4 overlapping sources) with a voice cap. Use 5–10 ms fades for retriggers and chokes (e.g. `player.fadeOut = 0.008`, or a per-voice gain ramp).
verifierNote: Each hit runs `player.stop(t); player.start(t);` (DrumMachineEngine.ts:220-221), and the choke runs `openHat.stop(t)`. Tone.Player defaults to `fadeOut: 0`, and `_stop` stops every active source at once (Player.js:169-171), so pads are monophonic with hard cuts.

title: Organ: ~20 audio nodes per note, an always-running Leslie/vibrato graph, and the overdrive curve rebuilt on every knob step
evidence: Each noteOn builds 9 OscillatorNodes, 9 GainNodes, a mixer, a click BufferSource plus gain, and optionally a percussion oscillator plus gain (TonewheelOrganEngine.ts:300-369), with MAX_VOICES = 12 (line 5). Each release schedules a setTimeout (lines 697-732). Each organ track also permanently runs 5 LFO oscillators and about 25 filter/delay/gain nodes, even when silent (buildVibrato 805-833; buildLeslie 855-975). setOverdrive rebuilds an 8192-point tanh curve and reassigns overdriveShaper.curve on every call (582-593, 837-851); OrganView calls it on every knob change. Voice stealing doesn't decrement activeNoteCount (286-292), so after a steal the percussion (gated by wasEmpty, lines 296/337) never retriggers until playback stops.
impact: A 4-note organ chord means about 40 running oscillators plus allocation churn on every note. Combined with other tracks, that is a measurable audio-thread load on low-end Chromebooks. Dragging the Drive knob allocates 32 KB and swaps the shaper curve about 60 times a second.
recommendation: All 9 drawbar ratios are integer harmonics of half the note frequency (0.5, 1.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8 → 1, 3, 2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 16). One oscillator per voice with a PeriodicWave built from the current drawbar settings reproduces the mix; rebuild it on drawbar changes with setPeriodicWave on active voices, optionally adding a second detuned oscillator for wheel imperfection. That is about 9× fewer nodes. Quantise and cache the overdrive curves (e.g. 32 steps), and derive wasEmpty from voices.length.
verifierNote: noteOn creates 9 oscillators plus 9 gains in a loop, a mixer, a click BufferSource plus gain, and an optional percussion oscillator plus gain (TonewheelOrganEngine.ts:300-369). updateOverdriveCurve allocates an 8192-sample Float32Array on every setOverdrive call (lines 837-851), and the Drive knob onChange calls it directly (OrganView.tsx:621-623). Voice stealing at lines 286-292 calls releaseVoice without decrementing activeNoteCount.

title: GuitarFxAdapter and VocalFxAdapter are ~90% duplicated and have already drifted apart (guitar rewires the graph on every knob step)
evidence: init, dispose, setDevice, setChannelConfig, channel routing, the recording and monitor taps, and getInputLevel are near-identical (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:60-433 vs VocalFxAdapter.ts:51-394), and ChannelConfig is declared in both files. Vocal has a param-only fast path, `updateChainParams` → `updateProcessorParams` (VocalFxAdapter.ts:255-258; GuitarPedalChain.ts:202-213). Guitar exposes only syncChain, which always calls wireChain() and disconnects and reconnects every edge (GuitarPedalChain.ts:110-143, 226-253); GuitarBassView calls it on every chain change (GuitarBassView.tsx:549-562). VocalFxAdapter reaches into the chain's private `processors` via `as any` (VocalFxAdapter.ts:316-326). Both header diagrams show the mute gate after the pedal chain, but the code gates before it (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:5-10 vs 70-75).
impact: Each amp or pedal knob drag on a guitar track tears down and rebuilds the live graph on every pointer event — wasted main-thread work and a dropout risk while monitoring. Fixes such as instruments-02 and instruments-13 have to be made twice.
recommendation: Pull the shared code into a LiveInputAdapter base (device lifecycle, channel routing, taps, metering, applyTrackState) with thin Guitar and Vocal subclasses. Use the updateProcessorParams fast path for both, and add a findProcessor(type) method to GuitarPedalChain instead of using `as any`.
verifierNote: Guitar exposes only syncChain, which always ends in wireChain() and disconnects and reconnects every edge (GuitarPedalChain.ts:110-143, 226-253). GuitarBassView calls it on every `[chain, trackId, bpm]` change (GuitarBassView.tsx:550-562). Vocal uses the updateProcessorParams fast path (VocalView.tsx:559-561) and reads private processors via `as any` (VocalFxAdapter.ts:316-326). The header diagram (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:5-10) puts muteGain after PedalChain, but init gates before it (lines 70-75).

title: Core instrument samples depend on three third-party github.io hosts, and the Studio piano differs from the lesson piano
evidence: Piano: `baseUrl: 'https://tonejs.github.io/audio/salamander/'` (PianoSampler.ts:57). Electric piano: gleitz.github.io (sampleConfigs.ts:21-24); the lesson bass voices come from the same host via genreBassVoices.ts:28. Cello and sampled organ: `https://nbrosowsky.github.io/tonejs-instruments/samples/` (sampleConfigs.ts:12-13, 106-108, 130-132). The app already self-hosts an 85-sample chromatic piano for the lessons (`baseUrl: '/samples/piano/'`, src/audio/pianoSampler.ts:26-36, 97-100), and sampleConfigs.ts:59-63 says a Practice Track must keep sounding like the lesson.
impact: These hosts are outside Music Atlas's control: no SLA, caching or CORS guarantees, and they are a common target for school web filters. Combined with PianoSampler's missing onerror (instruments-07), a blocked host means a silent piano. Students also hear a different piano in Studio than in the lessons.
recommendation: Self-host every instrument set under /daw-assets with immutable caching. Point the Studio piano at the lesson set (or a sparser subset, such as every minor third, for faster loading) so the two match, and keep the CDNs only as a fallback.
verifierNote: PianoSampler.ts:57 uses `https://tonejs.github.io/audio/salamander/`, sampleConfigs.ts:13 uses nbrosowsky.github.io, and sampleConfigs.ts:24 uses gleitz.github.io. The lesson piano is self-hosted at `/samples/piano/` (src/audio/pianoSampler.ts:99), and public/samples/piano holds 85 files.

title: Loop seams: allNotesOff has no time argument, so loop wraps cut notes and audio clips 50–100 ms early
evidence: `allNotesOff(): void; panic(): void;` take no time (InstrumentAdapter.ts:41-45). The Transport emits its loop event while processing ticks ahead of time (node_modules/tone/build/esm/core/clock/Transport.js:121-127), i.e. 50–100 ms before the loop seam. The handler ignores tickTime and calls `state.trackEngine.allNotesOff()` and `audioClipScheduler.cancelAll()` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-853). cancelAll calls source.stop() on audio clips immediately (AudioClipScheduler.ts:94-113). Sampler cc() also ignores the scheduled time and releases sustained notes at Tone's default now() plus look-ahead (PianoSampler.ts:89-100).
impact: When looping a section — the core practice workflow — held notes and audio clips stop 50–100 ms before the loop end, leaving an audible gap or stutter at every wrap.
recommendation: Add allNotesOff(time?: number) and panic(time?) to the contract and implement them in each adapter. In the loop handler, pass tickTime and schedule audio-clip stops at tickTime (`source.stop(tickTime)`) rather than now. Forward the event time in the samplers' cc() releases. This overlaps with the playback-engine slice.
verifierNote: Transport emits 'loop' inside _processTick ahead of audio time (Transport.js:124-129), and handleLoop ignores tickTime and calls allNotesOff() and cancelAll(), which does `source.stop()` immediately (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-852; AudioClipScheduler.ts:94-113). So audio clips, organ and SoundFont notes are cut early. However, the Tone samplers' releaseAll() and cc() release at Tone's default now() (currentTime + lookAhead), which lands at or near the seam rather than 50-100 ms early, so the claim doesn't hold for them.

title: Paste and clear rewrite every chord in the song, not just the selection
evidence: pasteChords reduces the regions outside the span to ChordStart {startTick, name, noteName, color, degreeKey, id} (leadSheetClipboard.ts:151-166). It then rebuilds the whole list with regionsFromStarts, which sets every endTick to the next chord's start (121-135). rawStartTick, midis and confidence (prismSlice.ts:53-64) are dropped from every region. ⌘V uses this (LeadSheetView.tsx:552), and so does Delete on bars or beats (708-735). setChordRegions(..., true) then replaces the whole chord lane (prismSlice.ts:1840-1861, 650). Copying a block also captures only the opening barline of each touched bar (LeadSheetView.tsx:439-443; leadSheetClipboard.ts:211-226), so the block's closing repeat is lost and the pasted repeat runs to the end of the piece.
impact:
Pasting two bars at bar 9 changes the whole song:
- Every N.C. gap in the song is closed.
- The voicings that merge mode relies on, and the raw hit times used for note colouring, are stripped from every chord.
- Low-confidence chords that regionToMeasures had hidden (leadSheetUtils.ts:63-65) reappear.

The student never sees these changes happen, because they are far from the selection. Copying a repeated 4-bar block and pasting it produces an open-ended repeat.
recommendation: Make pasteChords local to [from, to): trim or split only the regions that overlap the span, insert the incoming chords, and keep the original region objects ({...region, endTick}) so all their fields survive. Include the block's closing barline in the roadmap copy. Add tests asserting that regions outside the span are left untouched.
verifierNote: pasteChords (leadSheetClipboard.ts:142-181) maps every kept region to ChordStart, dropping rawStartTick, midis and confidence. regionsFromStarts (121-135) then sets every endTick to the next start, closing N.C. gaps song-wide. setChordRegions(…, true) replaces the whole lane. roadmapAt only reads each touched bar's opening barline (repeatEnd checks measureIndex−1), so a copied block loses its closing repeat. withRepeatStart then runs the pasted repeat to the next start or the end of the piece.
impactNote: The mechanics are correct. pasteChords reduces all kept regions to ChordStart {startTick,name,noteName,color,degreeKey,id} (src/daw/components/LeadSheet/leadSheetClipboard.ts:151-166), and regionsFromStarts rebuilds every region with endTick equal to the next chord's start (121-135). That drops rawStartTick, midis and confidence (prismSlice.ts:53-64) for the whole song, and setChordRegions(...,true) replaces the lane. Delete on bars or beats goes through the same path (LeadSheetView.tsx:708-735). roadmapAt reads only the opening barline (repeatEnd at endMeasure === measureIndex-1, leadSheetClipboard.ts:~211-226), so a block's closing repeat is not copied. User-noticeable impact is smaller than stated, though. For typed charts there are no midis or confidence to lose, and the lengthened durations mostly show up in chord playback and the merge-mode recalculation, not on the chart. The most visible effect is low-confidence detected chords reappearing after any paste or clear. That is a real data-integrity bug worth fixing, but medium rather than high.
regressionRisks: Making paste local means overlapping regions must be split or trimmed. Getting the boundary at `from` wrong (a region starting before `from` and ending inside the span) re-creates gaps or overlaps. Today's 'close gaps everywhere' behaviour may be what makes typed one-beat chords play legato. Check whether users depend on it before changing it. Keeping original region objects preserves ids, which matters for collab sync and the undo diff (this is good, but verify reconcileChordRegions in 'replace' mode doesn't dedupe by id). Including the closing barline in roadmap copy changes the paste of single bars.

title: Toolbar bar actions target a hidden, stale bar
evidence: selectedMeasureIdx is local state, set only when a bar or beat is clicked (LeadSheetView.tsx:143-145, 303-305), and it is never cleared. clearSelection (310-315) and Escape (681-684) leave it alone. A chord click goes through handleSelectItem, which does not update it (293-308; ChordSymbol.tsx:121-133 calls onSelectItem). The toolbar sits inside the column whose onClick runs clearSelection (884-888, 766-768). Clicking any toolbar button therefore clears the visible highlight but not selectedMeasureIdx, and that value drives − Measure, + Section and + Repeat (LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:103-139, 234-285).
impact: Click bar 3, press Escape, click a chord in bar 7, press '− Measure', and bar 3 is deleted. After '+ Section' the highlight disappears, but the next '− Measure' still deletes that invisible bar. Students can't predict what a toolbar button will change.
recommendation: Derive the toolbar's target from the selection the user can see (targetBarline or measuresInSelection), as LeadSheetScoreView already does (105-127). Clear it together with the selection. Stop toolbar clicks from bubbling to the background handler. Disable bar actions when nothing is selected, and name the target in the button, for example 'Delete bar 3'.
verifierNote: Confirmed: selectedMeasureIdx is set only for measure and beat clicks or a right-click (LeadSheetView.tsx:303-305, 317-324). It is never cleared by clearSelection (310-315) or Escape. The toolbar sits inside the onClick={handleBackgroundClick} column (884-888), so −Measure, +Section and +Repeat act on a stale, invisible bar. The edits are undoable, so this is predictability friction rather than a blocker; medium rather than high.
impactNote: selectedMeasureIdx is local state (src/daw/components/LeadSheet/LeadSheetView.tsx:143-145), set only for measure or beat items in handleSelectItem (293-305), and never cleared by clearSelection (310-315) or Escape. A chord click goes through ChordSymbol's onSelectItem (src/daw/components/LeadSheet/ChordSymbol.tsx:121-133) with kind 'chord', which leaves it alone. The toolbar sits inside the column whose onClick is handleBackgroundClick, which calls clearSelection (LeadSheetView.tsx:766-768, 884-888). '− Measure', '+ Section' and '+ Repeat' therefore act on an invisible, stale bar (LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:103-139). This is reproducible and confusing, but the edits are undoable with ⌘Z and the effect is visible right after it happens, so medium.
regressionRisks: Disabling bar actions when nothing is selected changes '+ Measure' (currently inserts after bar 1 with no selection), so coordinate with 07. Stopping toolbar click propagation must not break the toolbar's own popovers and menus that close on outside click. A tutorial step that clicks a bar and then a toolbar button would still work, but one relying on the stale index would not. The same toolbar is reused by LeadSheetScoreView, which already derives its target differently, so unify carefully.

title: Lead-sheet MusicXML export is always 4/4 and drops the melody and the roadmap
evidence: The toolbar calls downloadLeadSheet(chordRegions, {title, bpm, rootNote, mode}) (LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:61-69). It passes no beatsPerMeasure, beatType, sections, repeats, rests, fermatas or composer; FileMenu does the same (FileMenu.tsx:353-366). buildLeadSheetXml defaults to 4/4 and computes ticksPerMeasure = beatsPerMeasure * PPQ (MusicXmlExport.ts:221-231), which is wrong for x/8 metres even if a metre were passed. In melody mode the same button is shown (LeadSheetScoreView.tsx:141) and still exports chords over slash rests. The Score already has a full exporter (ScoreMusicXmlExport.ts: harmony, rehearsal marks, repeats, system breaks, composer, voices), but only ScoreView uses it. The lead-sheet file is named 'prism-lead-sheet.musicxml' and tagged <software>Prism DAW</software> (MusicXmlExport.ts:247, 331).
impact: A waltz opens in MuseScore or Finale as 4/4 with chords on the wrong beats. A student's melody lead sheet exports without the melody. Rehearsal letters, repeats and endings disappear. Two buttons both called MusicXML (Score and Lead Sheet) produce very different files.
recommendation: Export the lead sheet through buildScoreXml with one part: the melody part when it is shown, otherwise a slash-notation part built from the chart. Include chordRegions, sections, repeats, systemStarts, the composer and the real time signature. Delete buildLeadSheetXml or reduce it to a thin wrapper. Name the file after the project, sanitised the way downloadScoreXml does it.
verifierNote: LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:61-69 and FileMenu.tsx:353-366 call downloadLeadSheet with no metre, sections or repeats. buildLeadSheetXml defaults to 4/4 with ticksPerMeasure = beatsPerMeasure*PPQ (MusicXmlExport.ts:221-231), the default filename is 'prism-lead-sheet.musicxml', and the file is tagged <software>Prism DAW</software>. The same toolbar is rendered in melody mode (LeadSheetScoreView.tsx:141), but only ScoreView uses buildScoreXml.
impactNote: The toolbar calls downloadLeadSheet(chordRegions, {title, bpm, rootNote, mode}) (src/daw/components/LeadSheet/LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:61-69). buildLeadSheetXml defaults to beatsPerMeasure=4 and beatType=4, with ticksPerMeasure = beatsPerMeasure*PPQ (src/daw/midi/MusicXmlExport.ts:221-231), so non-4/4 charts are mis-barred. Sections, repeats, the melody and the composer are not exported, the file name is hard-coded 'prism-lead-sheet.musicxml', and the software tag is 'Prism DAW' (247, 328-331). FileMenu does the same. The bug is real, but MusicXML export to MuseScore or Finale is a power-user path for this audience, most student charts are 4/4, and nothing in the app is corrupted. Downgraded to medium.
regressionRisks: Routing through buildScoreXml changes the output for anyone importing the current chord-only file (harmony over slash rests becomes a full part). Check that the existing scoreMusicXml tests and any FileMenu export test still pass. Building a slash-notation part requires a NotationScore from the chart, which is new code. Melody mode needs the melody track's NotationScore, which the Score view computes, and recomputing it on export could be slow on Chromebooks for long songs. File-name sanitisation must handle empty project names.

title: Printing: melody mode prints the editor UI with mis-sized pages; chart mode prints the selection
evidence:
Melody mode:
- LeadSheetScoreView's root has the class leadsheet-container but not score-print-root.
- NoteEditorBar is rendered without the score-no-print wrapper (LeadSheetScoreView.tsx:130-142), and the print CSS hides only .leadsheet-toolbar and .leadsheet-palette (leadsheet-print.css:27-35).
- ScoreView draws the same StaffView pages but adds score-print-root and score-no-print and clears the selection before printing (ScoreView.tsx:157-199; grandStaff.css:80-84).
- The CSS notes that pages are drawn at true Letter size for a margin-0 named page (leadsheet-print.css:151-158). The lead sheet prints them under the default 0.75 in @page instead (8-11).

Chart mode:
- The PDF button calls window.print() synchronously (LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:71-73), before the click bubbles up to clearSelection.
- Selection washes are rects filled with --color-accent (LeadSheetMeasure.tsx:311-341), and the print rules only recolour text, line and circle (70-84).

Both modes: @page forces Letter paper.

title: Playhead position disagrees with the staff's width rule, and follow-scroll fights the user
evidence: LeadSheetStaff squeezes full systems to fit the container: svgWidth = Math.max(availableWidth, measures.length * 110) (LeadSheetStaff.tsx:100-112). The playhead maths in LeadSheetView only ever stretches: svgW = isFull && contentWidth && contentWidth > defaultW ? contentWidth : defaultW, with defaultW = bars × 200 (LeadSheetView.tsx:957-963). Whenever contentWidth is less than bars × 200, the computed bar width is too large. That covers 4-bar rows under about 800 px (1024–1280 px windows once the 216 px palette and 96 px of padding are taken out) and the 5–6-bar rows that library songs fold into. The follow effect calls scrollIntoView on every system change while playing (242-255), with no way to switch it off.

title: Typing a chord accepts any text, which breaks Numbers view and MusicXML for edited chords

title: VocalView re-renders entirely about 20 times a second whenever a Pitch Correction block exists

The worklet posts at about 24 Hz unconditionally while enabled ('reportInterval = Math.floor(sampleRate / (blockSize * 24))', pitch-correction-processor.js:498, 634-642). The hook is called at VocalView's top level (VocalView.tsx:511), although its only consumer is PitchMeter inside the expanded dialog (:1584-1587), which is usually closed. Each render rebuilds the pedal-catalog Map (:969-1013), every chain tile, and the inline 'const EmptySlot = ...' component type (:1022), so React unmounts and remounts every slot subtree each tick and their 150 ms transitions never run. Every RotaryKnob also re-renders with fresh closures. When the dialog is open, the overlay's backdrop-blur-sm plus the content's 'backdropFilter: blur(32px)' (:1541-1548) are re-composited at the same rate. Only TunerDisplay is spared, because it is memoised.

recommendation: Move usePitchInfo into PitchMeter (or a small PitchMeterContainer) and mount it only while the editor is open. Push updates through adapter.onPitchUpdate into a ref and update the SVG attributes in rAF without React state. Hoist EmptySlot to module scope with props and memoise the chain row.

title: Picking an input device switches on monitoring with no headphone or latency guidance, so feedback is likely

title: Mic permission and device errors are invisible, and a dead input cannot be revived by re-selecting it
evidence: Mounting either view calls getAudioInputs, which prompts for mic permission with no explanation first (VocalView.tsx:517-530, GuitarBassView.tsx:455-468). It swallows every error with 'console.warn('Could not enumerate audio inputs'); return [];' (AudioInputEnumerator.ts:54-57), so a blocked user sees 'No Input Device' and an empty menu (VocalView.tsx:724-726, 849-877), with no blocked state or recovery steps. Where permissions.query does not support 'microphone' it throws and is caught (AudioInputEnumerator.ts:28-36), so every mount and devicechange opens a temporary getUserMedia stream. A missing device is labelled 'globalInputDeviceId.slice(0, 8)', i.e. gibberish (VocalView.tsx:726). When the interface is unplugged, the adapter's 'ended' handler only stops the stream (VocalFxAdapter.ts:168-173, GuitarFxAdapter.ts:199-204). this.deviceId is assigned before the open attempt and is never cleared (VocalFxAdapter.ts:143-148), so 'if (deviceId === this.deviceId) return' makes every later attempt with the same id a no-op. title: Undo and collaborator edits to pedal chains never reach the UI or the sound, and the next local edit overwrites them
evidence: Each view copies storedChain into local state only in the useState initializer (VocalView.tsx:485-496, GuitarBassView.tsx:428-440). From then on it only writes the local chain to the store (VocalView.tsx:566-575, GuitarBassView.tsx:565-575) and drives the engine from the local copy (:548-563, :550-562). While a collaborator holds the track lock, guardTrack drops the write ('isTrackLockedByRemote(...) ? state : updater(state)', tracksSlice.ts:82-88), but the local view and engine still apply the change.
impact: Cmd+Z after a pedal tweak appears to do nothing and silently consumes an undo step, and the next knob move writes back the un-undone chain. A locked track sounds different locally than it does for everyone else and reverts on remount.
recommendation: Render the chain from the store selector and remove the local copy. Keep transient drag values in a ref or local preview only. Let the engine apply store changes (live-input-01), so undo, collab and locks are all handled by the existing track-sync path.
