title: Tuner opens a second voice-processed mic stream, ignores the selected channel, runs YIN every frame and never shows its errors
evidence: The views pass only deviceId ('<TunerDisplay deviceId={globalInputDeviceId} />', VocalView.tsx:949; GuitarBassView.tsx:878-882). useTuner therefore runs in standalone mode: getAudioStream plus 'new AudioContext()' (useTuner.ts:143-156), with constraints that leave browser echo cancellation, noise suppression and AGC at their defaults (AudioInputEnumerator.ts:66-70). The adapters deliberately disable these (GuitarFxAdapter.ts:183-192). The analyser also down-mixes all channels instead of using the track's channel. tick() runs yinDetectSingle on 4,096 samples every animation frame (useTuner.ts:173-225): about 1,778 lags × 2,048 samples ≈ 3.6M multiply-adds plus two Float32Array allocations per call (YinCore.ts:265-281). It also calls setNote, setOctave, setCents and setFrequency each frame, so TunerDisplay re-renders 60–120 times a second and rebuilds its 41 static LED ticks (TunerDisplay.tsx:55-82). In the catch block, 'setError('Could not access audio device'); stop();' is undone because stop() ends with setError(null) (useTuner.ts:121-126, 226-230); the same happens in onended (:158-164). As a result the error status (TunerDisplay.tsx:201-219) never appears. handleToggle calls onActiveChange(true) before start() resolves (TunerDisplay.tsx:230-238), so GuitarBassView mutes monitoring even when the tuner failed (GuitarBassView.tsx:485-496). That mute is also undone by the monitoring sync whenever tracks change (usePlaybackEngine.ts:594-605).
impact: Main-thread CPU spikes whenever a note sounds with the tuner on. With a multi-input interface the tuner can lock onto the mic rather than the guitar, and noise suppression can attenuate sustained notes. A failed start just flips the switch back to Off with no explanation, while guitar monitoring may stay muted.
recommendation: Pass externalAnalyser from the adapter, tapping after channel selection (it already has a 16,384-point chordAnalyserNode), and drop the second stream. Throttle YIN to 20–30 Hz or move it into a worklet, and drive the needle through a ref. Fix the error ordering (set the error after stop). Call onActiveChange only on a confirmed start, and route the tuner mute through store state that the monitoring sync respects.
verifierNote: In standalone mode useTuner calls getAudioStream and creates a new AudioContext (useTuner.ts:143-156), with constraints that leave EC/NS/AGC at their defaults (AudioInputEnumerator.ts:66-70). It runs yinDetectSingle every rAF and sets state per frame while a note sounds (:173-225). The catch's setError is reset by stop() calling setError(null) (:121-126, 226-230), and handleToggle calls onActiveChange(true) before start resolves (TunerDisplay.tsx:230-238). The re-render cost is limited to frames that have a pitch, because React bails out on identical values.

title: Pitch Correction 'Smooth' control is inverted: turning it up makes correction faster and more robotic
evidence: Both the knob and the slider are labelled SMOOTH/Smooth and bound to 'speed' (VocalView.tsx:1489-1504, 1643-1678), with formatValue '((1 - v) * 400).toFixed(0) ms'. In the worklet, 'this.speed = 50; // 0-100: retune speed (100=instant, 0=400ms)' and 'baseRetuneSec = (1 - this.speed / 100) * 0.4' (pitch-correction-processor.js:427, 582).
impact: Students learning auto-tune turn 'Smooth' up expecting a more natural sound and get the hard-tune effect instead. The ms readout falls as the control rises, which contradicts the label.
recommendation: Rename the control to 'Retune speed (ms)', following the Auto-Tune/Melodyne convention, or invert the mapping so that turning Smooth up increases the retune time. Add a one-line hint (e.g. 'fast = robotic, slow = natural').

title: PitchMeter pairs the corrected note name with cents measured from the detected pitch's nearest chromatic note
evidence: 'noteName = midiToNoteName(Math.round(correctedMidi), ...)' but 'centsOff = Math.round((detectedMidi - Math.round(detectedMidi)) * 100)' (PitchMeter.tsx:34-42). The comment says cents are measured 'from the nearest corrected note', but the code doesn't do that. The colour bands (green under 5c, amber under 20c) use the same value (:164-170).
impact: When a student sings F# in C major and correction pulls it to G, the meter shows 'G +0c' in green, telling them they are perfectly in tune on a note they did not sing. This undermines the practice value of the meter.
recommendation: Compute cents as 1200·log2(detected / targetHz), where targetHz is the equal-tempered frequency of the corrected note. Alternatively, show the sung note, the target note and the deviation separately. Use the same colour thresholds and palette as TunerDisplay.
verifierNote: PitchMeter.tsx:36-42 takes noteName from Math.round(correctedMidi) but cents from detectedMidi minus round(detectedMidi), which contradicts its own comment. A sung F# corrected to G shows 'G' with near-zero cents.

title: Input meter turns red long before clipping and misses real clipping
evidence: The meter computes 'pct = Math.min(100, Math.round(rms * 400))' and turns '#ef4444' above 90 (VocalView.tsx:640-646, GuitarBassView.tsx:582-588), using RMS over 256 samples (VocalFxAdapter.ts:233-243). Red therefore starts at about −13 dBFS RMS. A peaky vocal clipping at 0 dBFS can sit below 90%. There is no peak hold or clip latch, which differs from the DAW's peak meter (useMeterLevel.ts). The rAF loop runs at display rate for the life of the view even with no device connected (:636-654).
impact: Students learning gain staging are told they are clipping when they are not, and are not told when they really are.
recommendation: Show peak and RMS in dBFS with segments at −18/−6/−0.1 dBFS and a 1.5 s clip latch, sharing useMeterLevel/MeterSegments. Pause the loop while the adapter has no stream.
verifierNote: pct = min(100, round(rms*400)) turns red above 90 (VocalView.tsx:640-646, GuitarBassView.tsx:582-588), i.e. RMS ≈ 0.225 ≈ −13 dBFS, with no peak or clip latch. One correction: DOM updates are throttled to about 15 fps (the 66 ms gate), although the rAF itself keeps running.

title: Every drag frame commits to the global store and re-renders the whole DAW (undo JSON and collab update included)
evidence:
Writes per gesture:
- Note move/resize calls `onChange(currentEvents)` on every mousemove (PianoRoll.tsx:1212-1272); velocity drag does the same (:928-931), and so does every input event of the toolbar slider (:1684-1693).
- The modal forwards each call to updateMidiClipEvents (PianoRollModal.tsx:41-48), which replaces the `tracks` array (tracksSlice.ts:700-714).
What each write triggers:
- usePlaybackEngine subscribes to `s.tracks` (usePlaybackEngine.ts:363) and is called in DawAppInner (DawApp.tsx:80). The app root and every non-memoised child (Timeline, TrackList, ChannelStrip, LibraryPanel, both modals) re-render; only TransportBar is memo'd. 28 modules subscribe to the full tracks array.
- The undo tracker's handleChange calls watched() (JSON.stringify of all tracks, chord regions and score marks) before its identity check (undoMiddleware.ts:194-205, 222-224).
- In collab, every set() is diffed into Yjs immediately (collabMiddleware.ts:97-109).
- If the dock's PIANO ROLL tab is open on the same clip, a second PianoRoll redraws too (DawApp.tsx:511-512).
- PianoRoll redraws its canvases in passive effects after that render (PianoRoll.tsx:941-952).
impact: Drag smoothness gets worse as the project grows, because every mouse frame stringifies all tracks and re-renders the arrangement. Collaborators receive about 60 Yjs updates per second during a drag. The note trails the cursor by at least one frame.
recommendation: Keep the gesture as a local draft (ref + notes-layer redraw in rAF) and commit once on pointerup. That gives one store write, one undo step and one Yjs update per gesture. Commit the slider on release or at about 10 Hz. Hosts should select only the clip (`useStore(s => findClip(s, trackId, clipId))`) instead of `tracks`. Outside this slice: move the tracks subscription out of DawAppInner and make undo change detection lazy.

title: Grid, ruler and velocity canvases are sized to the whole clip (not the screen) and fully repainted on every change
evidence:
Canvas sizing and drawing:
- The grid uses `w = Math.max(container.clientWidth, gridW)`, `h = gridH`, `canvas.width = w * dpr` (PianoRoll.tsx:592-602).
- Each draw does a full fill, 73 full-width row fills, every beat and sub-grid line, and every note, with no viewport culling (:604-706).
- The ruler (:490-503) and velocity lane (:750-761) are also full width.
Size: gridW = totalTicks x 40*zoom/480 (:341-342), with zoom up to 6 (:318) and vZoom up to 4 (:321). For the default 16-bar 4/4 clip at DPR 2:
- zoom 1: 5,440 x 1,752 device px (~9.5 Mpx, ~38 MB);
- zoom 6 and vZoom 4: 32,640 x 7,008 (~229 Mpx, ~0.9 GB).
Other costs:
- The canvas is reallocated on every zoom wheel step (:596-602).
- getComputedStyle runs on every draw (:95-105, 394-396).
- marqueeRect and the selection are dependencies of drawGrid, drawVelLane and drawPiano (:717-733, 844-854, 351-358/435), so each marquee mousemove repaints all three canvases.
- There is no ResizeObserver.
- Keys, ruler and velocity panes copy the grid's scroll offsets in onScroll (:981-989), which runs after the grid has already scrolled.
impact: Memory and repaint cost grow with clip length times zoom, not with screen size. Longer clips or high zoom can hit browser canvas limits (Chrome about 32,767 px per side; iOS Safari about 16.7 Mpx of area, which a 32-bar clip at default zoom or vZoom 2 on an iPad already exceeds), and the grid goes blank. Every drag or marquee frame repaints millions of pixels. The key column and ruler visibly lag the grid during fast trackpad scrolls. Widening the window leaves an unpainted strip.
recommendation: Use viewport-sized canvases with a spacer element that provides the scroll extent, and draw from the scroll offset. Cache the static lane and grid layer per zoom (OffscreenCanvas), draw only visible notes, and put the marquee and playhead on an overlay. Redraw once per rAF when something is dirty. Add a ResizeObserver, and read theme colours once (again only on theme change).
verifierNote: The canvas is sized as `w = Math.max(container.clientWidth, gridW)`, `h = gridH` × dpr (PianoRoll.tsx:592-602), and drawGrid fills every row, line and note with no culling. drawGrid depends on marqueeRect and selectedIndices (:717-733), so marquee moves repaint it. There is no ResizeObserver, and scroll sync happens in onScroll (:981-989). The size math checks out: 68 beats × 40 px × DPR 2 = 5,440 px at zoom 1 and 32,640 at zoom 6; vZoom 4 gives a height of 73 × 48 × 2 = 7,008.
impactNote: The facts are right. The grid canvas is max(clientWidth, gridW) x gridH x DPR (PianoRoll.tsx:592-602), and every draw repaints all 73 rows and every beat line from x=0 (:604-650) with no culling. The size claims are inflated for this audience, though. On Chromebooks (DPR 1-1.25) at default zoom, a 16-bar clip is about 2720x876 CSS px, which canvas handles comfortably. The 0.9 GB case needs zoom 6 and vZoom 4 together, which is an edge case. The iOS Safari limit is outside the stated Chrome/Chromebook target. The 'unpainted strip on widen' only happens when gridW < container width, which is unlikely at 1366-1440 px with the 16-bar minimum. The marquee repainting all three canvases and the key column lagging the grid on scroll are real but cosmetic. This is a worthwhile perf refactor, but it is effort L for a mostly speculative user impact. Medium.
regressionRisks: Viewport canvases plus a scroll spacer is a substantial rewrite of hit-testing (getCanvasCoords and every handler that uses x/pixelsPerTick), playhead and loop placement, the initial auto-scroll, and the zoom-anchor logic. It's easy to bring back off-by-scroll bugs. An OffscreenCanvas cache must be invalidated on theme change, zoom, vZoom, gridSize, time signature and noteLabels (drum labels). Any tutorial anchors inside the roll must still resolve after the DOM structure changes.

Each change is committed to the store, undo history and collaborators. Group velocity edits are only possible through the toolbar slider.

title: Prism chord colours compare clip-relative note ticks with song-time chord regions
evidence: resolveNoteColor tests `ev.startTick >= (chordRegions[j].rawStartTick ?? chordRegions[j].startTick)` (PianoRoll.tsx:55-72), and it is called per note in drawGrid (:668-675) and drawVelLane (:806-813). Chord regions are in song ticks: the timeline draws them with `tickToPixel(region.startTick, ...)` (Timeline.tsx:1231). The timeline's mini-notes use the same mismatched comparison (Timeline.tsx:186-193).

recommendation: Compare `timelineStartTick + ev.startTick`. Precompute a sorted region list and binary-search it, instead of a reverse scan per note on each of two canvases. Fix the timeline copy in the same change.

title: Bar lines, ruler numbers and snapping are clip-relative, while playhead, loop and notation use song bars
evidence: Bar lines and numbers are drawn from x=0 starting at '1' (`barNum = beat / beatsPerBar + 1`, :534-553; grid :618-634). title: PitchAnalyzer's YIN costs O(frame²) on the main thread and still runs via UNISON after recordings
evidence: analyzeBuffer calls yinDetectOffline every 512 samples (PitchAnalyzer.ts:75-91). Its difference function is a full 1024x1024 double loop per frame (YinCore.ts:340-347), even though the pitch search stops at maxPeriod (sampleRate/50 = 882 at 44.1 kHz). That is about 1.05 M inner iterations per frame, roughly 90 M per second of audio, plus two Float32Array allocations per frame (:333-334). The grouping loop also re-sorts the current segment for a median on every frame (PitchAnalyzer.ts:153). It runs synchronously when UNISON is active: after each recording, useAudioChordDetection.ts:272-279 -> unisonSlice.analyzeAudio (:228-240) -> audioToUnison.ts:90.
impact: A 60-second take means about 5 billion iterations, i.e. several seconds of frozen UI right after the user stops recording, with no progress or cancel. 5-minute takes (the recording cap) are much worse.
recommendation: Run it in a Worker (src/daw/workers already exists). Compute the difference function with FFT autocorrelation, or limit tau to maxPeriod and downsample to about 11 kHz. Reuse buffers and report progress.
verifierNote: yinDetectOffline runs a full halfLen × halfLen difference loop (1024 × 1024 with FRAME_LENGTH 2048, YinCore.ts:340-347) and allocates two Float32Arrays per frame (:333-334). It is called every HOP_SIZE 512 samples (PitchAnalyzer.ts:62-63, 75-91), synchronously, via audioToUnison.ts:90 from unisonSlice.analyzeAudio (:228-240). useAudioChordDetection.ts:272-279 calls it only when unisonDoc is set, which matches the 'when UNISON is active' condition.

title: Practice view re-renders the whole screen and keyboard ~30x/s during playback
evidence: PracticeTrackView.tsx:85 subscribes at top level: `const position = useStore((s) => s.position);` (useTransport pushes it ~30x/s). chordNow (294-314) lists `position` in its deps and returns a fresh object every tick even when the chord hasn't changed. It is passed as `scales={[chordNow]}` (445) with an inline `onScaleChange={() => {}}` (453). In ScaleKeyboard, `scale` (111) is therefore new each tick, so scalePcs (137-140), litKeys (141-151, a new Map over up to 48 keys), playedKeys (153-165) and labels (167-175) are all rebuilt. PianoKeyboard (no React.memo, PianoKeyboard.tsx:43) then re-renders every key, and each key calls getActiveNote, which spreads and sortBy-sorts the note lists (177-195). ChordChart also receives `position` (PracticeTrackView.tsx:488) and re-formats every region symbol (ChordChart.tsx:53-64) only to move one highlight. The header, transport and PromptList re-render too.
impact: About 150–250 elements are reconciled ~30 times a second for as long as the student plays, though the lit chord and chart highlight change only at chord boundaries (about every 2 s at 120 BPM). On low-end school Chromebooks this competes with Tone.js scheduling on the main thread (late key highlights, risk of audio timing jitter) and drains battery.
recommendation: Replace the top-level position subscription with a selector that returns the current cycle index, a primitive that changes only at boundaries (e.g. `useStore(s => regionIndexAt(s.position % cycleTicks, cycleRegions))`). Memoize chordNow on that index and pass ChordChart an activeIndex instead of position. Wrap ScaleKeyboard, PianoKeyboard and PromptList in React.memo with stable props (memoized Maps, stable callbacks). Move the transport into its own component that subscribes only to isPlaying/isRecording/isCountingIn/loopEnabled/bpm.
verifierNote: Confirmed: PracticeTrackView.tsx:85 subscribes to `position`, which useTransport.ts writes about every 33 ms during playback. chordNow (294-314) depends on position and returns a new object every tick, PianoKeyboard has no memo, and getActiveNote spreads and sortBy-sorts the note lists for every key (PianoKeyboard.tsx:177-195). ChordChart also takes `position` (488). The lists being sorted are tiny and there are only about 36-48 keys, so this is measurable waste rather than lag that would disturb Tone's look-ahead scheduling. High overstates it.
impactNote: The mechanism is real. PracticeTrackView.tsx:85 subscribes to `position`, which useTransport.ts:72-97 pushes about 30 times a second through rAF. chordNow (PracticeTrackView.tsx:294-314) depends on `position` and builds a new object on every tick. ScaleKeyboard is not memoized, and PianoKeyboard.tsx:43 is not either; its getActiveNote (177-195) spreads and sorts the note lists once per key. ChordChart.tsx:53-64 re-formats every chord symbol on each tick. So the whole practice screen reconciles about 30 times a second while playing, even though the visible output changes only at chord boundaries. The impact is overstated, though. The arrays being sorted are tiny (held notes plus context notes), the keyboard is roughly 4 octaves, and Tone.js schedules audio ahead of time, so 'audio timing jitter' is speculative. On a 4-core Chromebook this is a few milliseconds of main-thread work per frame: measurable waste and battery drain, but not usually visible jank. The index selector has to handle the cycleTicks===0 case and loop wrap. Wrapping PianoKeyboard in React.memo affects every other user of this shared component (lessons and games). Those callers pass inline props, so the memo is useless there unless they are fixed too, but it is harmless. title: Finishing any lesson can report completion for an unrelated classroom activity

In fact, when the URL has no launch params the hook falls back to a sessionStorage stash: `paramsRef.current = readStashedMspLaunchParams();` (useMspModuleCompletion.ts:43-52). `clearStashedMspLaunchParams` (mspLaunchParams.ts:82-88) is defined and re-exported but never called. Nothing checks that the stashed module/activityRef is this tutorial, and firedRef resets on every DawApp mount.
impact: Once a student has opened any app-route slide in a tab (a Learn lesson, a Genre lesson or a Studio lesson), every Studio lesson they later finish in that tab records a completion for the stashed activity. Teachers can see 'completed' for work the student never finished, or duplicate submissions.
recommendation: In TutorialLayer, report only when `armed` and the stashed launch is module 'studio' with an activityRef matching this tutorial id. Clear the stash after a successful report, and when a lesson starts without launch params. Consider keying the stash by module.
verifierNote: useMspModuleCompletion.ts:43-52 falls back to readStashedMspLaunchParams() when the URL has no launch params. clearStashedMspLaunchParams has no non-test callers, and reportCompletion doesn't compare the stashed module or activityRef with the current tutorial. TutorialLayer calls it on every finish (110-111, 132-135). The layer's comment ('inert unless … opened from a live slide', 42-43) is therefore wrong. Whether the classroom side drops stale interactions wasn't verified.
impactNote: The mechanism is confirmed. useMspModuleCompletion.ts:43-52 falls back to readStashedMspLaunchParams() whenever the URL has no params. The stash is written by LessonContainer, GenreLessonContainerV2 and TutorialLayer, but clearStashedMspLaunchParams (mspLaunchParams.ts:82-88) is never called. reportCompletion (useMspModuleCompletion.ts:55-77) doesn't check that the stashed module or activityRef matches the current activity. firedRef is per-mount, so any later Studio lesson finished in the same tab writes an inbox completion for the stashed slide activity. Two things lower the impact. It needs a specific sequence: open an app-route slide in this tab, don't finish it, then finish a different Studio lesson in the same tab. And whether the live tab still accepts the response after the interaction ends is unverified, so the claimed false completion shown to teachers is plausible but unproven. The same bug also affects Learn and Genre lessons, so the fix belongs in the hook, not in TutorialLayer.

A mismatch would silently stop legitimate completions from reaching teachers, which is worse than the current bug, so verify it with a slide-launched end-to-end run. Clearing the stash after reporting must happen only after recordMspResponseForUser succeeds. Clearing the stash on a lesson start without params must not break the documented case where ActivityFlow navigate() strips the query mid-module.

title: On phones the scaled keyboard shrinks labels to 5–8 px, and 4-octave windows overflow
evidence: One octave is OCTAVE_WIDTH*2 = 238 px (ScaleKeyboard.tsx:37; useExpandedRange.ts:3). That makes the Theory board 714 px (3 octaves, PracticeTrackView.tsx:52), and a widened chord window 4 octaves, or 952 px (283-287). Labels ride inside the transformed box (ScaleKeyboard.tsx:222-279: text-sm/text-base at 259 and 267, octave labels text-[11px] at 300). At a 375 px phone width (343 px of content) fit ≈ 0.48, giving ~6.7 px degrees, ~7.7 px names and ~5.3 px octave labels. A 4-octave board hits MIN_SCALE 0.42 (57) and renders ~400 px wide in a 343 px column. Being centred with translateX(-50%) (229-233), it spills past both edges, and the left overflow (the lowest, bass and left-hand keys) can't be scrolled to. useFitScale re-measures only on host/root resize (406-410), not when content above the chart changes height (the take message, the voicing switch wrapping).
impact: The degree numbers and note names the screen exists to teach become unreadable on phones and small tablets, and bass keys can be cut off.
recommendation: Render the label bands outside the scaled element at a fixed minimum (≥12 px), positioned from the measured key centres × fit. On narrow screens, show a 2-octave window around the active voicing or tonic, or allow horizontal scroll with the active chord scrolled into view. Observe the chart and header with ResizeObserver so the fit stays right.
verifierNote: OCTAVE_WIDTH is 119 (useExpandedRange.ts:3), so OCTAVE_PX is 238 and a 3-octave board is 714 px. The labels sit inside the scaled box (ScaleKeyboard.tsx:222-279), which gives about 6.7/7.7/5.3 px text at a fit of about 0.48. title: Detection runs on every store update, and identity checks pass on undo or collab sync
evidence: Detection subscribes to the whole store: `useStore.subscribe((s) => evalMain(s, true))` (useTutorialDetection.ts:51-53). title: Suggest Chords reads display labels as chord types, so every real project counts as 'extended' and slash chords win
evidence: analyzeChordStyle classifies `unstepChord(region.name)` (suggestionEngine.ts:138) against TRIAD_QUALITIES and SEVENTH_QUALITIES (42-80), which hold full engine names ('major', 'minor7', 'dominant7'). Chord-region names in the store are abbreviated labels. prismSlice.ts:548-549 sets `name: abbreviateSequence(ionianToModeLabel(known, mode))`, giving '1 maj' or '5 dom7'. chordRegionNotation.ts:14-24 lists the other sources: 'G dom7' from Prism suggest and 'Dminor7' from the live analyzer. Since 'maj', 'min7' and 'dom7' are in neither set, classifyQuality (115-119) returns 'extended'. preferredQualities (157) becomes ['maj', 'min', ...], which never equals a graph name. filterByStyle (215-236) then scores every triad and 7th 0 and every slash or extended option 1.0. Trace: the '1 major' options include '4 major/1' and '1 major/6' (progressionGraph.ts:2-16), and '1 major|4 major/1' leads only to '1 major' (89). The 'Most Common' walk therefore loops C, F/C, C, F/C, and after I-IV it picks C/E. A second bug: extractGraphSeed's fallback expansion (193-198) uses /\bdom\b/ and similar patterns, which can't match 'dom7', 'maj7' or 'min7' (there is no word boundary before the 7).
impact: Affects every Suggest Chords open, Re-roll or measure change in a project that already has chords. The StyleBadge (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:50-71) says 'Style: Mixed' even for an all-triad pop song. Suggestions favour pedal slash chords (F/C, C/E) over the student's own chord vocabulary, the opposite of 'style-aware'.
recommendation: Classify from the canonical key, e.g. normalizeQuality(unstepChord(r.degreeKey ?? r.name)); normalizeQuality already exists in src/lib/chordNotation/qualities.ts:237. Remove the regex expansion in extractGraphSeed. Add unit tests that cover each label source listed in chordRegionNotation.ts.
verifierNote: The code matches the finding. analyzeChordStyle classifies `unstepChord(region.name)` (suggestionEngine.ts:138), and deriveChordRegions stores `name: abbreviateSequence(ionianToModeLabel(known, mode))`, e.g. '1 maj' (prismSlice.ts:548-549). 'maj', 'dom7' and similar fall through to 'extended' in classifyQuality (115-119), so slash options such as '4 major/1' score highest in filterByStyle (215-236). The regex fallback can't match 'maj7' because there is no word boundary before the 7 (193-198). Suggestions are skewed rather than blocked, so medium fits better than high.
impactNote: The bug is real. analyzeChordStyle classifies unstepChord(region.name) (suggestionEngine.ts:138), and unstepChord just returns the text after the first space (naming.ts:268-273). Region names are abbreviated: prismSlice.ts:548-549 builds them with abbreviateSequence (naming.ts:286-291, giving '1 maj' or '5 dom7'), and commitPrismSuggestion writes name = noteName such as 'G dom7' (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:170-177). 'maj', 'min', 'dom7', 'min7' and 'maj7' are in neither TRIAD_QUALITIES nor SEVENTH_QUALITIES (42-80), so classifyQuality (115-119) returns 'extended' and extendedRatio is about 1. filterByStyle (215-236) then gives every graph triad a score of 0 and every slash option ('major/1', 'major/6', which also fall to 'extended') a score of 1. The stable sort puts '4 major/1' first from '1 major' (progressionGraph.ts:2-16), and '1 major|4 major/1' only leads to '1 major' (progressionGraph.ts:89), so the C, F/C loop is plausible for 'Most Common'. title: Engine inputs don't survive reloads: cloud saves drop the mode, and strum/tilt and the progression being built are never saved

No save path includes strumMode, strumAmount, tiltMode or tiltAmount (defaults at prismSlice.ts:1397-1400). Collab syncs rootNote, mode, genre, rhythmName and swing, but not strum or tilt (YjsDocManager.ts:394-399).
impact: Opening a cloud project saved in A Aeolian restores it as A Ionian. The Prism palette is re-voiced from a different root, and degree labels, track colours and suggestions all change, so the student's minor song looks major. After any refresh, cloud open or collab join, genre, rhythm and swing come back but strum and tilt reset to Synchronized/0 and Balanced/0, so pressing Create again produces a different clip. The progression in the Prism builder is wiped and Create stays disabled until it is rebuilt, even though its clip and chord regions are still there.

Save stringSeq in both local and cloud saves; chordSeq can be recomputed with degreeNameToChord and availableNextChords with computeNextChords on load. Sync strum and tilt through Yjs.

title: Create mislabels the repeated bars of 2- and 3-chord loops and silently drops chords past the 7th
evidence: distributeChords plays 2 chords as A B A B (midiExport.ts:38-44) and 3 chords as A B C plus a random repeat (45-52). deriveChordRegions (prismSlice.ts:495-590, called at 1611-1618 with state.stringSeq) labels the i-th region with `collapsed[regionIndex]` (543, 571), which assumes the sequence plays once. In a 2-chord loop, regions 3 and 4 index past the end of `collapsed` and fall back to `name: abbreviateSequence(chordNameInKey(...))`, a letter name, with `degreeKey: undefined` (550-561, 576-585). The fallback names the chord from notes sorted lowest first (529), so slash voicings are misnamed: C/E sorts to [E,G,C,E] and comes out as plain 'E'. With 8 or more chords only bars 1-3 can be split (`const halves = [1, 2, 3]`, then `halves.length = chords.length - 4`, 55-60), so chords 8 and up are never played. The Prism builder has no chord-count limit.
impact: Triggered by Create with the 2-3 chord progressions the lessons ask for. In degree view the chord ruler reads '1 maj | 5 maj | C maj | G maj' (Timeline.tsx:1259-1261). Bars 3-4 lose their degreeKey, so later suggestions seeded from them lose context. Long progressions lose chords with no warning.
recommendation: Have generateChordMidi return chord spans ({startTick, endTick, chordIndex}[]) and build regions from them instead of reverse-engineering notes. Either cap the builder at 7 chords and say so, or extend Create beyond 4 bars.
verifierNote: distributeChords plays 2 chords as A B A B and 3 chords with a random 4th bar (midiExport.ts:38-52). deriveChordRegions indexes `collapsed[regionIndex]`, which is undefined for bars 3-4, so it falls back to chordNameInKey with `degreeKey: undefined` (prismSlice.ts:543-585). For more than 4 chords only 3 bars can be split (`halves = [1,2,3]`, midiExport.ts:55-60), so chords 8 and up are never played. I found no chord-count cap in the builder.

title: Committing a suggestion deletes whole chord regions that only partly overlap the insertion window

impact: A student right-clicks inside a long region (for example an 8-bar chord from audio detection) and commits a 1-bar suggestion. The labels for the other 7 bars disappear without notice and can only be recovered with Undo if noticed straight away.

verifierNote: commitPrismSuggestion keeps only regions entirely outside the window: `chordRegions.filter((r) => r.endTick <= prismSuggestInsertTick || r.startTick >= insertEnd)` (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:176-179). Any region that straddles the window is dropped whole, and only Undo can recover it.

title: Create starts a fresh module Worker per click for under a millisecond of work, with no error handling or loading state
evidence: generateToTracks runs `new Worker(new URL('../workers/midiWorker.ts', import.meta.url), { type: 'module' })` on every call (prismSlice.ts:1579-1582). It sets only `onmessage` and calls `worker.terminate()` only inside it (1595-1622); there is no onerror or onmessageerror. The response handler uses `state`, `rootMidi` and state.stringSeq/mode captured at click time (1569-1577, 1611-1617). The work itself is generateChordMidi (midiWorker.ts:25-53), at most 16 hits x 4 bars x 6 notes (midiExport.ts:113-185). The unused generateOrchestration already calls orchestrate synchronously (1671). handleGenerate shows no pending state (PrismStudio.tsx:98-100).
impact: Every Create pays for starting a thread and fetching, parsing and running the worker's modules before a few hundred events are produced, so the clip appears after a pause with no feedback (worse on Chromebooks). If the worker script fails to load, for example a stale hashed chunk after a deploy, Create silently does nothing and the worker is never terminated. The lesson's Create step only advances when chordRegions changes (tutorials.ts:190-201), so it can't complete. If the key changes while the worker is starting, the response overwrites the regions with ones derived for the old key.
recommendation: Call generateChordMidi synchronously inside generateToTracks (it is pure and takes under 1 ms) and delete midiWorker.ts. If a worker is kept, make it long-lived and add onerror, request ids and a loading state.
verifierNote: generateToTracks starts `new Worker(new URL('../workers/midiWorker.ts'...), {type:'module'})` on every click and sets only onmessage, with terminate() inside it (prismSlice.ts:1579-1622). title: Genre strum presets are off by one, and 'Synchronized' and 'Balanced' aren't implemented
evidence: GENRE_STRUM documents 'mode: 0=Synchronized, 1=Down, 2=Up, 3=Human' (genreMap.ts:90-114), but StrumMode starts at 1 (Synchronized=1 through Human=4, types.ts:46-51). selectGenre stores the raw value with `strumMode: strum.mode` (prismSlice.ts:1495-1505). generateChordMidi only special-cases Up and Human for strum, and HighsLeading and Human for tilt (midiExport.ts:118-132, 143-157). So whenever the amount is above 0, Synchronized behaves exactly like Down and Balanced like Bass Leading. The amount sliders are always enabled (ChordBuilder.tsx:280-304).
impact: Happens on every genre pick, including the lesson step 'Choose a genre — try Jazz'. Jazz, Neo Soul, R&B, Bossa, Jam Band and Indie (meant to be Human) become Up: chord notes reversed and up to 30 ticks late. Reggae (meant to be Up) becomes Down. Rock, Funk and Salsa display 'Synchronized' while strumming down. Pop, Hip Hop, Ballad and EDM store 0, which isn't a StrumMode at all. The lesson hint that a genre 'nudges swing, strum and rhythm' (tutorials.ts:165) is wrong for strum.
recommendation: Store StrumMode enum values in GENRE_STRUM (or add 1 in selectGenre, with a test). Make Synchronized and Balanced ignore the amount, or disable the amount slider for them.
verifierNote: GENRE_STRUM uses 0-3, with Jazz `{ mode: 3 }` (genreMap.ts:90-114), but StrumMode runs Synchronized=1 through Human=4 (types.ts:46-51). selectGenre stores `strumMode: strum.mode` unchanged (prismSlice.ts:1502). generateChordMidi only special-cases Up and Human for strum and HighsLeading and Human for tilt (midiExport.ts:118-157), so Jazz plays as Up and Synchronized with an amount above 0 acts like Down.

title: Swing silently does nothing on 7 of 41 rhythms, including the default
evidence: swingRhythm only delays a hit when `Math.floor(start/240) % 2 === 1 && dur === 240` or `Math.floor(start/120) % 2 === 1 && dur === 120` (rhythmUtils.ts:14-29). Whole Notes, Half Notes, Quarters and 3-3-2 Quarters have no off-beats. Staccato Eighths, Funk 1 and Funk 2a put their off-beat 8ths at ticks 240, 720 and so on with 120-tick durations, so they are skipped (chordRhythms.ts:4-14, 25-34, 53-57, 223-232, 239-244). The default rhythm is 'Whole Notes' (prismSlice.ts:1393), and selectGenre adds 'Whole Notes' four extra times to every genre's rhythm pool (378-395). As a result about 21% of Jazz picks and about 46% of Funk picks land on a pattern that can't swing. isSwingable (35-45) exists but nothing calls it, and the Swing slider is always enabled (ChordBuilder.tsx:280). The same length check means procedural drum hi-hats and rides never swing, e.g. the Jazz ride skip notes (drumPatterns.ts:325-339) and the Blues 'shuffle' hats (636-653) (drumGenerator.ts:62-66).
impact: Lesson 1 tells students to 'drag the Swing slider past 20' because 'Swing delays the off-beats' (tutorials.ts:171-178). On these patterns the step passes but nothing changes audibly, and nothing explains why. Staccato off-beat comping can never swing.
recommendation: Swing by position: delay any hit that starts on an off-beat 8th or 16th, shortening it only if it would overlap the next hit. Use isSwingable to disable or annotate the slider ('This pattern has no off-beats to swing'). Add a test for each rhythm.
verifierNote: swingRhythm only swings off-beat hits that are exactly 240 or 120 ticks long (rhythmUtils.ts:17-24). So 'Staccato Eighths' ([240,120]…, chordRhythms.ts:25-34) never swings, and isSwingable has no callers outside the barrel. However, Whole, Half and Quarter patterns have no off-beats, so swing doing nothing there is musically correct. The real defect is the short off-beat patterns plus the lack of slider feedback.

title: The 'Most Common' label has no data behind it, Re-roll leaves the visible set unchanged, and the walk ignores 24% of the graph
evidence: Graph options are listed by scale degree, not by how often they occur: '1 major' lists '#1 diminished', '2 minor', '2 major', '3 minor', and so on (progressionGraph.ts:2-16), and '2 minor7' lists 15 options in rising degree order (815-831). The 'Most Common' strategy takes `opts[0]` after style sorting (suggestionEngine.ts:321-334); in an empty C-major project this gives C, Dm, Em, F. Strategies 1-3 always give the same result and only 4-5 use Math.random (330-344). regeneratePrismSuggestions resets `prismSuggestActiveIdx: 0` (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:206-210), so Re-roll (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:489-501, key R) leaves the displayed set unchanged. History is capped at 3 chords (suggestionEngine.ts:174-175, whose comment says 'graph supports up to ~3-deep keys', and 301-302), but 130 of the 548 graph keys are 4-5 chords deep. getOptions' percent filter (progression.ts:19) would also drop the highest degrees (V, vi) rather than the rarest chords.
impact: Students are told a stepwise I-ii-iii-IV climb is the 'Most Common' progression, which misteaches theory. Re-roll looks broken. Longer curated progressions, such as ii-vi-ii-bVI-bVII resolving to I, can never come up in suggestions, even though the Prism palette reaches them from the same graph.
recommendation: Add weights to the graph (for example from the Music Atlas song library) and rank by them. Until then, rename the strategies (for example 'Smooth', 'Alternative', 'Bold', 'Surprise'). Make Re-roll re-randomise every set or jump to a random set. Look up with up to 5 chords of history before shortening.
verifierNote: Strategies 1-3 are deterministic (`opts[0]`, `opts[1]`, `opts[2]`), and only strategies 4-5 use Math.random (suggestionEngine.ts:321-344). regeneratePrismSuggestions resets `prismSuggestActiveIdx: 0` (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:206-210), so Re-roll redisplays the same 'Most Common' set. Graph options are listed in degree order (progressionGraph.ts:2-16), and history is capped at 3 chords (suggestionEngine.ts:301-302).

title: Committing a suggestion deletes chords outside the inserted bars, and the bar maths assumes 4/4
evidence:
- commitPrismSuggestion keeps only regions entirely outside the range: `chordRegions.filter((r) => r.endTick <= prismSuggestInsertTick || r.startTick >= insertEnd)` (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:177-179). A region that straddles either edge is removed whole instead of trimmed.
- `ticksPerMeasure = 1920` is a literal (161).
- The modal's 'Bar N' is computed as `insertTick / 1920` (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:170).
- Preview chords last `(4 * 60000) / bpm` (243).
- The transport supports other meters (setTimeSignature, transportSlice.ts:194-199), and LeadSheetView already uses `ticksPerBar(timeSignatureNumerator, beatUnit)` (LeadSheetView.tsx:78-81).
impact: Right-click at bar 3 inside a chord spanning bars 1–4 and commit: bars 1–2 lose their chord. In 3/4 or 6/8 projects the suggestion lands on the wrong bar lines (4 'measures' is 5⅓ bars of 3/4) and the header names the wrong bar.
recommendation:
- Trim straddling regions to the outside parts: [start, insertTick) and [insertEnd, end).
- Run respellLeadingChordRegions on the merged result.
- Compute ticks per bar from the store's time signature in the commit, the header and the preview, using the shared ticksPerBar helper.
verifierNote: commitPrismSuggestion keeps only `r.endTick <= prismSuggestInsertTick || r.startTick >= insertEnd` (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:177-179), so a region straddling either edge is dropped whole. `ticksPerMeasure = 1920` (161), `insertBar = Math.floor(insertTick / 1920) + 1` (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:170) and `wholeNoteDuration = (4 * 60000) / bpm` all assume 4/4.

The modal header uses insertTick / 1920 (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:170) and the preview uses (4*60000)/bpm (243). Both bugs are real. Songs do get non-4/4 time signatures (seedStudioFromSong.ts:35-36). The flow is narrower than the core Prism path: you reach it by right-clicking a blank track area, then committing. The lost chords are recoverable with undo because chordRegions is captured. Medium rather than high.
regressionRisks:
- Trimming straddling regions creates new region fragments. Mint unique ids for them (see prism-ui-05) and keep melodyOverrides consistent.
- respellLeadingChordRegions on the merged result can respell existing chords the user had spelled deliberately.
- Bar maths from the time signature must agree with Timeline/LeadSheet ticksPerBar, including beat unit (6/8).

title: Refresh, SPA return and collaboration restore Prism state inconsistently
evidence:
Saved data covers only part of the state: SessionData.prism holds rootNote, rhythmName, genre, swing and mode, plus chordRegions (SessionSerializer.ts:231-241, 325-332). deserializeSession spreads freshProjectHarmony() (762-793).

On refresh:
- The builder progression (stringSeq, chordSeq) is reset (512-517).
- strumMode, strumAmount, tiltMode and tiltAmount fall back to the slice defaults (prismSlice.ts:1397-1400), even though the restored genre is what set them (selectGenre, 1495-1506).
- measureRowSizes, measureRestMap and measureFermatas, seeded from songs (seedStudioFromSong.ts:39-46), become null.
- selectedTrackId stays at the default 'demo-chords' (prismSlice.ts:1410), an unused demo track (tracksSlice.ts:368-372), so Prism shows 'Select a MIDI track'.
- rootTrackColor stays null, so the Key chip loses its colour (TransportBar.tsx:415-419) and new tracks get palette colours instead of the key colour (tracksSlice.ts:571-574).

On SPA return: resetSessionToEmpty (649-678) clears rootNote but not rootTrackColor, so a new project's first tracks take the previous project's key colour.

In collaboration: peers apply rootNote and mode with a raw setState (yjsToZustand.ts:385-387), bypassing setRootNote, so their rootTrackColor goes stale.
impact: A student who refreshes mid-lesson loses the chords they built in Prism, so lesson checks on chordSeq fail. They also lose the strum and tilt they set and the song's lead-sheet layout. Track selection and the key colour disappear, and new tracks get mismatched colours.
recommendation:
- Decide field by field what belongs to the project. Treat key, mode, chord lane, lead-sheet layout and the feel settings as project data, saved locally and to the cloud.
- Save the builder progression in the autosave at least.
- Derive the key colour with a selector instead of storing rootTrackColor.
- Select the first MIDI track after every load, and drop the 'demo-chords' default.
verifierNote: SessionData.prism holds only rootNote, rhythmName, genre, swing and mode (SessionSerializer.ts:231-241), and deserializeSession spreads freshProjectHarmony(). That resets stringSeq, chordSeq and the measureRowSizes, measureRestMap and measureFermatas layout, and strum and tilt stay at the slice defaults. selectedTrackId defaults to 'demo-chords' (prismSlice.ts:1410), and only addTrack or loadProjectTemplate change it (tracksSlice.ts:607, 992), never deserialize. resetSessionToEmpty leaves rootTrackColor alone, which addTrack reuses (tracksSlice.ts:571-574), and yjsToZustand.ts:385-387 patches rootNote and mode directly.

Mostly accurate:
- SessionData.prism (SessionSerializer.ts:231-241) and deserializeSession (780-788) restore only key, mode, rhythm, genre, swing and chordRegions. The builder progression, strum and tilt, measureRowSizes/RestMap/Fermatas and leadSheetSections reset on refresh.
- selectedTrackId defaults to 'demo-chords' (prismSlice.ts:1410). That track is never created (createDemoTracks is unused, tracksSlice.ts:368). Only tracksSlice.ts:992 selects the first MIDI track, and deserializeSession does not use it.
- rootTrackColor is never restored or cleared on reset (TransportBar.tsx:415-419 uses it, addTrack uses it at tracksSlice.ts:571-574).

title: Building chords is silent and opaque: no audition, random colour picks, no key required
evidence:
- Nothing sounds when a chord is added. The grid calls addChord (ChordBuilder.tsx:190-203), which only updates chordSeq and stringSeq (prismSlice.ts:1525-1538).
- The spectrum adds a random chord from the clicked colour: `onSelectChord(chords[Math.floor(Math.random() * chords.length)])` (ColorSpectrum.tsx:89-97). Its segments are unlabelled divs (105-135).
- Grid buttons are neutral grey with degree codes in the default hybrid notation. The 15 first-chord options include '3 dom7#5' (visible in the a11y-studio-bottom-prism.png screenshot), with no link to the colours.
- With no key set, everything quietly uses C (PrismStudio.tsx:89).
- Each genre chip click also picks a random rhythm (findRandomRhythmForGenre, prismSlice.ts:383-395).
- Reusable alternatives exist:
  - `auditionNote(trackId, note, velocity)` already plays through the track's real instrument and effects (auditionNote.ts:16-41).
  - The landing tour's spectrum labels each colour with its chords and shows 'Pick a key to light up the spectrum' (HarmonySpectrum.tsx:96-102, 147-156).
impact: Students can't hear a chord before choosing it. The first time anything sounds is after a destructive Create followed by Play. The colour bar acts like a slot machine (the same click gives different chords) and nothing says what was added. That undercuts Prism's goal of linking colour to harmonic function.
recommendation:
- Play each chord on click (and optionally on hover or focus) through auditionNote on the selected track.
- Merge the grid and spectrum into one palette of colour-coded chord pills showing the name, Roman numeral and colour, grouped by colour family. Use the spectrum as a legend or filter.
- Make colour clicks deterministic and announce which chord was added.
- Require a key first.
- Show what each genre preset sets, or add an explicit dice button for its random rhythm.
verifierNote: The facts hold: addChord only updates chordSeq and stringSeq (prismSlice.ts:1525-1538) with no audition, ColorSpectrum picks `chords[Math.floor(Math.random() * chords.length)]` from unlabelled divs (ColorSpectrum.tsx:89-135), rootMidi falls back to C (PrismStudio.tsx:89), and selectGenre picks a random rhythm. But this is friction rather than a blocker, since students can still build and create progressions, so medium fits the rubric better than high.
impactNote:
The facts hold:
- addChord (prismSlice.ts:1525-1538) only updates the sequence; nothing plays.
- ColorSpectrum.tsx:89-97 picks Math.random() from the clicked colour group.
- The grid buttons are neutral grey (ChordBuilder.tsx:190-203).
- With no key, everything falls back to C (PrismStudio.tsx:89).
- auditionNote.ts exists for reuse.
These are real UX weaknesses that undercut Prism's teaching goal, but they are design improvements rather than defects that break a flow. Medium, not high. The 'no key required' part overlaps with prism-ui-01 and prism-ui-03.
regressionRisks:
- Auditioning through the track's instrument may need to start the Tone audio context on the first click; an unexpected sound during playback or recording could be captured, so skip audition while recording.
- Replacing the grid and spectrum with a merged palette risks the tutorial anchors and checks: lessons check chordSeq.length (tutorials.ts:159, 263, 502), and any data-tutorial-id on the Chord Selection grid must be kept.
- Deterministic colour clicks change existing behaviour that tests may rely on.
- A required key adds a step to lessons that currently allow Create without one.

title: The Harmony spectrum keeps adding major-scale chords in the 28 non-diatonic modes
evidence:
- ChordSelection limits options to diatonic modes: `!hasDiatonicProgressions ? [] : …`, and shows 'No progressions for this mode' (ChordBuilder.tsx:158-163, 204-211).
- PrismStudio passes the unfiltered options to the spectrum: `stringSeq.length === 0 ? availableFirstChords : availableNextChords` (PrismStudio.tsx:86-87, 198-203).
- addChord builds chords with degreeNameToChord, which calls getModeOffset(mode) (prismSlice.ts:463-472). getModeOffset returns 0 for any mode outside MODE_NAMES' seven diatonic modes (naming.ts:17-21; modes.ts:17-25), so the chord is built as major-scale (Ionian) on the tonic.
- The circle's mode menu lists all five MODE_GROUPS, 35 modes, with no warning (CircleOfFifths.tsx:308-339).
impact: Pick 'Phrygian Dominant' or 'Harmonic Minor': the grid says there are no progressions, but clicking colours still adds major-scale chords on the tonic, and Create writes chords that contradict the chosen mode.
recommendation: Apply the same isDiatonicMode check to the spectrum: dim it and show the same message. In the mode menu, separate 'Diatonic' from an 'Advanced (no chord suggestions)' group with a one-line explanation.
verifierNote: ChordSelection empties its options when `!isDiatonicMode(mode)` (ChordBuilder.tsx:158-163), but PrismStudio passes the unfiltered availableFirstChords or availableNextChords to ColorSpectrum (PrismStudio.tsx:86-87, 198-203). getModeOffset returns 0 for any mode outside MODE_NAMES (naming.ts:17-21), so degreeNameToChord builds Ionian chords on the tonic.

title: Prism edits sit outside undo: Cmd+Z skips them or half-reverts key changes
evidence:
- Undo captures only tracks, chordRegions and score marks (undoMiddleware.ts:38-43, 111-127), and only when those references change (196-206, 257-264).
- addChord, undoChord and clearSequence change chordSeq and stringSeq (prismSlice.ts:1525-1552), so they produce no snapshot.
- setRootNote and setMode change rootNote, mode, rootTrackColor, tracks and chordRegions (1431-1452, 1469-1490). Only tracks and chordRegions are captured.
impact: Add a chord in Prism and press Cmd+Z: the chord stays, and the previous track edit (e.g., the clip from the last Create) is undone instead. Change the key and press Cmd+Z: track colours and chord-lane names revert to the old key while the Key chip and circle still show the new one, so the chord lane's degree labels no longer match the key.
recommendation:
- Add rootNote and mode to the snapshot so key changes undo as one step, and derive the key colour instead of storing it.
- Route Cmd+Z to the builder's own Undo while focus is in the Prism panel, or include stringSeq and chordSeq in snapshots.
verifierNote: Undo watches only tracks, chordRegions and MARK_KEYS (undoMiddleware.ts:195-198, 257-264) and restores only those (124-127). addChord and undoChord touch chordSeq and stringSeq only, so Cmd+Z reverts the previous track edit instead. setRootNote and setMode rewrite tracks and chordRegions, which undo reverts, but rootNote, mode and rootTrackColor are not captured.

title: Every key or mode click rewrites every track and overwrites custom track colours
evidence:
setRootNote and setMode both run `tracks: tracks.map((t) => ({ ...t, color: hex }))` (prismSlice.ts:1434, 1472), creating new objects for every track on every click. That triggers:
- usePlaybackEngine's sync loop, which calls setVolume, setAudible, setPan and updateEffects on every track (usePlaybackEngine.ts:363, 379-426).
- Re-renders of Timeline, TimelineWithHeaders and TrackList, which all subscribe to s.tracks.
- The undo auto-capture, which JSON.stringify()s all tracks and chord regions immediately and again 300 ms later (undoMiddleware.ts:194-206, 222-254).
- The collab diff and a whole-session autosave.

The Library's KeySection calls setRootNote and then setMode on each click, so the work runs twice (KeySection.tsx:60-66). Users can pick per-track colours (`updateTrack(track.id, { color })`, TrackHeader.tsx:250-256), and these actions overwrite them.
impact: On larger projects each key change causes a visible main-thread hitch. Every track becomes the same key colour, erasing the colours students chose to tell parts apart.
recommendation:
- Stop storing the key colour on tracks: derive it where it is shown, or recolour only tracks marked as using the key colour.
- Otherwise, skip tracks whose colour is unchanged.
- Merge root and mode into one setKey(root, mode) action.
verifierNote: It is true that setRootNote and setMode run `tracks.map((t) => ({ ...t, color: hex }))` (prismSlice.ts:1434, 1472), overwriting colours users picked through updateTrack (TrackHeader.tsx:250-256), and KeySection calls both actions (KeySection.tsx:60-66). The performance claim is overstated, though: key changes are rare, discrete clicks, and the same usePlaybackEngine sync (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-426) already runs on every fader tick. The colour overwrite is the real problem, not a 'visible hitch'.

title: Five fixed-width cards don't fit the 33vh dock: clipped controls, nested scrolling, clipped mode menu
evidence:
Five scroll areas are nested:
- The dock body is a fixed `height: '33vh'` with overflow-y-auto (ChannelStrip.tsx:312-319).
- PrismPanel is another overflow-y-auto (PrismPanel.tsx:14).
- PrismStudio is `flex h-full overflow-x-auto` (PrismStudio.tsx:103-111), holding cards 160, 220, ≥200 (flexible), 200 and 180px wide (34-45, 113, 156-163, 194, 227-234, 240).
- The Chord Selection and Rhythm cards scroll themselves (158-161, 229-232).
- The option grid scrolls again (ChordBuilder.tsx:186-189).

RhythmExpression stacks seven controls (ChordBuilder.tsx:270-305). In a11y-studio-bottom-prism.png (1440×900) the chord grid is cut mid-row and Velocity Tilt and Tilt Amount are below the fold.

The mode menu is absolutely positioned with maxHeight 260 (CircleOfFifths.tsx:296-307) inside the overflow-x-auto row. That row's vertical overflow therefore also becomes auto, so the menu is clipped.

The pop-out (PrismPanel.tsx:38-42) repeats the same row, and the circle stays at size 130 (PrismStudio.tsx:151).
impact: On a 1366×768 school laptop the dock is about 250px tall, so half of Prism sits behind small scrollbars. Lesson spotlights point at half-visible cards, and the mode menu opens inside a clipped box.
recommendation:
- Lay Prism out in three zones that fit 250–300px: Key (circle at least 160px plus a mode select), Progression (sequence and palette, one scroller), and Feel (genre preset and rhythm, with strum and tilt under 'More').
- Add a sticky footer for Create.
- Open the mode list in a portal (Radix Select or Popover).
- Make the pop-out a genuinely larger layout or remove it.

Inside it, PrismPanel is `h-full overflow-y-auto` (PrismPanel.tsx:14), and PrismStudio is `flex h-full overflow-x-auto` with fixed 160, 220 and 200px cards plus a 180px card and a min-200 flex card; two of those cards scroll in Y, and the option grid has max-h-48 and overflow-y-auto. The absolutely positioned mode menu (CircleOfFifths.tsx:296-307, maxHeight 260) sits inside the overflow-x-auto row, which forces overflow-y to auto, so the menu is clipped.

title: Duplicated and misleading controls: two Undos, two Clears, two sequence views, a doubled heading
evidence:
- Two Undos: a Scissors icon in the Key card header (PrismStudio.tsx:134-147, aria-label 'Undo last chord'), plus an Undo button (ChordBuilder.tsx:226-237). Scissors means split elsewhere: it is tool 3 in the DAW's number-key tool shortcuts (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:15-20).

title: 'Suggest Chords' from a track only writes chord symbols, and can't feed the Prism builder
evidence:
- The menu item appears on a blank area of any track, including drum and audio tracks (Timeline.tsx:1812-1826, 3010-3017).
- The preview uses that track's instrument family (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:173-189).
- commitPrismSuggestion only sets chordRegions (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:166-186); no notes are written to the track.
- loadProgression, which could load a suggestion into the builder, has no callers (prismSlice.ts:1627-1655).
- Preview plays every chord as a whole note (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:243, 285-307), but commit spaces chords at measures×1920÷chord count (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:161-170).
- The header never shows the key. With no key set, suggestions are generated in C (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:70-79).
- In hybrid notation the pills show note names (SuggestionChordPill.tsx:35-42) while the builder shows degrees (ChordSequenceDisplay.tsx:44-51).
impact: A student right-clicks their Rhodes track, hears piano chords, presses Commit, and sees no new notes on the track. With two chords per bar, the preview runs twice as long as what gets committed. The two Prism surfaces name the same chord differently.
recommendation:
- Make suggestions a mode of the Prism panel. 'Use this' loads the progression into the builder via loadProgression, and the normal Create path writes notes and chord symbols at the right-clicked bar.
- Preview at the committed rhythm, and show context such as 'in G major · bars 9–12'.
- Rename 'Commit' to 'Add to song'.
- Hide the menu item on drum and audio tracks, or say that it adds chord symbols only.
verifierNote: commitPrismSuggestion only sets chordRegions (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:166-186); no notes are written. The context menu offers it on any blank track region with no type check (Timeline.tsx:1812-1826, 3010-3017). loadProgression has no callers (only a comment in exportToStudio.ts:346). Preview plays each chord as a whole note, while commit spreads the chords over measures×1920.

title: Re-roll shows the same 'Most Common' suggestion every time
evidence:
- regeneratePrismSuggestions recomputes the sets and resets `prismSuggestActiveIdx: 0` (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:189-211).
- In generateSuggestions the first three strategies are fixed picks (opts[0], opts[1], opts[2]; suggestionEngine.ts:331-341).
- walkGraph and filterByStyle contain no randomness (267-306).
- The seed and style are unchanged between re-rolls.

So set 1 is identical after every re-roll; only sets 4–5 ('Adventurous', 'Wild Card') change (342).
impact: Pressing Re-roll appears to do nothing, so students conclude the feature is broken or that only one answer exists.
recommendation: On re-roll, keep the current index and regenerate only the randomized sets. Or randomize among the top few options at each step for every strategy, and briefly highlight what changed.
verifierNote: regeneratePrismSuggestions resets `prismSuggestActiveIdx: 0` (prismSuggestionSlice.ts:189-211). Strategies 1-3 are fixed picks, `opts[0]`, `opts[1]` and `opts[2]` (suggestionEngine.ts:331-337), and walkGraph and filterByStyle are deterministic. Only strategies 4-5 use Math.random, so the 'Most Common' set the user sees after a re-roll never changes.

title: Suggestion preview: silent first play (31 MB SoundFont), routing that leaks into the master, wrong instrument
evidence:
First-play delay:
- Each open creates and initialises a new SoundFontAdapter (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:191-214).
- If no SoundFont track has loaded the shared synth yet, init triggers initSharedSynth: an audio-worklet module load plus `fetch('/daw-assets/GeneralUser_GS.sf2')` (SoundFontAdapter.ts:216-265). The file is 31,281,186 bytes.
- noteOn silently does nothing until the synth is ready (129-132), while playProgression already switches to 'Stop' and animates the pills (275-328).

Routing:
- init connects the shared synth to the master gain (102).
- spessasynth's connect() wires all 17 of its outputs (node_modules/spessasynth_lib/dist/index.js:497-498).
- The same synth is already connected to every SoundFont track's output.

Instrument: tracks that don't use SoundFont fall back to General MIDI programs (defaultGmProgram, 120-138).
impact: On first use the preview is silent for seconds with no loading cue. While the modal is open, any SoundFont track that plays is also heard straight into the master, bypassing its volume, effects and mute. Previews don't sound like the target track.
recommendation: Preview through the target track's own engine (auditionNote and trackEngineRegistry, auditionNote.ts:16-41); it is already loaded and respects mute and effects. If a SoundFont fallback is needed, show 'Loading sounds…' and disable Preview until it is ready.
verifierNote: Every time the modal opens it creates a new SoundFontAdapter and init()s it to the master gain (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:191-214). initSharedSynth fetches the 31,281,186-byte GeneralUser_GS.sf2 (SoundFontAdapter.ts:244-252), and noteOn returns silently until synthReady (129-132). sharedSynth.connect() wires all 17 worklet outputs (spessasynth_lib index.js:497-498), so while the modal is open every SoundFont channel also reaches master directly; channel bleed between SoundFont tracks already existed.

title: New accessibility gaps: mouse-only circle and spectrum, unlabelled dialog, 7px labels, white on teal
evidence:
Gaps not in the 2026-09-20 audit:
- Circle slices are `<g onClick>` with no role, tabIndex, name or key handler (CircleOfFifths.tsx:233-240). Their labels render at 10×scale, i.e. 7.2px, and 6.5px for F#, at size 130 (260; PrismStudio.tsx:151).
- The mode menu is a custom div list with no aria-expanded or listbox semantics, 8px group labels and 10px items with 3px padding (CircleOfFifths.tsx:276-341).
- Spectrum segments are `<div onClick>` (ColorSpectrum.tsx:105-135).
- The suggestion modal is a plain div (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:409-428): no role 'dialog' or aria-modal, focus is not moved in, trapped or returned, and the icon-only close button has no name (449-459).
- Create and the active genre chip use #fff on #7ecfcf (PrismStudio.tsx:213-216, 252-255), about 1.8:1.

Accessible versions already exist in the codebase:
- CircleOfFifthsSvg: role=button, tabIndex 0, aria-label, aria-pressed, Enter/Space (CircleOfFifthsSvg.tsx:160-178).
- The landing HarmonySpectrum: role=group, roving tabindex, labelled segments (HarmonySpectrum.tsx:85-131).

These overlap A11Y#3, #7, #8, #9, #14 and #19.
impact: Even after A11Y#3 is fixed, keyboard and screen-reader students can't pick a key or a harmony colour, so the lesson step 'Click G on the Circle of Fifths' is impossible for them. The 7px circle letters and the Create label are hard to read for everyone.
recommendation:
- Use CircleOfFifthsSvg bound to the store, and port the landing HarmonySpectrum.
- Use Radix Dialog for the modal and Radix Select for modes.
- Keep UI text at 11px or more and circle labels at 10px or more.
- Use dark text on teal, or the white pill.
- Add aria-pressed to the genre chips.
verifierNote: Circle slices are `<g onClick>` with no role, tabIndex or key handler (CircleOfFifths.tsx:233-240), and labels are `fontSize={(idx === 7 ? 9 : 10) * scale}`. The mode menu has 8px and 10px text (276-341). Spectrum segments are plain divs with onClick (ColorSpectrum.tsx:105-135). The modal is a plain div with no dialog role, and its close button has no name (PrismSuggestionModal.tsx:409-459). --color-accent is #7ecfcf (daw.css:15), so the white labels on Create and the active genre chip are about 1.8:1.

title: PrismStudio subscribes to the whole tracks array, so all of Prism re-renders during fader drags
evidence:
- `const tracks = useStore((s) => s.tracks)` plus a useMemo find (PrismStudio.tsx:77-83) is used only to read the selected track's type.
- Volume and pan sliders call updateTrack on every pointer move (TrackHeader.tsx:497; Mixer/ChannelStrip.tsx:185, 224).
- Each call creates a new tracks array, so PrismStudio and its unmemoized children re-render on every tick:
  - CircleOfFifths (12 slices and labels)
  - ChordSelection (up to 15 buttons with formatChord)
  - ChordSequenceDisplay
  - ColorSpectrum (16 segments)
  - RhythmExpression (three Radix sliders and three selects, one with about 41 rhythms)
impact: Wasted work on every fader drag, mute, solo or clip edit while the Prism tab is open. On low-end Chromebooks it adds jank to the drag.
recommendation: Subscribe to a primitive instead: `useStore((s) => s.tracks.find((t) => t.id === s.selectedTrackId)?.type === 'midi')`. Wrap the card components in React.memo.
verifierNote: `const tracks = useStore((s) => s.tracks)` (PrismStudio.tsx:78) is used only to work out isMidiTrack. TrackHeader's volume slider calls updateTrack on every onValueChange (TrackHeader.tsx:497), so every tick re-renders PrismStudio and its unmemoized children. The only memo in the Prism folder is SuggestionChordPill.

title: Lead-sheet Insert/Delete Measure assume 4/4 and leave rests, fermatas and row breaks on the wrong bars
evidence:
- insertMeasure and deleteMeasure shift by the literal 1920 (prismSlice.ts:2037-2085).
- LeadSheetView picks the measure using `ticksPerBar(timeSignatureNumerator, beatUnit)` (LeadSheetView.tsx:78-81, 323, 362) and calls these actions from the toolbar (LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:100-106).
- Neither action re-indexes the bar-indexed layout fields: measureRestMap (prismSlice.ts:94-95), measureFermatas (96-97) and measureRowSizes (92-93).
impact: In 3/4 or 6/8, inserting a measure shifts chords by 1⅓ bars and leaves chords mid-bar. In any meter, after inserting or deleting a measure, multi-bar rests, fermatas and row breaks stay on their old indices and land on different bars.
recommendation: Derive ticks per measure from the time signature, and re-index measureRestMap, measureFermatas and measureRowSizes (plus section and repeat marks) in the same set().
verifierNote: insertMeasure and deleteMeasure use the literal 1920 (prismSlice.ts:2037-2085) and only map chordRegions. measureRestMap, measureFermatas and measureRowSizes are never re-indexed, even though LeadSheetToolbar.tsx:100-106 calls these actions with measure indices derived from the time signature. Separately, deleteMeasure cuts a region that spans the whole deleted bar at delStart, losing its tail.

title: Text marks, breaks and spellings carry over into the next project you open
evidence: scoreSpellings, scoreSystemBreaks, scorePageBreaks, scoreSystemRuns and scoreTextMarks (uiSlice.ts:510-519) appear outside src/daw/components/Score only in uiSlice.ts and undoMiddleware.ts (repo grep). They are absent from freshProjectHarmony (SessionSerializer.ts:512-544) and resetSessionToEmpty (649-678), so deserializeCloudProject, resetSessionToEmpty and deserializeSession all leave them untouched. resetUndoHistory then rebaselines on them (undoMiddleware.ts:178-183).
impact: Within one session, a 'D.S. al Coda' at bar 8, staff text, and system or page breaks added in project A appear in project B or a new blank project, on screen and in its printed PDF, because they're keyed by bar number. Undo can't remove them, since they become the new baseline.
recommendation: Keep every Score field in one `scoreDoc` object with a single fresh value used by every load and reset path. Add a test that every MARK_KEY is covered by fresh, serialize and collab.
verifierNote: scoreSpellings, scoreSystemBreaks, scorePageBreaks, scoreSystemRuns and scoreTextMarks (uiSlice.ts:510-519) are missing from both freshProjectHarmony (SessionSerializer.ts:512-543) and resetSessionToEmpty (649-676). resetUndoHistory then rebaselines on the leftover values (undoMiddleware.ts:178-183, 209-217).
impactNote: scoreSpellings, scoreSystemBreaks, scorePageBreaks, scoreSystemRuns and scoreTextMarks are defined in uiSlice.ts:510-519 and appear elsewhere only in undoMiddleware.ts (MARK_KEYS 45-52) (grep). They are missing from freshProjectHarmony (SessionSerializer.ts:512-544), and resetSessionToEmpty (649-678) doesn't reset them either. They survive every project load or reset, and resetUndoHistory (undoMiddleware.ts:178-183) rebaselines on them, so undo can't remove them. title: Collab: some Score marks never sync, and the rest are overwritten by whoever writes last
evidence: The 'leadSheet' Y.Map carries sections, repeats, chordFormat, scoreChordTracks, scoreChordHidden, scoreArticulations, scoreSlurs and scoreSlashNotes, each written as a whole-array `JSON.stringify(...)` string (YjsDocManager.ts:425-437; diffEngine.ts:499-502 re-sends whenever the reference changes). Text marks, breaks, runs and spellings are not synced at all. writeEdit and writeEdits always replace both articulations and slurs with new arrays, even when unchanged (useScoreEditing.tsx:392-400, 427-430; dropNoteIds and remapNoteIds always allocate, noteEditor.ts:396-431). So every note edit re-broadcasts both full lists.
impact: In a class session, when student A drags a note while student B adds an accent, A's re-sent list can erase B's accent (last writer wins). Peers never see each other's text marks, jumps, breaks or hand-written accidentals, so 'the same' score looks and prints differently for each person. A rejoining peer gets only the partial set.
recommendation: Store marks as per-key Y.Maps (mark key to true, text mark id to object) so concurrent edits merge. Sync all Score fields. Skip setScoreArticulations/setScoreSlurs when the content is unchanged.
verifierNote: YjsDocManager.ts:426-437 and diffEngine.ts:485-502 sync whole-array JSON strings for sections, repeats, chord tracks, hidden chords, articulations, slurs and slash notes only. Text marks, breaks, runs, spellings, fermatas and row sizes are absent, and yjsToZustand.ts:431-440 has no keys for them. writeEdit always sets new arrays for articulations and slurs (useScoreEditing.tsx:394-399; remapNoteIds copies even when unchanged, noteEditor.ts:400-417), so each note edit re-sends both full lists.
impactNote: Text marks, breaks, runs, spellings, fermatas and row sizes are never synced. The leadSheet Y.Map in YjsDocManager.ts:425-437 and diffLeadSheet in diffEngine.ts:485-503 carry only sections, repeats, chordFormat, showRepeats, chord tracks/hidden, articulations, slurs and slashNotes. Peers in a class session will see and print different scores. writeEdit (useScoreEditing.tsx:392-400) and writeEdits (427-430) always set new articulation and slur arrays, so every note edit re-sends both whole lists as JSON strings. The last-writer-wins loss is real but narrower than claimed. A's re-send only erases B's accent if B's update hasn't reached A yet, which is about one network round-trip, so in practice it's rare. The missing-sync half is the part users will actually notice.
regressionRisks: Moving from JSON-string keys to nested Y.Maps changes the doc schema, so peers on old and new builds in the same room will desync. Version the room or keep reading the old keys. Mark keys hold note ids built from track/clip/tick/pitch, so when peers concurrently move the same note, marks can still orphan whatever the CRDT does. Skipping unchanged setScoreArticulations/setScoreSlurs calls also cuts undo snapshots and diff traffic, with no downside.

title: Playback re-renders the entire Score page about 30 times a second
evidence: `const position = useStore((s) => s.position);` sits at the top of the hook (useScoreEditing.tsx:134) and is used only as `playheadTick: position` (2376). Each tick re-renders ScoreView and everything below it. NoteEditorBar, ScorePalettes and ScorePartsPanel are plain functions fed new objects and inline arrow functions each render (editor object 2399-2433; ScoreView.tsx:164-173). The `overlay` JSX (useScoreEditing.tsx:1798-2360) is rebuilt without memoization, including a `layout.notes.find` per slur (1862-1866), a `layout.notes.filter` per tie (1905-1913), and `layout.barlines.some`, `sections.find` and `marksAt` per barline (2044-2062). StaffView reconciles all of it just to move one 2 px div (StaffView.tsx:1703-1797).
impact: Hundreds of React elements, plus O(slurs·notes + ties·notes + bars²) scans, run on every frame on the same main thread as Tone.js scheduling. On school Chromebooks this shows up as stutter and laggy clicks while the song plays, and it gets worse the longer the score is.
recommendation: Remove `position` from the hook. Render the playhead in a small component that uses useStore.subscribe and writes `transform` to a ref (the same in-place pattern StaffView already uses for highlights at 1591-1642), and expose StaffView's locate() through onLayout. Split the overlay into memoized layers. Wrap the toolbar, palettes and parts panel in memo with stable callbacks.
verifierNote: useScoreEditing.tsx:134 subscribes to position, which useTransport.ts:79-90 writes at about 30 fps during playback. Its only use is playheadTick (2376). The overlay JSX (1798+) is rebuilt every render with per-slur layout.notes.find (1862-1863), per-tie filter (1905-1907) and per-barline barlines.some, sections.find and marksAt (2044-2062). NoteEditorBar and ScorePalettes are not memoized. The engrave effect doesn't re-run because its deps are stable, so the cost is React reconciliation plus those scans.
impactNote: Confirmed: `const position = useStore((s) => s.position)` (useScoreEditing.tsx:134) is used only as `playheadTick: position` (2376). useTransport's rAF loop updates position about 30 times a second (src/daw/hooks/useTransport.ts:72-97), so the whole hook, the unmemoized `overlay` JSX (1798+), NoteEditorBar, ScorePalettes and ScorePartsPanel re-render every frame. None of them use memo. But noteStyles, noteOffsets, systemMarks, repeatStarts and multiRests are memoized (useScoreEditing.tsx:334-342, 1751-1772), and the VexFlow engrave effect depends only on those plus `parts` (StaffView.tsx:1533-1572). So nothing is re-engraved, and the per-frame cost is React reconciliation plus the overlay scans. That's a few ms to low tens of ms on a Chromebook, getting worse with long scores and many marks. Tone schedules ahead (about 100 ms lookahead), so an audible glitch is unlikely. Users would feel some sluggish clicks and playhead jitter during playback, not a broken experience. Medium, not high.
regressionRisks: Moving the playhead to a subscribe/ref component must keep follow-scroll working. StaffView's follow effect currently depends on playheadSystem computed from the playheadTick prop (StaffView.tsx:1703-1719), so it needs its own subscription. Wrapping the panels in memo needs stable callbacks, because the inline onUndo, onRedo, onDuration and onAddChord lambdas (useScoreEditing.tsx:2399-2433) would otherwise defeat it. Stale closures in memoized callbacks could bring back bugs like score-09.

title: Follow-playhead and page navigation never work in the Score
evidence: StaffView is rendered without className or style inside the `.leadsheet-scroll flex-1 overflow-y-auto` div (ScoreView.tsx:220-223, 290-294). `.ma-grand-staff` has no height rule (grandStaff.css), so StaffView's own root grows to its content height and never scrolls. Following the playhead compares against that root's scrollTop and clientHeight (StaffView.tsx:1708-1719). Page nav calls containerRef.scrollTo (1722-1727) and listens to that root's onScroll (1734-1743).
impact: In any score longer than one screen, the playhead runs off the bottom and the view doesn't follow. The 'Page 1 of N' pill is sticky inside a box that never scrolls, so it sits after the last page, never updates, and its ‹ › buttons do nothing. The Lead Sheet melody view has the same wiring.
recommendation: Make StaffView the scroll container (className 'min-h-0 flex-1' and a header slot for the title block), or have it locate its nearest scrolling ancestor for follow and nav. Add a 'Follow playback' toggle.
verifierNote: StaffView's root is 'ma-grand-staff relative overflow-y-auto' with no height (StaffView.tsx:1732), and ScoreView renders it without className or style inside the scrolling .leadsheet-scroll div (ScoreView.tsx:220-223, 290-294). grandStaff.css has no height rule. So the root never scrolls: the follow check (1713-1717), goToPage's scrollTo (1722-1727) and the onScroll page tracking (1734-1743) all act on a box that doesn't scroll.
impactNote: StaffView is rendered with no className or style (ScoreView.tsx:290-294) inside `.leadsheet-scroll flex-1 overflow-y-auto` (ScoreView.tsx:220-223), which is a block container, not flex. Its own root has `overflow-y-auto` (StaffView.tsx:1730-1732), but grandStaff.css sets no height, so it grows to its content height and never scrolls. The follow check compares against container.scrollTop (always 0) and clientHeight (the full content height) (StaffView.tsx:1708-1719), so it never fires. goToPage scrolls that same non-scrolling element (1722-1727).
