Lead Sheet uses StaffView differently, so check it separately. Smooth auto-follow while a user is scrolling by hand can fight them, so add a Follow toggle or pause follow on user scroll.

title: Edits move articulations and slurs onto the wrong notes; slashes and spellings fall off
evidence: writeEdit pairs ids by position: `new Map(before.map((id, i) => [id, after[i]]))` (useScoreEditing.tsx:396-399); writeEdits does the same (424-430). But applyNoteEdits returns ids grouped by clip, in each clip's event order (scoreEdit.ts:148-197). Selections are in ⌘-click order or layout order, and StaffView builds layout order system → measure → part (StaffView.tsx:1021-1040, 1158), which interleaves parts. Slash notation and pinned spellings are looked up by note id (scoreParts.ts:96-101, 110-112), but writeEdit never remaps them. Nothing outside this hook remaps note-keyed marks (repo grep for remapNoteIds and setScoreArticulations).
impact: ⌘-click two notes out of time order, or shift-select across two instruments, then press ↑: their staccatos, accents and slur ends swap, even between instruments. Dragging or transposing a rhythmic-slash note turns it back into a normal notehead, and a hand-written E♯ is respelled. Piano Roll edits silently drop Score marks, and the orphaned keys can reattach to a later note that lands on the same tick and pitch.
recommendation: Make applyNoteEdits return an explicit Map from old id to new id, and remap articulations, slurs, slashNotes and spellings in one place. Longer term, give MidiNoteEvent a stable id so marks don't depend on tick and pitch.
verifierNote: applyNoteEdits builds nextIds per clip, in the clip's own event order (scoreEdit.ts:162-194). writeEdit and writeEdits zip those ids by position against the caller's order (useScoreEditing.tsx:397, 426), so selection order and event order disagree whenever notes span clips or were ⌘-clicked out of order. Slash notes and spellings are keyed by note id (scoreParts.ts:96-112), and nothing remaps them on edit; grep finds remapNoteIds only in this hook.
impactNote: applyNoteEdits groups ids by clip in the order clips are first seen, and within each clip emits them in clip.events order (scoreEdit.ts:148-197). writeEdit pairs before[i] with after[i] (useScoreEditing.tsx:396-399), and writeEdits does the same (424-430). selectedNotes is a Set kept in click order, and range selection follows layout order (system, then measure, then part). Selecting two notes out of time order with ⌘-click, or across parts spanning bars, then pressing ↑/↓ or dragging, swaps their marks. If after.length !== before.length, the marks are left stale. slashNotes and spellings are looked up by note id (scoreParts.ts:96-112) and never remapped in writeEdit, so moving a slash note turns it back into a normal notehead and a pinned spelling is lost. That last part happens in single-note edits too. I lowered the severity because the swap needs a multi-note selection made out of order and the result is wrong marks, not lost notes. The slash/spelling loss is more common but cosmetic.
regressionRisks: Returning an explicit old-to-new Map from applyNoteEdits touches every caller (writeEdit, writeEdits, paste and others) and the selection-preserving return value. Remapping spellings has to recompute or drop them when the pitch changes, since a pinned E♯ moved up a step shouldn't stay E♯. Stable MIDI event ids would be a project-format change that affects saved projects, collab yMapToTrack, Piano Roll and clipboard. Do it only together with the persistence work in score-01.

title: A 3–4 px wobble while clicking a note changes its pitch
evidence: Every press on a note starts a drag (useScoreEditing.tsx:478-485). The dead zone is 3 px (502). After that, `steps = -Math.round(dy / stepPx)` with stepPx = 5 × scale (StaffView.tsx:1584), so dy ≈ 3 px already rounds to one staff step. The horizontal snap uses the first bar's ticks per pixel for every bar (473-477). pointerup commits writeEdit (512-527).
impact: Trackpad taps and young students' clicks move a note up or down a step (C→B) when they only meant to select it. The change is silent (no audition) and often goes unnoticed.
recommendation: Start a drag only after about 6–8 px or a 150 ms hold. Use hysteresis for vertical steps. Compute ticks per pixel from the bar under the pointer. Audition the pitch while dragging.
verifierNote: The dead zone is 3 px (useScoreEditing.tsx:502). steps = -Math.round(dy/stepPx) with stepPx = STAFF_STEP(5) × scale (StaffView.tsx:257, 1584), so a 3 px downward move rounds to one step when scale is 1.2 or less, and the move commits on pointerup (512-527). ticksPerPx comes from measures[0] (473-477). The bug is real, but Math.round(-0.5) is 0, so an exact 3 px upward wobble rounds to no step, and taps rarely move 3 px. Medium fits better than high.
impactNote: The dead zone is `Math.abs(dx) < 3 && Math.abs(dy) < 3` (useScoreEditing.tsx:502). After that, `steps = -Math.round(dy / stepPx)` with stepPx = STAFF_STEP(5) × scale (StaffView.tsx:257, 1584). At scale ≤ 1 a 3 px vertical wobble rounds to one step, and pointerup commits writeEdit (512-527). On the smaller page scale typical of a 1366-wide screen, stepPx gets smaller and it's worse. A sloppy mouse click or a physical trackpad click can move the note one diatonic step silently. ticksPerPx comes from layout.measures[0] (473-477), which skews horizontal snapping when bar widths differ. The bug is real, but it needs ≥3 px of movement during a click, the dragged note shows visual feedback, and ⌘Z fixes it. Medium.
regressionRisks: A bigger threshold or a hold delay makes intentional small drags feel sticky. Hysteresis needs tuning on both trackpad and mouse. Auditioning while dragging has to go through the existing preview-note path without stuck notes on pointercancel, and shouldn't fire into armed tracks or a collab session. Computing ticksPerPx per bar under the pointer changes drag snapping in multi-system layouts, so check it against systems with multi-bar rests.

title: The Score has no way to write new notes

The only code path that creates events is paste (1641-1649). Pressing a measure or rest only selects it (537-613).

title: Pasting into bars before a part's first clip piles every note onto one tick

recommendation: Create a clip at the target bar, or extend the existing clip's start, when nothing covers the target. Never clamp.

title: MeshGradientBg is invisible but redraws a full-viewport, high-DPI canvas every frame
evidence:
Every animation frame, MeshGradientBg.tsx:73-98 runs clearRect plus 4× createRadialGradient and 4× fillRect over the whole canvas, sized at devicePixelRatio (22-31). The loop never pauses for playback, idle, hidden panels or prefers-reduced-motion.

The canvas is absolute inset-0 with zIndex -1 (107-113). Its parent .daw-root (DawApp.tsx:482-486) has no position or z-index, so it is not a stacking context, and it paints an opaque var(--color-bg) (#101012, daw.css:6). CSS painting order draws negative-z children before in-flow block backgrounds, so .daw-root's own background covers the canvas completely. The Sep-20 screenshots show a flat background.
impact: Constant cost for no visual result. At 2× DPR on a 1440×900 screen that is about 4.6 M pixels × 4 gradient fills per frame at 60–120 Hz, plus compositing a full-screen layer. It keeps the GPU and main thread awake, drains student laptops, and competes with the playhead and meters. If it were made visible, its purple/teal/pink/blue orbs would clash with the neutral landing look.
recommendation: Delete the component and its mount (DawApp.tsx:486). If an ambient texture is ever wanted, use a static CSS background on .daw-root.
verifierNote: MeshGradientBg.tsx:73-98 runs clearRect plus 4 gradient fillRects per rAF over a DPR-scaled canvas, with no pause. The canvas is zIndex -1 (111). .daw-root (DawApp.tsx:482-486) is unpositioned and paints an inline opaque var(--color-bg), so per the CSS painting order it covers the negative-z canvas.
impactNote: The canvas runs an unconditional rAF loop of clearRect plus 4 full-surface radial-gradient fillRects at device pixel ratio (MeshGradientBg.tsx:22-31, 73-98). It is absolute with zIndex -1 (107-113) inside .daw-root, which has no position, z-index or isolation (daw.css:3; DawApp.tsx:482-486). Negative-z content paints beneath the in-flow .daw-root background (var(--color-bg) #101012), so the canvas is invisible. The waste is real and the fix (delete it) has no risk. The impact is speculative, though: GPU-backed 2D gradient fills are fairly cheap, and many Chromebooks run at DPR 1. It is a constant drain rather than the main source of jank, so I lowered it to medium.
regressionRisks: Very low. Removing it changes nothing visible. If a later change gives .daw-root a stacking context (position plus z-index, or isolation), the orbs would suddenly appear, which is another reason to delete it rather than leave it.

recommendation: Use Radix Popover (focus management, Escape, collision-aware positioning) with its portal container inside .daw-root, and put an explicit 'Lock key' switch inside the popover.

evidence: DawAppInner calls usePlaybackEngine, useCollabAudioLoader and useStudioMonitor (DawApp.tsx:80-85). These hooks subscribe at render level to tracks, masteringEffects, masterVolume, masterAutomation and returns (usePlaybackEngine.ts:363-376), to tracks (useCollabAudioLoader.ts:24), and to remoteUsers (useStudioMonitor.ts:25). DawAppInner renders TimelineWithHeaders, LibraryPanel, ChannelStrip, PianoRollModal, PitchEditorModal, ScoreView, LeadSheetView, TutorialLayer and the global modals (DawApp.tsx:486-536). Only TransportBar and StudioView are wrapped in memo.
impact: Every volume, pan or knob move, note edit and clip drag, and in collab every broadcast of a peer's cursor or selection, re-renders the entire editor tree. That comes on top of the undo stringify and the engine re-sync, and at the store level it is the main source of drag jank and collab lag.
recommendation: Move engine-sync logic into effects that use useStore.subscribe (no React subscription), or into a separate non-rendering EngineSync sibling. Subscribe to remoteUsers only where avatars are drawn, and wrap the heavy children in memo. Adopt a rule that the root subscribes to nothing that changes on every frame.

Of its children, only TransportBar (TransportBar.tsx:142) and StudioView use memo; TimelineWithHeaders, LibraryPanel, ChannelStrip, PianoRollModal, ScoreView, LeadSheetView and TutorialLayer do not.
impactNote: DawAppInner does subscribe through usePlaybackEngine to tracks, masteringEffects, masterVolume, masterAutomation and returns (usePlaybackEngine.ts:363-376), through useCollabAudioLoader to tracks (:24) and through useStudioMonitor to remoteUsers (:25). It renders the whole tree unmemoized (DawApp.tsx:480-536). However, most of the heavy children (Timeline, ChannelStrip, LibraryPanel) subscribe to tracks themselves and would re-render on track edits anyway, so the extra cost comes mainly from presence (remoteUsers) churn in collab and from rerendering modals or views that don't depend on tracks. The impact is real but secondary to -07 and the engine re-sync, so medium.
regressionRisks: Moving engine sync to useStore.subscribe must keep its effect ordering relative to isReady and engine init, otherwise there is a risk of silent tracks or double-created TrackEngines (audio glitches). Wrapping children in memo is safe if they take no unstable props; TimelineWithHeaders gets isReady only. Tutorial anchors (data-tutorial-id) are unaffected unless components are restructured.

title: Note-off is only half-scheduled: release starts from the level at call time, and voices are freed by a timer started at call time
evidence:
Envelope.release runs 'target.cancelScheduledValues(now); target.setValueAtTime(target.value, now); target.setTargetAtTime(0, now, release / 5)' (Envelope.ts:59-62). `now` is the scheduled note-off time, but target.value is the level at call time, 100-150 ms earlier. Voice.noteOff's no-envelope fade does the same (Voice.ts:333-339).

cancelScheduledValues(time) also deletes the attack ramp and decay of any note shorter than its attack (Envelope.ts:45-52), leaving only the 0.005 floor from line 42.

The free timer is setTimeout(freeVoice, maxRelease*1000 + 100), measured from the call (Voice.ts:346-351). It fires at T_off - L + release + 0.1, where L is the lookahead lead of 0.1-0.15 s. freeVoice stops the sources immediately (394-401).

allNotesOff/forceAllNotesOff take no time argument (SynthEngine.ts:406-416), and the host calls allNotesOff from Tone's 'loop' event without one (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-849, 907).
impact:
- STAB (amp release 0.05, factoryPresets.ts:1540) is freed between T_off and T_off + 50 ms. About half its notes stop at the 10% sustain level with a click and no tail.
- Sequenced notes shorter than about 150 ms (32nds, fast runs) release from the level before the note started and click at note-off.
- Notes shorter than the attack (slow pads) play at -46 dB and then jump at note-off.
- At a loop wrap, every note is released 100-150 ms early.
- In background tabs, timers are throttled to 1 s or more, so voices stay 'releasing' longer and force extra steals (synth-engine-02).
recommendation:
- Compute the envelope value at `time` from the trigger time and the ADSR parameters, and start the release from it (use cancelAndHoldAtTime where supported).
- Stop sources with osc.stop(time + about 5 time-constants) and free the voice from onended or a context-time queue.
- Add `time` to allNotesOff/forceAllNotesOff, and have the host pass the loop event's time.

Voice.ts:346-351 starts the free timer at call time, and freeVoice stops sources immediately (394-401). The mechanics are correct:
- Envelope.release reads target.value at call time and anchors it at the future `now` (Envelope.ts:55-62), and the no-envelope path does the same (Voice.ts:333-339).

- The free timer starts at call time (Voice.ts:346-351), and freeVoice stops sources immediately (382-389).
- allNotesOff has no time argument (SynthEngine.ts:406-416) and the loop handler calls it without one (usePlaybackEngine.ts:845-849).

The user-facing impact is narrower than claimed:
- Notes longer than about 150 ms and past their decay release correctly, because the call-time value is already the sustain level.
- The audible cases are 1/32 and sometimes 1/16 runs in the piano roll, and pad notes shorter than their attack.

- Analytic envelope evaluation must match the attack/decay curves exactly (linear ramp, then setTargetAtTime with tau decay/3), or releases will jump.
- cancelAndHoldAtTime has had cross-browser quirks (fine in Chrome).
- Passing `time` into allNotesOff from the loop handler changes the TrackEngine/instrument interface shared by every instrument (Piano, Sampler, Drum), so keep the parameter optional.

title: Toggling ARP while keys are held strands notes: stuck voices, leaked quantizer refs and phantom arpeggios
evidence:
SynthEngine routes each note event by the arp flag at that moment: 'if (this.arpParams?.enabled && this.arpeggiator) arpeggiator.noteOn/noteOff else rawNoteOn/rawNoteOff' (SynthEngine.ts:390-404).

Enabling the arp mid-hold:
- The held key's note-off goes to Arpeggiator.noteOff, which deletes from an empty heldNotes and calls stopArp (Arpeggiator.ts:165-170). The raw voice never receives its note-off.
- ScaleQuantizer.mapNoteOn already pushed a ref for that pitch (ScaleQuantizer.ts:131-141). It is never popped, so every later mapNoteOff for that pitch finds refs > 0 and returns null (suppressed, 156-160).
- The refs are only reset by clear() (165-168), which only allNotesOff/forceAllNotesOff call (SynthEngine.ts:406-416).

Disabling the arp mid-hold:
- setParams calls stopArp but leaves heldNotes intact (Arpeggiator.ts:115-118).
- The keys' note-offs then go to rawNoteOff, so heldNotes keeps them.
- The next enable sees 'this.heldNotes.size > 0' and restarts the pattern with no keys held (120-122).
impact: A student holding a chord who clicks ARP on gets a stuck chord when they let go. After that, that pitch can never be released by its own key (every note-off is suppressed) until a transport stop or loop wrap calls allNotesOff. Turning ARP off while holding keys and back on later starts a phantom arpeggio that runs until panic. Live keyboard practice with the transport stopped never recovers on its own.
recommendation:
- Record which path (arp or raw) started each held key and send its note-off to the same path.
- On enable, hand raw held notes to the arp: release the raw voices and seed heldNotes.
- On disable, clear heldNotes and either replay the held keys as raw notes or release them.
- Add unit tests for both toggle sequences.
verifierNote: The mechanics are correct. SynthEngine.ts:390-404 routes each note-off by the arp flag at that moment, Arpeggiator.noteOff on an empty map just calls stopArp (165-170), and the quantizer refs leak, so later note-offs for that pitch are suppressed (ScaleQuantizer mapNoteOff refs>0 returns null) until clear(). Disabling keeps heldNotes (Arpeggiator.ts:115-118) and re-enabling restarts them (120-122). It only happens when ARP is toggled while keys are held, and allNotesOff or stop recovers it, so medium fits better than high.
impactNote:
The logic holds.

Enabling ARP mid-hold:
- SynthEngine.noteOn/noteOff route by the arp flag at that moment (SynthEngine.ts:390-404).
- After enabling, the held key's note-off goes to Arpeggiator.noteOff, which runs heldNotes.delete and stopArp (Arpeggiator.ts:165-176). The raw voice never gets rawNoteOff.
- The ScaleQuantizer ref pushed in mapNoteOn (ScaleQuantizer.ts:131-141) is never popped, so every later mapNoteOff for that pitch returns null (156-160). The pitch stays stuck until clear() via allNotesOff/forceAllNotesOff.

Disabling ARP mid-hold:
- setParams calls stopArp but keeps heldNotes (Arpeggiator.ts:115-118).
- The next enable with heldNotes.size>0 restarts a phantom pattern (120-122).

When users hit this:
- Toggling ARP during sequenced playback is a natural exploratory action, and three factory presets ship with the arp on (factoryPresets.ts:1343, 1467, 1565).
- With the transport running, a stop or loop wrap calls allNotesOff and clears it, so the damage is a stuck note until stop.
- With the transport stopped (live keyboard practice), it persists.

Severity: medium, not high, because recovery is one Stop press and the trigger is a specific toggle-while-holding sequence. The fix is small and the recommendation is sound.
regressionRisks:
- Tracking the routing path per held key must also cover the ScaleQuantizer stacks, or refs leak differently.
- Handing raw held notes to the arp on enable will retrigger sound, so do it with a short release to avoid clicks.
- Collab: arp-enabled is patch state synced through the synth store, so a remote toggle could hit the same path; the fix covers that too.
- No save-format or tutorial impact.

title: Reverb is never applied when a project loads or exports; never-opened tracks also run a hidden convolver
evidence:
applySynthStateToEngine pushes drive, chorus, phaser, delay and compressor but never calls setReverbParams (synthTrackState.ts:257-261). The panel's initial sync does call it (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:335).

applySynthStateToEngine is the only place the patch is applied at instrument init (usePlaybackEngine.ts:516-521) and in export (renderProject.ts:256-259).

FXProcessor attaches the wet path at construction ('connectWetPath' sets wetAttached = true, FXProcessor.ts:44-48) and only detaches it inside setEnabled (50-54, 65-78). A ReverbEffect that never receives params therefore keeps its damping biquad and its 2.5 s stereo ConvolverNode (ReverbEffect.ts:36-51) processing behind a wet gain of 0.
impact: After a refresh (crash-recovery restore), opening a saved project (SessionSerializer.ts:556/721 seeds patches) or loading a demo, any Oracle track whose patch has reverb on plays dry until its synth panel is opened. Exports are always dry. Every Oracle track whose panel hasn't been opened this session also runs a convolution reverb at zero wet during playback, which wastes audio-thread CPU per track.
recommendation:
- Add engine.setReverbParams(s.fx.reverb) to applySynthStateToEngine.
- Better: replace applySynthStateToEngine and the panel's initial sync with one shared function, unit-tested against SYNTH_STATE_KEYS, so no section can be missed.
- Construct FX processors with the wet path detached until they are enabled.
verifierNote: applySynthStateToEngine (synthTrackState.ts:257-263) sets drive, chorus, phaser, delay and compressor but not reverb, while the panel's initial sync does (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:335). It is the only patch application at init (usePlaybackEngine.ts:516-521) and in export (renderProject.ts:256-259). FXProcessor attaches the wet path at construction (FXProcessor.ts:44-48) and detaches it only through setEnabled, so a never-configured ReverbEffect keeps its convolver processing behind a zero wet gain.
impactNote:
applySynthStateToEngine pushes drive, chorus, phaser, delay, compressor and routing but never calls setReverbParams (synthTrackState.ts:257-262). The panel's initial sync does call it (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:335). applySynthStateToEngine is the only patch application at init (usePlaybackEngine.ts:516-521) and in export (renderProject.ts:256-259).

FXProcessor.connectWetPath leaves the wet path attached (FXProcessor.ts:43-47), and only setEnabled detaches it (50-78). So a never-synced ReverbEffect keeps its damping biquad and ConvolverNode (ReverbEffect.ts:36-51) processing behind a wet gain of 0 whenever the track makes sound.

The user-facing correctness impact is limited:
- Reverb defaults to disabled (fxSlice.ts:60), no factory preset enables it (factoryPresets.ts:67), and none of the 82 pack presets do.
- Only patches where the student turned reverb on are affected. They play dry after a reload until the panel is opened, and they always export dry.

The CPU cost is real but unmeasured: one convolver per unopened Oracle track during playback, which matters on Chromebooks with several Oracle tracks.

The fix is a one-line addition and very low risk, so do it now regardless of severity. The 'shared function tested against SYNTH_STATE_KEYS' suggestion is the right way to stop this happening again.
regressionRisks:
- Constructing processors with the wet path detached must still re-attach correctly when setEnabled(true) arrives. updateWetAttachment is idempotent, so it should, but verify all six effects.
- Unifying applySynthStateToEngine with the panel's initial sync could change the order of setBPM and LFO calls, which matters for finding 07 and 10.
- No save-format or collab impact (reverb params are already saved).

title: Wavetable-position and unison-blend modulation never runs in the Studio, although 50 of 82 bundled pack presets use it
evidence:
The matrix cannot resolve these targets: 'wtPos/blend are absent: they are not AudioParams (control-rate only)' (ModulationMatrix.ts:210). resolveTarget returns null for them (211-243).

The only driver for them is useWtPosModulation, a 30 fps rAF hook (useWtPosModulation.ts:29, 71-73) that skips per-voice sources (66-67). It is mounted only by the standalone SynthLayout (SynthLayout.tsx:48, used by oracle-synth/App.tsx:17). The DAW's DawSynthLayout imports (lines 1-30) do not include it.

In public/daw-assets/oracle-packs/serum2/presets, 50 of 82 presets contain 76 enabled wtPos routes: 53 from macros, 18 from LFOs, 4 from envelopes and 1 from the mod wheel.
impact: In /studio/editor, pack presets' 'morph' macros and LFO wavetable sweeps do nothing: the sound stays frozen at the base WT position, and turning a macro labelled for the morph has no audible effect. Even the standalone driver runs only while its panel is mounted, at 30 fps on the main thread, never in background tabs and never in export.
recommendation:
- Short term: run the control-rate WT/blend driver inside SynthEngine rather than a React hook, independent of panel visibility, fed by macros, LFOs, the mod wheel and per-voice envelope contours, and also during export.
- Long term: implement the wavetable oscillator as an AudioWorklet whose frame position is an audio-rate AudioParam (Vital/Serum style). That also removes the dual-engine crossfade (synth-engine-12).
verifierNote: ModulationMatrix.ts:210-243 has no wtPos or blend resolvers. The only driver, useWtPosModulation, is imported only by SynthLayout.tsx:6,48, and DawSynthLayout.tsx's imports (1-30) do not include it. The serum2 pack has 50 of 82 presets containing 76 '"param": "wtPos"' occurrences.
impactNote:
The behaviour is as described:
- ModulationMatrix has no resolver for wtPos or blend (ModulationMatrix.ts:210-243).
- The only driver is useWtPosModulation, which is mounted only in the standalone SynthLayout (SynthLayout.tsx:6, 48). Nothing under src/daw/components imports it; DawSynthLayout only borrows its CSS (DawSynthLayout.tsx:30).
- Of the 82 pack presets, 50 contain 76 wtPos routes.

In /studio/editor these presets therefore sound static, and macros meant to morph the wavetable do nothing.

This is a missing feature rather than a regression. Students only notice when they turn a morph macro and hear no change, or compare a preset with its description, and the presets still make sound. That is why it is medium rather than high.

The short-term fix (a control-rate driver inside SynthEngine, independent of React, also run in export) is reasonable. The AudioWorklet rewrite is a large project and should be scoped separately.
regressionRisks:
- A main-thread control-rate driver inside the engine adds per-track timer work. On Chromebooks with several Oracle tracks it must be cheap (skip when there are no wtPos routes) and must not use rAF, which pauses in background tabs.
- Rebuilding a PeriodicWave per frame position is expensive, so cache the frames.
- An AudioWorklet oscillator rewrite risks sound changes in every saved patch and needs careful A/B testing.
- Running the driver during export requires offline-time scheduling (see 01).
- No save-format change.

title: LFOs free-run from their last rebuild and restart on every edit, so bar shapes don't line up with song bars
evidence: createSource calls 'this.source.start()' with no offset (LFO.ts:105-110). Every BPM, node or smooth change destroys the source and starts a new one from phase 0 (51-81). The class documents 'The LFO runs freely' (9-12). LFOParams.sync (types.ts:202) is never read by the engine. Nothing aligns the loop to Tone.Transport.
impact: The editor shows four bars with quarter-note rate divisions, but a shape drawn in LFO bar 3 does not play in song bar 3. Its position depends on when the engine was last rebuilt. Panel mounts, preset loads and tempo changes restart the LFO, so modulated cutoff or level jumps (an audible click) mid-phrase. Playback differs from export, which starts the loop at render time 0.
recommendation:
- Start the buffer source at a transport-aligned offset (source.start(when, offsetInLoop) from the transport position) on play, loop and seek, and after each rebuild.
- Crossfade from the old source to the new one over a few ms when editing.
- Either implement LFOParams.sync (free-running vs. synced) or remove it.
verifierNote: createSource calls source.start() with no offset (LFO.ts:110). Every set* call restarts the source from phase 0 (51-81), the class documents free-running behaviour (11), and LFOParams.sync (types.ts:202) is never read by the engine.

title: Duplicate unison engine and per-note node rebuilds double oscillator CPU, with no voices × unison budget
evidence:
Each Oscillator always runs two unison engines, A and B (Oscillator.ts:89-99, 108-123). All 22 oscillator wavetables in factoryPresets.ts are single-frame SAWTOOTH, SQUARE or TRIANGLE. For those, getInterpolationPair returns indexA = indexB = 0 and mix = 0 (WavetableBank.ts:331-334), so gainB targets 0 (Oscillator.ts:333-334) while unisonB keeps N OscillatorNodes running.

Every note-on rebuilds N oscillators + N gains + N panners per engine (UnisonEngine.ts:150-176) and destroys the previous set (190-221). With unison N on both oscillators that is 12N nodes per voice per note, half of them silent duplicates. Unison clamps at 16 (UnisonEngine.ts:80) and voices at 16 (constants.ts:33), so up to 1,024 oscillators per track with no budget.
impact: Every factory preset spends twice the oscillator CPU it needs on the shared audio thread. Chords with unison 4 create and destroy about 48 nodes per voice inside the MIDI scheduler callback, which adds GC churn. A student turning UNISON up to 16 on a chord can overload the audio thread and crackle the entire project, because all tracks share one AudioContext.
recommendation:
- Run unisonB only while the table has more than one frame and mix is strictly between 0 and 1, or during a morph.
- Keep per-voice unison gain and panner nodes persistent and recreate only the OscillatorNodes on each note.
- Enforce a CPU budget on total oscillator count (voices × unison × engines) and show it in the UI.
verifierNote: Oscillator.start always starts both unisonA and unisonB (Oscillator.ts:112-120). For single-frame tables, mix is 0, so gainB targets 0 (333-334) while unisonB keeps running. UnisonEngine.rebuildOscillators recreates N oscillator+gain+panner sets on every note (UnisonEngine.ts:150-176), and unison clamps at 16 (80).

title: Unison gains start at 1.0 and settle with a 20 ms time constant, so live notes start with a loud spike
evidence: rebuildOscillators creates each unison gain with createGain(), whose default gain is 1 (UnisonEngine.ts:155). It starts all oscillators together at phase 0 (167), then calls recalculateGains, which smoothParam-glides each gain to totalGain = 1/sqrt(N) scaled by blend with a 0.02 s time constant (174-175, 245-259). With the default blend 0.1 the targets are 0.725 for the centre voice and 0.275 for detuned voices at N = 4.
impact: With live keys or MIDI input, the first 20-60 ms of each note sums to about 2.6× the settled level (+8 dB) at unison 4 and about 6.6× (+16 dB) at unison 16. Because the oscillators start in phase, the peaks add coherently. Fast-attack presets (PLUCK, STAB at 0.001 s) let this through as a pop or thump on every key press. Sequenced notes avoid it only because their oscillators start 100-150 ms early (synth-engine-02).
recommendation:
- Set each new unison gain directly to its target value at creation (gain.gain.value = target) and only smooth later changes.
- Optionally stagger start times by a few samples to decorrelate phases.
verifierNote: New unison gains default to 1 (UnisonEngine.ts:155), and all oscillators start in phase (167). recalculateGains uses smoothParam, which is cancelScheduledValues plus setTargetAtTime from the current value (constants.ts:26-28), with a 0.02 s time constant (253,257). At N=4 with blend 0.1 the gains start summing to 4 against a settled sum of about 1.55.

title: Dragging a mod-amount knob tears down and rebuilds the entire matrix for every sounding voice on each pointer move
evidence:
Call chain:
1. The amount Knob calls onUpdate(route.id, {amount}) on every pointer move (ModulationSlot.tsx:180-189; Knob.tsx:136-147).
2. updateModRoute writes a new modRoutes array (modulationSlice.ts:42-47).
3. The subscription, which has no equality function (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:199-205), calls SynthEngine.setModRoutes.
4. setModRoutes calls modMatrix.setRoutes, which disconnects everything (ModulationMatrix.ts:83-86), then reconnectActiveVoices (SynthEngine.ts:534-541; ModulationMatrix.ts:114-119).
5. Reconnecting creates a new WaveShaper, scaler gain and offset gain per route per voice (121-187).

The scaler and offset gain are connected in separate calls (166-176).
impact: Turning a mod amount while notes play creates (sounding voices × routes × 1-3) nodes per move, doubled when the pop-out is open. The audio thread can render quanta between the disconnect and the reconnect, or with a scaler but no offset. For cutoff routes that offset is up to ±4800 cents, so modulated parameters can jump and zipper or click during the drag.
recommendation:
- Diff the routes. When only amount, polarity or curve changes, update the existing scaler and offset gains with smoothParam, or swap the WaveShaper curve.
- Rebuild only routes whose source or target changed.
- Throttle store-to-engine pushes during drags.
verifierNote: The modRoutes subscription has no equality function, and updateModRoute creates a new array on each move (modulationSlice.ts:42-47). setModRoutes calls setRoutes, which runs disconnectAll (ModulationMatrix.ts:83-86), then reconnectActiveVoices (SynthEngine.ts:534-541). connectRouteToVoice creates a new WaveShaper, scaler and offset gain per route per voice (ModulationMatrix.ts:121-187).

title: Every unipolar cutoff route, including the default new route, sweeps the filter DOWN from the knob
evidence:
ModulationMatrix sets 'legacyCutoff = route.target.param === 'cutoff' && route.polarity === 'unipolar'' for all routes, not just migrated v1 routes (ModulationMatrix.ts:149-151). computeGainOffset then returns {gain: A, offset: -A}, a down-sweep (modMath.ts:39-44). That contradicts its own documented rule, 'unipolar route + unipolar source: sweep base -> base+A' (21-24).

addModRoute creates exactly this route by default: LFO 1 to flt1 cutoff, amount 0.5, unipolar (modulationSlice.ts:21-34). The UI ring copies the same rule (useModIndicator.ts:49-50, 117-118).
impact: With range 4800 cents, a positive amount of 0.5 makes the cutoff move between 2 octaves below the knob and the knob value. A classic filter envelope (ENV MOD to cutoff, positive amount) therefore darkens the patch at rest instead of opening it on the attack. This is the opposite of every other unipolar target in Oracle and of mainstream synths, which confuses students learning modulation.
recommendation:
- Mark migrated v1 routes in migrateModRoute (for example legacyDownSweep: true when isV1) and apply the down-sweep only to them.
- New routes sweep from base to base + A.
- Drive the UI indicator from the same flag.

title: MONO and LEG behave the same, and glide is inaudible in the piano roll or starts from the wrong pitch
evidence:
Voice modes:
- VoiceManager.noteOn treats mono and legato identically: 'if (voiceMode === 'mono' || voiceMode === 'legato') this.allNotesOff(time)' (VoiceManager.ts:36-40). The envelope always retriggers.
- noteOff only releases (57-63). There is no held-note stack.

Glide:
- New unison oscillators start at the engine's last frequency, initially 440 (UnisonEngine.ts:20, 158).
- The glide is setTargetAtTime(freq, this.ctx.currentTime, glideTime/3), anchored to currentTime instead of `time` (51-56). SubOscillator does the same (98-106).

The UI exposes POLY/MONO/LEG and GLIDE (RightSidebar.tsx:9-11, 50). Presets that rely on them: BASS (mono, glide 0.05), LEAD (legato, glide 0.08), WOBBLE (mono, glide 0.03) (factoryPresets.ts:446-448, 578-580, 831-833).
impact:
- LEG never ties notes, so there is no legato phrasing.
- In the piano roll the glide finishes inside the 100-150 ms lookahead, before the note is audible, so LEAD and BASS never slide.
- Live, the first note on a fresh voice swoops from A4 (440 Hz). With several voices, glides start from whatever pitch that voice last played.
- In MONO, releasing the newer of two held keys silences the line instead of returning to the still-held key.
recommendation:
- Implement a mono note stack: LEG keeps the envelope running and only glides when notes overlap, MONO retriggers, and release returns to the last held key.
- Start glide at `time` from the engine's last played pitch: setValueAtTime(prev, time), then setTargetAtTime(next, time, glide/3).
- Limit mono and legato to a single voice.
verifierNote: VoiceManager.ts:38-40 treats mono and legato identically, and there is no note stack in noteOff (57-63). Glide uses setTargetAtTime anchored at ctx.currentTime (UnisonEngine.ts:51-56), and new oscillators start at currentFreq, initially 440 (20, 158). BASS, LEAD and WOBBLE use mono or legato with glides of 0.03-0.08 s, which finish inside the 0.1 s lookahead.

title: Filter ON/OFF and PAN do nothing, GAIN has no effect on LP/HP, and RES goes to +30 dB
evidence: Filter.setParams stores `enabled` but never applies it (Filter.ts:92-94), and never reads `pan`; there is no panner in the filter graph (17-60, types.ts:162). GAIN sets biquad.gain (83-86), which the biquad uses only for peaking and shelf types. RES feeds biquad.Q directly (79-82); for lowpass and highpass the Web Audio spec defines Q in dB. FilterModule exposes the ON/OFF Toggle (FilterModule.tsx:92-96), PAN (139-154), GAIN (155-164) and RES from 0 to 30 (125-135). Modulation can add up to ±15 more (modMath.ts:63-64).

recommendation:
- Implement `enabled` as a smoothed bypass (wet 0 / dry 1, or route sources to bypassBus).
- Add a StereoPanner after the filter output for `pan`.
- Disable or hide GAIN for filter types that ignore it.
- Map RES to a safe, perceptually even range per filter type, for example up to 24 dB with a soft cap for LP/HP.

RES feeds Q directly (79-82), and FilterModule exposes RES from 0 to 30, plus the ON toggle, PAN and GAIN (FilterModule.tsx ~92-164).

title: Voices are built inside note-on, each generating 4 s of noise even when noise is off
evidence: allocateVoice constructs 'new Voice(...)' and runs onVoiceCreated's full parameter seeding inside noteOn (VoiceManager.ts:96-107; SynthEngine.ts:240-266). A Voice builds about 43 nodes and starts 4 ConstantSources (Voice.ts:104-185). Its NoiseGenerator constructor calls generateBuffers (NoiseGenerator.ts:40), which fills 2 s of white and 2 s of pink noise per voice with Math.random (116-159). Noise defaults to disabled (28), and the buffers are identical across voices and tracks.
impact: The first chord after a load, refresh or track creation builds its voices synchronously inside the MIDI scheduler callback or key handler. That adds input latency and can make the first notes late. It costs about 0.75 MB per voice at 48 kHz (about 6 MB per 8-voice Oracle track) of duplicated noise.
recommendation:
- Share the white and pink buffers per AudioContext (a static WeakMap) and create them on first noise enable.
- Pre-allocate voices up to voiceCount in idle time after init (requestIdleCallback) so note-on never builds graphs.
- Create NoiseGenerator and SubOscillator lazily when they are enabled.
verifierNote: allocateVoice constructs new Voice(...) plus onVoiceCreated seeding inside noteOn (VoiceManager.ts:96-107; SynthEngine.ts:240-266). The constructor builds the full graph and starts 4 ConstantSources (Voice.ts:104-185), and NoiseGenerator's constructor calls generateBuffers unconditionally (NoiseGenerator.ts:40).

title: WavetableBank duplicates 56 PeriodicWaves per track, builds imported tables inside note-on, and never evicts warp variants
evidence:
- The constructor builds 56 PeriodicWaves: 4 single-frame tables, PWM 16, SUPER SAW 8, FORMANT 12 and HARMONIC 16 (WavetableBank.ts:30-33, 154-208). Every engine does this, although the waves are identical for the shared AudioContext.
- Imported tables (the serum2 pack's are 1-32 frames of 2048 samples) are built on first read by resolveTable (143-152), at one JS FFT plus one createPeriodicWave per frame (58-64). Oscillator.start calls applyWavetablePosition, which reads the table, inside note-on (Oscillator.ts:108-123, 292-297).
- Phase-warp variants are keyed per 5% step, q = round(amount*20) (79-80). They are built synchronously when a warp-amount drag crosses each step and, along with their frame copies (44-47), are never evicted.
impact: Each Oracle track's init repeats the same 56 PeriodicWave builds on the main thread. The first note that uses a pack table can stall the scheduler callback, making notes late and the playhead stutter. Sweeping WARP in a phase mode builds and keeps up to 20 derived tables per base table for the life of the engine, with jank on each new step.
recommendation:
- Cache procedural PeriodicWaves per AudioContext and share them across engines.
- Prebuild imported tables when ensureFramesLoaded resolves, outside note-on and chunked in idle time.
- LRU-evict derived warp tables (keep the current step and its neighbours) and bake on pointer-up or after a debounce.
verifierNote: The WavetableBank constructor calls generateBasicTables per engine (WavetableBank.ts:30-33). resolveTable builds imported tables lazily on first read (143-152), which is reached from Oscillator.start via applyWavetablePosition inside note-on. resolveWarpedTable caches a variant per q = round(amount*20) with no eviction (79-89).

title: Every knob move re-sends the whole module object to every voice with no diffing, and routing changes reconnect all voices
evidence:
The store pushes the whole oscillator object on any field change (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:30-39). SynthEngine sends it to every created voice, including free ones (SynthEngine.ts:446-451; VoiceManager.ts:159-163).

Oscillator.setParams compares only wavetable and warp (145-249), so unison detune, blend, level, pan and tuning are re-applied on every move:
- recalculateDetune writes each unison oscillator's detune.value (UnisonEngine.ts:223-236).
- recalculateGains re-smooths every unison gain (238-260).
- setFrequency calls setValueAtTime on every unison oscillator, twice (Oscillator.ts:243-245 and Voice.ts:432-439).

Routing: setRouting calls applyFilterRouting, which disconnects all source connections with 12 try/catch disconnects per voice and reconnects them (Voice.ts:200-241, 419-422). This also runs for envelope-only routing changes (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:262-268).
impact: At unison 16 a single LEVEL drag issues hundreds of AudioParam automation calls per pointer move. That doubles in the pop-out, where two bridges are mounted, and adds main-thread time that shows up as knob and UI jank. Touching any oscillator knob snaps an in-progress glide to its target. Routing edits and preset loads drop sounding notes for a moment.
recommendation:
- Compare each field in the Oscillator, Filter and Voice setters and skip unchanged values.
- Apply changes only to sounding voices; free voices pick up the seed at their next note-on.
- Handle envelope-only routing changes without reconnecting.
- Track connections explicitly instead of disconnecting through try/catch.
verifierNote: The store pushes the whole oscillator object on any field change (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:30-39), to every voice (SynthEngine.ts:446-451). Oscillator.setParams diffs only the wavetable and warp fields (145-249), so octave, semitone and fine are always defined, setFrequency snaps with no glide (243-245), and Voice calls it a second time (Voice.ts:432-439). setRouting runs applyFilterRouting's 12 try/catch disconnects per voice (Voice.ts:200-241) even for envelope-only changes.

title: Phaser's feedback loop has no DelayNode (silent in Firefox) and its sweep clamps at 0 Hz
evidence:
PhaserEffect wires filters[3] to feedbackGain to filters[0] (PhaserEffect.ts:50-54). That cycle contains no DelayNode. The Web Audio spec mutes such cycles; Firefox follows the spec, while Chromium processes them with an implicit one-render-quantum delay.

The sweep is 1000 Hz ± depth × 3000 Hz (16-17, 83-85). For depth above 0.33 the allpass frequency goes negative and clamps at 0 Hz for part of every LFO cycle.
impact: In Firefox the phaser's wet path is silent. At MIX 100% the equal-power dry gain is cos(π/2) = 0 (FXProcessor.ts:91-100), so enabling PHASER silences the synth entirely. In Chromium the feedback acts as a 128-sample comb filter rather than phaser resonance. At the default depth of 0.5 the sweep sits at 0 Hz for about a quarter of each cycle.
recommendation:
- Insert a short DelayNode (1-2 ms) in the feedback path so the cycle is valid and behaves the same in every browser.
- Sweep exponentially (base × 2^(lfo × octaves)) or clamp the allpass frequency to about 100 Hz to 8 kHz.
verifierNote: PhaserEffect.ts:51-54 connects filters[3] to feedbackGain to filters[0], a cycle with no DelayNode, which the spec mutes and Firefox follows. The sweep is lfoGain = depth×3000 around BASE_FREQ 1000 (16-17, 83-85), so the allpass frequency goes negative and clamps to 0 Hz for depth above about 0.33.

title: FX/mod route ids come from per-page-load counters and collide with restored routes, corrupting patches
evidence: fxSlice.ts:72 `let fxRouteId = 0;` and :118 `const id = `fx-${++fxRouteId}``. modulationSlice.ts:11 `let routeCounter = 0;` and :26 `id: `route-${++routeCounter}``. Both counters restart at 0 on every page load, while the ids persist in snapshots, user presets and exports, and migrateModRoute keeps them (modMath.ts:115 `id: route.id`). removeFXRoute disables only the FIRST route with the id but filters out EVERY match (fxSlice.ts:129-137). updateModRoute and removeModRoute map or filter all matches (modulationSlice.ts:37-47). Both panels key by id (FXPanel.tsx:78, ModulationPanel.tsx:29).
impact: Example: a student adds Drive (fx-1) and Delay (fx-2), refreshes, then adds Chorus, which also gets id fx-1. Removing the Chorus slot deletes both the Drive and Chorus slots and disables Drive, but leaves chorus enabled: an audible effect with no slot to turn it off. With mod routes, editing the new route-1 also rewrites the restored route-1's target and amount, and removing one removes both. React also logs duplicate-key warnings.
recommendation: Mint ids with crypto.randomUUID(). In the shared migration, re-key duplicate ids when loading patches and presets. Make removeFXRoute disable the type of every removed route.

Re-keying duplicate ids during migration changes React keys on load (a harmless remount) but must not run every time the panel mounts, or it causes churn and LFO rebuilds. Ids must be stable across collab peers if routes are ever synced. Changing removeFXRoute to disable every removed type is a strict improvement. No tutorial anchors are affected, unless tutorials target route rows by id, which they don't appear to do (they target 'synth-preset-selector' etc.).

title: Snapshot restore skips the preset migrations; pre-v3 projects can crash the whole app when the synth panel opens
evidence: normalizeSynthTrackState (synthTrackState.ts:119-128) fixes only modRoutes, macros and keyScale. applyPresetData also backfills LFO smooths, rateDivs and rateModifiers (presetSlice.ts:65-80), osc warpMode and warpAmount (85-89), fx merged over DEFAULT_FX including reverb (94), and the fxRoutes, routing and arp defaults (97-107). The file's own comment says pre-v2 project snapshots exist (synthTrackState.ts:113-117), and v3 added warp and reverb (PresetData.ts:27-29). Restoring such a snapshot leaves fx.reverb undefined. On panel mount, `engine.setReverbParams(s.fx.reverb)` (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:335) passes it to FXChain.ts:71 and then ReverbEffect.ts:82 `if (params.enabled !== undefined)`, which throws a TypeError inside a passive effect. The only boundary is the app-root GlobalErrorBoundary (main.tsx:52). restoreSynthState merges instead of replacing (synthTrackState.ts:132-134), so any other missing key keeps the previous track's value. A missing bpm would make LFO.setBPM compute `Math.max(1, undefined)` = NaN (LFO.ts:52). SynthTrackState also has no version field.
impact: Opening the Oracle panel on an old project's track can replace the whole app with the global error screen. Less severely, an old patch silently picks up the previous track's values.
recommendation: Create one version-driven migratePatch(raw) shared by presets, snapshots, import and demos. It should fill every key from defaults and apply patch keys with replace semantics. Add `version` to SynthTrackState. Add fixture tests for v1, v2 and v3 snapshots. Add a DAW-level error boundary around the ChannelStrip.

There's no error boundary inside src/daw, so the global boundary takes over the app. But the crash needs pre-v3 Oracle snapshots saved in real users' projects, and this read-only audit can't confirm those exist. Adding a version field means older clients loading newer saves must ignore unknown fields. Wrapping the ChannelStrip in a DAW-level error boundary is good containment, but the reset must not keep a broken bridge mounted, and anchors inside it (data-tutorial-id 'synth-preset-selector', etc.) must survive remount.

title: Oracle patches are not part of collab: peers hear different sounds and patch edits never propagate
evidence: trackToYMap (YjsDocManager.ts:139-186) writes instrument, presetName, effects, drumPads, organState, sends and automation, but no Oracle patch. The patch lives in useSynthStore and the module cache rather than on the Track (synthTrackState.ts:11-18), so the collab diff, which observes useStore, never sees synth edits. Live notes ARE relayed (useMidiInputRouting.ts:146-157) and each peer plays them on its own local engine and patch.
impact: In a class jam or collab session, every participant hears their own patch for each Oracle track; a joiner usually hears the engine default (INITIALIZE). Knob and preset changes never reach others. A participant who saves serialises their local view, which drops the patch for tracks they never opened (getTrackSynthState returns undefined).
recommendation: Sync the per-track patch as a JSON field per track, as organState and drumPads already are, debounced to the end of each gesture. Better, keep patches in the main store so the existing diffEngine and Yjs path carry them.
verifierNote: trackToYMap (YjsDocManager.ts:139-186) writes effects, drumPads, organState, sends and automation, but no Oracle patch. Nothing under src/daw/collab references oracleSynth or the synth state. The patch lives only in useSynthStore and the module cache, so the useStore-based collab diff never sees it. Live notes are relayed (useMidiInputRouting.ts:146-157) and each peer renders them with its own local patch. The claim that a joiner hears INITIALIZE was not fully verified; it depends on how the joiner hydrates.
impactNote: Confirmed as a gap: trackToYMap serializes drumPads and organState (YjsDocManager.ts:178-181) but never the Oracle patch, and nothing in src/daw/collab references oracleSynth or getTrackSynthState. Patches live outside useStore, so the diff/middleware path can't see them. Peers in a jam hear their own local patch, and knob or preset edits don't propagate. A save from a peer that never opened a track drops that track's patch (SessionSerializer.ts:67-68 → undefined). That is the most concrete harm. How often classrooms use collab is unknown, and this is a missing feature rather than a regression. Medium, raise if collab with Oracle tracks is a promoted classroom flow.
regressionRisks: Syncing a ~10-50 KB JSON patch per edit through Yjs during knob drags floods the doc. Debounce to gesture end, as recommended, and consider sending only the diff of the patch keys. Remote patch application on each peer triggers full engine re-application and the LFO rebuild cost from 09. Rebuilding all 4 LFOs on every remote tweak will stutter audio on Chromebooks unless coalesced. Conflict resolution: a whole-patch JSON field means last-writer-wins, so two students editing different knobs at once lose one edit. Remote applies must not land in local undo history, and must not mark the tutorial synthCheck as complete for the wrong user.

title: The preset 'modified *' flag is wrong both ways: set right after loading a preset, cleared after a track switch
evidence: The dirty watcher (store/index.ts:45-71) calls markDirty whenever any audio-key reference changes. zustand calls listeners synchronously after assigning state (vanilla.mjs setState). applyPresetData returns `isDirty: false` in the SAME set call as new cloned oscillators, filters and the rest (presetSlice.ts:118-139). The watcher then sees new references and sets isDirty back to true, right after loadPreset, initPreset and importPreset (presetSlice.ts:189-208, 234-247). synthTrackState.ts:135-137 already works around this exact race for restores ('the dirty watcher fires on the new object references'), but the preset actions do not. Restore also forces `isDirty: false` (synthTrackState.ts:137), so a modified WOBBLE shows as clean after switching tracks. The UI renders `${presetName} *` (PresetSelector.tsx:135).
impact: Picking 'PAD' immediately shows 'PAD *', and an edited patch looks pristine after a track switch. Students learn that the asterisk means nothing, and any future 'unsaved sound' prompt built on it would misfire.
recommendation: Clear isDirty after the set in the preset actions (as restoreSynthState does), or suppress the watcher while applying. Better, compute dirty as patchHash !== loadedPresetHash and persist that per track.
verifierNote: applyPresetData returns isDirty:false together with freshly cloned audio objects (presetSlice.ts:118-139). The subscribeWithSelector dirty watcher (store/index.ts:45-71) fires synchronously on the new references and calls markDirty, so loadPreset, initPreset and importPreset all leave isDirty true. restoreSynthState works around this with a second setState (synthTrackState.ts:137), and that same workaround makes an edited patch look clean after a track switch. PresetSelector.tsx:135 renders the asterisk.

title: Cmd+Z ignores synth edits and undoes an unrelated timeline edit instead
evidence: The synth store is created with only subscribeWithSelector and no undo (store/index.ts:23-24). useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:59-66 binds Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z to smartUndo and smartRedo, which use either the main-store snapshot history or the Yjs UndoManager (undoMiddleware.ts:309-334). Neither ever records a synth change.
impact: A student turns the cutoff, dislikes it and presses Cmd+Z. The synth stays changed and their last note, clip move or track edit is undone instead, possibly off-screen. Redo recovers it, but students won't notice. Bandlab, Soundtrap and Ableton all undo instrument parameter changes.
recommendation: Record per-gesture patch history (push on pointer-up or preset load) and route Cmd+Z to it while the synth panel has focus. Or move patches into the main store so the existing undo covers them, coalescing knob drags into one step.
verifierNote: The synth store is created with only subscribeWithSelector (store/index.ts:23-24). useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:59-66 sends Cmd+Z and Cmd+Shift+Z unconditionally to smartUndo and smartRedo, which only cover main-store and Yjs history. A synth tweak followed by Cmd+Z therefore undoes the previous DAW edit.

title: User preset library is per-browser, can be shadowed or lost silently, and can't be deleted
evidence: Presets live in localStorage key 'oracle-synth-presets', and write errors are swallowed ('Storage full or unavailable — silently fail', presetSlice.ts:28-34). The list is read once at store creation (:179) with no 'storage' listener, so a second tab saving later overwrites the first tab's additions (:215-217). loadPreset resolves factory, then pack, then user (:189-208), while savePreset accepts any name (:210-219) and the UI upper-cases names (PresetSelector.tsx:88), matching factory naming. Saving 'pad' therefore creates a USER 'PAD' that loads the factory PAD when clicked. deletePreset (:221-226) has no caller in the UI. importPreset checks only name, version and oscillators (:237), and PresetSelector ignores its boolean result (PresetSelector.tsx:117). Partial JSON is applied with e.g. `filters: structuredClone(undefined)` (:124), which crashes subscribers. The DAW autosave shares the same origin's localStorage quota (localSession.ts:12, failures only logged at :18-21).
impact: Sounds saved on a school Chromebook don't exist at home. A saved name can be unreachable, nothing can be deleted or renamed, a bad import fails silently or crashes, and a large preset library can silently starve the crash-recovery autosave of quota.
recommendation: Use an account-backed preset library (API) with a local cache. Reject or auto-suffix factory and pack names. Add delete and rename to the menu. Validate imports through migratePatch and show a toast on success or failure. Listen for 'storage' events, and report quota errors to the user.
verifierNote: saveUserPresets swallows storage errors (presetSlice.ts:28-34), and the user preset list is read once at store creation (:179) with no storage-event listener. loadPreset resolves factory presets first (:189-208), so saving 'pad', which the UI upper-cases (PresetSelector.tsx:88), produces a user preset that can never be loaded. deletePreset has no UI caller (grep). importPreset only checks name, version and oscillators (:237), and handleFileChange ignores its return value.

No tests cover presetSlice, the synthTrackState apply/normalize functions or the Oracle save/load round-trip; only useStoreBridge.test.tsx exists. factoryPresets.ts is about 37 KB of repeated literals with 40 `as [...]` tuple casts, and every preset is labelled `version: 2` although it is shaped as v3 (warp plus reverb, e.g. lines 127 and 141-142).

title: Edits made only to the synth never trigger an autosave
evidence: useAutosave subscribes only to the DAW store (useStore.subscribe, useAutosave.ts:19-25). All synth edits go to the separate useSynthStore (store/index.ts:23-42). The serializer captures the live patch (SessionSerializer.ts:67-68, via getTrackSynthState) only when some DAW-store change has scheduled a write.
impact: A student spends minutes shaping a sound, then refreshes or the tab crashes. Crash recovery restores the patch as it was before those edits, unless an unrelated DAW edit happened afterwards.
recommendation: Also subscribe useAutosave to useSynthStore; the dirty-watcher selector in store/index.ts:45-71 can be reused. Flush on pagehide and visibilitychange.
verifierNote: useAutosave.ts:19-25 subscribes only to useStore, and writeLocalSession has no other caller. There are no pagehide/beforeunload handlers. Synth edits live in useSynthStore (store/index.ts:23-42). DAW `position` updates during playback do schedule a save after playback stops, but synth-only editing with the transport stopped is never autosaved.
impactNote: The mechanism is real. useAutosave.ts:19 subscribes only to useStore, synth edits go only to useSynthStore (store/index.ts:23-42), and nothing bridges them (the only other synth subscriber is useTutorialDetection). The loss window is narrower than claimed, though. Any DAW-store change schedules a write that captures the live patch through getTrackSynthState (synthTrackState.ts:196 returns captureSynthState for the active track). Such changes include transport `position` updates during playback (transportSlice.ts:46), selecting another track, hwActiveNotes from a MIDI keyboard, and clip edits. So a student who tweaks while a loop plays gets an autosave about 1.5s after stopping. The data loss happens only when a student designs sound with transport stopped and then refreshes or crashes before any other DAW interaction. That is plausible but not the common case, so medium. The fix is cheap and correct.
regressionRisks: Subscribing to the whole synth store fires on every knob tick, but the 1.5s debounce absorbs that. Use the existing dirty-watcher selector rather than every state change, so UI-only fields (activeLFOIndex, modWheel, pitchBend) don't schedule writes. writeLocalSession serializes the whole project synchronously, which can be a few ms on Chromebooks with large projects. Debouncing is fine, but a pagehide flush must stay synchronous and quick. File → New clears the session; make sure a pending synth-triggered timer can't rewrite it afterwards (clear the timer on clear).

title: The docked synth cuts off its own controls, hides half of itself off-screen, and lacks the features the tutorial asks for
evidence: The dock body is 33vh (ChannelStrip.tsx:318). Each module sits in a fixed-width slot with overflow:hidden (OracleSynthInline.tsx:56-62) and is forced to the slot's height ([&>*]:h-full, 101-140). The strip scrolls only horizontally (71-79). From the CSS, OscillatorModule needs about 370px (a 40px knob row plus two 28px knob rows, OscillatorModule.module.css:31-45) and EnvelopeModule about 290px (its title has padding-bottom:24px, EnvelopeModule.module.css:17). 33vh is about 215-250px on a 1366×768 laptop, so the UNI/DETUNE/BLEND/WARP and SUS/REL rows are cut off with no scrollbar. The slots add up to about 3,200px (83-155), so LFO, MOD, FX, ARP and ROUTING start about 1,660px in. Macros, voice/glide, Key Lock and Snap to song key, the wheels, master volume and any keyboard exist only in the pop-out (DawSynthLayout.tsx:130-219). Yet tutorial step 'tweak-wobble' requires the CONTROLS dock and says 'Play a few notes … try the macros and filter' (tutorials.ts:470-478). While the engine loads, the dock shows 'Synth engine not available' (OracleSynthInline.tsx:43-51).
impact: In the default container, students can't reach the lower rows of every source module and must scroll sideways to find modulation and FX. Without MIDI hardware they can't play any notes. They can't follow the lesson's instruction to use the macros.

title: Route ids restart after a reload, so new FX and mod routes collide with saved ones
evidence: Route ids come from module-level counters that reset on every page load: `fx-${++fxRouteId}` (fxSlice.ts:72, 118) and `route-${++routeCounter}` (modulationSlice.ts:11, 26). Saved patches keep their ids (captureSynthState clones fxRoutes and modRoutes, synthTrackState.ts:79-88). After a refresh or project load, the first '+ ADD' reuses fx-1 or route-1. removeFXRoute deletes every route with that id but disables only the first route's effect (fxSlice.ts:129-137). updateModRoute and removeModRoute act on every route with the id (modulationSlice.ts:37-47). The panels use route.id as the React key (FXPanel.tsx:76-85; ModulationPanel.tsx:27-34).
impact: Turning one AMT knob also moves a second route. Deleting one FX slot removes both slots but leaves the second effect audibly on, with no slot left to switch it off. Duplicate React keys can also mis-render slots.
recommendation: Use crypto.randomUUID() for new route ids, and de-duplicate ids in normalizeSynthTrackState and applyPresetData.
verifierNote: Ids come from module-level counters: `fx-${++fxRouteId}` (fxSlice.ts:72, 118) and `route-${++routeCounter}` (modulationSlice.ts:11, 26). Both reset on page load, while saved patches keep their ids, and migrateModRoute preserves route.id (modMath.ts:115). removeFXRoute finds the first match, filters out every match, and disables only the first route's type (fxSlice.ts:129-137). updateModRoute maps every route with that id.
impactNote: The mechanism is verified: `let fxRouteId = 0` with `fx-${++fxRouteId}` (fxSlice.ts:72, 118), `let routeCounter = 0` with `route-${++routeCounter}` (modulationSlice.ts:11, 26), and removeFXRoute deletes every route with the id but disables only the first match's type (129-137). Collisions need a saved patch that contains user-created route-N/fx-N ids from an earlier page load. Factory and pack routes use distinct ids ('pad-fx-1', 'serum-3'), and the counters are module-global, so there are no collisions within one session. The trigger is a student who added routes in one session, reloads, and adds more to the same patch. That is realistic for engaged students, and the outcome (coupled knobs, an effect left on with no slot, duplicate React keys) is confusing. But it requires a multi-session editing pattern, so I'd rate it medium rather than high. The fix is small and low-risk.
regressionRisks: Use crypto.randomUUID(), which is available in Chrome secure contexts; add a fallback for http dev or LAN classroom setups. De-duplication in normalizeSynthTrackState/applyPresetData must re-id only the later duplicates and keep the first, and must not rename ids that collab ops or the mod-indicator reference mid-session. If collab syncs synth patches by route id, renaming on load on one client can desync peers, so dedupe deterministically (same input gives the same output on every client).

title: Store-to-engine sync pushes whole sections, rebuilds the mod graph on every drag tick, and runs twice while the pop-out is open
evidence: Any oscillator change calls engine.setOscillatorParams(i, osc) with every field (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:29-51). Oscillator.setParams then re-runs tuning (setFrequency), unison detune and blend, and wavetable position on every voice whenever those keys are present (Oscillator.ts:174-215, 243-248), even for a PAN tweak. Any modRoutes change calls setModRoutes (199-205; SynthEngine.ts:534-541), which runs disconnectAll and then rebuilds every route on every sounding voice, allocating new GainNode and WaveShaperNode objects (ModulationMatrix.ts:83-86, 115-176). This happens on every AMT-knob pointermove. Knob calls onChange on every move even when the snapped value hasn't changed (Knob.tsx:136-150), and setOscParam always allocates a new object (oscillatorSlice.ts:39-47), so the module re-renders anyway. With the pop-out open, both the dock (OracleSynthInline.tsx:30) and the pop-out (OracleSynthView.tsx:22) mount useStoreBridge → useSyncStoreToEngine (useStoreBridge.ts:71), so every change is applied twice.
impact: Dragging a mod amount over held notes causes about 60-120 audio-graph rebuilds per second, plus GC churn. On low-end Chromebooks this risks clicks and zipper noise, and every cost doubles in the pop-out.
recommendation: Diff previous and next state and push only the changed keys. Update a route's existing scaler gain in place (setTargetAtTime) and rebuild only on structural changes. Skip onChange when the snapped value is unchanged, and coalesce knob writes per animation frame. Keep one bridge per engine: ref-count by engine, or unmount the dock's synth content while the pop-out is open.
verifierNote: The modRoutes subscription has no equalityFn (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:199-205), and updateModRoute always returns a new array. Each AMT pointermove therefore runs setRoutes→disconnectAll plus reconnectActiveVoices, allocating new Gain and WaveShaper nodes (ModulationMatrix.ts:83-86, 115-176). The oscillator subscriptions use shallow equality, so unchanged snapped values don't reach the engine, but the module still re-renders. The dock and the pop-out are mounted together (TrackControlsPanel renders both), and each runs useStoreBridge, so the work doubles.

title: The modulation live dot is missing after any remount; when it does run, it re-renders whole modules 30 times a second
evidence: The live-dot effect reads a module-level currentEngine (useModIndicator.ts:26-39, 103-108), and its only dependency is [lfoRoute] (146). The engine is registered by the parent's useSyncStoreToEngine effect (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:22), but React runs child effects before parent effects. So on every fresh mount (selecting the synth track, returning to CONTROLS, switching tracks, loading a project), OscillatorModule and FilterModule see null and never start polling until the route object itself changes. When polling does run, setLiveOffset fires 30 times a second (133-140) from OscillatorModule.tsx:75-76 and FilterModule.tsx:56-57. Each call re-renders the whole module: 8-9 Knobs whose inline closures defeat memo, a 74-option wavetable <select>, and the steppers. Each hook also subscribes to s.modRoutes (70), so any route edit re-renders all four osc and filter modules.
impact: The moving ring that shows a student the LFO riding the cutoff (the WOBBLE lesson) disappears whenever the panel remounts. When it does show, it costs about 30 module renders per second per routed knob, doubled in the pop-out.
recommendation: Pass the engine through context or props instead of a module-level slot. Poll each LFO once per frame in a shared store read with useSyncExternalStore. Render the dot in a tiny <ModLiveDot> that updates SVG attributes through a ref.
verifierNote: currentEngine is a module-level slot set by the parent's useSyncStoreToEngine effect (line 22). The effect in useModIndicator.ts:103-108 bails out when currentEngine is null and depends only on [lfoRoute] (146). Child effects run before parent effects, so on a fresh mount (with no other bridge alive) the dot never starts. title: The visualizers redraw continuously, even when nothing has changed or nothing is visible
evidence: Every WaveformVisualizer redraws a 2,048-point path (the analysers use fftSize 2048, SynthEngine.ts:136-137, 182-187) at 30fps whenever an analyser exists, including in silence. It reads clientWidth and clientHeight every frame and ignores devicePixelRatio (WaveformVisualizer.tsx:17-75). FilterResponseVisualizer calls getFrequencyResponse every frame (43, 89), and each call allocates two Float32Arrays (Filter.ts:129-141). Yet the visualization filter shows only the base response: 'per-voice modulation … is not reflected' (SynthEngine.ts:733-742). The component's own comment says it reflects LFO modulation, which is wrong (FilterResponseVisualizer.tsx:19-23). useAnimationFrame has no visibility gating and gives each canvas its own rAF loop (useAnimationFrame.ts:16-32). The dock runs 5 loops and keeps them going under the pop-out, which runs 6 more. The `time - lastTime < 1000/30` throttle produces an uneven 20-30fps cadence on 60Hz screens. EnvelopeVisualizer stretches a fixed 140px bitmap to 100% width (EnvelopeVisualizer.tsx:24, 123-129).
impact: Up to 11 canvas loops plus constant allocation run on student laptops, competing with audio scheduling. The scopes are blurry on Retina screens and in the scaled pop-out.
recommendation: Draw the filter response only when filter params change. Downsample the scope to the canvas width, and either trigger-align it or draw the static wavetable frame. Use one shared scheduler gated by IntersectionObserver, document.hidden and whether any voices are sounding. Size canvases for devicePixelRatio. Unmount the dock content while the pop-out is open.
verifierNote: WaveformVisualizer draws all fftSize points every frame while an analyser exists, with no silence check, sets canvas.width to clientWidth with no DPR scaling, and runs useAnimationFrame(draw, !!analyser). useAnimationFrame has no visibility gating. Filter.getFrequencyResponse allocates two Float32Arrays per call (Filter.ts:129-141). SynthEngine.ts:733-742 states the viz filter shows only the base response, which contradicts the comment at FilterResponseVisualizer.tsx:19-23.

title: Time knobs are linear and snap to 10ms, and Shift+Arrow fine adjustment does nothing
evidence: Knob defaults step to 0.01 for every range (Knob.tsx:71) and snaps with Math.round(v/step)*step (145, 187-191). Shift+Arrow adds 0.001, which rounds back to the same value, so keyboard fine adjustment does nothing. ATK and DEC run linearly over 0.001-5s and REL over 0.001-10s (EnvelopeModule.tsx:84-134), so one pixel of drag is 25-50ms and values snap to 10ms steps. The PIANO shape's 5ms attack (EnvelopeModule.tsx:28) can't be set by hand, and the compressor's 3ms default attack (FXSlot.tsx:316-326) can't be reached by dragging.
impact: Students can't shape plucks or percussive sounds, which depend on the 1-30ms range, and fine control doesn't work as advertised.
recommendation: Give Knob a scale option ('log' or 'exp'), reusing the cutoff's hzToNorm pattern. Derive the step from the range. Make fine mode use step/10 without re-rounding to the coarse step. Add mouse-wheel support.
verifierNote: Knob defaults step to 0.01 and FINE_MULTIPLIER is 0.1 (Knob.tsx:36, 71). Keyboard fine adjustment rounds (value ± 0.001) back to the 0.01 grid, so it is a no-op. The ATK, DEC and REL knobs pass no step and are linear over 0.001-5s / 0.001-10s (EnvelopeModule.tsx:84-134). At DRAG_SENSITIVITY 0.005, one pixel is 25ms. The compressor's 3ms default can be restored by double-click but can't be reached by dragging.

title: Pointer gestures have no cancel path, causing stuck pitch bend, stuck notes and runaway knobs
evidence: The pitch wheel springs back only in onPointerUp (WheelControl.tsx:61-66, 71-77); there is no onPointerCancel or onLostPointerCapture. PianoKey sends noteOff only on pointerup or pointerleave (PianoKey.tsx:39-47), so closing the pop-out with Esc while holding a key unmounts it without sending noteOff. Knob's move handler ignores e.buttons (Knob.tsx:136-150), so after a lost capture (e.g. alt-tab mid-drag) the knob follows the hovering mouse. The QWERTY hook never releases held notes on cleanup or blur (useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:81-84).
impact: Pitch stays bent or a note drones until the same key is pressed again. Students read this as the synth being broken.
recommendation: Handle pointercancel and lostpointercapture: spring the wheel back, send noteOff, and end the drag. Release all notes and call engine.allNotesOff when the panel or pop-out unmounts or the window loses focus.
verifierNote: The wheel springs back only in onPointerUp, with no cancel handlers (WheelControl.tsx:61-77). Nothing calls allNotesOff on unmount, and the QWERTY cleanup doesn't release notes. But PianoKey's onPointerLeave does fire after pointercancel or capture loss and sends noteOff (PianoKey.tsx:44-46). The Knob 'runaway' only happens while hovering the knob itself, because handlers are element-bound.

title: A new synth track copies whichever patch was last open, and its sound changes when its panel first opens
evidence: useStoreBridge's doc comment says 'defaults are used for first visit' (useStoreBridge.ts:19-26). The code restores only when a cache entry exists (47-49) and never resets the store. useSyncStoreToEngine's initial sync then pushes whatever patch is live in the shared store to the new engine (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:302-342). Until that moment the engine runs its built-in defaults, because usePlaybackEngine applies nothing to tracks with no cached patch (usePlaybackEngine.ts:517-520).
impact: A newly added synth track plays engine defaults, then becomes a copy of the previous track's patch, including its preset name, the moment its panel opens. Saving before the panel is opened stores no patch at all.
recommendation: Give every new oracle-synth track an explicit patch when it's created (INITIALIZE or a chosen preset) via setTrackSynthState, apply it at instrument init, and reset the store to it on first visit.
verifierNote: useStoreBridge.ts:47-49 restores only when a cache entry exists and never resets the store. The only setTrackSynthState callers are the SessionSerializer load paths (556, 721), so new tracks get no seeded patch. The initial sync (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:302-342) then pushes the previous track's live patch. getTrackSynthState returns undefined for tracks that were never opened, so nothing is saved for them.

title: Synth patches and live synth playing don't reach collaborators
evidence: trackToYMap writes scalars, effects and clips but no synth patch (YjsDocManager.ts:139-167), and TRACK_SCALAR_KEYS has no patch field (diffEngine.ts:54-66). The patch lives only in the local useSynthStore and the synthTrackState cache. When a peer opens a track that has no cached patch, their own store's patch is pushed to the engine (useStoreBridge.ts:47-49 plus the initial sync). Notes played on the pop-out keyboard go straight to engine.noteOn (DawSynthLayout.tsx:81-99), whereas KeyboardView relays live notes through studioRealtime (KeyboardView.tsx:95-108).
impact: In a classroom collab session, each participant hears a different synth sound on the same track. Peers who are monitoring a student don't hear that student's synth playing.
recommendation: Store the patch in the Y.Doc (per-track JSON with throttled updates, or per-section maps) and apply remote changes through the bridge. Relay live synth notes the way KeyboardView does.
verifierNote: YjsDocManager.ts and diffEngine.ts have no reference to oracleSynth, synth or settings patch fields. DawSynthLayout's handleNoteOn (81-87) calls engine.noteOn directly, while KeyboardView relays notes through studioRealtime (KeyboardView.tsx:100-101).

title: The preset browser doesn't scale to 93+ presets, and pack presets load eagerly
evidence: A single flat menu lists 11 factory presets, 82 pack presets and all user presets (PresetSelector.tsx:55-58, 161-203) inside a box capped at 360px (computeMenuPlacement, 19-22). It has no search and no categories, even though the pack manifest defines 10 categories (Bass 20, Lead 10, SFX 10, …) and the loader receives a category per preset (packLoader.ts:45-56). There are no prev/next buttons, no audition and no keyboard navigation. A failed import is silent (handleFileChange, 110-124; importPreset returns false). The first synth-panel mount calls loadOraclePacks (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:25), which fetches the manifest plus all 82 preset JSONs (about 1.6MB) in parallel (packLoader.ts:28-56).
impact: Finding a sound means scrolling through about 90 names. The burst of 83 requests on school networks competes with loading the project's samples.
recommendation: Build a browser with category chips, search, favourites, prev/next arrows and click-to-audition. Ship a single index JSON with names and categories, and lazy-load a preset's data when it is selected. Show an error message when an import fails.
verifierNote: computeMenuPlacement caps maxHeight at 360 (PresetSelector.tsx:19-22), and the menu has no search or categories. handleFileChange ignores importPreset's result. loadOraclePacks fetches the manifest plus every preset JSON via Promise.all (packLoader.ts:28-56), and the presets total about 1.7MB on disk. It runs on the first bridge mount (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:25).

title: The synth uses its own grey-and-rainbow visual language instead of the Music Atlas look
evidence: The synth components hard-code 46 distinct hex colours, most often #333 (27 uses), #888 (16) and #444 (15). Module cards are #242424 with #333 borders and 4px radii (OscillatorModule.module.css:6-8; the Filter, Envelope, Noise and Sub modules are the same), and the dock repeats these colours inline (OracleSynthInline.tsx:63-68). Accents form a rainbow: osc #e87070/#d05050, filter #e8a040/#d08830, envelopes and pitch wheel yellow #e8c840/#d0b030 (EnvelopeModule.tsx:41; SynthLayout.tsx:151), noise #70e870, macros #b8a4e3, routing #9d7fce, arp #c785d3, key lock #8fd694 (KeyScaleBar.tsx:11). The primary SAVE button is a bluish #345/#567 (PresetSelector.module.css:60-64). Sibling views use tokens: KeyboardView has 20 lines using var(--color-*).
impact: The synth looks like a bolted-on third-party plugin. It breaks the Music Atlas system (near-black base, white-opacity steps, hairline borders), the rule that colour carries musical meaning, and the no-yellow rule.
recommendation: Restyle from tokens: white/6 surfaces on #101012, white/8 hairlines, #e8e8f0 text, a dim text colour that passes contrast (A11Y#7), 8-12px radii, the white pill for primary actions, and a single neutral control accent. Keep colour for musical meaning: the key colour on Key Lock and scale-highlighted keys, and chord colours on held keys (already in place).
