title: In collab, clip moves, splits and deletes ignore track locks and can delete or duplicate clips
evidence: Moving a clip to another track is two separate store writes, remove then add (MIDI Timeline.tsx:2345-2351, audio 2368-2374). Each write passes through guardTrack, which silently returns the state unchanged when a remote user has that track selected (tracksSlice.ts:82-88). Neither the canvas hit-test nor the commit checks locks or track types (addMidiClip has no type check, 664-671). Audio split and delete call removeAudioBuffer before the guarded store calls (Timeline.tsx:1679-1683, 1964-1968, 2014-2019; useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:399-400).
impact: In a collab session, dragging a clip onto a track a classmate has selected deletes it: the remove succeeds and the add is refused. Dragging a clip out of a locked track duplicates it, with the same id on two tracks. Splitting or deleting audio on a locked track removes the audio while the clip stays, now silent. MIDI clips can also be dropped onto audio tracks and audio clips onto MIDI tracks.
recommendation: Add one store action, moveClip(fromTrackId, toTrackId, clipId, tick), that checks both locks and track-type compatibility before writing anything and makes a single write. On refusal, show a toast and snap the clip back. Only touch AudioBufferStore after the store change succeeds. Refuse drags on locked tracks in hitTestClip and show a lock cursor.
verifierNote: A cross-track move is a separate removeMidiClip/addMidiClip pair (Timeline.tsx:2345-2349, 2368-2372). Each write passes through guardTrack, which silently returns state on a remote lock (tracksSlice.ts:82-88). Timeline.tsx has no lock or remoteUsers check. removeAudioBuffer runs before the guarded remove (1681, 1966, 2016; useKeyboardShortcuts.ts:399-400). addMidiClip has no track-type check (tracksSlice.ts:664-671).
impactNote: The mechanics are confirmed. A cross-track move is removeX then addX, each wrapped in guardTrack, which returns the state unchanged when the track is remote-locked (tracksSlice.ts:82-88, 664-671; Timeline.tsx:2345-2351, 2368-2374). That deletes the clip if the target is locked and duplicates it if the source is locked. Audio split and delete free the buffer before the guarded remove (Timeline.tsx:1679-1683, 1964-1968, 2014-2019). However, locks only exist in collab (isTrackLockedByRemote is a no-op when remoteUsers is empty, tracksSlice.ts:62-75), and TrackHeader already makes locked headers inert, so it's a narrower, conditional scenario. Collab Yjs undo can recover it. The part that also affects solo users isn't reflected in the severity: dragTrackRef picks any track index (Timeline.tsx:2167-2170) with no type check, so a slightly-off vertical drag can drop a MIDI clip into an audio track's midiClips, or the reverse, where it's likely silent. Medium overall, and the moveClip action fixes both.
regressionRisks: A single moveClip action changes what Yjs sees (one transaction instead of remove + add). Check that diffEngine and yjsToZustand handle a clip's track changing without a remote flicker. The snap-back on refusal needs a redraw, which ties to timeline-10's gating. Refusing drags in hitTestClip for locked tracks must still allow selection and playback cursor clicks. If the type check uses track.type, cover tracks whose instrument implies a type, e.g. vocal-fx on audio tracks. Moving the AudioBufferStore calls after the store write affects the timeline-01 fix, so do both together.

title: Level meters re-render every track header each animation frame, and track meters stay dead after a reload
evidence: useMeterLevel runs an endless requestAnimationFrame loop that calls setLevel(Math.round(peak)) on every frame while an analyser exists (useMeterLevel.ts:16-55). TrackHeader turns that into `width: ${liveLevel}%` (TrackHeader.tsx:93, 505-516), and MasterTrackHeader runs two such loops (47-52). Each update re-renders a header built from a motion.div, 6-8 motion.buttons, a Radix Popover and Slider, a select, an input and FixedDigits, plus the unmemoised MasterFxPanel while its pop-out is open. The analyser is looked up during render (TrackHeader.tsx:91-92) inside a memo component (51) whose only props are track and index (TimelineWithHeaders.tsx:107). Track engines are registered in an effect after isReady flips (usePlaybackEngine.ts:379-574), and that change writes nothing to the store (src/daw/hooks/useAudioEngine.ts:13-24). subscribeEngineReady exists (usePlaybackEngine.ts:94-106) but TrackHeader doesn't use it.
impact: During playback, 10 tracks at 60-120 fps means 600-1,200 header renders per second plus the master, all on the main thread alongside Tone scheduling and the canvas. The loops also keep running while stopped. After a refresh, track meters stay flat (only the master meter moves) until the student happens to select or edit each track.
recommendation: Replace the per-header loops with one shared meter loop that runs only while playing, recording or monitoring. It reads all analysers and writes meter widths via refs or CSS variables, with no React state, and stops once levels decay to 0. Look up analysers through useSyncExternalStore(subscribeEngineReady, getEngineReadyVersion) so headers pick them up once audio starts.

During playback that's about 60 renders/s per track, which is real but secondary main-thread load. The 'loops keep running while stopped' cost is overstated: once the level decays to 0, setLevel(0) with an unchanged value bails out without re-rendering, leaving only a cheap getByteTimeDomainData per frame. The dead-meter claim is also overstated. The analyser is looked up during render (91-92), and every header subscribes to selectedTrackId (66), so selecting any track (or any track edit) re-renders all headers and picks up their analysers. Meters stay flat after a reload only until the first track click. Writing widths through refs or CSS variables bypasses React, so the red/yellow/green threshold colouring (TrackHeader.tsx:509-514) needs to move into the imperative path. title: The arrange view never follows the playhead, and you can't scroll past content plus 4 bars

Scrolling is clamped to content + PROJECT_PAD_BARS (4) (Timeline.tsx:60-61, 300-330, 2142-2149, 2551-2559), and nothing scrolls when a drag reaches the edge.

It pages (or scrolls smoothly) when the playhead passes about 85% of the viewport, pauses while the user scrolls or drags, and resumes on play or stop. title: The canvas isn't redrawn when its container resizes, and its height can only grow

After that, the timeline keeps an extra empty scroll range that the header column doesn't have (see timeline-12), and deleting tracks never shrinks the canvas.

title: Audio files can't be dropped onto the timeline, and drops ignore where they land

title: Disposed NAM and pitch-correction worklets stay alive; dispose during async init leaks nodes; worklet registration isn't per context
evidence:
NamWorkletNode.dispose and PitchCorrectionNode.dispose only disconnect (NamWorkletNode.ts:124-129; PitchCorrectionNode.ts:185-190). - PitchCorrectionPedal.dispose nulls pitchNode while initWorklet is still awaiting init, so the continuation throws (caught at 118-121) and the node created in init() is never disposed (102-110).
- NamAmpPedal assigns namNode after init resolves even if the pedal was already disposed (185-199, 223-225).

The worklet module-loaded flag is module-global rather than per AudioContext (PitchCorrectionNode.ts:97-114), although the app already runs a second context for Learn (AudioContextOwner.ts:1-8).

title: Flanger sweep is clamped by the feedback loop; phaser sweep goes below 0 Hz; rate knobs are linear
evidence: FlangerPedal feeds its modulated DelayNode back into itself (delay ↔ feedback, lines 32-33) with a 3 ms base delay ± up to 3 ms of LFO depth (26-27, 40-41, 78-80). Under the Web Audio spec, a DelayNode in a cycle is clamped to at least one render quantum (128 frames, about 2.67 ms at 48 kHz). Feedback is fixed at 0.5 with no control (31). PhaserPedal sweeps its allpass centres linearly at 1000 Hz ± depth × 2000 Hz (92, 98, 154-157), so for depth > 0.5 the frequency goes negative and clamps at 0 Hz for part of each cycle. The Hz-mode knob maps 0–1 linearly to 0.01–40 Hz (143-146).
impact: The flanger loses its characteristic 'jet' sweep. The phaser has a dead spot and an unnatural sweep at high depth. The musically useful 0.1–2 Hz rate range occupies about the first 5% of a 52 px knob.
recommendation: For the flanger, keep the feedback loop on a fixed delay of at least one quantum and modulate a separate delay that isn't part of the loop, or move it to a worklet; expose a feedback control. For the phaser, sweep exponentially between a minimum and maximum frequency (e.g. 200 Hz to 4 kHz) and give the rate knob a logarithmic taper.
verifierNote: FlangerPedal wires delay↔feedback in a cycle with a 3 ms base delay and up to ±3 ms of LFO depth (FlangerPedal.ts:26-33, 78-80), so the Web Audio cycle clamp applies. Feedback is fixed at 0.5. PhaserPedal sets the allpass base to 1000 Hz with LFO gain `depth * 2000` (PhaserPedal.ts:92-98, 154-157), which goes negative for depth > 0.5, and its Hz-mode rate maps linearly to 0.01-40 Hz (143-146).

title: NAM tone accuracy: 48 kHz models run at the device rate; output level ignores each model's loudness metadata
evidence: The bundled models declare 48 kHz training (`"sample_rate":48000` in e.g. roland-jc120.nam and ampeg-svt.nam). The parser reads sample_rate (NamModelParser.ts:52, 116-117), but nothing compares it with the context rate, and the worklet runs at whatever rate the hardware context uses. Output level is a hand-set category constant (gainCompensation 1.0/0.7/0.5 in NamModelStore.ts:29-255) plus a global ×14 for WaveNet (nam-processor.js:476-480). Each file ships metadata.loudness (e.g. −14.89 in roland-jc120.nam), which NamMetadata doesn't model (NamModelParser.ts:7-14). The worklet uses only input channel 0 (nam-processor.js:521).

title: Tuner string indicator measures distance wrongly across octave boundaries

verifierNote: dist = |octave diff|*12 + |pc diff| (TunerDisplay.tsx:134-136), so B3 against C4 gives 12+11=23 and fails the bestDist<=3 cutoff (:141).

title: Latent defects that would surface if the pitch editor were wired back up
evidence:
(a) getCanvasCoords adds scrollLeft/scrollTop to coordinates that are already canvas-relative (PitchEditor.tsx:548-557), so once scrolled, every hit test and every drag pitch (:617-619) is off by the scroll offset.
(b) A top-level `position` subscription (:95) is a drawGrid dependency (:488-502). That means about 30 full redraws per second during playback, each re-scanning raw samples for every segment's waveform (:370-397) and running `edits.find` per segment (:317).
(c) preventDefault in the React onWheel handler (:650-657) is ignored because React wheel listeners are passive, so Ctrl-wheel also zooms the page.
(d) Cmd+Z runs a local one-step undo without stopPropagation (:663-677). The global undo then also fires and reverts an unrelated track edit, because pitchData isn't in undo snapshots (undoMiddleware.ts:111-118).
(e) Analysis runs on the main thread with no error path or retry (PitchEditorModal.tsx:35-48). A throw leaves 'Analyzing pitch...' on screen forever, and an audio buffer that isn't loaded yet is never retried.
(f) smbPitchShift starts its rover at 0 and never compensates the FIFO latency (PitchRenderer.ts:104-112). The first 2,048 output samples are zeros and the shifted audio lags by 2,048 samples (~46 ms), and crossfade() writes it back unaligned (:204-231, 291-297). Segments shorter than 2,048 samples are silently left unedited (:288).
(g) It uses a bluish palette (#111118, #0a0a0f, #7a7a90 at :142-158, 209, 232, 269) and 8-10 px text (:175, 461, 724-789).
impact: No impact today because the editor can't be opened. Each item would become a user-visible bug if the modal were wired back up.
recommendation: Don't revive it as-is. If vocal tuning is wanted, rebuild it on the shared editor core: viewport canvases, pointer events, analysis in a worker, saved segments and edits, and a latency-compensated renderer in a worker.

title: Spotlight queries the DOM and reads layout every frame for the whole lesson
evidence: Spotlight runs an endless rAF loop calling resolveTargetRect each frame (Spotlight.tsx:33-40). For each candidate id, resolveTargetRect runs document.querySelector on the data-tutorial-id attribute plus getBoundingClientRect, then reads the winner's rect again (targetRect.ts:20-36). Targets list up to three ids (e.g. tutorials.ts:594), and ids not yet in the DOM are searched across the whole document every frame. CoachCard repeats the same resolution, plus its own rect read, every 150 ms (CoachCard.tsx:161-185). During playback the per-frame read lands right after React's ~30 Hz commits, forcing synchronous layout.
impact: This is constant main-thread work at the display refresh rate (60–120 Hz) for the entire lesson, even when nothing moves. It is modest on fast machines but adds to the DAW's playback rendering on student hardware.
recommendation: Write one shared useTutorialTarget(target) hook. It resolves the element once per step and re-resolves on a throttled MutationObserver (childList/subtree). It tracks the rect with ResizeObserver plus a capture-phase scroll listener, and runs a short rAF burst only after a mutation, scroll or transition. Spotlight and CoachCard both read from it.

Attribute queries are cheap, and the forced layout mostly replaces layout the frame would do anyway. It is low-level waste, not medium.

title: Track colour palette includes colours that vanish on the dark background
evidence: TRACK_PALETTES (trackColors.ts:5-35) includes #450920 (about 1.2:1 against #101012), #0b3954 (about 1.6:1) and #4a5759 (about 2.5:1), plus near-white pastels (#f7e1d7, #dedbd2, #f9dbbd). New tracks cycle through it until a key is set (tracksSlice.ts:566-573); after that every track is recoloured to the key colour (prismSlice.ts:1430-1434).
impact: Track dots and clips in those colours are hard to see or tell apart (WCAG 1.4.11 needs 3:1), and arbitrary hues compete with the meaning of the key colours.
recommendation: Keep only hues with at least 3:1 contrast against #101012 that don't clash with key colours, or use neutral greys until a key is chosen.

title: Reverb IR is generated at construction and regenerated during SIZE/DECAY drags, cutting the tail and blocking the main thread
evidence: The constructor calls rebuildIR (ReverbEffect.ts:46) even though reverb defaults to off. setSize and setDecay rebuild whenever the value crosses into one of 25 buckets (54-72). An uncached rebuild generates up to 4.5 s × sampleRate × 2 channels of Math.random and Math.pow on the main thread (101-112), then assigns a new AudioBuffer to convolver.buffer (121-124), which reinitializes the convolver.
impact: Every Oracle track pays for IR setup at creation and reload. Dragging SIZE or DECAY while audio plays produces up to 25 main-thread stalls per sweep and drops the reverb tail at each swap, which sounds like stutter and dropouts while sound-designing.
recommendation:
- Build the IR lazily on first enable.
- Debounce rebuilds during drags (pointer-up or about 150 ms idle) and crossfade between two convolvers when swapping.
- Generate IR samples in a worker, or move to an AudioWorklet FDN reverb.
verifierNote: The constructor does call rebuildIR (ReverbEffect.ts:46), and bucket crossings rebuild (54-72). However, the generated IR data is cached in a static, context-independent irCache keyed by size, decay and sample rate (34, 97-119). Tracks after the first therefore pay only the AudioBuffer copy and convolver.buffer assignment, and the Math.random generation stalls happen only on the first visit to each bucket.

title: OSC 2 / SUB / NOISE on-off toggles only take effect at the next note
evidence: Voice.setOscillatorParams, setSubOscillatorParams and setNoiseParams only update the osc1Enabled/osc2Enabled/subEnabled/noiseEnabled flags (Voice.ts:426-453). Sources are started only in startActiveSources at note-on (403-408) and stopped when the voice is freed or stolen.
impact: Turning OSC 2, SUB or NOISE on while a chord or long note sounds does nothing until the next note, and turning one off leaves it sounding until the note ends. Students exploring the synth get no immediate feedback.
recommendation: When a source is enabled on an active voice, start it immediately, since its envelope gain already tracks the voice's envelope. When it is disabled, fade it out and stop it.
verifierNote: setOscillatorParams, setSubOscillatorParams and setNoiseParams only update the enabled flags (Voice.ts:426-453). Sources are started only in startActiveSources at note-on (403-408).

title: Compressor is a hidden 50/50 parallel blend, and FX card order has no effect on processing
evidence:
CompressorEffect.updateParams never calls setMix (CompressorEffect.ts:42-48), and CompressorParams has no mix field (types.ts:229-235). FXProcessor's default mixValue of 0.5 (FXProcessor.ts:18) therefore gives an equal-power blend of 0.707 dry + 0.707 wet (85-101).

FXChain hard-wires the order drive > chorus > phaser > delay > reverb > compressor (FXChain.ts:44-51). FXPanel renders user-added, re-typable cards in fxRoutes order (FXPanel.tsx:76-86), and the engine never reads fxRoutes or their `target`.
impact: Turning COMP on makes the patch louder (two coherent paths plus the compressor's automatic makeup gain) and leaves about 70% of the signal uncompressed, so it cannot control resonance peaks. A student who adds REVERB before DELAY sees that order on screen, but the audio always runs delay into reverb.
recommendation:
- Make the compressor serial (100% wet) or add an explicit MIX control.
- Either rewire FXChain to follow fxRoutes order, or present the chain as a fixed order in the UI.
verifierNote: CompressorEffect.updateParams never calls setMix (CompressorEffect.ts:42-48), so the mixValue default of 0.5 gives about 0.707 dry + 0.707 wet (FXProcessor.ts:18, 85-101). FXChain hard-wires the processing order (FXChain.ts:44-51), while FXPanel renders cards in fxRoutes order (FXPanel.tsx:76-86). No file in audio/ or hooks/ reads fxRoutes.

title: If the track is disposed while init is still awaiting ctx.resume(), the half-built engine's running nodes leak
evidence: init awaits 'if (this.ctx.state === 'suspended') await this.ctx.resume()' on the host's shared context with no cancellation (SynthEngine.ts:123-126). It then builds and starts about 17 source nodes and connects analyser -> ctx.destination (139-142, 168-218). OracleSynthAdapter.init uses this.engine after that await (OracleSynthAdapter.ts:16-29). If dispose() ran in the meantime, for example after a track delete, instrument switch, undo or collab edit while the context was still suspended after a refresh, this.engine is null and init throws. The half-built engine's sources stay connected to the destination and are never stopped.
impact: Running nodes and their CPU leak on the shared context for the life of the page. There is no audible symptom, but the leak grows with each such edit made before the first user gesture.
recommendation:
- Don't call resume() from an engine embedded in a host context; the host owns the context state.
- Add a disposed flag that is checked after every await in SynthEngine.init and OracleSynthAdapter.init, and release the half-built engine if it is set.
verifierNote: OracleSynthAdapter sets this.engine before awaiting init (OracleSynthAdapter.ts:17-18). A dispose() during the await calls releaseResources on a not-yet-built engine. SynthEngine.init then continues after `await this.ctx.resume()` (SynthEngine.ts:124-126), builds and starts sources, and connects the analyser to ctx.destination (142). The adapter then dereferences a null this.engine (21), and the built nodes are never released.

title: The mod wheel position isn't re-applied after a remount or track switch
evidence: The initial sync pushes every parameter except modWheel and pitchBend (useSyncStoreToEngine.ts:302-342). modWheel is global store state that isn't part of SynthTrackState (synthTrackState.ts:27-50), and its subscription fires only on change (163-169).
